metric_name_standard: sample (maximum-likelihood, divisor T) covariance matrix
canonical_ref: Anderson 2003, An Introduction to Multivariate Statistical Analysis (3rd ed.), Wiley, §3.2 (MLE of the covariance matrix, divisor N)
canonical_definition: Sigma_hat = (1/T) sum_t (x_t - xbar)(x_t - xbar)^T; for unit-variance inputs the off-diagonal is Pearson r
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, p.3-4 (supplement.txt:136-157): 'Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1].' Keywords: undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous. GitBook basic-statistics.md:15-45 repeats the text (its keyword line says 'undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate'). Neither source documents the '-sq' (squared) variants generated by pyspi/config.yaml.
delegate_lib: scikit-learn==1.9.1 sklearn.covariance.EmpiricalCovariance().fit(X).covariance_; numpy==2.5.4
implemented_as: Data z-scores each channel with ddof=1 (pipeline default); sklearn.covariance.EmpiricalCovariance() with defaults is fit on the (T x P) array; no shrinkage; covariance_ off-diagonal returned (diagonal NaN). Sample covariance uses divisor T (np.cov bias=1) after sample-mean centring, so on the default pipeline the off-diagonal equals (T-1)/T * Pearson r. Squared variant (cov-sq_*) = np.square of the same matrix, labelled unsigned.

what_changed: Canonical MLE covariance (divisor T), fp-exact. complexity_P_T: O(P^2 T) for the empirical covariance + O(P^3) for scipy.linalg.pinvh (a full eigh) that sklearn _empirical_covariance.py:_set_covariance runs for precision_ on every fit; one fit per Data and estimator (pyspi/statistics/basic.py:Estimators._from_cache). Measured fresh P_exponent 0.13, T_exponent 0.14: between 8 and 32 channels and 256 and 1024 samples the ~0.7 ms of fixed sklearn validation dominates, so neither exponent reflects the algorithm. At 118x1024 the P^3 term dominates: in the 118x1024 EmpiricalCovariance profile eigh is 58.7% and np.cov 15.4% of the call; the same pinvh on a 118x118 matrix runs for every estimator of this family.

opportunity: Compute precision_ with a Cholesky factorisation (scipy.linalg.cho_factor + cho_solve, or LAPACK potri) instead of scipy.linalg.pinvh, which sklearn's _empirical_covariance.py:_set_covariance runs as a full eigh for every fit; in pyspi this means fitting with store_precision=False in basic.py:Estimators._from_cache and inverting there at fit time (before any identifier's in-place np.fill_diagonal at basic.py:49-50), with a pinvh fallback when the factorisation fails.
speedup_basis: profile:audit/profiles/micro/prof_basic.cov.EmpiricalCovariance__118x1024.pstats scipy/linalg/_decomp.py:eigh 58.7% (pinvh 63.0%) of this call, the same 118x118 pinvh + complexity: Cholesky inverse ~P^3 vs eigh ~9P^3 flops; scratch timing at 118x118 pinvh 2.17 ms vs Cholesky inverse 0.21 ms; this unit's measured fresh 118x1024 wall is 3.77 ms (summary.json), so the 2.17 ms pinvh is ~58% of it and the Amdahl bound is 1/(1-0.58) = 2.4x. metric_name_standard: Reweighted Minimum Covariance Determinant (FAST-MCD) robust covariance matrix entry (computed by sklearn EllipticEnvelope, an outlier detector whose fitted covariance is the MinCovDet estimate); cov-sq_EllipticEnvelope is its square
canonical_ref: Rousseeuw P.J. 1985, "Multivariate estimation with high breakdown point", in Mathematical Statistics and Applications Vol. B, 283-297 (MCD definition); Rousseeuw P.J. & Van Driessen K. 1999, Technometrics 41(3):212-223 (FAST-MCD: C-step theorem, raw consistency factor med(d^2)/chi2_{p,0.5}, reweighting with hard weights d^2 <= chi2_{p,0.975}); consistency factor c_alpha = alpha / F_{chi2_{p+2}}(chi2_{p,alpha}): Croux C. & Haesbroeck G. 1999, J Multivar Anal 71:161-190; small-sample factors: Pison G., Van Aelst S., Willems G. 2002, Metrika 55:111-123
canonical_definition: Raw MCD: among all h-subsets (default h = floor((n+p+1)/2), maximal breakdown) choose H minimising det(S_H); mu_raw = mean(H), Sigma_raw = c(p,h/n) * S_H. Reweighted MCD: w_i = 1[d^2(x_i; mu_raw, Sigma_raw) <= chi2_{p,0.975}], mu = weighted mean, Sigma = c(p,0.975) * weighted sample covariance (robustbase uses divisor sum(w)-1 and optional small-sample factors). Off-diagonal Sigma_ij is a robust, Gaussian-consistent covariance.
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, pp.3-4: "Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1]. We use v0.24.1 of scikit-learn [2] ... the elliptic envelope (EllipticEnvelope) [3] and the minimum covariance determinant (MinCovDet) methods for outlier removal"; [3] = Rousseeuw & Van Driessen 1999 Technometrics 41:212. Keywords "undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous". GitBook basic-statistics.md:21-25 same text (links to sklearn EllipticEnvelope / MinCovDet pages; no version). The -sq variant is not described in the supplement (only items 2/3 cov_EllipticEnvelope, cov_MinCovDet).
delegate_lib: scikit-learn==1.9.1 (scipy==1.17.1 linalg.pinvh, numpy==2.5.4): sklearn.covariance.EllipticEnvelope().fit -> MinCovDet.fit (via EllipticEnvelope.fit super call) -> fast_mcd, correct_covariance, reweight_covariance; attribute covariance_
implemented_as: Data z-scored per channel over the full sample (ddof=1; optional detrend first). z (T x P) passed to sklearn EllipticEnvelope() with all defaults and random_state=None (global numpy RNG). FAST-MCD raw search: h = ceil((T+P+1)/2); T<=500: 30 random h-subsets x 2 C-steps, best 10 refined; T>500: random partition into T//300 subsets, 500 trials, merge on <=1500 samples. Raw distances divided by the Croux-Haesbroeck factor c(P,h/T); rows with d2 < chi2_{P,0.975} kept; Sigma = c(P,0.975) * MLE covariance (divisor n_w) of kept rows; precision_ = scipy.linalg.pinvh(Sigma). EllipticEnvelope.fit runs exactly MinCovDet.fit and then only sets offset_ (contamination=0.1 never affects covariance_/precision_). pyspi returns the covariance_ matrix as is (no normalisation to correlation), diagonal set to NaN in place on the cached fit; cov-sq_EllipticEnvelope returns its elementwise square. One fit per Data object per estimator name, shared by cov/prec and squared/unsquared identifiers.

deviation_from_documented: Version: documented sklearn v0.24.1, executed 1.9.1; the MCD correction and reweighting changed (raw median factor -> Croux-Haesbroeck factor; reweighted covariance now multiplied by c(P,0.975) = 1.055-1.104 for P=5..2), so values are not those of the documented version (probe p4.py, ratios 1.055-1.10). Range: documented "equivalent to correlation, within [-1,1]" is false for this estimator: the robust scatter of z-scored data has diagonal != 1 (0.19 on contaminated, 0.43-1.17 on iid T=64) and off-diagonals exceeding 1 occur (1.141 cointegrated T=256; 1.0478 rank-deficient shared_envelope). Estimator identity: documented as a separate "elliptic envelope" outlier-removal method; its covariance/precision are exactly MinCovDet (bit-identical under equal RNG state), so the EllipticEnvelope and MinCovDet identifiers are the same quantity up to RNG noise. cov-sq_EllipticEnvelope undocumented in the supplement. Stochastic output (global RNG) not documented in the supplement (documented in tests/README.md).
deviation_from_canonical: Close variant of reweighted FAST-MCD: (1) the search is a stochastic approximation of the MCD optimum (inherent to FAST-MCD) but the random starts come from the global numpy RNG, so the selected h-subset and hence values vary run to run (spread up to 0.34 at T=64); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2) instead of floor; (3) reweighted covariance uses the MLE divisor n_w (robustbase: n_w - 1) and no small-sample correction (Pison et al. 2002); (4) raw consistency factor is the asymptotic Croux-Haesbroeck factor rather than RVD 1999 median rescaling; (5) the input is z-scored with non-robust mean/SD over the full sample before the robust fit, so the output is a robust covariance in units of the contaminated SD, not a robust correlation.

From the same raw h-subset robustbase agrees to 3.5e-15 (rdet 5/6; the sixth differs by one reweighting point, 0.0118). what_changed: Same computation as cov_MinCovDet: EllipticEnvelope.fit is MinCovDet.fit plus offset_, so the output is bitwise the MinCovDet covariance for the same RNG state and differs from cov_MinCovDet in a Calculator pass only by RNG position (up to 0.111 at T=64). Reweighted FAST-MCD covariance of the z-scored data, computed exactly as sklearn 1.9.1 defines it (external robustbase agrees to 3.5e-15 given the same raw h-subset). Differs from the canonical reweighted MCD by: (1) the raw h-subset is a FAST-MCD local optimum drawn from the global numpy RNG, so the value depends on the seed and on RNG position (20-seed spread 0.155-0.257 at T=64, 0.0027-0.0044 at T=4096) and is often not the lowest-determinant subset (sklearn's seed_all(42) subset is the best found in 3/14 runs; rrcov's search finds lower determinants on contaminated|256 in all 20 seeds); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2); (3) MLE divisor n_w and c(p,0.975) applied even when every point is kept. Differs from the supplement: it is not a correlation in [-1,1] (values up to 1.141; 0.15 on contaminated data where the robust correlation is 0.81, because the non-robust z-score sets the scale), and sklearn 1.9.1 multiplies the reweighted covariance by c(p,0.975), which the documented 0.24.1 did not (source only).

metric_name_standard: Reweighted Minimum Covariance Determinant (FAST-MCD) robust covariance matrix entry (computed by sklearn EllipticEnvelope, an outlier detector whose fitted covariance is the MinCovDet estimate); cov-sq_EllipticEnvelope is its square
canonical_ref: Rousseeuw P.J. 1985, "Multivariate estimation with high breakdown point", in Mathematical Statistics and Applications Vol. B, 283-297 (MCD definition); Rousseeuw P.J. & Van Driessen K. 1999, Technometrics 41(3):212-223 (FAST-MCD: C-step theorem, raw consistency factor med(d^2)/chi2_{p,0.5}, reweighting with hard weights d^2 <= chi2_{p,0.975}); consistency factor c_alpha = alpha / F_{chi2_{p+2}}(chi2_{p,alpha}): Croux C. & Haesbroeck G. 1999, J Multivar Anal 71:161-190; small-sample factors: Pison G., Van Aelst S., Willems G. 2002, Metrika 55:111-123
canonical_definition: Raw MCD: among all h-subsets (default h = floor((n+p+1)/2), maximal breakdown) choose H minimising det(S_H); mu_raw = mean(H), Sigma_raw = c(p,h/n) * S_H. Reweighted MCD: w_i = 1[d^2(x_i; mu_raw, Sigma_raw) <= chi2_{p,0.975}], mu = weighted mean, Sigma = c(p,0.975) * weighted sample covariance (robustbase uses divisor sum(w)-1 and optional small-sample factors). Off-diagonal Sigma_ij is a robust, Gaussian-consistent covariance.
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, pp.3-4: "Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1]. We use v0.24.1 of scikit-learn [2] ... the elliptic envelope (EllipticEnvelope) [3] and the minimum covariance determinant (MinCovDet) methods for outlier removal"; [3] = Rousseeuw & Van Driessen 1999 Technometrics 41:212. Keywords "undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous". GitBook basic-statistics.md:21-25 same text (links to sklearn EllipticEnvelope / MinCovDet pages; no version). The -sq variant is not described in the supplement (only items 2/3 cov_EllipticEnvelope, cov_MinCovDet).

implemented_as: Data z-scored per channel over the full sample (ddof=1; optional detrend first). z (T x P) passed to sklearn EllipticEnvelope() with all defaults and random_state=None (global numpy RNG). FAST-MCD raw search: h = ceil((T+P+1)/2); T<=500: 30 random h-subsets x 2 C-steps, best 10 refined; T>500: random partition into T//300 subsets, 500 trials, merge on <=1500 samples. Raw distances divided by the Croux-Haesbroeck factor c(P,h/T); rows with d2 < chi2_{P,0.975} kept; Sigma = c(P,0.975) * MLE covariance (divisor n_w) of kept rows; precision_ = scipy.linalg.pinvh(Sigma). EllipticEnvelope.fit runs exactly MinCovDet.fit and then only sets offset_ (contamination=0.1 never affects covariance_/precision_). pyspi returns the covariance_ matrix as is (no normalisation to correlation), diagonal set to NaN in place on the cached fit; cov-sq_EllipticEnvelope returns its elementwise square. One fit per Data object per estimator name, shared by cov/prec and squared/unsquared identifiers.

deviation_from_documented: Version: documented sklearn v0.24.1, executed 1.9.1; the MCD correction and reweighting changed (raw median factor -> Croux-Haesbroeck factor; reweighted covariance now multiplied by c(P,0.975) = 1.055-1.104 for P=5..2), so values are not those of the documented version (probe p4.py, ratios 1.055-1.10). Range: documented "equivalent to correlation, within [-1,1]" is false for this estimator: the robust scatter of z-scored data has diagonal != 1 (0.19 on contaminated, 0.43-1.17 on iid T=64) and off-diagonals exceeding 1 occur (1.141 cointegrated T=256; 1.0478 rank-deficient shared_envelope). Estimator identity: documented as a separate "elliptic envelope" outlier-removal method; its covariance/precision are exactly MinCovDet (bit-identical under equal RNG state), so the EllipticEnvelope and MinCovDet identifiers are the same quantity up to RNG noise. cov-sq_EllipticEnvelope undocumented in the supplement. Stochastic output (global RNG) not documented in the supplement (documented in tests/README.md).
deviation_from_canonical: Close variant of reweighted FAST-MCD: (1) the search is a stochastic approximation of the MCD optimum (inherent to FAST-MCD) but the random starts come from the global numpy RNG, so the selected h-subset and hence values vary run to run (spread up to 0.34 at T=64); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2) instead of floor; (3) reweighted covariance uses the MLE divisor n_w (robustbase: n_w - 1) and no small-sample correction (Pison et al. 2002); (4) raw consistency factor is the asymptotic Croux-Haesbroeck factor rather than RVD 1999 median rescaling; (5) the input is z-scored with non-robust mean/SD over the full sample before the robust fit, so the output is a robust covariance in units of the contaminated SD, not a robust correlation.

It differs from canonical MCD (RNG-dependent h-subset, h = ceil, MLE divisor) and from the supplement (values up to 1.141, so not a correlation).
what_changed: Same computation as cov_MinCovDet: EllipticEnvelope.fit is MinCovDet.fit plus offset_, so the output is bitwise the MinCovDet covariance for the same RNG state and differs from cov_MinCovDet in a Calculator pass only by RNG position (up to 0.111 at T=64). Reweighted FAST-MCD covariance of the z-scored data, computed exactly as sklearn 1.9.1 defines it (external robustbase agrees to 3.5e-15 given the same raw h-subset). Differs from the canonical reweighted MCD by: (1) the raw h-subset is a FAST-MCD local optimum drawn from the global numpy RNG, so the value depends on the seed and on RNG position (20-seed spread 0.155-0.257 at T=64, 0.0027-0.0044 at T=4096) and is often not the lowest-determinant subset (sklearn's seed_all(42) subset is the best found in 3/14 runs; rrcov's search finds lower determinants on contaminated|256 in all 20 seeds); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2); (3) MLE divisor n_w and c(p,0.975) applied even when every point is kept. Differs from the supplement: it is not a correlation in [-1,1] (values up to 1.141; 0.15 on contaminated data where the robust correlation is 0.81, because the non-robust z-score sets the scale), and sklearn 1.9.1 multiplies the reweighted covariance by c(p,0.975), which the documented 0.24.1 did not (source only).

metric_name_standard: Reweighted Minimum Covariance Determinant (FAST-MCD) robust covariance matrix entry (computed by sklearn EllipticEnvelope, an outlier detector whose fitted covariance is the MinCovDet estimate); cov-sq_EllipticEnvelope is its square
canonical_ref: Rousseeuw P.J. 1985, "Multivariate estimation with high breakdown point", in Mathematical Statistics and Applications Vol. B, 283-297 (MCD definition); Rousseeuw P.J. & Van Driessen K. 1999, Technometrics 41(3):212-223 (FAST-MCD: C-step theorem, raw consistency factor med(d^2)/chi2_{p,0.5}, reweighting with hard weights d^2 <= chi2_{p,0.975}); consistency factor c_alpha = alpha / F_{chi2_{p+2}}(chi2_{p,alpha}): Croux C. & Haesbroeck G. 1999, J Multivar Anal 71:161-190; small-sample factors: Pison G., Van Aelst S., Willems G. 2002, Metrika 55:111-123
canonical_definition: Raw MCD: among all h-subsets (default h = floor((n+p+1)/2), maximal breakdown) choose H minimising det(S_H); mu_raw = mean(H), Sigma_raw = c(p,h/n) * S_H. Reweighted MCD: w_i = 1[d^2(x_i; mu_raw, Sigma_raw) <= chi2_{p,0.975}], mu = weighted mean, Sigma = c(p,0.975) * weighted sample covariance (robustbase uses divisor sum(w)-1 and optional small-sample factors). Off-diagonal Sigma_ij is a robust, Gaussian-consistent covariance.
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, pp.3-4: "Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1]. We use v0.24.1 of scikit-learn [2] ... the elliptic envelope (EllipticEnvelope) [3] and the minimum covariance determinant (MinCovDet) methods for outlier removal"; [3] = Rousseeuw & Van Driessen 1999 Technometrics 41:212. Keywords "undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous". GitBook basic-statistics.md:21-25 same text (links to sklearn EllipticEnvelope / MinCovDet pages; no version). The -sq variant is not described in the supplement (only items 2/3 cov_EllipticEnvelope, cov_MinCovDet).
delegate_lib: scikit-learn==1.9.1 (scipy==1.17.1 linalg.pinvh, numpy==2.5.4): sklearn.covariance.EllipticEnvelope().fit -> MinCovDet.fit (via EllipticEnvelope.fit super call) -> fast_mcd, correct_covariance, reweight_covariance; attribute covariance_
implemented_as: Data z-scored per channel over the full sample (ddof=1; optional detrend first). z (T x P) passed to sklearn EllipticEnvelope() with all defaults and random_state=None (global numpy RNG). FAST-MCD raw search: h = ceil((T+P+1)/2); T<=500: 30 random h-subsets x 2 C-steps, best 10 refined; T>500: random partition into T//300 subsets, 500 trials, merge on <=1500 samples. Raw distances divided by the Croux-Haesbroeck factor c(P,h/T); rows with d2 < chi2_{P,0.975} kept; Sigma = c(P,0.975) * MLE covariance (divisor n_w) of kept rows; precision_ = scipy.linalg.pinvh(Sigma). EllipticEnvelope.fit runs exactly MinCovDet.fit and then only sets offset_ (contamination=0.1 never affects covariance_/precision_). pyspi returns the covariance_ matrix as is (no normalisation to correlation), diagonal set to NaN in place on the cached fit; cov-sq_EllipticEnvelope returns its elementwise square. One fit per Data object per estimator name, shared by cov/prec and squared/unsquared identifiers.

deviation_from_documented: Version: documented sklearn v0.24.1, executed 1.9.1; the MCD correction and reweighting changed (raw median factor -> Croux-Haesbroeck factor; reweighted covariance now multiplied by c(P,0.975) = 1.055-1.104 for P=5..2), so values are not those of the documented version (probe p4.py, ratios 1.055-1.10). Range: documented "equivalent to correlation, within [-1,1]" is false for this estimator: the robust scatter of z-scored data has diagonal != 1 (0.19 on contaminated, 0.43-1.17 on iid T=64) and off-diagonals exceeding 1 occur (1.141 cointegrated T=256; 1.0478 rank-deficient shared_envelope). Estimator identity: documented as a separate "elliptic envelope" outlier-removal method; its covariance/precision are exactly MinCovDet (bit-identical under equal RNG state), so the EllipticEnvelope and MinCovDet identifiers are the same quantity up to RNG noise. cov-sq_EllipticEnvelope undocumented in the supplement. Stochastic output (global RNG) not documented in the supplement (documented in tests/README.md).
deviation_from_canonical: Close variant of reweighted FAST-MCD: (1) the search is a stochastic approximation of the MCD optimum (inherent to FAST-MCD) but the random starts come from the global numpy RNG, so the selected h-subset and hence values vary run to run (spread up to 0.34 at T=64); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2) instead of floor; (3) reweighted covariance uses the MLE divisor n_w (robustbase: n_w - 1) and no small-sample correction (Pison et al. 2002); (4) raw consistency factor is the asymptotic Croux-Haesbroeck factor rather than RVD 1999 median rescaling; (5) the input is z-scored with non-robust mean/SD over the full sample before the robust fit, so the output is a robust covariance in units of the contaminated SD, not a robust correlation.
units_and_range: cov: dimensionless (z-score units), signed, symmetric, unbounded in principle; typical |value| <= ~1.2 (observed max 1.141); cov-sq >= 0. Diagonal NaN. NaN for all entries only if the fit raises (e.g. "covariance of the support data is equal to 0", _robust_covariance.py:853-857), which Calculator converts to an all-NaN block.

It differs from canonical MCD (RNG-dependent h-subset, h = ceil, MLE divisor) and from the supplement (values up to 1.141, so not a correlation).
what_changed: Same computation as cov_MinCovDet: EllipticEnvelope.fit is MinCovDet.fit plus offset_, so the output is bitwise the MinCovDet covariance for the same RNG state and differs from cov_MinCovDet in a Calculator pass only by RNG position (up to 0.111 at T=64). Reweighted FAST-MCD covariance of the z-scored data, computed exactly as sklearn 1.9.1 defines it (external robustbase agrees to 3.5e-15 given the same raw h-subset). Differs from the canonical reweighted MCD by: (1) the raw h-subset is a FAST-MCD local optimum drawn from the global numpy RNG, so the value depends on the seed and on RNG position (20-seed spread 0.155-0.257 at T=64, 0.0027-0.0044 at T=4096) and is often not the lowest-determinant subset (sklearn's seed_all(42) subset is the best found in 3/14 runs; rrcov's search finds lower determinants on contaminated|256 in all 20 seeds); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2); (3) MLE divisor n_w and c(p,0.975) applied even when every point is kept. Differs from the supplement: it is not a correlation in [-1,1] (values up to 1.141; 0.15 on contaminated data where the robust correlation is 0.81, because the non-robust z-score sets the scale), and sklearn 1.9.1 multiplies the reweighted covariance by c(p,0.975), which the documented 0.24.1 did not (source only).

metric_name_standard: graphical-lasso (l1-penalised Gaussian MLE) covariance estimate W = Theta_hat^{-1}, off-diagonal entries; alpha = 0.01; cov-sq is its square
canonical_ref: Friedman J, Hastie T, Tibshirani R 2008, 'Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso', Biostatistics 9(3):432-441, eq. (1)/(2.1) (diagonal penalised); off-diagonal-only penalty: Yuan M, Lin Y 2007, 'Model selection and estimation in the Gaussian graphical model', Biometrika 94(1):19-35, eq. (4); Banerjee O, El Ghaoui L, d'Aspremont A 2008, JMLR 9:485-516
canonical_definition: Theta_hat = argmin_{Theta > 0} -log det Theta + tr(S Theta) + alpha * sum_{i != j} |Theta_ij| (Friedman 2008 sums over all i,j incl. the diagonal; Yuan & Lin 2007 penalise off-diagonals only); Sigma_hat = W = Theta_hat^{-1}; KKT: W_ii = S_ii (+alpha if diagonal penalised), W_ij = S_ij + alpha*sign(Theta_ij) if Theta_ij != 0, |W_ij - S_ij| <= alpha otherwise; partial correlation rho_ij|rest = -Theta_ij / sqrt(Theta_ii Theta_jj)
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, p.3-4: 'Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1]. We use v0.24.1 of scikit-learn ... the Lasso technique, which uses an l1-regularization to sparsify the covariance matrix GraphicalLasso (as well as a method with the regularization method chosen through cross validation with five splits, GraphicalLassoCV)'; keywords 'undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous'. GitBook basic-statistics.md (Covariance) repeats the text but gives keywords 'undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, contemporaneous'. The -sq (squared) identifiers are not described in the supplement. Identifiers: cov_GraphicalLasso, cov-sq_GraphicalLasso.

implemented_as: Each channel z-scored (ddof=1, optional detrend); X = (T, P) array; sklearn.GraphicalLasso() with library defaults: S = biased empirical covariance (divide by T, so S_ii=(T-1)/T); alpha = 0.01 fixed (absolute, on the (T-1)/T-scaled correlation matrix). Solver: sklearn block coordinate descent (Friedman 2008 glasso algorithm) with off-diagonal-only l1 penalty, start 0.95*S off-diagonal, stop when |dual gap| < 1e-4 or after 100 sweeps (warning silenced). Returns covariance_ (the solver's W iterate, diagonal = S_ii) with diagonal set to NaN; -sq returns the elementwise square. Fit shared through data.covariance['GraphicalLasso'] by cov, cov-sq, prec, prec-sq; exactly symmetric because rows/columns are written together.

deviation_from_documented: (1) The supplement says the l1 penalty 'sparsif[ies] the covariance matrix'; it sparsifies the precision matrix (penalty on Theta, _graph_lasso.py:52, :64); W = covariance_ is generally dense (probe sparse_precision T=1024: no exact zeros in W while Theta has 2). (2) 'correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent': here W is a shrunk estimate with |W_ij - S_ij| <= alpha and S_ij = (T-1)/T * r_ij, so values differ from Pearson r by up to alpha + r/T. Range [-1,1] holds. (3) Documented scikit-learn v0.24.1; executed 1.9.1 (inner CD max_iter changed from max_iter to max(20, max_iter), do_screening and a pre-loop duality-gap early exit added (1.9.1 _cd_fast.pyx:1173-1182; absent in 0.24.1, whose first gap check is inside the loop after a coordinate pass, 0.24.1 _cd_fast.pyx:571-610). Overall numeric effect versus 0.24.1 not measured; the 1.9.1 exit causes the var2_bivariate T=4096 stall, see candidates). (4) GitBook keywords 'nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate' contradict the supplement/class labels 'linear, signed, multivariate'. (5) -sq variants undocumented.
deviation_from_canonical: Variant of Friedman et al. 2008: the diagonal is not penalised (sklearn docstring _graph_lasso.py:328-329; W_ii = S_ii exactly, probe), which matches Yuan & Lin 2007 / R glasso(penalize.diagonal=FALSE). S uses divisor T on ddof=1 z-scored data. Optimisation is approximate: default tol=1e-4 on the absolute dual gap, 100 sweeps, and the result is returned even without convergence; on ill-conditioned inputs the output can be measurably sub-optimal (candidate). alpha=0.01 is an arbitrary fixed absolute penalty, not data-adaptive. The reported value is W itself; canonical W = Theta_hat^{-1} holds only to solver tolerance.

metric_name_standard: graphical-lasso (l1-penalised Gaussian MLE) covariance estimate W = Theta_hat^{-1}, off-diagonal entries; alpha chosen by 5-fold CV; cov-sq is its square
canonical_ref: Friedman J, Hastie T, Tibshirani R 2008, 'Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso', Biostatistics 9(3):432-441, eq. (1)/(2.1) (diagonal penalised); off-diagonal-only penalty: Yuan M, Lin Y 2007, 'Model selection and estimation in the Gaussian graphical model', Biometrika 94(1):19-35, eq. (4); Banerjee O, El Ghaoui L, d'Aspremont A 2008, JMLR 9:485-516 CV variant: alpha chosen by K-fold cross-validated Gaussian log-likelihood (e.g. Friedman et al. 2008 §4; sklearn GraphicalLassoCV, iteratively refined log grid); there is no single canonical CV rule.
canonical_definition: Theta_hat = argmin_{Theta > 0} -log det Theta + tr(S Theta) + alpha * sum_{i != j} |Theta_ij| (Friedman 2008 sums over all i,j incl. the diagonal; Yuan & Lin 2007 penalise off-diagonals only); Sigma_hat = W = Theta_hat^{-1}; KKT: W_ii = S_ii (+alpha if diagonal penalised), W_ij = S_ij + alpha*sign(Theta_ij) if Theta_ij != 0, |W_ij - S_ij| <= alpha otherwise; partial correlation rho_ij|rest = -Theta_ij / sqrt(Theta_ii Theta_jj)
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, p.3-4: 'Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1]. We use v0.24.1 of scikit-learn ... the Lasso technique, which uses an l1-regularization to sparsify the covariance matrix GraphicalLasso (as well as a method with the regularization method chosen through cross validation with five splits, GraphicalLassoCV)'; keywords 'undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous'. GitBook basic-statistics.md (Covariance) repeats the text but gives keywords 'undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, contemporaneous'. The -sq (squared) identifiers are not described in the supplement. Identifiers: cov_GraphicalLassoCV, cov-sq_GraphicalLassoCV.

implemented_as: Each channel z-scored (ddof=1, optional detrend); X = (T, P) array; sklearn.GraphicalLassoCV() with library defaults: S = biased empirical covariance (divide by T, so S_ii=(T-1)/T); alpha selected by 5-fold contiguous KFold CV on Gaussian test log-likelihood over 16 alphas from 4 refinement rounds of a 4-point log grid starting at [0.01, 1]*max|S_offdiag|, training-fold fits capped at 10 iterations and warm-started; then a full-data fit at alpha_ (max_iter 100). Solver: sklearn block coordinate descent (Friedman 2008 glasso algorithm) with off-diagonal-only l1 penalty, start 0.95*S off-diagonal, stop when |dual gap| < 1e-4 or after 100 sweeps (warning silenced). Returns covariance_ (the solver's W iterate, diagonal = S_ii) with diagonal set to NaN; -sq returns the elementwise square. Fit shared through data.covariance['GraphicalLassoCV'] by cov, cov-sq, prec, prec-sq; exactly symmetric because rows/columns are written together.

deviation_from_documented: (1) The supplement says the l1 penalty 'sparsif[ies] the covariance matrix'; it sparsifies the precision matrix (penalty on Theta, _graph_lasso.py:52, :64); W = covariance_ is generally dense (probe sparse_precision T=1024: no exact zeros in W while Theta has 2). (2) 'correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent': here W is a shrunk estimate with |W_ij - S_ij| <= alpha and S_ij = (T-1)/T * r_ij, so values differ from Pearson r by up to alpha + r/T. Range [-1,1] holds. (3) Documented scikit-learn v0.24.1; executed 1.9.1 (inner CD max_iter changed from max_iter to max(20, max_iter), do_screening and a pre-loop duality-gap early exit added (1.9.1 _cd_fast.pyx:1173-1182; absent in 0.24.1, whose first gap check is inside the loop after a coordinate pass, 0.24.1 _cd_fast.pyx:571-610). Overall numeric effect versus 0.24.1 not measured; the 1.9.1 exit causes the var2_bivariate T=4096 stall, see candidates). (4) GitBook keywords 'nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate' contradict the supplement/class labels 'linear, signed, multivariate'. (5) -sq variants undocumented. (6) 'five splits' confirmed: KFold(5), unshuffled contiguous blocks.
deviation_from_canonical: Variant of Friedman et al. 2008: the diagonal is not penalised (sklearn docstring _graph_lasso.py:328-329; W_ii = S_ii exactly, probe), which matches Yuan & Lin 2007 / R glasso(penalize.diagonal=FALSE). S uses divisor T on ddof=1 z-scored data. Optimisation is approximate: default tol=1e-4 on the absolute dual gap, 100 sweeps, and the result is returned even without convergence; on ill-conditioned inputs the output can be measurably sub-optimal (candidate). CV rule is sklearn-specific (contiguous KFold, 10-iteration warm-started fold fits, ties to smaller alpha, alpha=0 never selectable). The reported value is W itself; canonical W = Theta_hat^{-1} holds only to solver tolerance.

metric_name_standard: graphical-lasso (l1-penalised Gaussian MLE) covariance estimate W = Theta_hat^{-1}, off-diagonal entries; alpha chosen by 5-fold CV; cov-sq is its square
canonical_ref: Friedman J, Hastie T, Tibshirani R 2008, 'Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso', Biostatistics 9(3):432-441, eq. (1)/(2.1) (diagonal penalised); off-diagonal-only penalty: Yuan M, Lin Y 2007, 'Model selection and estimation in the Gaussian graphical model', Biometrika 94(1):19-35, eq. (4); Banerjee O, El Ghaoui L, d'Aspremont A 2008, JMLR 9:485-516 CV variant: alpha chosen by K-fold cross-validated Gaussian log-likelihood (e.g. Friedman et al. 2008 §4; sklearn GraphicalLassoCV, iteratively refined log grid); there is no single canonical CV rule.
canonical_definition: Theta_hat = argmin_{Theta > 0} -log det Theta + tr(S Theta) + alpha * sum_{i != j} |Theta_ij| (Friedman 2008 sums over all i,j incl. the diagonal; Yuan & Lin 2007 penalise off-diagonals only); Sigma_hat = W = Theta_hat^{-1}; KKT: W_ii = S_ii (+alpha if diagonal penalised), W_ij = S_ij + alpha*sign(Theta_ij) if Theta_ij != 0, |W_ij - S_ij| <= alpha otherwise; partial correlation rho_ij|rest = -Theta_ij / sqrt(Theta_ii Theta_jj)

GitBook basic-statistics.md (Covariance) repeats the text but gives keywords 'undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, contemporaneous'. The -sq (squared) identifiers are not described in the supplement. Identifiers: cov_GraphicalLassoCV, cov-sq_GraphicalLassoCV.

implemented_as: Each channel z-scored (ddof=1, optional detrend); X = (T, P) array; sklearn.GraphicalLassoCV() with library defaults: S = biased empirical covariance (divide by T, so S_ii=(T-1)/T); alpha selected by 5-fold contiguous KFold CV on Gaussian test log-likelihood over 16 alphas from 4 refinement rounds of a 4-point log grid starting at [0.01, 1]*max|S_offdiag|, training-fold fits capped at 10 iterations and warm-started; then a full-data fit at alpha_ (max_iter 100). Solver: sklearn block coordinate descent (Friedman 2008 glasso algorithm) with off-diagonal-only l1 penalty, start 0.95*S off-diagonal, stop when |dual gap| < 1e-4 or after 100 sweeps (warning silenced). Returns covariance_ (the solver's W iterate, diagonal = S_ii) with diagonal set to NaN; -sq returns the elementwise square. Fit shared through data.covariance['GraphicalLassoCV'] by cov, cov-sq, prec, prec-sq; exactly symmetric because rows/columns are written together.

metric_name_standard: Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage covariance estimator (shrinkage toward scaled identity)
canonical_ref: Ledoit & Wolf 2004, J. Multivariate Analysis 88(2):365-411, §3 (estimator S* = (b^2/d^2) m I + (a^2/d^2) S, with m = <S,I>, d^2 = ||S - mI||^2, b^2 = min(bbar^2, d^2), bbar^2 = n^-2 sum_k ||x_k x_k^T - S||^2, normalised Frobenius norm ||A||^2 = tr(AA^T)/p)
canonical_definition: Sigma_LW = (1 - s) S + s (tr(S)/p) I with s = min(bbar^2, d^2)/d^2, S = (1/n) sum x_k x_k^T on (assumed) zero-mean data
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, p.3-4 (supplement.txt:136-157): 'Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1].' Keywords: undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous. GitBook basic-statistics.md:15-45 repeats the text (its keyword line says 'undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate'). Neither source documents the '-sq' (squared) variants generated by pyspi/config.yaml.
delegate_lib: scikit-learn==1.9.1 sklearn.covariance.LedoitWolf().fit(X).covariance_; numpy==2.5.4
implemented_as: Data z-scores each channel with ddof=1 (pipeline default); sklearn.covariance.LedoitWolf() with defaults is fit on the (T x P) array; data-driven Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage s; covariance_ off-diagonal returned (diagonal NaN). Sample covariance uses divisor T (np.cov bias=1) after sample-mean centring, so on the default pipeline the off-diagonal equals (1 - s) * (T-1)/T * Pearson r, s the estimated shrinkage (diagonal mu = (T-1)/T). Squared variant (cov-sq_*) = np.square of the same matrix, labelled unsigned.

metric_name_standard: Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage covariance estimator (shrinkage toward scaled identity)
canonical_ref: Ledoit & Wolf 2004, J. Multivariate Analysis 88(2):365-411, §3 (estimator S* = (b^2/d^2) m I + (a^2/d^2) S, with m = <S,I>, d^2 = ||S - mI||^2, b^2 = min(bbar^2, d^2), bbar^2 = n^-2 sum_k ||x_k x_k^T - S||^2, normalised Frobenius norm ||A||^2 = tr(AA^T)/p)
canonical_definition: Sigma_LW = (1 - s) S + s (tr(S)/p) I with s = min(bbar^2, d^2)/d^2, S = (1/n) sum x_k x_k^T on (assumed) zero-mean data
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, p.3-4 (supplement.txt:136-157): 'Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1].' Keywords: undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous. GitBook basic-statistics.md:15-45 repeats the text (its keyword line says 'undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate'). Neither source documents the '-sq' (squared) variants generated by pyspi/config.yaml.
delegate_lib: scikit-learn==1.9.1 sklearn.covariance.LedoitWolf().fit(X).covariance_; numpy==2.5.4
implemented_as: Data z-scores each channel with ddof=1 (pipeline default); sklearn.covariance.LedoitWolf() with defaults is fit on the (T x P) array; data-driven Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage s; covariance_ off-diagonal returned (diagonal NaN). Sample covariance uses divisor T (np.cov bias=1) after sample-mean centring, so on the default pipeline the off-diagonal equals (1 - s) * (T-1)/T * Pearson r, s the estimated shrinkage (diagonal mu = (T-1)/T). Squared variant (cov-sq_*) = np.square of the same matrix, labelled unsigned.

metric_name_standard: Reweighted Minimum Covariance Determinant (FAST-MCD) robust covariance matrix entry; cov-sq_MinCovDet is its square
canonical_ref: Rousseeuw P.J. 1985, "Multivariate estimation with high breakdown point", in Mathematical Statistics and Applications Vol. B, 283-297 (MCD definition); Rousseeuw P.J. & Van Driessen K. 1999, Technometrics 41(3):212-223 (FAST-MCD: C-step theorem, raw consistency factor med(d^2)/chi2_{p,0.5}, reweighting with hard weights d^2 <= chi2_{p,0.975}); consistency factor c_alpha = alpha / F_{chi2_{p+2}}(chi2_{p,alpha}): Croux C. & Haesbroeck G. 1999, J Multivar Anal 71:161-190; small-sample factors: Pison G., Van Aelst S., Willems G. 2002, Metrika 55:111-123
canonical_definition: Raw MCD: among all h-subsets (default h = floor((n+p+1)/2), maximal breakdown) choose H minimising det(S_H); mu_raw = mean(H), Sigma_raw = c(p,h/n) * S_H. Reweighted MCD: w_i = 1[d^2(x_i; mu_raw, Sigma_raw) <= chi2_{p,0.975}], mu = weighted mean, Sigma = c(p,0.975) * weighted sample covariance (robustbase uses divisor sum(w)-1 and optional small-sample factors). Off-diagonal Sigma_ij is a robust, Gaussian-consistent covariance.
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, pp.3-4: "Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1]. We use v0.24.1 of scikit-learn [2] ... the elliptic envelope (EllipticEnvelope) [3] and the minimum covariance determinant (MinCovDet) methods for outlier removal"; [3] = Rousseeuw & Van Driessen 1999 Technometrics 41:212. Keywords "undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous". GitBook basic-statistics.md:21-25 same text (links to sklearn EllipticEnvelope / MinCovDet pages; no version). The -sq variant is not described in the supplement (only items 2/3 cov_EllipticEnvelope, cov_MinCovDet).
delegate_lib: scikit-learn==1.9.1 (scipy==1.17.1 linalg.pinvh, numpy==2.5.4): sklearn.covariance.MinCovDet().fit -> MinCovDet.fit -> fast_mcd, correct_covariance, reweight_covariance; attribute covariance_
implemented_as: Data z-scored per channel over the full sample (ddof=1; optional detrend first). z (T x P) passed to sklearn MinCovDet() with all defaults and random_state=None (global numpy RNG). FAST-MCD raw search: h = ceil((T+P+1)/2); T<=500: 30 random h-subsets x 2 C-steps, best 10 refined; T>500: random partition into T//300 subsets, 500 trials, merge on <=1500 samples. Raw distances divided by the Croux-Haesbroeck factor c(P,h/T); rows with d2 < chi2_{P,0.975} kept; Sigma = c(P,0.975) * MLE covariance (divisor n_w) of kept rows; precision_ = scipy.linalg.pinvh(Sigma). pyspi returns the covariance_ matrix as is (no normalisation to correlation), diagonal set to NaN in place on the cached fit; cov-sq_MinCovDet returns its elementwise square. One fit per Data object per estimator name, shared by cov/prec and squared/unsquared identifiers.

deviation_from_documented: Version: documented sklearn v0.24.1, executed 1.9.1; the MCD correction and reweighting changed (raw median factor -> Croux-Haesbroeck factor; reweighted covariance now multiplied by c(P,0.975) = 1.055-1.104 for P=5..2), so values are not those of the documented version (probe p4.py, ratios 1.055-1.10). Range: documented "equivalent to correlation, within [-1,1]" is false for this estimator: the robust scatter of z-scored data has diagonal != 1 (0.19 on contaminated, 0.43-1.17 on iid T=64) and off-diagonals exceeding 1 occur (1.141 cointegrated T=256; 1.0478 rank-deficient shared_envelope). cov-sq_MinCovDet undocumented in the supplement. Stochastic output (global RNG) not documented in the supplement (documented in tests/README.md).
deviation_from_canonical: Close variant of reweighted FAST-MCD: (1) the search is a stochastic approximation of the MCD optimum (inherent to FAST-MCD) but the random starts come from the global numpy RNG, so the selected h-subset and hence values vary run to run (spread up to 0.34 at T=64); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2) instead of floor; (3) reweighted covariance uses the MLE divisor n_w (robustbase: n_w - 1) and no small-sample correction (Pison et al. 2002); (4) raw consistency factor is the asymptotic Croux-Haesbroeck factor rather than RVD 1999 median rescaling; (5) the input is z-scored with non-robust mean/SD over the full sample before the robust fit, so the output is a robust covariance in units of the contaminated SD, not a robust correlation.
units_and_range: cov: dimensionless (z-score units), signed, symmetric, unbounded in principle; typical |value| <= ~1.2 (observed max 1.141); cov-sq >= 0. Diagonal NaN. score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: sklearn 1.9.1 reweighted FAST-MCD. From the same raw h-subset robustbase agrees to 3.5e-15 (rdet 7/8; the eighth differs by one reweighting point, 0.0118). It differs from canonical MCD: the h-subset depends on the RNG and is the best found in only 3/14 runs, h = ceil, and the divisor is MLE. It differs from the supplement because values reach 1.141, so it is not a correlation.
what_changed: Reweighted FAST-MCD covariance of the z-scored data, computed exactly as sklearn 1.9.1 defines it (external robustbase agrees to 3.5e-15 given the same raw h-subset). Differs from the canonical reweighted MCD by: (1) the raw h-subset is a FAST-MCD local optimum drawn from the global numpy RNG, so the value depends on the seed and on RNG position (20-seed spread 0.155-0.257 at T=64, 0.0027-0.0044 at T=4096) and is often not the lowest-determinant subset (sklearn's seed_all(42) subset is the best found in 3/14 runs; rrcov's search finds lower determinants on contaminated|256 in all 20 seeds); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2); (3) MLE divisor n_w and c(p,0.975) applied even when every point is kept. Differs from the supplement: it is not a correlation in [-1,1] (values up to 1.141; 0.15 on contaminated data where the robust correlation is 0.81, because the non-robust z-score sets the scale), and sklearn 1.9.1 multiplies the reweighted covariance by c(p,0.975), which the documented 0.24.1 did not (source only). EEG scope (Workflow 4b challenge probes; not check runs): the checks use P <= 5 and no average-referenced input, while the EEG workflow uses up to about 118 channels with reference: car in the example config (examples/workflow/preflight.yaml:12). At T=1024 the 5-seed off-diagonal spread grows with P (iid, no reference: max 0.0207/0.0187/0.0267/0.046-0.047, median 0.009/0.008/0.010/0.018 at P=8/19/32/64, against a median |cov| of about 0.023), so at EEG P the seed noise is of the order of null-level values and larger than the 20-seed 0.013-0.015 seen at P <= 5. With CAR (rank P-1) every h-subset scatter is singular (the exact-fit situation of Rousseeuw and Van Driessen 1999) and every fit raised 18-38 sklearn 'Determinant has increased; this should not happen' warnings (_robust_covariance.py:188-195) at P = 5-64, none without CAR; pyspi suppresses them (basic.py:37-38). The canonical objective is therefore degenerate on CAR EEG input; the score rests on the synthetic evidence above and is unchanged.

metric_name_standard: Reweighted Minimum Covariance Determinant (FAST-MCD) robust covariance matrix entry; cov-sq_MinCovDet is its square
canonical_ref: Rousseeuw P.J. 1985, "Multivariate estimation with high breakdown point", in Mathematical Statistics and Applications Vol. B, 283-297 (MCD definition); Rousseeuw P.J. & Van Driessen K. 1999, Technometrics 41(3):212-223 (FAST-MCD: C-step theorem, raw consistency factor med(d^2)/chi2_{p,0.5}, reweighting with hard weights d^2 <= chi2_{p,0.975}); consistency factor c_alpha = alpha / F_{chi2_{p+2}}(chi2_{p,alpha}): Croux C. & Haesbroeck G. 1999, J Multivar Anal 71:161-190; small-sample factors: Pison G., Van Aelst S., Willems G. 2002, Metrika 55:111-123
canonical_definition: Raw MCD: among all h-subsets (default h = floor((n+p+1)/2), maximal breakdown) choose H minimising det(S_H); mu_raw = mean(H), Sigma_raw = c(p,h/n) * S_H. Reweighted MCD: w_i = 1[d^2(x_i; mu_raw, Sigma_raw) <= chi2_{p,0.975}], mu = weighted mean, Sigma = c(p,0.975) * weighted sample covariance (robustbase uses divisor sum(w)-1 and optional small-sample factors). Off-diagonal Sigma_ij is a robust, Gaussian-consistent covariance.
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, pp.3-4: "Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1]. We use v0.24.1 of scikit-learn [2] ... the elliptic envelope (EllipticEnvelope) [3] and the minimum covariance determinant (MinCovDet) methods for outlier removal"; [3] = Rousseeuw & Van Driessen 1999 Technometrics 41:212. Keywords "undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous". GitBook basic-statistics.md:21-25 same text (links to sklearn EllipticEnvelope / MinCovDet pages; no version). The -sq variant is not described in the supplement (only items 2/3 cov_EllipticEnvelope, cov_MinCovDet).
delegate_lib: scikit-learn==1.9.1 (scipy==1.17.1 linalg.pinvh, numpy==2.5.4): sklearn.covariance.MinCovDet().fit -> MinCovDet.fit -> fast_mcd, correct_covariance, reweight_covariance; attribute covariance_
implemented_as: Data z-scored per channel over the full sample (ddof=1; optional detrend first). z (T x P) passed to sklearn MinCovDet() with all defaults and random_state=None (global numpy RNG). FAST-MCD raw search: h = ceil((T+P+1)/2); T<=500: 30 random h-subsets x 2 C-steps, best 10 refined; T>500: random partition into T//300 subsets, 500 trials, merge on <=1500 samples. Raw distances divided by the Croux-Haesbroeck factor c(P,h/T); rows with d2 < chi2_{P,0.975} kept; Sigma = c(P,0.975) * MLE covariance (divisor n_w) of kept rows; precision_ = scipy.linalg.pinvh(Sigma). pyspi returns the covariance_ matrix as is (no normalisation to correlation), diagonal set to NaN in place on the cached fit; cov-sq_MinCovDet returns its elementwise square. One fit per Data object per estimator name, shared by cov/prec and squared/unsquared identifiers.

deviation_from_documented: Version: documented sklearn v0.24.1, executed 1.9.1; the MCD correction and reweighting changed (raw median factor -> Croux-Haesbroeck factor; reweighted covariance now multiplied by c(P,0.975) = 1.055-1.104 for P=5..2), so values are not those of the documented version (probe p4.py, ratios 1.055-1.10). Range: documented "equivalent to correlation, within [-1,1]" is false for this estimator: the robust scatter of z-scored data has diagonal != 1 (0.19 on contaminated, 0.43-1.17 on iid T=64) and off-diagonals exceeding 1 occur (1.141 cointegrated T=256; 1.0478 rank-deficient shared_envelope). cov-sq_MinCovDet undocumented in the supplement. deviation_from_canonical: Close variant of reweighted FAST-MCD: (1) the search is a stochastic approximation of the MCD optimum (inherent to FAST-MCD) but the random starts come from the global numpy RNG, so the selected h-subset and hence values vary run to run (spread up to 0.34 at T=64); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2) instead of floor; (3) reweighted covariance uses the MLE divisor n_w (robustbase: n_w - 1) and no small-sample correction (Pison et al. 2002); (4) raw consistency factor is the asymptotic Croux-Haesbroeck factor rather than RVD 1999 median rescaling; (5) the input is z-scored with non-robust mean/SD over the full sample before the robust fit, so the output is a robust covariance in units of the contaminated SD, not a robust correlation.

score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: sklearn 1.9.1 reweighted FAST-MCD. From the same raw h-subset robustbase agrees to 3.5e-15 (rdet 7/8; the eighth differs by one reweighting point, 0.0118). It differs from canonical MCD: the h-subset depends on the RNG and is the best found in only 3/14 runs, h = ceil, and the divisor is MLE. It differs from the supplement because values reach 1.141, so it is not a correlation.
what_changed: Reweighted FAST-MCD covariance of the z-scored data, computed exactly as sklearn 1.9.1 defines it (external robustbase agrees to 3.5e-15 given the same raw h-subset). Differs from the canonical reweighted MCD by: (1) the raw h-subset is a FAST-MCD local optimum drawn from the global numpy RNG, so the value depends on the seed and on RNG position (20-seed spread 0.155-0.257 at T=64, 0.0027-0.0044 at T=4096) and is often not the lowest-determinant subset (sklearn's seed_all(42) subset is the best found in 3/14 runs; rrcov's search finds lower determinants on contaminated|256 in all 20 seeds); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2); (3) MLE divisor n_w and c(p,0.975) applied even when every point is kept. Differs from the supplement: it is not a correlation in [-1,1] (values up to 1.141; 0.15 on contaminated data where the robust correlation is 0.81, because the non-robust z-score sets the scale), and sklearn 1.9.1 multiplies the reweighted covariance by c(p,0.975), which the documented 0.24.1 did not (source only). EEG scope (Workflow 4b challenge probes; not check runs): the checks use P <= 5 and no average-referenced input, while the EEG workflow uses up to about 118 channels with reference: car in the example config (examples/workflow/preflight.yaml:12). At T=1024 the 5-seed off-diagonal spread grows with P (iid, no reference: max 0.0207/0.0187/0.0267/0.046-0.047, median 0.009/0.008/0.010/0.018 at P=8/19/32/64, against a median |cov| of about 0.023), so at EEG P the seed noise is of the order of null-level values and larger than the 20-seed 0.013-0.015 seen at P <= 5. With CAR (rank P-1) every h-subset scatter is singular (the exact-fit situation of Rousseeuw and Van Driessen 1999) and every fit raised 18-38 sklearn 'Determinant has increased; this should not happen' warnings (_robust_covariance.py:188-195) at P = 5-64, none without CAR; pyspi suppresses them (basic.py:37-38). The canonical objective is therefore degenerate on CAR EEG input; the score rests on the synthetic evidence above and is unchanged.

metric_name_standard: Oracle Approximating Shrinkage (OAS) covariance estimator
canonical_ref: Chen, Wiesel, Eldar & Hero 2010, IEEE Trans. Signal Processing 58(10):5016-5029, Eq. 22-23 (arXiv:0907.4698v1 Eq. 23); target F = tr(S)/p I (Eq. 3), S = (1/n) sum x_i x_i^T (Eq. 2)
canonical_definition: Sigma_OAS = (1 - rho) S + rho (tr(S)/p) I, rho = min( [(1 - 2/p) tr(S^2) + tr^2(S)] / [(n + 1 - 2/p)(tr(S^2) - tr^2(S)/p)], 1 )
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.1, p.3-4 (supplement.txt:136-157): 'Due to the z-scoring of the time series, the correlation and covariance matrices are equivalent and thus the covariance statistic is within [-1, 1].' Keywords: undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous. GitBook basic-statistics.md:15-45 repeats the text (its keyword line says 'undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate'). Neither source documents the '-sq' (squared) variants generated by pyspi/config.yaml.

implemented_as: Data z-scores each channel with ddof=1 (pipeline default); sklearn.covariance.OAS() with defaults is fit on the (T x P) array; data-driven OAS shrinkage rho (sklearn variant); covariance_ off-diagonal returned (diagonal NaN). Sample covariance uses divisor T (np.cov bias=1) after sample-mean centring, so on the default pipeline the off-diagonal equals (1 - s) * (T-1)/T * Pearson r, s the estimated shrinkage (diagonal mu = (T-1)/T). Squared variant (cov-sq_*) = np.square of the same matrix, labelled unsigned.

deviation_from_documented: Docs say covariance equals correlation and lies in [-1,1]. Implemented value is (T-1)/T * r on the default pipeline (ddof=1 z-score vs divisor-T covariance), further multiplied by (1 - s) from shrinkage. With normalise=False the value is the raw MLE covariance, not bounded by 1. The '-sq' squared variants are undocumented in the supplement and GitBook. GitBook keyword line ('undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate') contradicts the supplement and the code labels (linear, signed, multivariate). Supplement describes OAS as Chen et al. 2010 [5]; the executed shrinkage formula drops the 2/p terms of Eq. 23 (see deviation_from_canonical).
deviation_from_canonical: sklearn drops the 2/p terms of Chen et al. Eq. 23: executed rho = min((tr S^2 + tr^2 S)/((n+1)(tr S^2 - tr^2 S/p)),1) (_shrunk_covariance.py:83-85, comment lines 70-71). For EEG-sized p this is not negligible: probe shrinkage 0.18388 vs Eq.23 0.16058 (bivariate_gaussian, p=4, T=64), 0.014569 vs 0.012728 (T=1024), 0.21778 vs 0.19936 (sparse_precision, p=5, T=64). Also sample-mean centring while Chen assumes known zero mean. The omission is documented by sklearn itself: OAS class docstring (_shrunk_covariance.py:754-758, and oas() docstring :655-659) states the shrinkage 'differs from Eq. 23' and that 2/p is dropped because 'for a large p' it does not affect the estimator. scikit-learn 0.24.1 (the version named in supplement §1.1.1, p.4) computes the same num/den (0.24.1 sklearn/covariance/_shrunk_covariance.py:487-492, comment line 487 'formula from Chen et al.'s **implementation**'; oas() docstring 466-467 'slightly modified compared to the one given in the article'; OAS class docstring 508-512), so the documented pyspi version used this variant too. It is therefore a documented sklearn approximation, not a version change; it still departs from Eq. 23 by +14.5% (p=4) and +9.2% (p=5) relative in the shrinkage at T=64.

what_changed: sklearn fixed-coefficient shrinkage 0.9 S + 0.1 tr(S)/p I, fp-exact, as the supplement describes. On the pipeline the value is 0.9 (T-1)/T r, so |value| <= 0.9 and it is never 'equivalent to correlation'. -sq is an undocumented elementwise square.

symmetry_observed: sym: max|A - A.T| = 0.0 (bitwise) on all 51 matrix runs, including delayed_noise, var2_bivariate, var2_chain, logistic_maps_chaotic, anm and cointegrated (sym runs)
direction_observed: undirected: on delayed_noise, var2_bivariate, var2_chain, logistic_maps_chaotic and anm (pipeline, T=1024) A[i,j] equals A[j,i] bitwise and equals the (i,j) entry of the independent estimate (sym runs, value_ok=1); it carries no direction information: A[i,j] is the zero-lag (shrunk) covariance of processes i and j (rows of the Data array)
complexity_P_T: O(P^2 T) for the empirical covariance + O(P^3) for scipy.linalg.pinvh (a full eigh) that sklearn _empirical_covariance.py:_set_covariance runs for precision_ on every fit; one fit per Data and estimator (pyspi/statistics/basic.py:Estimators._from_cache). Measured fresh P_exponent 0.17, T_exponent 0.10: between 8 and 32 channels and 256 and 1024 samples the ~0.7 ms of fixed sklearn validation dominates, so neither exponent reflects the algorithm. At 118x1024 the P^3 term dominates: in the 118x1024 EmpiricalCovariance profile eigh is 58.7% and np.cov 15.4% of the call; the same pinvh on a 118x118 matrix runs for every estimator of this family.
hotspot_1: scipy/linalg/_basic.py:pinvh (third-party:scipy) 10.8% cumulative of the profiled SPI call at 8x1024, of which scipy/linalg/_decomp.py:eigh 4.9%; at 118x1024 eigh is 58.7% (pinvh 63.0%) of the EmpiricalCovariance call (audit/profiles/micro/prof_basic.cov.EmpiricalCovariance__118x1024.pstats, index prof_basic__index.json), the same 118x118 pinvh this estimator runs
hotspot_2: sklearn/utils/validation.py:check_array (third-party:sklearn) 32.5% at 8x1024 (fixed input validation; 10.6% at 118x1024 in the EmpiricalCovariance profile); sklearn/covariance/_empirical_covariance.py:empirical_covariance 14.7% at 8x1024
opportunity: Compute precision_ with a Cholesky factorisation (scipy.linalg.cho_factor + cho_solve, or LAPACK potri) instead of scipy.linalg.pinvh, which sklearn's _empirical_covariance.py:_set_covariance runs as a full eigh for every fit; in pyspi this means fitting with store_precision=False in basic.py:Estimators._from_cache and inverting there at fit time (before any identifier's in-place np.fill_diagonal at basic.py:49-50), with a pinvh fallback when the factorisation fails.
speedup_basis: profile:audit/profiles/micro/prof_basic.cov.EmpiricalCovariance__118x1024.pstats scipy/linalg/_decomp.py:eigh 58.7% (pinvh 63.0%) of the EmpiricalCovariance call, the same 118x118 pinvh + complexity: Cholesky inverse ~P^3 vs eigh ~9P^3 flops; scratch timing at 118x118 pinvh 2.17 ms vs Cholesky inverse 0.21 ms; this unit's measured fresh 118x1024 wall is 3.87 ms (summary.json), so the 2.17 ms pinvh is ~56% of it and the Amdahl bound is 1/(1-0.56) = 2.3x. Subsumed by cov_prec_simple-2 on this unit (subsumed_by), because in a cov-only run that avenue skips the pinvh this one makes cheaper; cov_prec_simple-2 gives no gain on the EEG selection (eeg_applicable false), so in tier 0 this avenue is ranked on its own k
risk_evidence: the cov/cov-sq identifiers read only covariance_, which sklearn _empirical_covariance.py:_set_covariance assigns (line 210) before and independently of the precision step (line 213), so a different inverse cannot change it; the ~1e-15 rounding change and the rank-deficient pinvh fallback concern precision_ only (the basic.prec.* units)

metric_name_standard: inverse (pseudo-inverse) of the maximum-likelihood sample covariance (sample precision / concentration matrix)
canonical_ref: Dempster 1972, Biometrics 28(1):157-175 (covariance selection; concentration/precision matrix); partial-correlation relation rho_ij|rest = -Theta_ij / sqrt(Theta_ii Theta_jj) in Whittaker 1990, Graphical Models in Applied Multivariate Statistics, Wiley, ch. 5. Covariance estimator: Anderson 2003, An Introduction to Multivariate Statistical Analysis (3rd ed.), Wiley, §3.2 (MLE of the covariance matrix, divisor N)
canonical_definition: Theta = Sigma_hat^{-1} where Sigma_hat is: Sigma_hat = (1/T) sum_t (x_t - xbar)(x_t - xbar)^T; for unit-variance inputs the off-diagonal is Pearson r; partial correlation is -Theta_ij/sqrt(Theta_ii Theta_jj), not Theta_ij itself
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.2, p.4 (supplement.txt:158-171): 'The precision matrix is the matrix inverse of the covariance matrix ... For normalized time-series data, the precision matrix is equivalent to the partial correlation between each pairwise time series, conditioned on all other time series, and is within [-1, 1].' GitBook basic-statistics.md:101-122 has the same text. Neither source documents the '-sq' (squared) variants generated by pyspi/config.yaml.

implemented_as: Same cached sklearn.covariance.EmpiricalCovariance() fit as cov_EmpiricalCovariance; returns precision_ = scipy.linalg.pinvh(covariance_) computed at fit time (Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse via eigh with relative cutoff max(P,P)*eps*max|eig|), diagonal NaN. Off-diagonals are raw inverse-covariance entries, not normalised; on the default pipeline Theta = T/(T-1) * R^{-1} with R the Pearson correlation matrix. Not symmetrised (Estimators.multivariate bypasses Undirected.multivariate). Squared variant (prec-sq_*) = np.square of the same matrix.

metric_name_standard: Off-diagonal entry of the inverse of the reweighted MCD robust covariance (robust precision matrix) (computed by sklearn EllipticEnvelope, an outlier detector whose fitted covariance is the MinCovDet estimate); prec-sq_EllipticEnvelope is its square
canonical_ref: Rousseeuw P.J. 1985, "Multivariate estimation with high breakdown point", in Mathematical Statistics and Applications Vol. B, 283-297 (MCD definition); Rousseeuw P.J. & Van Driessen K. 1999, Technometrics 41(3):212-223 (FAST-MCD: C-step theorem, raw consistency factor med(d^2)/chi2_{p,0.5}, reweighting with hard weights d^2 <= chi2_{p,0.975}); consistency factor c_alpha = alpha / F_{chi2_{p+2}}(chi2_{p,alpha}): Croux C. & Haesbroeck G. 1999, J Multivar Anal 71:161-190; small-sample factors: Pison G., Van Aelst S., Willems G. 2002, Metrika 55:111-123; precision -> partial correlation: Whittaker J. 1990, Graphical Models in Applied Multivariate Statistics, Wiley, ch. 5 (Prop. 5.7.1 scaled-inverse identity)
canonical_definition: Omega = Sigma_MCD^{-1} (reweighted robust MCD scatter, see Covariance unit); the partial correlation is rho_ij|rest = -Omega_ij / sqrt(Omega_ii Omega_jj) (Whittaker 1990, Graphical Models in Applied Multivariate Statistics, ch. 5; Lauritzen 1996, Graphical Models). Omega_ij itself is not bounded and has the opposite sign of the partial correlation.
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.2, p.4: "The precision matrix is the matrix inverse of the covariance matrix ... For normalized time-series data, the precision matrix is equivalent to the partial correlation between each pairwise time series, conditioned on all other time series, and is within [-1, 1]. The precision matrix is computed via the same module as the covariance matrix (in scikit-learn [2]), and has the same estimators." Items 10 prec_EllipticEnvelope, 11 prec_MinCovDet. GitBook basic-statistics.md:107 same text. The -sq variant is not described.
delegate_lib: scikit-learn==1.9.1 (scipy==1.17.1 linalg.pinvh, numpy==2.5.4): sklearn.covariance.EllipticEnvelope().fit -> MinCovDet.fit (via EllipticEnvelope.fit super call) -> fast_mcd, correct_covariance, reweight_covariance; attribute precision_
implemented_as: Data z-scored per channel over the full sample (ddof=1; optional detrend first). z (T x P) passed to sklearn EllipticEnvelope() with all defaults and random_state=None (global numpy RNG). FAST-MCD raw search: h = ceil((T+P+1)/2); T<=500: 30 random h-subsets x 2 C-steps, best 10 refined; T>500: random partition into T//300 subsets, 500 trials, merge on <=1500 samples. Raw distances divided by the Croux-Haesbroeck factor c(P,h/T); rows with d2 < chi2_{P,0.975} kept; Sigma = c(P,0.975) * MLE covariance (divisor n_w) of kept rows; precision_ = scipy.linalg.pinvh(Sigma). EllipticEnvelope.fit runs exactly MinCovDet.fit and then only sets offset_ (contamination=0.1 never affects covariance_/precision_). pyspi returns the precision_ matrix as is (no normalisation to correlation / partial correlation, no sign flip), diagonal set to NaN in place on the cached fit; prec-sq_EllipticEnvelope returns its elementwise square. One fit per Data object per estimator name, shared by cov/prec and squared/unsquared identifiers.

deviation_from_documented: Version: documented sklearn v0.24.1, executed 1.9.1; the MCD correction and reweighting changed (raw median factor -> Croux-Haesbroeck factor; reweighted covariance now multiplied by c(P,0.975) = 1.055-1.104 for P=5..2), so values are not those of the documented version (probe p4.py, ratios 1.055-1.10). Definition: documented "equivalent to the partial correlation ... within [-1,1]" is false: the raw precision entry is returned, Omega_ij = -rho_ij|rest * sqrt(Omega_ii Omega_jj), opposite in sign to the partial correlation and unbounded (probe -2.63 vs partial correlation +0.81; up to 368 on narrowband). Estimator identity: documented as a separate "elliptic envelope" outlier-removal method; its covariance/precision are exactly MinCovDet (bit-identical under equal RNG state), so the EllipticEnvelope and MinCovDet identifiers are the same quantity up to RNG noise. prec-sq_EllipticEnvelope undocumented in the supplement. Stochastic output (global RNG) not documented in the supplement (documented in tests/README.md).
deviation_from_canonical: Close variant of reweighted FAST-MCD: (1) the search is a stochastic approximation of the MCD optimum (inherent to FAST-MCD) but the random starts come from the global numpy RNG, so the selected h-subset and hence values vary run to run (spread up to 0.34 at T=64); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2) instead of floor; (3) reweighted covariance uses the MLE divisor n_w (robustbase: n_w - 1) and no small-sample correction (Pison et al. 2002); (4) raw consistency factor is the asymptotic Croux-Haesbroeck factor rather than RVD 1999 median rescaling; (5) the input is z-scored with non-robust mean/SD over the full sample before the robust fit, so the output is a robust covariance in units of the contaminated SD, not a robust correlation. (6) precision via pseudo-inverse pinvh: for singular scatter (collinear channels) a Moore-Penrose inverse is returned silently instead of failing.
units_and_range: prec: dimensionless (inverse z-score units), signed (sign opposite to partial correlation), symmetric up to round-off, unbounded (observed |value| up to 368 on narrowband_f0-0.25 T=64); prec-sq >= 0. Diagonal NaN. Finite pseudo-inverse values for singular scatter.

canonical_definition: Omega = Sigma_MCD^{-1} (reweighted robust MCD scatter, see Covariance unit); the partial correlation is rho_ij|rest = -Omega_ij / sqrt(Omega_ii Omega_jj) (Whittaker 1990, Graphical Models in Applied Multivariate Statistics, ch. 5; Lauritzen 1996, Graphical Models). Omega_ij itself is not bounded and has the opposite sign of the partial correlation.

The precision matrix is computed via the same module as the covariance matrix (in scikit-learn [2]), and has the same estimators." Items 10 prec_EllipticEnvelope, 11 prec_MinCovDet. Raw distances divided by the Croux-Haesbroeck factor c(P,h/T); rows with d2 < chi2_{P,0.975} kept; Sigma = c(P,0.975) * MLE covariance (divisor n_w) of kept rows; precision_ = scipy.linalg.pinvh(Sigma). deviation_from_documented: Version: documented sklearn v0.24.1, executed 1.9.1; the MCD correction and reweighting changed (raw median factor -> Croux-Haesbroeck factor; reweighted covariance now multiplied by c(P,0.975) = 1.055-1.104 for P=5..2), so values are not those of the documented version (probe p4.py, ratios 1.055-1.10). Estimator identity: documented as a separate "elliptic envelope" outlier-removal method; its covariance/precision are exactly MinCovDet (bit-identical under equal RNG state), so the EllipticEnvelope and MinCovDet identifiers are the same quantity up to RNG noise. prec-sq_EllipticEnvelope undocumented in the supplement. Stochastic output (global RNG) not documented in the supplement (documented in tests/README.md).
deviation_from_canonical: Close variant of reweighted FAST-MCD: (1) the search is a stochastic approximation of the MCD optimum (inherent to FAST-MCD) but the random starts come from the global numpy RNG, so the selected h-subset and hence values vary run to run (spread up to 0.34 at T=64); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2) instead of floor; (3) reweighted covariance uses the MLE divisor n_w (robustbase: n_w - 1) and no small-sample correction (Pison et al. 2002); (4) raw consistency factor is the asymptotic Croux-Haesbroeck factor rather than RVD 1999 median rescaling; (5) the input is z-scored with non-robust mean/SD over the full sample before the robust fit, so the output is a robust covariance in units of the contaminated SD, not a robust correlation. (6) precision via pseudo-inverse pinvh: for singular scatter (collinear channels) a Moore-Penrose inverse is returned silently instead of failing.

metric_name_standard: Off-diagonal entry of the inverse of the reweighted MCD robust covariance (robust precision matrix) (computed by sklearn EllipticEnvelope, an outlier detector whose fitted covariance is the MinCovDet estimate); prec-sq_EllipticEnvelope is its square
canonical_ref: Rousseeuw P.J. 1985, "Multivariate estimation with high breakdown point", in Mathematical Statistics and Applications Vol. B, 283-297 (MCD definition); Rousseeuw P.J. & Van Driessen K. 1999, Technometrics 41(3):212-223 (FAST-MCD: C-step theorem, raw consistency factor med(d^2)/chi2_{p,0.5}, reweighting with hard weights d^2 <= chi2_{p,0.975}); consistency factor c_alpha = alpha / F_{chi2_{p+2}}(chi2_{p,alpha}): Croux C. & Haesbroeck G. 1999, J Multivar Anal 71:161-190; small-sample factors: Pison G., Van Aelst S., Willems G. 2002, Metrika 55:111-123; precision -> partial correlation: Whittaker J. 1990, Graphical Models in Applied Multivariate Statistics, Wiley, ch. 5 (Prop. 5.7.1 scaled-inverse identity)
canonical_definition: Omega = Sigma_MCD^{-1} (reweighted robust MCD scatter, see Covariance unit); the partial correlation is rho_ij|rest = -Omega_ij / sqrt(Omega_ii Omega_jj) (Whittaker 1990, Graphical Models in Applied Multivariate Statistics, ch. 5; Lauritzen 1996, Graphical Models). Omega_ij itself is not bounded and has the opposite sign of the partial correlation.
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.2, p.4: "The precision matrix is the matrix inverse of the covariance matrix ... For normalized time-series data, the precision matrix is equivalent to the partial correlation between each pairwise time series, conditioned on all other time series, and is within [-1, 1]. The precision matrix is computed via the same module as the covariance matrix (in scikit-learn [2]), and has the same estimators." Items 10 prec_EllipticEnvelope, 11 prec_MinCovDet. GitBook basic-statistics.md:107 same text. The -sq variant is not described.

implemented_as: Data z-scored per channel over the full sample (ddof=1; optional detrend first). z (T x P) passed to sklearn EllipticEnvelope() with all defaults and random_state=None (global numpy RNG). FAST-MCD raw search: h = ceil((T+P+1)/2); T<=500: 30 random h-subsets x 2 C-steps, best 10 refined; T>500: random partition into T//300 subsets, 500 trials, merge on <=1500 samples. Raw distances divided by the Croux-Haesbroeck factor c(P,h/T); rows with d2 < chi2_{P,0.975} kept; Sigma = c(P,0.975) * MLE covariance (divisor n_w) of kept rows; precision_ = scipy.linalg.pinvh(Sigma). EllipticEnvelope.fit runs exactly MinCovDet.fit and then only sets offset_ (contamination=0.1 never affects covariance_/precision_). pyspi returns the precision_ matrix as is (no normalisation to correlation / partial correlation, no sign flip), diagonal set to NaN in place on the cached fit; prec-sq_EllipticEnvelope returns its elementwise square. One fit per Data object per estimator name, shared by cov/prec and squared/unsquared identifiers.

deviation_from_documented: Version: documented sklearn v0.24.1, executed 1.9.1; the MCD correction and reweighting changed (raw median factor -> Croux-Haesbroeck factor; reweighted covariance now multiplied by c(P,0.975) = 1.055-1.104 for P=5..2), so values are not those of the documented version (probe p4.py, ratios 1.055-1.10). Definition: documented "equivalent to the partial correlation ... within [-1,1]" is false: the raw precision entry is returned, Omega_ij = -rho_ij|rest * sqrt(Omega_ii Omega_jj), opposite in sign to the partial correlation and unbounded (probe -2.63 vs partial correlation +0.81; up to 368 on narrowband). Estimator identity: documented as a separate "elliptic envelope" outlier-removal method; its covariance/precision are exactly MinCovDet (bit-identical under equal RNG state), so the EllipticEnvelope and MinCovDet identifiers are the same quantity up to RNG noise. prec-sq_EllipticEnvelope undocumented in the supplement. Stochastic output (global RNG) not documented in the supplement (documented in tests/README.md).
deviation_from_canonical: Close variant of reweighted FAST-MCD: (1) the search is a stochastic approximation of the MCD optimum (inherent to FAST-MCD) but the random starts come from the global numpy RNG, so the selected h-subset and hence values vary run to run (spread up to 0.34 at T=64); (2) h = ceil((n+p+1)/2) instead of floor; (3) reweighted covariance uses the MLE divisor n_w (robustbase: n_w - 1) and no small-sample correction (Pison et al. 2002); (4) raw consistency factor is the asymptotic Croux-Haesbroeck factor rather than RVD 1999 median rescaling; (5) the input is z-scored with non-robust mean/SD over the full sample before the robust fit, so the output is a robust covariance in units of the contaminated SD, not a robust correlation. (6) precision via pseudo-inverse pinvh: for singular scatter (collinear channels) a Moore-Penrose inverse is returned silently instead of failing.
units_and_range: prec: dimensionless (inverse z-score units), signed (sign opposite to partial correlation), symmetric up to round-off, unbounded (observed |value| up to 368 on narrowband_f0-0.25 T=64); prec-sq >= 0. Diagonal NaN. Finite pseudo-inverse values for singular scatter.

metric_name_standard: graphical-lasso sparse precision (inverse covariance) estimate Theta_hat, raw off-diagonal entries (not partial correlations); alpha = 0.01; prec-sq is its square
canonical_ref: Friedman J, Hastie T, Tibshirani R 2008, 'Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso', Biostatistics 9(3):432-441, eq. (1)/(2.1) (diagonal penalised); off-diagonal-only penalty: Yuan M, Lin Y 2007, 'Model selection and estimation in the Gaussian graphical model', Biometrika 94(1):19-35, eq. (4); Banerjee O, El Ghaoui L, d'Aspremont A 2008, JMLR 9:485-516
canonical_definition: Theta_hat = argmin_{Theta > 0} -log det Theta + tr(S Theta) + alpha * sum_{i != j} |Theta_ij| (Friedman 2008 sums over all i,j incl. the diagonal; Yuan & Lin 2007 penalise off-diagonals only); Sigma_hat = W = Theta_hat^{-1}; KKT: W_ii = S_ii (+alpha if diagonal penalised), W_ij = S_ij + alpha*sign(Theta_ij) if Theta_ij != 0, |W_ij - S_ij| <= alpha otherwise; partial correlation rho_ij|rest = -Theta_ij / sqrt(Theta_ii Theta_jj)
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.2, p.4: 'The precision matrix is the matrix inverse of the covariance matrix ... For normalized time-series data, the precision matrix is equivalent to the partial correlation between each pairwise time series, conditioned on all other time series, and is within [-1, 1]. The precision matrix is computed via the same module as the covariance matrix (in scikit-learn [2]), and has the same estimators.' Estimator described in §1.1.1, p.3-4 ('Lasso technique, which uses an l1-regularization to sparsify the covariance matrix'; CV variant 'with five splits'); keywords 'undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous'. GitBook basic-statistics.md (Precision) same text. The -sq identifiers are not described in the supplement. Identifiers: prec_GraphicalLasso, prec-sq_GraphicalLasso.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Documented as 'equivalent to the partial correlation ... within [-1, 1]': the code returns raw precision entries Theta_ij, whose sign is opposite to the partial correlation -Theta_ij/sqrt(Theta_ii Theta_jj) and whose magnitude is unbounded (probe: bivariate_gaussian T=256 prec[2,3] = -2.385 vs partial correlation +0.811; up to |Theta_ij| ~ 49 on shared_envelope and ~95 for the CV variant on narrowband). (2) 'the matrix inverse of the covariance matrix': it is the l1-penalised estimate, and it is not the exact inverse of the reported cov_GraphicalLasso (solver iterates, see candidates). (3) The supplement says the l1 penalty sparsifies the covariance; it sparsifies this precision matrix. (4) Documented scikit-learn v0.24.1, executed 1.9.1. (5) -sq variants undocumented.
deviation_from_canonical: Variant of Friedman et al. 2008: the diagonal is not penalised (sklearn docstring _graph_lasso.py:328-329; W_ii = S_ii exactly, probe), which matches Yuan & Lin 2007 / R glasso(penalize.diagonal=FALSE). S uses divisor T on ddof=1 z-scored data. Optimisation is approximate: default tol=1e-4 on the absolute dual gap, 100 sweeps, and the result is returned even without convergence; on ill-conditioned inputs the output can be measurably sub-optimal (candidate). alpha=0.01 is an arbitrary fixed absolute penalty, not data-adaptive. Reported value is Theta_ij, a precision entry, not a partial correlation.

metric_name_standard: graphical-lasso sparse precision (inverse covariance) estimate Theta_hat, raw off-diagonal entries (not partial correlations); alpha chosen by 5-fold CV; prec-sq is its square
canonical_ref: Friedman J, Hastie T, Tibshirani R 2008, 'Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso', Biostatistics 9(3):432-441, eq. (1)/(2.1) (diagonal penalised); off-diagonal-only penalty: Yuan M, Lin Y 2007, 'Model selection and estimation in the Gaussian graphical model', Biometrika 94(1):19-35, eq. (4); Banerjee O, El Ghaoui L, d'Aspremont A 2008, JMLR 9:485-516 CV variant: alpha chosen by K-fold cross-validated Gaussian log-likelihood (e.g. Friedman et al. 2008 §4; sklearn GraphicalLassoCV, iteratively refined log grid); there is no single canonical CV rule.
canonical_definition: Theta_hat = argmin_{Theta > 0} -log det Theta + tr(S Theta) + alpha * sum_{i != j} |Theta_ij| (Friedman 2008 sums over all i,j incl. the diagonal; Yuan & Lin 2007 penalise off-diagonals only); Sigma_hat = W = Theta_hat^{-1}; KKT: W_ii = S_ii (+alpha if diagonal penalised), W_ij = S_ij + alpha*sign(Theta_ij) if Theta_ij != 0, |W_ij - S_ij| <= alpha otherwise; partial correlation rho_ij|rest = -Theta_ij / sqrt(Theta_ii Theta_jj)
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.2, p.4: 'The precision matrix is the matrix inverse of the covariance matrix ... For normalized time-series data, the precision matrix is equivalent to the partial correlation between each pairwise time series, conditioned on all other time series, and is within [-1, 1]. The precision matrix is computed via the same module as the covariance matrix (in scikit-learn [2]), and has the same estimators.' Estimator described in §1.1.1, p.3-4 ('Lasso technique, which uses an l1-regularization to sparsify the covariance matrix'; CV variant 'with five splits'); keywords 'undirected, linear, signed, multivariate, contemporaneous'. GitBook basic-statistics.md (Precision) same text. The -sq identifiers are not described in the supplement. Identifiers: prec_GraphicalLassoCV, prec-sq_GraphicalLassoCV.

implemented_as: Each channel z-scored (ddof=1, optional detrend); X = (T, P) array; sklearn.GraphicalLassoCV() with library defaults: S = biased empirical covariance (divide by T, so S_ii=(T-1)/T); alpha selected by 5-fold contiguous KFold CV on Gaussian test log-likelihood over 16 alphas from 4 refinement rounds of a 4-point log grid starting at [0.01, 1]*max|S_offdiag|, training-fold fits capped at 10 iterations and warm-started; then a full-data fit at alpha_ (max_iter 100). Solver: sklearn block coordinate descent (Friedman 2008 glasso algorithm) with off-diagonal-only l1 penalty, start 0.95*S off-diagonal, stop when |dual gap| < 1e-4 or after 100 sweeps (warning silenced). Returns precision_ (the solver's Theta iterate, not inv(covariance_)) with diagonal set to NaN; -sq returns the elementwise square. Fit shared through data.covariance['GraphicalLassoCV'] by cov, cov-sq, prec, prec-sq; exactly symmetric because rows/columns are written together.
