metric_name_standard: square root of the normalised biased HSIC (V-statistic) with a Gaussian median-heuristic kernel, i.e. sqrt of centred kernel alignment; kernel analogue of dCor_n
canonical_ref: Gretton, Bousquet, Smola & Scholkopf 2005, ALT, LNCS 3734:63-77 (HSIC_b); Gretton et al. 2007, NIPS 20 (= supplement ref [15]; eq. (3) unbiased U-statistic estimator, eq. (4) biased HSIC_b = (1/m^2) tr(KHLH); Sec. 4 Gaussian kernel with 'kernel size set to the median distance between points in input space', whether per variable is not stated); normalisation: centred kernel alignment, Cortes, Mohri & Rostamizadeh 2012, JMLR 13:795-828; equivalence with dCov: Sejdinovic et al. 2013, Ann. Statist. 41(5):2263-2291
canonical_definition: HSIC_b(x,y) = (1/n^2) tr(K H L H), H = I - 11'/n, K_ij = exp(-|x_i-x_j|^2/(2 sigma_x^2)), L likewise with sigma_y, sigma = median inter-sample distance (Gretton et al. 2007 Sec. 4; a separate median for each variable is the common reading, not stated explicitly there); unnormalised, >= 0
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.5, p.6: 'HSIC yields a biased statistic, where the unbiased (and consistent) estimator can be derived by double centering the kernel distance matrix [15]. Both biased and unbiased estimators are computed using hyppo' (identifier 30, hsic_biased). GitBook distance-similarity.md 'Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion'

implemented_as: Default preprocessing: z-score (ddof=1), no detrend. T time points as iid 1-D samples. sigma = median off-diagonal distance of x (first argument) used for both kernels. D = 1 - K double-centred (equals -HKH, the constant vanishes), stat = sqrt( tr(HKH HLH)/sqrt(tr(HKH HKH) tr(HLH HLH)) ) = sqrt of normalised HSIC_b (probe: 0.8773521262252134 vs from-scratch 0.8773521262252156; raw HSIC_b 0.0577). Returns 0 if a variance or the covariance <= 0. Upper triangle mirrored.

deviation_from_documented: (a) The supplement and GitBook describe HSIC as 'an RKHS-based statistic' with biased and unbiased estimators; neither says that the returned value is NORMALISED (HSIC(x,y)/sqrt(HSIC(x,x) HSIC(y,y)), a correlation-like number), nor that the Gaussian kernel bandwidth is the median heuristic computed from the first argument only and reused for the second. (b) 'the unbiased (and consistent) estimator can be derived by double centering the kernel distance matrix [15]': citing [15] for both estimators is supported (Gretton et al. 2007 eq. (3) is the unbiased U-statistic estimator, eq. (4) the biased HSIC_b). The deviation is the 'double centering' wording: double centring of 1-K is what this biased variant computes, while the unbiased variant U-centres (equal to Gretton 2007 eq. (3) / Song et al. 2012 eq. (5)). (c) Labelled 'undirected' but the bivariate value depends on argument order (made symmetric only by mirroring). (d) The square root (dcorr.py:446-447) is not mentioned; hsic_biased is on the root scale while hsic is on the squared scale.
deviation_from_canonical: (1) Returns sqrt(HSIC_b(x,y)/sqrt(HSIC_b(x,x) HSIC_b(y,y))) rather than HSIC_b (probe: 0.8774 vs 0.0577); (2) bandwidth from x only, reused for y (a separate median per variable, the common reading of Gretton et al. 2007 Sec. 4, would give 0.8805 instead of 0.8774 on the probe pair); (3) hence asymmetric in (x, y) before pyspi mirrors it. The 1/n^2 vs 1/(n-1)^2 normalisation of HSIC_b is irrelevant after normalisation.
units_and_range: dimensionless; [0, 1] (Gaussian Gram matrices are PSD, so the centred inner products are >= 0); positively biased under independence; invariant to common positive scaling and shifts, not to rescaling y relative to x (probe, normalise=False: 0.890 -> 0.603 for y*10), default z-scoring removes pure scale differences.

metric_name_standard: Heller-Heller-Gorfine (HHG) test statistic: sum over all ordered sample pairs of Pearson chi-square statistics of rank-of-distance 2x2 tables (sum.chisq variant, no p-value)
canonical_ref: Heller R, Heller Y, Gorfine M (2013) A consistent multivariate test of association based on ranks of distances. Biometrika 100(2):503-510, Section 2 (Table 2, definition of S(i,j) and T); arXiv:1201.3522v3 p.3
canonical_definition: T = sum_{i=1}^N sum_{j!=i} S(i,j), S(i,j) = (N-2){A12(i,j)A21(i,j) - A11(i,j)A22(i,j)}^2 / {A1.(i,j)A2.(i,j)A.1(i,j)A.2(i,j)}, with A11(i,j) = sum_{k!=i,j} I{d(x_i,x_k) <= d(x_i,x_j)} I{d(y_i,y_k) <= d(y_i,y_j)} (A12, A21, A22 analogously, N-2 points per table); S(i,j) = 0 when a margin is 0. d is a norm-induced distance (here Euclidean, 1-D: |x_i - x_k|).

HSIC in Sec. 1.2.5). This SPI is computed via the hyppo package'. GitBook spi-descriptions/distance-similarity.md:184-199 repeats the text; base identifier hhg.

implemented_as: Calculator default preprocessing: per-process z-score along time (scipy.stats.zscore ddof=1), no detrend. For each ordered pair (i,j), i!=j: x = process i, y = process j as (T,1) arrays (single realisation). Distances: sklearn euclidean_distances dot-product formula sqrt(max(x_a^2 + x_b^2 - 2 x_a x_b, 0)) with diagonal forced to 0 (not exactly |x_a - x_b| and not bit-symmetric; probe max |D - |x_a - x_b|| = 3.5e-14 at T=64). Kernel: for every ordered sample pair (a,b), a!=b: mask_x = D^x[a,:] <= D^x[a,b], mask_y likewise; t11 = sum(mask_x & mask_y) - 2 (removes k=a and k=b, which always satisfy both <=), t12, t21, t22 the other cells; S = (n-2)(t12 t21 - t11 t22)^2/denom if denom > 0 else 0; statistic = sum of off-diagonal S. Raw T is returned (no normalisation, no permutation p-value; auto/fast Hoeffding variant not used because auto=False). Directed base class: both orders (i,j) and (j,i) are computed; A has NaN diagonal.

deviation_from_documented: (1) The supplement and GitBook describe HHG as 'an RKHS-based statistic that uses the ranks of random variables to obtain sample kernel matrices'. The code computes Heller et al.'s sum of Pearson chi-square statistics over 2x2 tables built from ranks of distances (hhg.py:282-295). No kernel or RKHS is involved and the ranks are ranks of distances, not of the variables. (2) The supplement keywords and config.yaml:180-186 say 'undirected', but the class is Directed with the label 'directed' (distance.py:66, 71). The statistic is exactly symmetric anyway. (3) 'unsigned' is consistent with the output (T >= 0).
deviation_from_canonical: The kernel matches Heller et al. 2013 §2: '<=' indicators, k = i and k = j excluded via the -2 on t11, S = 0 when a margin is 0 (denom > 0 test), and T sums over all ordered pairs. One input deviates: the distances are sklearn dot-product Euclidean distances, not the exact |x_a - x_b|. Near-equal and exactly tied distances can therefore be ordered differently from the exact metric, which changes the counts. In probes, exact and sklearn distances gave identical T on 17 of 19 datasets at T=256. The relative difference was 1.4% on logistic_maps (process 1 has 8 distinct values) and 0.43% on shared_envelope, and shared_envelope T=64 pair (0,1) differed by exactly 62 = n-2. Scope: pyspi returns the raw T, which grows like N^2 under independence and N^3 under dependence. It is not a normalised effect size, so values are not comparable across series lengths. Check-stage addition: on the raw (kernel-path) logistic_maps rows the rounding effect is larger, 4.9% relative at T=256 (distance.hhg|logistic_maps|256|kernel|exact: pyspi 858472.24 vs exact-distance 818546.71), against 1.4% after z-scoring (|pipeline|exact: 825361.34 vs 813945.24). For the bit-identical copy shared_envelope (0,2) on raw rows at T=64, pyspi gives 242110 = N(N-2)(N-3) + (N-2), one more non-zero-margin table than the analytic maximum 242048 that exact distances reproduce.
units_and_range: Dimensionless, >= 0, unbounded, and dependent on T. Under independence each S ~ chi2_1 approximately, so T is near the number of non-zero-margin pairs, which is about N(N-1); iid T=64 probe gave 2714-4212 against N(N-1)=4032. For identical 1-D series with no tied distances, every pair except each point's nearest and farthest neighbour (zero margin) contributes N-2, giving T = N(N-2)(N-3). The probe on shared_envelope (0,2) at T=64 gave 242048 = 64*62*61. T is exactly symmetric in (x,y). The diagonal is NaN. Check-stage addition: under independence (continuous data) the exact null mean is E[T] = n(n-2)(n-3)/(n-1), derived from the hypergeometric table (E[S | margins > 0] = N/(N-1), N = n-2) and P(no zero margin) = ((n-3)/(n-1))^2: 3842.0 at n=64 and 64514.0 at n=256 (Monte Carlo of 2000 iid pairs at n=256: 64814 +- 328 SE, skewness 0.98).
direction_convention: A[i,j] = HHG(x = process i, y = process j). Directed.multivariate at base.py:91-93 calls bivariate(data, i, j), which unpacks x, y = data[[i, j]] at distance.py:75-76. Swapping x and y swaps A12 with A21 and A1. with A.1, leaving S unchanged, and all counts are integer. The matrix is therefore exactly symmetric (probe max |A - A.T| = 0.0 on iid_gaussian, bivariate_gaussian, nonlinear_dependence, delayed_noise and shared_envelope at T=64) and carries no direction information.

what_changed: The computation is the canonical Heller, Heller & Gorfine (2013) sum of Pearson chi-square statistics, reproduced bit for bit on continuous data by an independent from-scratch reference (14 def runs, max_abs 0.0; refs/hhg_mgc.py imports neither hyppo nor sklearn). Score mapping: on continuous data the numeric half of anchor 10 is met and its supplement half fails, because the supplement/GitBook text misdescribes the statistic ('RKHS-based statistic that uses the ranks of random variables to obtain sample kernel matrices') and labels it undirected while the class is Directed. That is not one of anchor 9's trivial value conventions; 9 is the score for 'canonical computation reproduced, supplement wrong' (README "Score columns: original, rubric reading, adjusted"; for hhg the rubric reading is anchor 9 through the estimator-variance clause, see score_rubric_note), applied the same way to misc.gpfit.DotProduct and misc.coint.johansen_order-0_*. The one value deviation, on tied or grid-valued data, is placed under the anchor-9 clause 'within statistical tolerance consistent with estimator variance', by analogy: ranks are taken over sklearn dot-product distances, so exact ties and near-ties are resolved by floating-point rounding of the dot-product distance formula (a numerical artefact, root cause REVIEW M2, not a convention). Against exact distances this moves the value by 2.6e-4 (shared_envelope T64 kernel, abs 62) to 4.9e-2 relative (raw logistic_maps T256), while the null sampling SD at n=256 is 14225 on a mean of 64514, about 22% (distance.hhg|iid_gaussian|256|pipeline|null); the sampling SD on dependent data was not measured, so the comparison is by analogy only. metric_name_standard: Heller-Heller-Gorfine (HHG) test statistic: sum over all ordered sample pairs of Pearson chi-square statistics of rank-of-distance 2x2 tables (sum.chisq variant, no p-value)
canonical_ref: Heller R, Heller Y, Gorfine M (2013) A consistent multivariate test of association based on ranks of distances. Biometrika 100(2):503-510, Section 2 (Table 2, definition of S(i,j) and T); arXiv:1201.3522v3 p.3
canonical_definition: T = sum_{i=1}^N sum_{j!=i} S(i,j), S(i,j) = (N-2){A12(i,j)A21(i,j) - A11(i,j)A22(i,j)}^2 / {A1.(i,j)A2.(i,j)A.1(i,j)A.2(i,j)}, with A11(i,j) = sum_{k!=i,j} I{d(x_i,x_k) <= d(x_i,x_j)} I{d(y_i,y_k) <= d(y_i,y_j)} (A12, A21, A22 analogously, N-2 points per table); S(i,j) = 0 when a margin is 0. d is a norm-induced distance (here Euclidean, 1-D: |x_i - x_k|).

implemented_as: Calculator default preprocessing: per-process z-score along time (scipy.stats.zscore ddof=1), no detrend. For each ordered pair (i,j), i!=j: x = process i, y = process j as (T,1) arrays (single realisation). Distances: sklearn euclidean_distances dot-product formula sqrt(max(x_a^2 + x_b^2 - 2 x_a x_b, 0)) with diagonal forced to 0 (not exactly |x_a - x_b| and not bit-symmetric; probe max |D - |x_a - x_b|| = 3.5e-14 at T=64). Kernel: for every ordered sample pair (a,b), a!=b: mask_x = D^x[a,:] <= D^x[a,b], mask_y likewise; t11 = sum(mask_x & mask_y) - 2 (removes k=a and k=b, which always satisfy both <=), t12, t21, t22 the other cells; S = (n-2)(t12 t21 - t11 t22)^2/denom if denom > 0 else 0; statistic = sum of off-diagonal S. Raw T is returned (no normalisation, no permutation p-value; auto/fast Hoeffding variant not used because auto=False). Directed base class: both orders (i,j) and (j,i) are computed; A has NaN diagonal.

deviation_from_documented: (1) The supplement and GitBook describe HHG as 'an RKHS-based statistic that uses the ranks of random variables to obtain sample kernel matrices'. The code computes Heller et al.'s sum of Pearson chi-square statistics over 2x2 tables built from ranks of distances (hhg.py:282-295). No kernel or RKHS is involved and the ranks are ranks of distances, not of the variables. (2) The supplement keywords and config.yaml:180-186 say 'undirected', but the class is Directed with the label 'directed' (distance.py:66, 71). The statistic is exactly symmetric anyway. (3) 'unsigned' is consistent with the output (T >= 0).
deviation_from_canonical: The kernel matches Heller et al. 2013 §2: '<=' indicators, k = i and k = j excluded via the -2 on t11, S = 0 when a margin is 0 (denom > 0 test), and T sums over all ordered pairs. One input deviates: the distances are sklearn dot-product Euclidean distances, not the exact |x_a - x_b|. Near-equal and exactly tied distances can therefore be ordered differently from the exact metric, which changes the counts. In probes, exact and sklearn distances gave identical T on 17 of 19 datasets at T=256. The relative difference was 1.4% on logistic_maps (process 1 has 8 distinct values) and 0.43% on shared_envelope, and shared_envelope T=64 pair (0,1) differed by exactly 62 = n-2. Scope: pyspi returns the raw T, which grows like N^2 under independence and N^3 under dependence. It is not a normalised effect size, so values are not comparable across series lengths. Check-stage addition: on the raw (kernel-path) logistic_maps rows the rounding effect is larger, 4.9% relative at T=256 (distance.hhg|logistic_maps|256|kernel|exact: pyspi 858472.24 vs exact-distance 818546.71), against 1.4% after z-scoring (|pipeline|exact: 825361.34 vs 813945.24). For the bit-identical copy shared_envelope (0,2) on raw rows at T=64, pyspi gives 242110 = N(N-2)(N-3) + (N-2), one more non-zero-margin table than the analytic maximum 242048 that exact distances reproduce.
units_and_range: Dimensionless, >= 0, unbounded, and dependent on T. Under independence each S ~ chi2_1 approximately, so T is near the number of non-zero-margin pairs, which is about N(N-1); iid T=64 probe gave 2714-4212 against N(N-1)=4032. For identical 1-D series with no tied distances, every pair except each point's nearest and farthest neighbour (zero margin) contributes N-2, giving T = N(N-2)(N-3). The probe on shared_envelope (0,2) at T=64 gave 242048 = 64*62*61. T is exactly symmetric in (x,y). The diagonal is NaN. Check-stage addition: under independence (continuous data) the exact null mean is E[T] = n(n-2)(n-3)/(n-1), derived from the hypergeometric table (E[S | margins > 0] = N/(N-1), N = n-2) and P(no zero margin) = ((n-3)/(n-1))^2: 3842.0 at n=64 and 64514.0 at n=256 (Monte Carlo of 2000 iid pairs at n=256: 64814 +- 328 SE, skewness 0.98).

Swapping x and y swaps A12 with A21 and A1. with A.1, leaving S unchanged, and all counts are integer. The matrix is therefore exactly symmetric (probe max |A - A.T| = 0.0 on iid_gaussian, bivariate_gaussian, nonlinear_dependence, delayed_noise and shared_envelope at T=64) and carries no direction information.

metric_name_standard: cross multiscale graph correlation (MGCX), temporal dependence statistic with MGC
canonical_ref: Shen, Chung, Mehta, Xu & Vogelstein 2024, "Independence Testing for Temporal Data", TMLR (05/2024), arXiv:1908.06486v5, Sec. 2.2 Alg. Steps 1-3 (p.3); lag statistic MGC: Vogelstein et al. 2019 eLife 8:e41690 and Shen, Priebe & Vogelstein 2020 JASA 115(529):280-291
canonical_definition: T_n(X,Y) = sum_{l=0}^{L} ((n-l)/n) * MGC_n(X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}), where (X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}) = {(X_{1+l},Y_1),...,(X_n,Y_{n-l})} are the n-l lagged sample pairs (present X with past Y, i.e. tests Y_{t-l} -> X_t); here L = 1. Optimal lag = argmax_l of the weighted terms. The lag-l statistic is computed on the distances among the lagged samples themselves.
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.4, p.6 "Cross multiscale graph correlation (mgcx)": "defined similarly to dcorrx (Sec. 1.2.2) but uses lagged MGCs instead of lagged distance correlations (see Sec. 1.2.3)"; via §1.2.2, p.5 this is "the average of lagged ... between the past of time series x to the future of time series y, up to a given lag". Keywords: "undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent". GitBook distance-similarity.md "Cross Multiscale Graph Correlation" repeats the text.

implemented_as: pyspi z-scores each series (Data default), then calls hyppo MGCX(max_lag=1).statistic(x=z[i], y=z[j]). hyppo forms Euclidean distance matrices D_x, D_y of the series; term 0 = MGC (scipy multiscale_graphcorr) of the raw series (weight 1); for j = 1..1, term j = (n-j)/n * MGC(compute_distance="euclidean").statistic(D_x[j:n,j:n], D_y[0:n-j,0:n-j]), which re-applies Euclidean pairwise_distances to the ROWS of the sliced distance matrices (each time point represented by its vector of distances to the other retained time points), i.e. a distance of distances, not the distance among the lagged samples. Output = np.sum of the 2 weighted terms (lag 0 included, no division by 2). x_t (future, process i) is paired with y_{t-j} (past, process j). After the sum, hyppo runs compute_scale_at_lag (MGC.test with reps=0) to obtain opt_scale, which pyspi discards: two extra multiscale_graphcorr evaluations per pair, no effect on the value and no global RNG consumption (probe).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Supplement says "the average of lagged distance correlations"; code returns the (n-j)/n-weighted SUM over j = 0..1 (time_series/_utils.py:102,106), so values can exceed 1 (up to about 2). (2) Supplement does not say the contemporaneous lag-0 term is included; it is, with weight 1. (3) Supplement says "between the past of time series x to the future of time series y"; with x = z[i], y = z[j] the code pairs FUTURE of x (z[i]) with PAST of y (z[j]) (time_series/_utils.py:99-100), so A[i,j] measures j -> i, and the GitBook glossary convention (rows = sources) is reversed. (4) Keywords in supplement and config.yaml say "undirected", the class labels say "directed" (pyspi treats it as directed; it is asymmetric). (5) "unsigned" (keyword and class label) is not honoured: values are negative on independent data (iid_gaussian T64 probe min -0.0318, 13 of 20 off-diagonal entries negative). The negativity comes from scipy's MGC statistic, not from an unbiased dcorr: scipy multiscale_graphcorr returns a local-correlation value documented as lying in [-1, 1] (scipy/stats/_mgc.py:396, 493); when the thresholded significant region is empty or too small, _smooth_mgc_map returns the global-scale entry stat_mgc_map[m-1][n-1] (_mgc.py:502), and that entry takes both signs. hyppo Dcorr and its unbiased U-centring are not on this path (hyppo independence/mgc.py:151-166 calls scipy directly). The sign mechanism inside the compiled _local_correlations was not traced. (6) Lag terms j>=1 are computed on distances between rows of the sliced distance matrices rather than on the lagged series (not stated anywhere in the docs).
deviation_from_canonical: Weights (n-l)/n, inclusion of lag 0, summation (not averaging), the pairing (X_{t}, Y_{t-l}) and the use of MGC all match Shen et al. 2024 Alg. Step 3. Deviation: for every l >= 1 the lag statistic is not MGC_n of the lagged samples but MGC_n of Euclidean distances between rows of D_x[l:n,l:n] and D_y[0:n-l,0:n-l] (hyppo time_series/_utils.py:92,101 constructs the test with compute_distance="euclidean" and passes distance matrices). Toy probe (n=64, x_t = y_{t-1} + 0.3 noise, max_lag=1): MGCX = 0.746817 = dist-of-dist sum; canonical (slices used as precomputed distances) = 0.804596. The deviation is a different but still consistent-looking dependence statistic (each time point embedded by its distance profile); whether it keeps the universal-consistency guarantee of the paper is a hypothesis to examine. Upstream status: neurodata/hyppo main, hyppo/time_series/_utils.py (raw.githubusercontent.com, fetched 2026-10-14), still has "indep_test = indep_test(compute_distance=compute_distance, **kwargs)" and "stat = indep_test.statistic(slice_distx, slice_disty)" on slices of the distance matrices, identical to the installed 0.5.2 time_series/_utils.py:85-108, and main's Dcorr.statistic / MGC.statistic still recompute compute_dist whenever is_distance is False; the branch "if not compute_distance: compute_distance = precomputed" in compute_scale_at_lag is present in both main and the installed 0.5.2 (time_series/_utils.py:114-115) and is unreachable on the pyspi path (compute_distance="euclidean" is truthy), so it cannot rescue the lag terms from the distance-of-distances construction. The distance-of-distances construction is therefore present in current upstream, not specific to 0.5.2. Upstream main also differs from 0.5.2 in small-sample handling: its MGC.statistic wraps multiscale_graphcorr in "except (IndexError, ValueError): stat = 0.0" and compute_scale_at_lag catches ValueError, so slices with fewer than 5 samples give 0.0 there instead of raising.

metric_name_standard: cross multiscale graph correlation (MGCX), temporal dependence statistic with MGC
canonical_ref: Shen, Chung, Mehta, Xu & Vogelstein 2024, "Independence Testing for Temporal Data", TMLR (05/2024), arXiv:1908.06486v5, Sec. 2.2 Alg. Steps 1-3 (p.3); lag statistic MGC: Vogelstein et al. 2019 eLife 8:e41690 and Shen, Priebe & Vogelstein 2020 JASA 115(529):280-291
canonical_definition: T_n(X,Y) = sum_{l=0}^{L} ((n-l)/n) * MGC_n(X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}), where (X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}) = {(X_{1+l},Y_1),...,(X_n,Y_{n-l})} are the n-l lagged sample pairs (present X with past Y, i.e. tests Y_{t-l} -> X_t); here L = 1. Optimal lag = argmax_l of the weighted terms. The lag-l statistic is computed on the distances among the lagged samples themselves.
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.4, p.6 "Cross multiscale graph correlation (mgcx)": "defined similarly to dcorrx (Sec. 1.2.2) but uses lagged MGCs instead of lagged distance correlations (see Sec. 1.2.3)"; via §1.2.2, p.5 this is "the average of lagged ... between the past of time series x to the future of time series y, up to a given lag". Keywords: "undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent". GitBook distance-similarity.md "Cross Multiscale Graph Correlation" repeats the text.
delegate_lib: hyppo==0.5.2 hyppo.time_series.MGCX(max_lag=1).statistic -> hyppo.independence.MGC -> scipy==1.17.1 scipy.stats.multiscale_graphcorr, sklearn==1.9.1 pairwise_distances
implemented_as: pyspi z-scores each series (Data default), then calls hyppo MGCX(max_lag=1).statistic(x=z[i], y=z[j]). hyppo forms Euclidean distance matrices D_x, D_y of the series; term 0 = MGC (scipy multiscale_graphcorr) of the raw series (weight 1); for j = 1..1, term j = (n-j)/n * MGC(compute_distance="euclidean").statistic(D_x[j:n,j:n], D_y[0:n-j,0:n-j]), which re-applies Euclidean pairwise_distances to the ROWS of the sliced distance matrices (each time point represented by its vector of distances to the other retained time points), i.e. a distance of distances, not the distance among the lagged samples. Output = np.sum of the 2 weighted terms (lag 0 included, no division by 2). x_t (future, process i) is paired with y_{t-j} (past, process j). After the sum, hyppo runs compute_scale_at_lag (MGC.test with reps=0) to obtain opt_scale, which pyspi discards: two extra multiscale_graphcorr evaluations per pair, no effect on the value and no global RNG consumption (probe).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Supplement says "the average of lagged distance correlations"; code returns the (n-j)/n-weighted SUM over j = 0..1 (time_series/_utils.py:102,106), so values can exceed 1 (up to about 2). (2) Supplement does not say the contemporaneous lag-0 term is included; it is, with weight 1. (3) Supplement says "between the past of time series x to the future of time series y"; with x = z[i], y = z[j] the code pairs FUTURE of x (z[i]) with PAST of y (z[j]) (time_series/_utils.py:99-100), so A[i,j] measures j -> i, and the GitBook glossary convention (rows = sources) is reversed. (4) Keywords in supplement and config.yaml say "undirected", the class labels say "directed" (pyspi treats it as directed; it is asymmetric). (5) "unsigned" (keyword and class label) is not honoured: values are negative on independent data (iid_gaussian T64 probe min -0.0318, 13 of 20 off-diagonal entries negative). The negativity comes from scipy's MGC statistic, not from an unbiased dcorr: scipy multiscale_graphcorr returns a local-correlation value documented as lying in [-1, 1] (scipy/stats/_mgc.py:396, 493); when the thresholded significant region is empty or too small, _smooth_mgc_map returns the global-scale entry stat_mgc_map[m-1][n-1] (_mgc.py:502), and that entry takes both signs. hyppo Dcorr and its unbiased U-centring are not on this path (hyppo independence/mgc.py:151-166 calls scipy directly). The sign mechanism inside the compiled _local_correlations was not traced. (6) Lag terms j>=1 are computed on distances between rows of the sliced distance matrices rather than on the lagged series (not stated anywhere in the docs).
deviation_from_canonical: Weights (n-l)/n, inclusion of lag 0, summation (not averaging), the pairing (X_{t}, Y_{t-l}) and the use of MGC all match Shen et al. 2024 Alg. Step 3. Deviation: for every l >= 1 the lag statistic is not MGC_n of the lagged samples but MGC_n of Euclidean distances between rows of D_x[l:n,l:n] and D_y[0:n-l,0:n-l] (hyppo time_series/_utils.py:92,101 constructs the test with compute_distance="euclidean" and passes distance matrices). Toy probe (n=64, x_t = y_{t-1} + 0.3 noise, max_lag=1): MGCX = 0.746817 = dist-of-dist sum; canonical (slices used as precomputed distances) = 0.804596. The deviation is a different but still consistent-looking dependence statistic (each time point embedded by its distance profile); whether it keeps the universal-consistency guarantee of the paper is a hypothesis to examine. Upstream status: neurodata/hyppo main, hyppo/time_series/_utils.py (raw.githubusercontent.com, fetched 2026-10-14), still has "indep_test = indep_test(compute_distance=compute_distance, **kwargs)" and "stat = indep_test.statistic(slice_distx, slice_disty)" on slices of the distance matrices, identical to the installed 0.5.2 time_series/_utils.py:85-108, and main's Dcorr.statistic / MGC.statistic still recompute compute_dist whenever is_distance is False; the branch "if not compute_distance: compute_distance = precomputed" in compute_scale_at_lag is present in both main and the installed 0.5.2 (time_series/_utils.py:114-115) and is unreachable on the pyspi path (compute_distance="euclidean" is truthy), so it cannot rescue the lag terms from the distance-of-distances construction. The distance-of-distances construction is therefore present in current upstream, not specific to 0.5.2. Upstream main also differs from 0.5.2 in small-sample handling: its MGC.statistic wraps multiscale_graphcorr in "except (IndexError, ValueError): stat = 0.0" and compute_scale_at_lag catches ValueError, so slices with fewer than 5 samples give 0.0 there instead of raising.

metric_name_standard: cross multiscale graph correlation (MGCX), temporal dependence statistic with MGC
canonical_ref: Shen, Chung, Mehta, Xu & Vogelstein 2024, "Independence Testing for Temporal Data", TMLR (05/2024), arXiv:1908.06486v5, Sec. 2.2 Alg. Steps 1-3 (p.3); lag statistic MGC: Vogelstein et al. 2019 eLife 8:e41690 and Shen, Priebe & Vogelstein 2020 JASA 115(529):280-291
canonical_definition: T_n(X,Y) = sum_{l=0}^{L} ((n-l)/n) * MGC_n(X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}), where (X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}) = {(X_{1+l},Y_1),...,(X_n,Y_{n-l})} are the n-l lagged sample pairs (present X with past Y, i.e. tests Y_{t-l} -> X_t); here L = 1. Optimal lag = argmax_l of the weighted terms. The lag-l statistic is computed on the distances among the lagged samples themselves.
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.4, p.6 "Cross multiscale graph correlation (mgcx)": "defined similarly to dcorrx (Sec. 1.2.2) but uses lagged MGCs instead of lagged distance correlations (see Sec. 1.2.3)"; via §1.2.2, p.5 this is "the average of lagged ... between the past of time series x to the future of time series y, up to a given lag". Keywords: "undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent". GitBook distance-similarity.md "Cross Multiscale Graph Correlation" repeats the text.

implemented_as: pyspi z-scores each series (Data default), then calls hyppo MGCX(max_lag=1).statistic(x=z[i], y=z[j]). hyppo forms Euclidean distance matrices D_x, D_y of the series; term 0 = MGC (scipy multiscale_graphcorr) of the raw series (weight 1); for j = 1..1, term j = (n-j)/n * MGC(compute_distance="euclidean").statistic(D_x[j:n,j:n], D_y[0:n-j,0:n-j]), which re-applies Euclidean pairwise_distances to the ROWS of the sliced distance matrices (each time point represented by its vector of distances to the other retained time points), i.e. a distance of distances, not the distance among the lagged samples. Output = np.sum of the 2 weighted terms (lag 0 included, no division by 2). x_t (future, process i) is paired with y_{t-j} (past, process j). After the sum, hyppo runs compute_scale_at_lag (MGC.test with reps=0) to obtain opt_scale, which pyspi discards: two extra multiscale_graphcorr evaluations per pair, no effect on the value and no global RNG consumption (probe).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Supplement says "the average of lagged distance correlations"; code returns the (n-j)/n-weighted SUM over j = 0..1 (time_series/_utils.py:102,106), so values can exceed 1 (up to about 2). (2) Supplement does not say the contemporaneous lag-0 term is included; it is, with weight 1. (3) Supplement says "between the past of time series x to the future of time series y"; with x = z[i], y = z[j] the code pairs FUTURE of x (z[i]) with PAST of y (z[j]) (time_series/_utils.py:99-100), so A[i,j] measures j -> i, and the GitBook glossary convention (rows = sources) is reversed. (4) Keywords in supplement and config.yaml say "undirected", the class labels say "directed" (pyspi treats it as directed; it is asymmetric). (5) "unsigned" (keyword and class label) is not honoured: values are negative on independent data (iid_gaussian T64 probe min -0.0318, 13 of 20 off-diagonal entries negative). The negativity comes from scipy's MGC statistic, not from an unbiased dcorr: scipy multiscale_graphcorr returns a local-correlation value documented as lying in [-1, 1] (scipy/stats/_mgc.py:396, 493); when the thresholded significant region is empty or too small, _smooth_mgc_map returns the global-scale entry stat_mgc_map[m-1][n-1] (_mgc.py:502), and that entry takes both signs. hyppo Dcorr and its unbiased U-centring are not on this path (hyppo independence/mgc.py:151-166 calls scipy directly). The sign mechanism inside the compiled _local_correlations was not traced. (6) Lag terms j>=1 are computed on distances between rows of the sliced distance matrices rather than on the lagged series (not stated anywhere in the docs).
deviation_from_canonical: Weights (n-l)/n, inclusion of lag 0, summation (not averaging), the pairing (X_{t}, Y_{t-l}) and the use of MGC all match Shen et al. 2024 Alg. Step 3. Deviation: for every l >= 1 the lag statistic is not MGC_n of the lagged samples but MGC_n of Euclidean distances between rows of D_x[l:n,l:n] and D_y[0:n-l,0:n-l] (hyppo time_series/_utils.py:92,101 constructs the test with compute_distance="euclidean" and passes distance matrices). Toy probe (n=64, x_t = y_{t-1} + 0.3 noise, max_lag=1): MGCX = 0.746817 = dist-of-dist sum; canonical (slices used as precomputed distances) = 0.804596. The deviation is a different but still consistent-looking dependence statistic (each time point embedded by its distance profile); whether it keeps the universal-consistency guarantee of the paper is a hypothesis to examine. Upstream status: neurodata/hyppo main, hyppo/time_series/_utils.py (raw.githubusercontent.com, fetched 2026-10-14), still has "indep_test = indep_test(compute_distance=compute_distance, **kwargs)" and "stat = indep_test.statistic(slice_distx, slice_disty)" on slices of the distance matrices, identical to the installed 0.5.2 time_series/_utils.py:85-108, and main's Dcorr.statistic / MGC.statistic still recompute compute_dist whenever is_distance is False; the branch "if not compute_distance: compute_distance = precomputed" in compute_scale_at_lag is present in both main and the installed 0.5.2 (time_series/_utils.py:114-115) and is unreachable on the pyspi path (compute_distance="euclidean" is truthy), so it cannot rescue the lag terms from the distance-of-distances construction. The distance-of-distances construction is therefore present in current upstream, not specific to 0.5.2. Upstream main also differs from 0.5.2 in small-sample handling: its MGC.statistic wraps multiscale_graphcorr in "except (IndexError, ValueError): stat = 0.0" and compute_scale_at_lag catches ValueError, so slices with fewer than 5 samples give 0.0 there instead of raising.

metric_name_standard: cross multiscale graph correlation (MGCX), temporal dependence statistic with MGC
canonical_ref: Shen, Chung, Mehta, Xu & Vogelstein 2024, "Independence Testing for Temporal Data", TMLR (05/2024), arXiv:1908.06486v5, Sec. 2.2 Alg. Steps 1-3 (p.3); lag statistic MGC: Vogelstein et al. 2019 eLife 8:e41690 and Shen, Priebe & Vogelstein 2020 JASA 115(529):280-291
canonical_definition: T_n(X,Y) = sum_{l=0}^{L} ((n-l)/n) * MGC_n(X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}), where (X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}) = {(X_{1+l},Y_1),...,(X_n,Y_{n-l})} are the n-l lagged sample pairs (present X with past Y, i.e. tests Y_{t-l} -> X_t); here L = 10. Optimal lag = argmax_l of the weighted terms. The lag-l statistic is computed on the distances among the lagged samples themselves.
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.4, p.6 "Cross multiscale graph correlation (mgcx)": "defined similarly to dcorrx (Sec. 1.2.2) but uses lagged MGCs instead of lagged distance correlations (see Sec. 1.2.3)"; via §1.2.2, p.5 this is "the average of lagged ... between the past of time series x to the future of time series y, up to a given lag". Keywords: "undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent". GitBook distance-similarity.md "Cross Multiscale Graph Correlation" repeats the text.

implemented_as: pyspi z-scores each series (Data default), then calls hyppo MGCX(max_lag=10).statistic(x=z[i], y=z[j]). hyppo forms Euclidean distance matrices D_x, D_y of the series; term 0 = MGC (scipy multiscale_graphcorr) of the raw series (weight 1); for j = 1..10, term j = (n-j)/n * MGC(compute_distance="euclidean").statistic(D_x[j:n,j:n], D_y[0:n-j,0:n-j]), which re-applies Euclidean pairwise_distances to the ROWS of the sliced distance matrices (each time point represented by its vector of distances to the other retained time points), i.e. a distance of distances, not the distance among the lagged samples. Output = np.sum of the 11 weighted terms (lag 0 included, no division by 11). x_t (future, process i) is paired with y_{t-j} (past, process j). After the sum, hyppo runs compute_scale_at_lag (MGC.test with reps=0) to obtain opt_scale, which pyspi discards: two extra multiscale_graphcorr evaluations per pair, no effect on the value and no global RNG consumption (probe).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Supplement says "the average of lagged distance correlations"; code returns the (n-j)/n-weighted SUM over j = 0..10 (time_series/_utils.py:102,106), so values can exceed 1 (up to about 11). (2) Supplement does not say the contemporaneous lag-0 term is included; it is, with weight 1. (3) Supplement says "between the past of time series x to the future of time series y"; with x = z[i], y = z[j] the code pairs FUTURE of x (z[i]) with PAST of y (z[j]) (time_series/_utils.py:99-100), so A[i,j] measures j -> i, and the GitBook glossary convention (rows = sources) is reversed. (4) Keywords in supplement and config.yaml say "undirected", the class labels say "directed" (pyspi treats it as directed; it is asymmetric). (5) "unsigned" (keyword and class label) is not honoured: values are negative on independent data (iid_gaussian T64 probe min -0.0972, 8 of 20 off-diagonal entries negative). The negativity comes from scipy's MGC statistic, not from an unbiased dcorr: scipy multiscale_graphcorr returns a local-correlation value documented as lying in [-1, 1] (scipy/stats/_mgc.py:396, 493); when the thresholded significant region is empty or too small, _smooth_mgc_map returns the global-scale entry stat_mgc_map[m-1][n-1] (_mgc.py:502), and that entry takes both signs. hyppo Dcorr and its unbiased U-centring are not on this path (hyppo independence/mgc.py:151-166 calls scipy directly). The sign mechanism inside the compiled _local_correlations was not traced. (6) Lag terms j>=1 are computed on distances between rows of the sliced distance matrices rather than on the lagged series (not stated anywhere in the docs).
deviation_from_canonical: Weights (n-l)/n, inclusion of lag 0, summation (not averaging), the pairing (X_{t}, Y_{t-l}) and the use of MGC all match Shen et al. 2024 Alg. Step 3. Deviation: for every l >= 1 the lag statistic is not MGC_n of the lagged samples but MGC_n of Euclidean distances between rows of D_x[l:n,l:n] and D_y[0:n-l,0:n-l] (hyppo time_series/_utils.py:92,101 constructs the test with compute_distance="euclidean" and passes distance matrices). Toy probe (n=64, x_t = y_{t-1} + 0.3 noise, max_lag=1): MGCX = 0.746817 = dist-of-dist sum; canonical (slices used as precomputed distances) = 0.804596. The deviation is a different but still consistent-looking dependence statistic (each time point embedded by its distance profile); whether it keeps the universal-consistency guarantee of the paper is a hypothesis to examine. Upstream status: neurodata/hyppo main, hyppo/time_series/_utils.py (raw.githubusercontent.com, fetched 2026-10-14), still has "indep_test = indep_test(compute_distance=compute_distance, **kwargs)" and "stat = indep_test.statistic(slice_distx, slice_disty)" on slices of the distance matrices, identical to the installed 0.5.2 time_series/_utils.py:85-108, and main's Dcorr.statistic / MGC.statistic still recompute compute_dist whenever is_distance is False; the branch "if not compute_distance: compute_distance = precomputed" in compute_scale_at_lag is present in both main and the installed 0.5.2 (time_series/_utils.py:114-115) and is unreachable on the pyspi path (compute_distance="euclidean" is truthy), so it cannot rescue the lag terms from the distance-of-distances construction. The distance-of-distances construction is therefore present in current upstream, not specific to 0.5.2. Upstream main also differs from 0.5.2 in small-sample handling: its MGC.statistic wraps multiscale_graphcorr in "except (IndexError, ValueError): stat = 0.0" and compute_scale_at_lag catches ValueError, so slices with fewer than 5 samples give 0.0 there instead of raising.

metric_name_standard: cross multiscale graph correlation (MGCX), temporal dependence statistic with MGC
canonical_ref: Shen, Chung, Mehta, Xu & Vogelstein 2024, "Independence Testing for Temporal Data", TMLR (05/2024), arXiv:1908.06486v5, Sec. 2.2 Alg. Steps 1-3 (p.3); lag statistic MGC: Vogelstein et al. 2019 eLife 8:e41690 and Shen, Priebe & Vogelstein 2020 JASA 115(529):280-291
canonical_definition: T_n(X,Y) = sum_{l=0}^{L} ((n-l)/n) * MGC_n(X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}), where (X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}) = {(X_{1+l},Y_1),...,(X_n,Y_{n-l})} are the n-l lagged sample pairs (present X with past Y, i.e. tests Y_{t-l} -> X_t); here L = 10. Optimal lag = argmax_l of the weighted terms. The lag-l statistic is computed on the distances among the lagged samples themselves.
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.4, p.6 "Cross multiscale graph correlation (mgcx)": "defined similarly to dcorrx (Sec. 1.2.2) but uses lagged MGCs instead of lagged distance correlations (see Sec. 1.2.3)"; via §1.2.2, p.5 this is "the average of lagged ... between the past of time series x to the future of time series y, up to a given lag". Keywords: "undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent". GitBook distance-similarity.md "Cross Multiscale Graph Correlation" repeats the text.

implemented_as: pyspi z-scores each series (Data default), then calls hyppo MGCX(max_lag=10).statistic(x=z[i], y=z[j]). hyppo forms Euclidean distance matrices D_x, D_y of the series; term 0 = MGC (scipy multiscale_graphcorr) of the raw series (weight 1); for j = 1..10, term j = (n-j)/n * MGC(compute_distance="euclidean").statistic(D_x[j:n,j:n], D_y[0:n-j,0:n-j]), which re-applies Euclidean pairwise_distances to the ROWS of the sliced distance matrices (each time point represented by its vector of distances to the other retained time points), i.e. a distance of distances, not the distance among the lagged samples. Output = np.sum of the 11 weighted terms (lag 0 included, no division by 11). x_t (future, process i) is paired with y_{t-j} (past, process j). After the sum, hyppo runs compute_scale_at_lag (MGC.test with reps=0) to obtain opt_scale, which pyspi discards: two extra multiscale_graphcorr evaluations per pair, no effect on the value and no global RNG consumption (probe).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Supplement says "the average of lagged distance correlations"; code returns the (n-j)/n-weighted SUM over j = 0..10 (time_series/_utils.py:102,106), so values can exceed 1 (up to about 11). (2) Supplement does not say the contemporaneous lag-0 term is included; it is, with weight 1. (3) Supplement says "between the past of time series x to the future of time series y"; with x = z[i], y = z[j] the code pairs FUTURE of x (z[i]) with PAST of y (z[j]) (time_series/_utils.py:99-100), so A[i,j] measures j -> i, and the GitBook glossary convention (rows = sources) is reversed. (4) Keywords in supplement and config.yaml say "undirected", the class labels say "directed" (pyspi treats it as directed; it is asymmetric). (5) "unsigned" (keyword and class label) is not honoured: values are negative on independent data (iid_gaussian T64 probe min -0.0972, 8 of 20 off-diagonal entries negative). The negativity comes from scipy's MGC statistic, not from an unbiased dcorr: scipy multiscale_graphcorr returns a local-correlation value documented as lying in [-1, 1] (scipy/stats/_mgc.py:396, 493); when the thresholded significant region is empty or too small, _smooth_mgc_map returns the global-scale entry stat_mgc_map[m-1][n-1] (_mgc.py:502), and that entry takes both signs. hyppo Dcorr and its unbiased U-centring are not on this path (hyppo independence/mgc.py:151-166 calls scipy directly). The sign mechanism inside the compiled _local_correlations was not traced. (6) Lag terms j>=1 are computed on distances between rows of the sliced distance matrices rather than on the lagged series (not stated anywhere in the docs).
deviation_from_canonical: Weights (n-l)/n, inclusion of lag 0, summation (not averaging), the pairing (X_{t}, Y_{t-l}) and the use of MGC all match Shen et al. 2024 Alg. Step 3. Deviation: for every l >= 1 the lag statistic is not MGC_n of the lagged samples but MGC_n of Euclidean distances between rows of D_x[l:n,l:n] and D_y[0:n-l,0:n-l] (hyppo time_series/_utils.py:92,101 constructs the test with compute_distance="euclidean" and passes distance matrices). metric_name_standard: cross distance correlation (DCorrX), temporal dependence statistic with unbiased distance correlation
canonical_ref: Shen, Chung, Mehta, Xu & Vogelstein 2024, "Independence Testing for Temporal Data", Trans. Mach. Learn. Res. (05/2024), arXiv:1908.06486v5, Sec. 2.2 Alg. Steps 1-3 (p.3); lag statistic: unbiased distance correlation, Szekely & Rizzo 2014 Ann. Stat. 42(6):2382-2412 (original dcorr: Szekely, Rizzo & Bakirov 2007 Ann. Stat. 35(6):2769-2794)
canonical_definition: T_n(X,Y) = sum_{l=0}^{L} ((n-l)/n) * unbiased dcorr*_n(X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}), where (X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}) = {(X_{1+l},Y_1),...,(X_n,Y_{n-l})} are the n-l lagged sample pairs (present X with past Y, i.e. tests Y_{t-l} -> X_t); here L = 1. Optimal lag = argmax_l of the weighted terms. The lag-l statistic is computed on the distances among the lagged samples themselves.
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.2, p.5 "Cross distance correlation (dcorrx)": "The cross-distance correlation [11] quantifies the independence between two univariate time series based on distance correlation [13] ... This measure is the average of lagged distance correlations between the past of time series x to the future of time series y, up to a given lag." Keywords listed: "undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent". GitBook distance-similarity.md "Cross Distance Correlation" repeats the same text (key reference arXiv:1907.02088).

implemented_as: pyspi z-scores each series (Data default), then calls hyppo DcorrX(max_lag=1).statistic(x=z[i], y=z[j]). hyppo forms Euclidean distance matrices D_x, D_y of the series; term 0 = unbiased (U-centred) Dcorr of the raw series (weight 1); for j = 1..1, term j = (n-j)/n * Dcorr(compute_distance="euclidean").statistic(D_x[j:n,j:n], D_y[0:n-j,0:n-j]), which re-applies Euclidean pairwise_distances to the ROWS of the sliced distance matrices (each time point represented by its vector of distances to the other retained time points), i.e. a distance of distances, not the distance among the lagged samples. Output = np.sum of the 2 weighted terms (lag 0 included, no division by 2). x_t (future, process i) is paired with y_{t-j} (past, process j).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Supplement says "the average of lagged distance correlations"; code returns the (n-j)/n-weighted SUM over j = 0..1 (time_series/_utils.py:102,106), so values can exceed 1 (up to about 2). (2) Supplement does not say the contemporaneous lag-0 term is included; it is, with weight 1. (3) Supplement says "between the past of time series x to the future of time series y"; with x = z[i], y = z[j] the code pairs FUTURE of x (z[i]) with PAST of y (z[j]) (time_series/_utils.py:99-100), so A[i,j] measures j -> i, and the GitBook glossary convention (rows = sources) is reversed. (4) Keywords in supplement and config.yaml say "undirected", the class labels say "directed" (pyspi treats it as directed; it is asymmetric). (5) "unsigned"/dcorr in [0,1] (GitBook glossary) is not honoured: the unbiased estimator gives negative values (iid probe min -0.031 at T=64). (6) Lag terms j>=1 are computed on distances between rows of the sliced distance matrices rather than on the lagged series (not stated anywhere in the docs).
deviation_from_canonical: Weights (n-l)/n, inclusion of lag 0, summation (not averaging), the pairing (X_{t}, Y_{t-l}) and the use of unbiased dcorr all match Shen et al. 2024 Alg. Step 3. Deviation: for every l >= 1 the lag statistic is not unbiased dcorr*_n of the lagged samples but unbiased dcorr*_n of Euclidean distances between rows of D_x[l:n,l:n] and D_y[0:n-l,0:n-l] (hyppo time_series/_utils.py:92,101 constructs the test with compute_distance="euclidean" and passes distance matrices). metric_name_standard: cross distance correlation (DCorrX), temporal dependence statistic with unbiased distance correlation
canonical_ref: Shen, Chung, Mehta, Xu & Vogelstein 2024, "Independence Testing for Temporal Data", Trans. Mach. Learn. Res. (05/2024), arXiv:1908.06486v5, Sec. 2.2 Alg. Steps 1-3 (p.3); lag statistic: unbiased distance correlation, Szekely & Rizzo 2014 Ann. Stat. 42(6):2382-2412 (original dcorr: Szekely, Rizzo & Bakirov 2007 Ann. Stat. 35(6):2769-2794)
canonical_definition: T_n(X,Y) = sum_{l=0}^{L} ((n-l)/n) * unbiased dcorr*_n(X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}), where (X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}) = {(X_{1+l},Y_1),...,(X_n,Y_{n-l})} are the n-l lagged sample pairs (present X with past Y, i.e. tests Y_{t-l} -> X_t); here L = 1. Optimal lag = argmax_l of the weighted terms. The lag-l statistic is computed on the distances among the lagged samples themselves.
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.2, p.5 "Cross distance correlation (dcorrx)": "The cross-distance correlation [11] quantifies the independence between two univariate time series based on distance correlation [13] ... This measure is the average of lagged distance correlations between the past of time series x to the future of time series y, up to a given lag." Keywords listed: "undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent". GitBook distance-similarity.md "Cross Distance Correlation" repeats the same text (key reference arXiv:1907.02088).
delegate_lib: hyppo==0.5.2 hyppo.time_series.DcorrX(max_lag=1).statistic -> hyppo.independence.Dcorr(bias=False) (numba-jitted _dcorr), sklearn==1.9.1 pairwise_distances
implemented_as: pyspi z-scores each series (Data default), then calls hyppo DcorrX(max_lag=1).statistic(x=z[i], y=z[j]). hyppo forms Euclidean distance matrices D_x, D_y of the series; term 0 = unbiased (U-centred) Dcorr of the raw series (weight 1); for j = 1..1, term j = (n-j)/n * Dcorr(compute_distance="euclidean").statistic(D_x[j:n,j:n], D_y[0:n-j,0:n-j]), which re-applies Euclidean pairwise_distances to the ROWS of the sliced distance matrices (each time point represented by its vector of distances to the other retained time points), i.e. a distance of distances, not the distance among the lagged samples. Output = np.sum of the 2 weighted terms (lag 0 included, no division by 2). x_t (future, process i) is paired with y_{t-j} (past, process j).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Supplement says "the average of lagged distance correlations"; code returns the (n-j)/n-weighted SUM over j = 0..1 (time_series/_utils.py:102,106), so values can exceed 1 (up to about 2). (2) Supplement does not say the contemporaneous lag-0 term is included; it is, with weight 1. (3) Supplement says "between the past of time series x to the future of time series y"; with x = z[i], y = z[j] the code pairs FUTURE of x (z[i]) with PAST of y (z[j]) (time_series/_utils.py:99-100), so A[i,j] measures j -> i, and the GitBook glossary convention (rows = sources) is reversed. (4) Keywords in supplement and config.yaml say "undirected", the class labels say "directed" (pyspi treats it as directed; it is asymmetric). (5) "unsigned"/dcorr in [0,1] (GitBook glossary) is not honoured: the unbiased estimator gives negative values (iid probe min -0.031 at T=64). (6) Lag terms j>=1 are computed on distances between rows of the sliced distance matrices rather than on the lagged series (not stated anywhere in the docs).
deviation_from_canonical: Weights (n-l)/n, inclusion of lag 0, summation (not averaging), the pairing (X_{t}, Y_{t-l}) and the use of unbiased dcorr all match Shen et al. 2024 Alg. Step 3. Deviation: for every l >= 1 the lag statistic is not unbiased dcorr*_n of the lagged samples but unbiased dcorr*_n of Euclidean distances between rows of D_x[l:n,l:n] and D_y[0:n-l,0:n-l] (hyppo time_series/_utils.py:92,101 constructs the test with compute_distance="euclidean" and passes distance matrices). Toy probe (n=64, x_t = y_{t-1} + 0.3 noise, max_lag=1): DcorrX = 0.746513 = dist-of-dist sum; canonical (slices used as precomputed distances) = 0.804605, identical to dcorr of the series slices x[1:], y[:-1]. The deviation is a different but still consistent-looking dependence statistic (each time point embedded by its distance profile); whether it keeps the universal-consistency guarantee of the paper is a hypothesis to examine. metric_name_standard: cross distance correlation (DCorrX), temporal dependence statistic with unbiased distance correlation
canonical_ref: Shen, Chung, Mehta, Xu & Vogelstein 2024, "Independence Testing for Temporal Data", Trans. Mach. Learn. Res. (05/2024), arXiv:1908.06486v5, Sec. 2.2 Alg. Steps 1-3 (p.3); lag statistic: unbiased distance correlation, Szekely & Rizzo 2014 Ann. Stat. 42(6):2382-2412 (original dcorr: Szekely, Rizzo & Bakirov 2007 Ann. Stat. 35(6):2769-2794)
canonical_definition: T_n(X,Y) = sum_{l=0}^{L} ((n-l)/n) * unbiased dcorr*_n(X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}), where (X_vec, Y_vec_{-l}) = {(X_{1+l},Y_1),...,(X_n,Y_{n-l})} are the n-l lagged sample pairs (present X with past Y, i.e. tests Y_{t-l} -> X_t); here L = 10. Optimal lag = argmax_l of the weighted terms. The lag-l statistic is computed on the distances among the lagged samples themselves.
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.2, p.5 "Cross distance correlation (dcorrx)": "The cross-distance correlation [11] quantifies the independence between two univariate time series based on distance correlation [13] ... This measure is the average of lagged distance correlations between the past of time series x to the future of time series y, up to a given lag." Output = np.sum of the 11 weighted terms (lag 0 included, no division by 11). x_t (future, process i) is paired with y_{t-j} (past, process j).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Supplement says "the average of lagged distance correlations"; code returns the (n-j)/n-weighted SUM over j = 0..10 (time_series/_utils.py:102,106), so values can exceed 1 (up to about 11). (2) Supplement does not say the contemporaneous lag-0 term is included; it is, with weight 1. (3) Supplement says "between the past of time series x to the future of time series y"; with x = z[i], y = z[j] the code pairs FUTURE of x (z[i]) with PAST of y (z[j]) (time_series/_utils.py:99-100), so A[i,j] measures j -> i, and the GitBook glossary convention (rows = sources) is reversed. (4) Keywords in supplement and config.yaml say "undirected", the class labels say "directed" (pyspi treats it as directed; it is asymmetric). (5) "unsigned"/dcorr in [0,1] (GitBook glossary) is not honoured: the unbiased estimator gives negative values (iid probe min -0.099 at T=64). (6) Lag terms j>=1 are computed on distances between rows of the sliced distance matrices rather than on the lagged series (not stated anywhere in the docs).
deviation_from_canonical: Weights (n-l)/n, inclusion of lag 0, summation (not averaging), the pairing (X_{t}, Y_{t-l}) and the use of unbiased dcorr all match Shen et al. 2024 Alg. Step 3. Deviation: for every l >= 1 the lag statistic is not unbiased dcorr*_n of the lagged samples but unbiased dcorr*_n of Euclidean distances between rows of D_x[l:n,l:n] and D_y[0:n-l,0:n-l] (hyppo time_series/_utils.py:92,101 constructs the test with compute_distance="euclidean" and passes distance matrices). Toy probe (n=64, x_t = y_{t-1} + 0.3 noise, max_lag=1): DcorrX = 0.746513 = dist-of-dist sum; canonical (slices used as precomputed distances) = 0.804605, identical to dcorr of the series slices x[1:], y[:-1]. The deviation is a different but still consistent-looking dependence statistic (each time point embedded by its distance profile); whether it keeps the universal-consistency guarantee of the paper is a hypothesis to examine. what_changed: pyspi/hyppo compute the weighted SUM over lags 0..10 with weights (n-l)/n, lag 0 included, pairing x_t = z[i] (future) with y_(t-l) = z[j] (past), as in Shen et al. 2024 Alg. Step 3 and hyppo's own docstring (time_series/dcorrx.py:69-72). But for every lag l >= 1 hyppo passes the SLICED DISTANCE MATRICES D_x[l:,l:], D_y[:n-l,:n-l] to a test object built with compute_distance='euclidean' (time_series/_utils.py:92, 99-101), which recomputes Euclidean distances between their ROWS (dcorr.py:144-147 / mgc.py:154-157): the lag terms are U-centred dCor^2 (hyppo Dcorr, bias=False) of each time point's distance profile, not of the lagged samples. The lag-0 term is the canonical one. Size of the change on 12 canonical comparisons: up to 1.216 on the total (narrowband_f0-0.25 T256, pyspi 7.116 vs canonical 5.899, 21% above; -0.736 on another pair of the same run), 0.260 below (24%) on gauss_ar1_pair, lag-1 term 0.170 vs 0.238 on var2_bivariate, about 0.8% on the near-deterministic delayed_noise delays. The gap has no fixed sign: on narrowband_f0-0.25 the even-lag terms are about 2.4 times the canonical ones (0.42 vs 0.17), every entry is below the canonical value on var2_bivariate and gauss_ar1_pair and above it on logistic_maps; the sign of A[i,j] - A[j,i] agrees with the canonical statistic at every truth-claimed pair. Against the documentation: a weighted SUM (values up to 7.12, bound 10.79) where the supplement says 'average'; lag 0 included; A[i,j] measures j -> i (rows = targets) where the GitBook glossary says rows are sources; keywords 'undirected' and 'unsigned' do not hold (strongly asymmetric, negative on independent data). Score 3 (README anchor 3 names 'mgcx lag handling': the max_lag label promises lagged distance correlations of the series, the lag terms are a different statistic of a sample-dependent embedding); not 4 because the documented quantity is not what the lag terms compute, and the score is the same for dcorrx and mgcx since the lag construction is shared.

what_changed: tslearn's DTW is sqrt(min over warping paths of sum (x_i - y_j)^2) with weight-1 steps and no length normalisation. Sakoe & Chiba 1978 (symmetric form, P = 0) uses |x_i - y_j| with diagonal weight 2 and divides by n + m. On this unit's 4 canon runs the two disagree in scale by a factor 23.96-55.18 (pyspi / 1978 form) and in ranking (Spearman 0.77-0.96 over the 6 pairs of a dataset), so this is a value-changing convention rather than a constant factor. pyspi documents only 'computed with tslearn', so it matches the supplement variant (rubric 7). The value grows with T (null mean 11.2 at T256, 21.8 at T1024, about sqrt(T)). Without z-scoring the value scales with amplitude (scaled_offset kernel/z-scored ratio 3.0-15.5) and a linear trend changes it by up to 279% (trending pipeline without detrend). On z-scored noise it barely separates an anti-correlated pair from independent pairs (see candidate 1).

canonical_ref: Sakoe H, Chiba S 1978, IEEE Trans. Acoust. Speech Signal Process. 26(1):43-49, symmetric DP-equation (Table I / eq. for P=0) and adjustment window |i-j| <= r; global path constraints also in Itakura F 1975, IEEE Trans. ASSP 23(1):67-72 (slope limits 1/2..2)

deviation_from_documented: The slope parameter (2) is undocumented; otherwise none.
deviation_from_canonical: Three convention differences from the Sakoe-Chiba 1978 symmetric form: (1) local cost is the SQUARED difference and the result is sqrt of the minimal accumulated squared cost (Euclidean-over-path DTW), not the sum of |a_i-b_j|; (2) step pattern is 'symmetric1' (diagonal move weight 1, not 2); (3) no normalisation by I+J (or by path length), so the value grows with T (about sqrt(T) for independent noise). Probe (T=50 iid N(0,1)): tslearn 6.5668 == from-scratch sqrt(min sum sq) 6.5668; abs-cost unweighted DP 36.674. This is the convention of most ML libraries (tslearn docstring _dtw.py:41-46; dtaidistance 2.5.1 dtw.distance(use_c=False) gives the identical unconstrained value on seeded probes T=50 seed 0 and T=80 seed 5). Constraint: Itakura 1975 imposes LOCAL slope constraints (no two consecutive horizontal moves, slopes 1/2..2), whose reachable region is the parallelogram; tslearn imposes only the GLOBAL parallelogram with ordinary symmetric1 local moves, so arbitrarily long horizontal/vertical runs are allowed inside the region (common 'Itakura window' practice, e.g. R dtw itakuraWindow).
units_and_range: Same units as the (z-scored, hence dimensionless) input; >= 0; 0 iff an admissible warping aligns the series exactly; unnormalised, grows with T; symmetric in its two arguments for equal-length inputs; finite for finite input (an infeasible Itakura mask raises instead of returning NaN). Diagonal of the pyspi matrix is NaN.
direction_convention: Undirected: A[i,j] = A[j,i] = dtw(z_min(i,j), z_max(i,j)) (Undirected.multivariate mirrors the upper triangle); both orders are computed and the function is argument-symmetric, so the copy only removes last-bit differences; diagonal NaN.

deviation_from_documented: The band width is undocumented; it is fixed at 1 sample for every T (tslearn default, _masks.py:339-341). Identifier spelling: the code produces 'dtw_constraint-sakoe-chiba' (distance.py:161 replaces '_' by '-'), the supplement and GitBook list 'dtw_constraint-sakoe_chiba' (cosmetic).
deviation_from_canonical: Three convention differences from the Sakoe-Chiba 1978 symmetric form: (1) local cost is the SQUARED difference and the result is sqrt of the minimal accumulated squared cost (Euclidean-over-path DTW), not the sum of |a_i-b_j|; (2) step pattern is 'symmetric1' (diagonal move weight 1, not 2); (3) no normalisation by I+J (or by path length), so the value grows with T (about sqrt(T) for independent noise). Probe (T=50 iid N(0,1)): tslearn 6.5668 == from-scratch sqrt(min sum sq) 6.5668; abs-cost unweighted DP 36.674. This is the convention of most ML libraries (tslearn docstring _dtw.py:41-46; dtaidistance 2.5.1 dtw.distance(use_c=False) gives the identical unconstrained value on seeded probes T=50 seed 0 and T=80 seed 5). Band: Sakoe-Chiba define the adjustment window r as a tunable parameter (the canonical practice is a width proportional to series length); a fixed r=1 allows at most a one-sample local shift, so the measure stays close to the lock-step Euclidean distance. Probe (T=50): dtw_SC 8.06 vs unconstrained 6.57 vs Euclidean 10.13.
units_and_range: Same units as the (z-scored, hence dimensionless) input; >= 0; 0 iff an admissible warping aligns the series exactly; unnormalised, grows with T; symmetric in its two arguments for equal-length inputs; finite for finite input (an infeasible Itakura mask raises instead of returning NaN). Diagonal of the pyspi matrix is NaN.

score_rubric_note: A radius fixed at 1 sample blocks the documented shifting. Delays of 3 and 5 keep dtw/||z0-zk|| at 0.724/0.731, against 0.098/0.123 under itakura (delayed_noise T1024).
what_changed: tslearn's DTW is sqrt(min over warping paths of sum (x_i - y_j)^2) with weight-1 steps and no length normalisation. Sakoe & Chiba 1978 (symmetric form, P = 0) uses |x_i - y_j| with diagonal weight 2 and divides by n + m. On this unit's 4 canon runs the two disagree in scale by a factor 24.4-51.1 (pyspi / 1978 form) and in ranking (Spearman 0.76-0.94 over the 6 pairs of a dataset), so this is a value-changing convention rather than a constant factor. In addition the band radius is fixed at 1 sample at every T (tslearn default, pyspi passes no radius), an undocumented choice. Sakoe & Chiba treat r as a tuning parameter, usually a fraction of the length; with r = 1 the SPI absorbs at most a 1-sample shift and stays at 70-74% of the lock-step Euclidean distance on noise, so it behaves as a slightly relaxed Euclidean distance. Documented statement the r = 1 band contradicts: the supplement (supplement.txt:283-286; GitBook distance-similarity.md:150) describes DTW as finding the minimum distance 'through alignment (shifting and dilating of the sequences)' and adds the band 'to prevent pathological warpings'. With r = 1 the band also prevents ordinary shifts: delays of 3 and 5 samples keep dtw/||z0 - zk|| at 0.724 / 0.731 (distance.dtw.constraint-sakoe_chiba|delayed_noise|1024|pipeline|delay), against 0.098 / 0.123 under the itakura parallelogram on the same data (distance.dtw.constraint-itakura|delayed_noise|1024|pipeline|delay). The unit therefore deviates from the documented description as well as from canonical practice, in an interpretable way (rubric 6); the itakura unit (rubric 7) does perform the documented shifting.

score_rubric_note: A radius fixed at 1 sample blocks the documented shifting. Delays of 3 and 5 keep dtw/||z0-zk|| at 0.724/0.731, against 0.098/0.123 under itakura (delayed_noise T1024).
what_changed: tslearn's DTW is sqrt(min over warping paths of sum (x_i - y_j)^2) with weight-1 steps and no length normalisation. Sakoe & Chiba 1978 (symmetric form, P = 0) uses |x_i - y_j| with diagonal weight 2 and divides by n + m. On this unit's 4 canon runs the two disagree in scale by a factor 24.4-51.1 (pyspi / 1978 form) and in ranking (Spearman 0.76-0.94 over the 6 pairs of a dataset), so this is a value-changing convention rather than a constant factor. In addition the band radius is fixed at 1 sample at every T (tslearn default, pyspi passes no radius), an undocumented choice. Sakoe & Chiba treat r as a tuning parameter, usually a fraction of the length; with r = 1 the SPI absorbs at most a 1-sample shift and stays at 70-74% of the lock-step Euclidean distance on noise, so it behaves as a slightly relaxed Euclidean distance. Documented statement the r = 1 band contradicts: the supplement (supplement.txt:283-286; GitBook distance-similarity.md:150) describes DTW as finding the minimum distance 'through alignment (shifting and dilating of the sequences)' and adds the band 'to prevent pathological warpings'. With r = 1 the band also prevents ordinary shifts: delays of 3 and 5 samples keep dtw/||z0 - zk|| at 0.724 / 0.731 (distance.dtw.constraint-sakoe_chiba|delayed_noise|1024|pipeline|delay), against 0.098 / 0.123 under the itakura parallelogram on the same data (distance.dtw.constraint-itakura|delayed_noise|1024|pipeline|delay). The unit therefore deviates from the documented description as well as from canonical practice, in an interpretable way (rubric 6); the itakura unit (rubric 7) does perform the documented shifting.

metric_name_standard: Soft-DTW discrepancy (Cuturi-Blondel soft-min DTW value, gamma = 1, squared Euclidean cost); not the soft-DTW divergence

canonical_definition: dtw_gamma(x,y) = min^gamma { <A, Delta(x,y)> : A in A_{n,m} }, min^gamma(a_1..a_k) = -gamma log sum_i exp(-a_i/gamma), Delta_ij = ||x_i - y_j||^2; computed by r_ij = Delta_ij + min^gamma(r_{i-1,j-1}, r_{i-1,j}, r_{i,j-1}), r_00 = 0, borders +inf

metric_name_standard: Soft-DTW discrepancy (Cuturi-Blondel soft-min DTW value, gamma = 1, squared Euclidean cost); not the soft-DTW divergence
canonical_ref: Cuturi M, Blondel M 2017, Soft-DTW: a Differentiable Loss Function for Time-Series, ICML (PMLR 70:894-903), eq. (1)-(2) and Algorithm 1
canonical_definition: dtw_gamma(x,y) = min^gamma { <A, Delta(x,y)> : A in A_{n,m} }, min^gamma(a_1..a_k) = -gamma log sum_i exp(-a_i/gamma), Delta_ij = ||x_i - y_j||^2; computed by r_ij = Delta_ij + min^gamma(r_{i-1,j-1}, r_{i-1,j}, r_{i,j-1}), r_00 = 0, borders +inf

metric_name_standard: Longest common subsequence similarity with Sakoe-Chiba band (radius 1)
canonical_ref: Vlachos M, Kollios G, Gunopulos D 2002, Proc. 18th ICDE pp. 673-684, definitions of LCSS_{delta,eps} and similarity S1 = LCSS/min(n,m) (Sec. 2; definition numbering not re-checked against the PDF; the paper states the eps test per coordinate for 2-D trajectories)
canonical_definition: LCSS(A,B) = 0 if A or B empty; 1+LCSS(Head(A),Head(B)) if |a_n-b_m| < eps and |n-m| <= delta; else max(LCSS(Head(A),B), LCSS(A,Head(B))); similarity S1 = LCSS_{delta,eps}(A,B)/min(n,m)
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.8, p.7 (pack lines 302-311) and GitBook 'Longest Common Subsequence': "measuring the similarity between continuous subsections of time series... subject to distance thresholds and alignment constraints. We use the default threshold from the tslearn package (eps = 1), and include the three global constraints"; keywords undirected, nonlinear, unsigned.
delegate_lib: tslearn==0.9.0 tslearn.metrics.lcss (dtw_variants.py:2383) -> numba _njit_lcss
implemented_as: Intended: matches allowed only for |i-j| <= 1 (tslearn default radius 1), which equals Vlachos delta = 1. Actual (numpy backend, tslearn 0.9.0): the boolean mask is computed and passed but njit_lcss_accumulated_matrix tests numpy.isfinite(mask) which is True for every boolean entry, so the full grid is used and the value equals unconstrained lcss exactly. Score = LCSS / T with match rule |x_i - y_j| <= 1 on z-scored rows.

metric_name_standard: Summary (time-mean or time-max) of the Euclidean Fréchet mean (pointwise average (x+y)/2) of two z-scored series; squared variant summarises ((x+y)/2)^2
canonical_ref: Fréchet 1948, Ann. Inst. Henri Poincaré 10(4):215-310 (Fréchet mean); for squared Euclidean distance the Fréchet mean of {x_k} is the arithmetic mean (e.g. Petitjean et al. 2011, Pattern Recognit. 44:678, §2). The scalar mean/max summary is a pyspi construction (Cliff et al. 2023, Nat. Comput. Sci., supplement §1.2.10) with no literature counterpart.
canonical_definition: b* = argmin_b sum_k ||b - x_k||^2 = (x + y)/2; SPI = mean_t b*(t) or max_t b*(t); squared: mean_t b*(t)^2 or max_t b*(t)^2
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.10, p.7 (supplement.txt lines 321-335): "A barycenter (or Fréchet mean) [21, 22] is a (univariate) time series that minimizes the sum of squared distances between MTS ... For each pair of (bivariate) time series ... we compute the raw barycenters then summarize them by taking their mean (modifier mean) and maximum (max), yielding seven SPIs" (keywords: undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent). GitBook distance-similarity.md:41-75 repeats this, adds "timepoint at which the maximum occurs (max_time)" and lists 12 identifiers bary_{euclidean,dtw,softdtw,sgddtw}_{mean,max,max_time}; neither source documents the squared (bary-sq_*) variants.
delegate_lib: tslearn==0.9.0 tslearn.barycenters.euclidean_barycenter (numpy.average over axis 0, uniform weights)
implemented_as: Each process z-scored (scipy zscore, ddof=1; detrend only if requested); b = numpy.average(z[[i,j]] as (2,T,1), axis=0) = (z_i + z_j)/2, shape (T,1); statistic = nanmean/nanmax of b or of b**2. Consequences on z-scored input: mean(b) = (mean z_i + mean z_j)/2 = 0 up to rounding; mean(b**2) = (1 + r)(T-1)/(2T) with r the Pearson correlation; max(b) = max_t (z_i+z_j)/2 >= 0; max(b**2) = (max_t |z_i+z_j|/2)^2. Cached per pair on the Data object and mirrored, so A is exactly symmetric.

Supplement says "seven SPIs" (lists euclidean_max, dtw_mean/max, softdtw_mean/max, sgddtw_mean/max); config computes 16, including bary_euclidean_mean and all eight bary-sq_* variants, none of which are documented; GitBook lists max_time variants that exist in code (distance.py:240-241) but are absent from every config. bary_euclidean_mean (in config and in the EEG selection) is not among the supplement's seven SPIs; on the default z-scored input it is structurally zero (probe: |A| <= 1.8e-17 on bivariate_gaussian T=256).
deviation_from_canonical: Barycenter itself matches the canonical Euclidean Fréchet mean exactly (numpy.average with equal weights). The summaries are pyspi-defined: bary_euclidean_mean is identically 0 (degenerate) under normalise=True; bary-sq_euclidean_mean is an affine function of Pearson r, (1+r)(T-1)/(2T), i.e. a rescaled correlation rather than a distance; the max variants are extreme-value statistics of x+y and depend on tail behaviour and T.
units_and_range: z-score units (dimensionless after normalisation). mean: 0 up to ~1e-16 rounding, either sign. max: >= 0 (max of a zero-mean series), grows with T for Gaussian data. sq-mean: in [0, (T-1)/T]. sq-max: >= sq-mean, >= 0. Never NaN for finite input. Labelled signed. Symmetric.
direction_convention: undirected: A[i,j] = A[j,i] bit-identical (shared cached barycenter); the barycenter is computed once from z[[max(i,j), min(i,j)]] and the Euclidean average is order-invariant anyway

metric_name_standard: Summary (time-mean or time-max) of the DTW barycenter (DBA / Fréchet mean under DTW) of two z-scored series; squared variant summarises its square
canonical_ref: Petitjean, Ketterlin & Gançarski 2011, Pattern Recognit. 44(3):678-693 (DBA, §4 Alg. 5); Schultz & Jain 2018, Pattern Recognit. 74:340-358 (Fréchet function, MM algorithm Alg. 2). Mean/max summary: pyspi construction (supplement §1.2.10).
canonical_definition: b* in argmin_b F(b) = (1/n) sum_k DTW(b, x_k)^2 with DTW(b,x)^2 = min over warping paths of sum (b_t - x_s)^2 (unconstrained); DBA/MM iterate: align each x_k to b by DTW, set b_t = average of all x_k samples aligned to t; non-convex, returns a local minimiser. SPI = mean_t b(t) or max_t b(t) (squared: of b(t)^2).
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.10, p.7 (supplement.txt lines 321-335): "A barycenter (or Fréchet mean) [21, 22] is a (univariate) time series that minimizes the sum of squared distances between MTS ... For each pair of (bivariate) time series ... we compute the raw barycenters then summarize them by taking their mean (modifier mean) and maximum (max), yielding seven SPIs" (keywords: undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent). GitBook distance-similarity.md:41-75 repeats this, adds "timepoint at which the maximum occurs (max_time)" and lists 12 identifiers bary_{euclidean,dtw,softdtw,sgddtw}_{mean,max,max_time}; neither source documents the squared (bary-sq_*) variants. Mode dtw is documented as "alignment via expectation maximization".

implemented_as: z-scored pair (ddof=1). Init b0 = nanmean of the two series = Euclidean barycenter (dba.py:23-25, 707). Up to 30 iterations: DTW path of b against each x_k (squared-Euclidean local cost, no global constraint), cost = mean_k DTW^2 (weights ones/2); valence V = sum of path counts per barycenter index, b <- diag(1/V) sum_k W_k x_k (Petitjean averaging); stop when |cost_prev - cost| < 1e-5 (absolute) or the cost increases (ConvergenceWarning). The returned b is the update after the last assignment step. Single initialisation; deterministic; input order irrelevant (probe2 order-diff 0). Then nanmean/nanmax of b or b**2.

score_rubric_note: Anchor 7, first clause: pyspi runs the DBA the supplement names, and the from-scratch DBA reproduces it (52/52 runs, max_rel 4.2e-14). It differs from the canonical Frechet mean: one mean-initialised run has a cost a relative 0.12-0.56 (bivariate_gaussian) and 1.85-44.5 (delayed_noise) above the best of 8 starts.
what_changed: pyspi/tslearn compute DBA exactly as the from-scratch reference (single run, init = (x+y)/2, absolute tol 1e-5). This is the variant the supplement names ("alignment via expectation maximization"), so the score is anchor 7 (supplement variant, value-changing difference from canonical), not 6; the descent check F(pyspi) <= F(init) is not counted as an optimality pass. The canonical target is the DTW Frechet mean argmin_b F(b); a single mean-initialised DBA run returns a local minimiser whose cost is 12-56% above an 8-start minimum on Gaussian pairs and 1.9-45x above it on delayed copies (where it is worse than simply returning one input series). The value of every bary_dtw_* identifier therefore depends on the initialisation rule; Petitjean et al. initialise from an input sequence. On one narrowband pair DBA stays at the Euclidean mean (a strict local minimum), so bary_dtw_max equals bary_euclidean_max there. bary_dtw_mean is near zero (<= 0.09) because the barycenter starts at a zero-mean average.

metric_name_standard: Summary (time-mean or time-max) of the DTW barycenter of two z-scored series estimated by stochastic subgradient descent; squared variant summarises its square
canonical_ref: Schultz & Jain 2018, Pattern Recognit. 74:340-358 (stochastic subgradient mean algorithm; Alg. 3 in arXiv:1701.06393v1, where Alg. 1 is the batch subgradient mean and Alg. 2 the majorize-minimize mean) for the DTW Fréchet function; Petitjean et al. 2011, Pattern Recognit. 44:678 (DBA). Mean/max summary: pyspi construction.
canonical_definition: b* in argmin_b F(b) = (1/n) sum_k DTW(b, x_k)^2; SSG: for k in a random order, b <- b - eta * 2 (V_k b - W_k x_k) with (V_k, W_k) from the optimal warping path of x_k to b, step size decreasing; SPI = mean_t b(t) or max_t b(t) (squared: of b(t)^2).
documented_definition: supplement §1.2.10, p.7 (supplement.txt lines 321-335): "A barycenter (or Fréchet mean) [21, 22] is a (univariate) time series that minimizes the sum of squared distances between MTS ... For each pair of (bivariate) time series ... we compute the raw barycenters then summarize them by taking their mean (modifier mean) and maximum (max), yielding seven SPIs" (keywords: undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent). GitBook distance-similarity.md:41-75 repeats this, adds "timepoint at which the maximum occurs (max_time)" and lists 12 identifiers bary_{euclidean,dtw,softdtw,sgddtw}_{mean,max,max_time}; neither source documents the squared (bary-sq_*) variants. Mode sgddtw is documented as "alignment via a subgradient descent algorithm".

implemented_as: z-scored pair (ddof=1). Init b0 = (x+y)/2. Each epoch: rng.permutation(2) from the global numpy RNG; for each series k: DTW path b->x_k, b <- b - 2*eta*(V_k*b - W_k x_k) (wi.sum() = 1). eta decreases by (0.05-0.005)/2 after each sample during epoch 0 only, then stays 0.005. After each epoch the variable "cost" holds only the LAST processed series' dist^2 * weights[0]/sum(weights) (half its squared DTW); stop if |cost_prev - cost| < 1e-5 or cost > cost_prev (ConvergenceWarning). Result depends on the global numpy RNG state and on input order; within a Calculator run the four sgddtw identifiers share one cached barycenter per pair. Then nanmean/nanmax of b or b**2.

deviation_from_canonical: Update rule is SSG (Schultz & Jain 2018; arXiv:1701.06393v1 Alg. 3, line 8) except that tslearn steps by 2*eta where Alg. 3 steps by eta, with a step size falling 0.05 -> 0.005 over the first epoch then constant. The stopping rule is not a test on F(b): it compares the per-sample cost of whichever series happened to be processed last in two consecutive epochs, so any increase in that noisy quantity stops the descent. Probe4: bivariate_gaussian T=256 stops after 4 epochs (last-sample costs 35.05, 28.16, 27.89, 31.23) with F(b)=57.77, while 30 uninterrupted epochs reach 50.26 and MM-DBA reaches 44.69; delayed_noise T=1024 stops with F=331.46 vs 185.01 uninterrupted and 135.86 for MM-DBA. The barycenter is therefore an under-converged estimate of the DTW Fréchet mean. Mean/max summaries are pyspi-defined.

what_changed: The update rule and step schedule match tslearn's stochastic subgradient mean exactly (independent replication to 1e-13, including the global-RNG stream). It deviates from Schultz & Jain (arXiv:1701.06393v1, Sec. 3 termination criteria T1/T2; Sec. 5.1 runs fixed 50 epochs): tslearn stops when the pre-update DTW^2 of the single last-processed series rises between epochs, which happens after 3-5 epochs on most Gaussian pairs, so the returned barycenter is an under-converged Frechet-mean estimate (cost 2-43% above DBA on bivariate_gaussian, up to 3.6x on delayed copies). The update uses 2*eta where arXiv v1 Alg. 3 line 8 has eta (a factor-2 step-size scaling). The value depends on the global numpy RNG state, hence on every RNG draw consumed earlier in a Calculator run (already documented, tests/README.md:134/146); within one Data object the first sgddtw identifier fixes the barycenter for the other three. Scored 5: a non-standard estimator with no literature definition (SSG with last-sample early stopping), computed exactly as the code states.
