deviation_from_canonical: The target term differs from Massey/Kramer. For a stationary target with block entropies H_k, sum_{k=1}^n H_k/k >= H_n (H_k/k is non-increasing), with equality only for a serially independent target. pyspi DI = canonical DI + B, with B = sum_k H_k/k - H_n >= 0. B is not zero under independence of X and Y when Y is autocorrelated. For a Gaussian AR(1) target with coefficient phi, B = (H_5harmonic - 1) * (-0.5 log(1 - phi^2)) = 1.2833 * (-0.5 log(1-phi^2)): 0.185 nat (phi=0.5), 1.066 nat (phi=0.9). The gap di_pyspi - [H_KL(Y^5) - CCE] is, sample by sample, the KL plug-in of B (sum_k H_KL(Y^k)/k - H_KL(Y^5) on the same estimates; probe8 agreement <= 2.7e-4 nat, the residual being the 1e-8 noise). At T=1024 one realisation of that KL gap is noisy and seed-dependent: probe8, 10 seeds of independent AR(1) pairs, mean (sd, range) 0.040 (0.046, -0.039..0.116) at phi=0, 0.200 (0.069, 0.096..0.318) at phi=0.5, 1.036 (0.148, 0.881..1.414) at phi=0.9; the single probe4 draws were 0.034, 0.322 and 1.111. The Gaussian plug-in of B on the same targets (0.5 log det of the sample k-lag covariances) is tighter: 0.001 (0.001), 0.190 (0.020), 1.082 (0.081), close to the population B. Composition as coded is reproduced by a from-scratch KL to <= 1.4e-14 with noise off (probe3). At T >= 2005 the JIDT naive-distance defect corrupts the CCE term (probe6 T=4096 iid_gaussian: 2.614 vs reference 0.028; var2_bivariate 2.409 vs 0.574).

metric_name_standard: Directed information I(X^n -> Y^n) from source i to target j (Massey), n = 5, box-kernel plug-in, bits (pyspi variant of the H(Y^n) term)
canonical_ref: Massey JL (1990) 'Causality, feedback and directed information', Proc. ISITA, Eq. I(X^N -> Y^N) = sum_n I(X^n; Y_n | Y^{n-1}) = H(Y^N) - H(Y^N || X^N); Kramer G (1998) PhD thesis ETH; Quinn et al. (2011) J Comput Neurosci 30:17; Amblard P-O, Michel OJJ (2011) J Comput Neurosci 30:7
canonical_definition: I(X^n -> Y^n) = H(Y^n) - H(Y^n || X^n), with H(Y^n) = sum_{m=1}^n H(Y_m | Y^{m-1}) (block entropy of n consecutive target samples); >= 0; = 0 when X does not influence Y causally (incl. contemporaneously)
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.8, p.11 (supplement.txt:526-538; pack lines 537-550): 'Directed information [42, 45] is a measure of information flow from a source time series x to a target time series y that is related to transfer entropy, but has no time lag between source and target [46, App. C]. The directed information can be computed as a difference between the conditional entropy of y given its own past, and causally conditioned entropy [42-44]. For the same reasons as for causally conditioned entropy, we restrict its computation up to a history length of 10.' identifier 87 di_kernel_W-0.5. GitBook information-theory.md:68-86 same text.

metric_name_standard: Directed information I(X^n -> Y^n) from source i to target j (Massey), n = 5, box-kernel plug-in, bits (pyspi variant of the H(Y^n) term)
canonical_ref: Massey JL (1990) 'Causality, feedback and directed information', Proc. ISITA, Eq. I(X^N -> Y^N) = sum_n I(X^n; Y_n | Y^{n-1}) = H(Y^N) - H(Y^N || X^N); Kramer G (1998) PhD thesis ETH; Quinn et al. (2011) J Comput Neurosci 30:17; Amblard P-O, Michel OJJ (2011) J Comput Neurosci 30:7
canonical_definition: I(X^n -> Y^n) = H(Y^n) - H(Y^n || X^n), with H(Y^n) = sum_{m=1}^n H(Y_m | Y^{m-1}) (block entropy of n consecutive target samples); >= 0; = 0 when X does not influence Y causally (incl. contemporaneously)
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.8, p.11 (supplement.txt:526-538; pack lines 537-550): 'Directed information [42, 45] is a measure of information flow from a source time series x to a target time series y that is related to transfer entropy, but has no time lag between source and target [46, App. C]. The directed information can be computed as a difference between the conditional entropy of y given its own past, and causally conditioned entropy [42-44]. For the same reasons as for causally conditioned entropy, we restrict its computation up to a history length of 10.' identifier 87 di_kernel_W-0.5. GitBook information-theory.md:68-86 same text.

implemented_as: DI(i,j) = R - CCE(i,j) with R = sum_{m=1}^{5} H_kernel(Y^m)/m, where Y^m = makeDelayEmbeddingVector(z_j, m) (T-m+1 rows of m consecutive target samples) and CCE as in infotheory.cce.kernel (n=5, cache shared). R is a sum of per-symbol block entropies, NOT the block entropy H(Y^5) = sum_m H(Y_m|Y^{m-1}); the two coincide only for an i.i.d. target. Kernel half-width 0.5*sampleSD, closed box, self-included.

canonical_definition: For a stationary Markov process X = (X^1, X^2) with lag tau: SI_tau = sum_k H(X^k_t | X^k_{t-tau}) - H(X_t | X_{t-tau}) >= 0 (a KL divergence between the joint transition kernel and the product of the marginal kernels); 0 when the two components evolve independently.
documented_definition: Supplement §1.4.9, p.12 (supplement.txt:539; the pack lists 551): "a measure of integrated information between two processes in the context of their own past. It is quantified by the difference between the joint entropy of the bivariate process and the individual entropies of each univariate process. Both entropies are measured in context of (conditioned on) the history of the processes; we restrict this history to be only one-step, assuming a first-order Markov process"; keywords "undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent"; SPI 89 si_kozachenko_k-1. canonical_definition: SI(X;Y) = sum_k H(M^k_t | M^k_{t-tau}) - H(M_t | M_{t-tau}) for the bipartition M = (X,Y), tau = 1; >= 0 for the true distribution
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.9, p.12 (supplement.txt:539-549; pack lines 551-561): 'Stochastic interaction [47, 48] is a measure of integrated information between two processes in the context of their own past. It is quantified by the difference between the joint entropy of the bivariate process and the individual entropies of each univariate process. Both entropies are measured in context of (conditioned on) the history of the processes; we restrict this history to be only one-step, assuming a first-order Markov process.' identifier 90 si_kernel_W-0.5_k-1; keywords undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent. canonical_definition: SI(X;Y) = sum_k H(M^k_t | M^k_{t-tau}) - H(M_t | M_{t-tau}) for the bipartition M = (X,Y), tau = 1; >= 0 for the true distribution
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.9, p.12 (supplement.txt:539-549; pack lines 551-561): 'Stochastic interaction [47, 48] is a measure of integrated information between two processes in the context of their own past. It is quantified by the difference between the joint entropy of the bivariate process and the individual entropies of each univariate process. Both entropies are measured in context of (conditioned on) the history of the processes; we restrict this history to be only one-step, assuming a first-order Markov process.' identifier 90 si_kernel_W-0.5_k-1; keywords undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent. canonical_ref: Kraskov, Stögbauer & Grassberger 2004, Phys. Rev. E 69, 066138, algorithm 1 (their Eq. 8; equation number from memory); MI definition: Cover & Thomas 2006, Elements of Information Theory, 2nd ed., §8.5. The supplement's own reference for MI is [33] MacKay 2003.
canonical_definition: I(X;Y) = ∫∫ p(x,y) log[p(x,y) / (p(x) p(y))] dx dy (nats). KSG1: Î = ψ(k) − ⟨ψ(n_x(i)+1) + ψ(n_y(i)+1)⟩_i + ψ(N), where ε(i) is the max-norm distance from z_i = (x_i, y_i) to its k-th nearest neighbour (j ≠ i) and n_x(i), n_y(i) count j ≠ i with |x_j − x_i| < ε(i), |y_j − y_i| < ε(i); samples assumed i.i.d.

deviation_from_documented: Estimator matches the documentation (KSG, k=4). Undocumented details: 1e-8 Gaussian jitter with fixed seed 42, no bias correction, results in nats, and estimates can be negative although the SPI is labelled 'unsigned'. Version: supplement says JIDT v1.5, GitBook v1.6.1, the shipped jar is a post-1.6.1 master build. The time series samples are treated as i.i.d.; the supplement itself notes that autocorrelation biases the estimate (§1.4, p.9) and offers the DCE variant for that.
deviation_from_canonical: Matches KSG algorithm 1 (a from-scratch brute-force KSG1 reproduces pyspi to <= 3e-15 on bivariate_gaussian, delayed_noise, var2_bivariate, gauss_ar1_pair and narrowband_f0-0.1 at T=256, probe p5). Implementation choices on top of the paper: inputs re-standardised, 1e-8 jitter (changes the value only with ties, e.g. logistic_maps, see candidates), ψ(N) with N = T, max-norm. Applying an i.i.d. estimator to autocorrelated time series is outside the estimator's assumptions (gauss_ar1_pair T=256: 0.1195 vs analytic 0.1578).

metric_name_standard: mutual information I(X;Y) in nats, KSG1 estimator (k=4, max-norm) with a Theiler window (dynamic correlation exclusion) of W_ij samples
canonical_ref: Kraskov, Stögbauer & Grassberger 2004, Phys. Rev. E 69, 066138, algorithm 1 (their Eq. 8; equation number from memory); MI definition: Cover & Thomas 2006, Elements of Information Theory, 2nd ed., §8.5. The supplement's own reference for MI is [33] MacKay 2003. Theiler window: Theiler 1986, Phys. Rev. A 34, 2427 (supplement [36]); Kantz & Schreiber 2004, Nonlinear Time Series Analysis, 2nd ed. (section on the Theiler window, cited by the JIDT javadoc). Window heuristic: see infotheory.theiler_window (Bartlett 1946, supplement [37]).
canonical_definition: I(X;Y) = ∫∫ p(x,y) log[p(x,y) / (p(x) p(y))] dx dy (nats). KSG1: Î = ψ(k) − ⟨ψ(n_x(i)+1) + ψ(n_y(i)+1)⟩_i + ψ(N), where ε(i) is the max-norm distance from z_i = (x_i, y_i) to its k-th nearest neighbour (j ≠ i) and n_x(i), n_y(i) count j ≠ i with |x_j − x_i| < ε(i), |y_j − y_i| < ε(i); samples assumed i.i.d. With a Theiler window W, neighbours j with |t_j − t_i| <= W are excluded from both the k-NN search and the marginal counts, so temporally correlated points do not count as independent neighbours.
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.3, p.10 (pack lines 469-476): 'Mutual information [33] is an undirected measure of the (potentially nonlinear) dependence between paired observations of x and y.' Estimator: supplement §1.4, p.9 (pack lines 414-453): 'The Kraskov–Stögbauer-Grassberger (KSG) technique (ksg) combines nearest-neighbor estimators for mutual information based measures (default of four nearest neighbors, indicated by modifier NN-4)'; 'We primarily use v1.5 of the Java Information Dynamics Toolkit [32]'. GitBook information-theory.md:11 says v1.6.1, :16 repeats the KSG text, :160-180 lists mi_kraskov_NN-4 and mi_kraskov_NN-4_DCE. DCE: supplement §1.4, p.9-10: 'A common solution to reduce bias in nonlinear estimators (like the KSG technique) is to use dynamic correlation exclusion (also known as a Theiler window) [35, 36], which excludes any data points within a given time window from the density estimate ... here, we set the window as the product of the autocorrelation functions of both time series (a heuristic for the autocorrelation time based on Bartlett's formula [10, 37]). The DCE modifier indicates that the Theiler window is used for the KSG estimator.' Same text GitBook information-theory.md:20.

JIDT then excludes every point with |t − t'| <= W from the joint k-NN search and both marginal counts, keeps ψ(N) with N = T, and raises (-> NaN) if T <= 4 + 2W.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Window formula: documented as 'the product of the autocorrelation functions of both time series'; implemented as 2 × the inner product of the two full sample ACFs over lags 0..T−1, truncated with int(). (2) Documented as a heuristic for the autocorrelation time from Bartlett's formula; the implemented value equals Bartlett's 1 + 2Σ_{k>=1} r_i(k) r_j(k) plus exactly 1 before truncation (probe p3: raw − Bartlett = 1.00 on every pair). (3) Because all T−1 lags are summed, W is not an autocorrelation time for oscillatory or trending inputs: it grows linearly with T (narrowband ≈ T/3: 22/85/339/1353 at T=64/256/1024/4096). (4) Other undocumented details as in infotheory.mi.kraskov (jitter, seed, nats, negative values).

metric_name_standard: lag-1 time-lagged mutual information I(X_t; Y_{t+1}) in nats, KSG1 (k=4) with Theiler window W_ij
canonical_ref: Lagged (time-delayed) mutual information I(X_t; Y_{t+τ}), as discussed by Schreiber 2000, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85, 461 (supplement [35]) as the conventional predecessor of transfer entropy; estimator Kraskov, Stögbauer & Grassberger 2004, Phys. Rev. E 69, 066138, algorithm 1. Theiler window: Theiler 1986, Phys. Rev. A 34, 2427.
canonical_definition: τ = 1: I(X_t; Y_{t+1}) = ∫∫ p(x_t, y_{t+1}) log[p(x_t, y_{t+1}) / (p(x_t) p(y_{t+1}))], estimated by KSG1 on the N = T − 1 pairs (x_t, y_{t+1}), t = 1..T−1; not symmetric in (X, Y). With a Theiler window W, pairs with |t − t'| <= W are excluded from neighbour searches and counts.
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.4, p.10 (pack lines 477-485): 'Keywords: undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent. Time-lagged mutual information [35] is an undirected measure of the dependence between time series x and a time-lagged instance of the series y. We include statistics for only lag-one mutual information'. GitBook information-theory.md:235-251: keywords 'directed', 'Time-lagged mutual information is a directed measure ...', lists tlmi_kraskov_NN-4 and tlmi_kraskov_NN-4_DCE. [35] = Schreiber 2000. Estimator text as in supplement §1.4, p.9. DCE text: supplement §1.4, p.9-10 ('we set the window as the product of the autocorrelation functions of both time series (a heuristic for the autocorrelation time based on Bartlett's formula [10, 37])').

metric_name_standard: transfer entropy T_{X→Y} in nats, KSG1 conditional-MI estimator (k=4 neighbours), target and source embeddings (k, kt), (l, lt) selected per pair by maximum KSG active information storage (k <= 10, tau <= 4), source-target delay u = 1
canonical_ref: Schreiber 2000, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85, 461, Eq. (4) (supplement [35]); embedding delays and source-target delay u: Wibral et al. 2013, PLoS ONE 8, e55809; estimator: Frenzel & Pompe 2007, Phys. Rev. Lett. 99, 204101 (KSG-type conditional MI) with Kraskov et al. 2004 algorithm 1; JIDT: Lizier 2014, Front. Robot. AI 1:11 (supplement [32]). Equation numbers from memory. Embedding selection: Garland, James & Bradley 2016, Phys. Rev. E 93, 022221 (cited by JIDT for MAX_CORR_AIS).
canonical_definition: T_{X→Y} = I(Y_{t+1}; X_t^{(l,lt)} | Y_t^{(k,kt)}) = E[log p(y_{t+1} | y_t^{(k)}, x_t^{(l)}) / p(y_{t+1} | y_t^{(k)})], with y_t^{(k,kt)} = (y_t, y_{t−kt}, ..., y_{t−(k−1)kt}) and source embedding ending at t+1−u (u = 1). KSG CMI (algorithm 1): Î = ψ(K) + ⟨ψ(n_z+1) − ψ(n_xz+1) − ψ(n_yz+1)⟩, ε from the K-th neighbour (max-norm) in the joint (x, y, z) space. Embedding selection (MAX_CORR_AIS, Garland, James & Bradley 2016, Phys. Rev. E 93, 022221, as cited by JIDT): for each series choose (k, τ), k <= k_max, τ <= τ_max, maximising the (bias-corrected) active information storage A = I(Y_t^{(k,τ)}; Y_{t+1}); target embedding from the target's AIS, source embedding from the source's AIS.
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.5, p.10-11 (pack lines 486-510): 'Transfer entropy [35] is a measure of information transfer from a source time series x to a target time series y, based on the Takens time-delay embedding ... The embedding lengths are denoted by modifier's l and k for the source, x, and target, y, respectively; the time delay is denoted lt and kt ... The fixed parameters are minimal values, i.e., typically with a fixed target embedding length of 1 (denoted by k-1) or 2 (denoted by k-2). The optimized parameters are inferred by choosing the embedding parameters (up to a maximum embedding length of 10, denoted by k-max-10, and maximum time delay of 2, tau-max-2) that maximize a univariate information-theoretic measure known as active information storage (see the MAX_CORR_AIS method of [32] for details).' Same text GitBook information-theory.md:206-226 (also 'tau-max-2'), which lists the five te_kraskov identifiers.

metric_name_standard: transfer entropy T_{X→Y} in nats, KSG1 conditional MI (k=4) with Theiler window W_ij, embeddings selected per pair by maximum KSG AIS (k <= 10, tau <= 4) computed with the same window, u = 1
canonical_ref: Schreiber 2000, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85, 461, Eq. (4) (supplement [35]); embedding delays and source-target delay u: Wibral et al. 2013, PLoS ONE 8, e55809; estimator: Frenzel & Pompe 2007, Phys. Rev. Lett. 99, 204101 (KSG-type conditional MI) with Kraskov et al. 2004 algorithm 1; JIDT: Lizier 2014, Front. Robot. AI 1:11 (supplement [32]). Equation numbers from memory. Embedding selection: Garland, James & Bradley 2016, Phys. Rev. E 93, 022221. Theiler window: Theiler 1986, Phys. Rev. A 34, 2427.
canonical_definition: T_{X→Y} = I(Y_{t+1}; X_t^{(l,lt)} | Y_t^{(k,kt)}) = E[log p(y_{t+1} | y_t^{(k)}, x_t^{(l)}) / p(y_{t+1} | y_t^{(k)})], with y_t^{(k,kt)} = (y_t, y_{t−kt}, ..., y_{t−(k−1)kt}) and source embedding ending at t+1−u (u = 1). KSG CMI (algorithm 1): Î = ψ(K) + ⟨ψ(n_z+1) − ψ(n_xz+1) − ψ(n_yz+1)⟩, ε from the K-th neighbour (max-norm) in the joint (x, y, z) space. Embedding selection (MAX_CORR_AIS, Garland, James & Bradley 2016, Phys. Rev. E 93, 022221, as cited by JIDT): for each series choose (k, τ), k <= k_max, τ <= τ_max, maximising the (bias-corrected) active information storage A = I(Y_t^{(k,τ)}; Y_{t+1}); target embedding from the target's AIS, source embedding from the source's AIS. Theiler window: neighbours with |t − t'| <= W excluded.
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.5, p.10-11 (pack lines 486-510): 'Transfer entropy [35] is a measure of information transfer from a source time series x to a target time series y, based on the Takens time-delay embedding ... The embedding lengths are denoted by modifier's l and k for the source, x, and target, y, respectively; the time delay is denoted lt and kt ... The fixed parameters are minimal values, i.e., typically with a fixed target embedding length of 1 (denoted by k-1) or 2 (denoted by k-2). The optimized parameters are inferred by choosing the embedding parameters (up to a maximum embedding length of 10, denoted by k-max-10, and maximum time delay of 2, tau-max-2) that maximize a univariate information-theoretic measure known as active information storage (see the MAX_CORR_AIS method of [32] for details).' Same text GitBook information-theory.md:206-226 (also 'tau-max-2'), which lists the five te_kraskov identifiers. DCE: supplement §1.4, p.9-10 (window = 'the product of the autocorrelation functions of both time series').

metric_name_standard: transfer entropy T_{X→Y} in nats, KSG1 conditional MI (k=4 neighbours), fixed embedding k=2, kt=1, l=1, lt=1, u=1, Theiler window W_ij
canonical_ref: Schreiber 2000, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85, 461, Eq. (4) (supplement [35]); embedding delays and source-target delay u: Wibral et al. 2013, PLoS ONE 8, e55809; estimator: Frenzel & Pompe 2007, Phys. Rev. Lett. 99, 204101 (KSG-type conditional MI) with Kraskov et al. 2004 algorithm 1; JIDT: Lizier 2014, Front. Robot. AI 1:11 (supplement [32]). Equation numbers from memory. Theiler window: Theiler 1986, Phys. Rev. A 34, 2427.
canonical_definition: T_{X→Y} = I(Y_{t+1}; X_t^{(l,lt)} | Y_t^{(k,kt)}) = E[log p(y_{t+1} | y_t^{(k)}, x_t^{(l)}) / p(y_{t+1} | y_t^{(k)})], with y_t^{(k,kt)} = (y_t, y_{t−kt}, ..., y_{t−(k−1)kt}) and source embedding ending at t+1−u (u = 1). KSG CMI (algorithm 1): Î = ψ(K) + ⟨ψ(n_z+1) − ψ(n_xz+1) − ψ(n_yz+1)⟩, ε from the K-th neighbour (max-norm) in the joint (x, y, z) space. Here k=2, kt=1, l=1, lt=1, u=1, neighbours with |t − t'| <= W excluded.
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.5, p.10-11 (pack lines 486-510): 'Transfer entropy [35] is a measure of information transfer from a source time series x to a target time series y, based on the Takens time-delay embedding ... The embedding lengths are denoted by modifier's l and k for the source, x, and target, y, respectively; the time delay is denoted lt and kt ... The fixed parameters are minimal values, i.e., typically with a fixed target embedding length of 1 (denoted by k-1) or 2 (denoted by k-2). The optimized parameters are inferred by choosing the embedding parameters (up to a maximum embedding length of 10, denoted by k-max-10, and maximum time delay of 2, tau-max-2) that maximize a univariate information-theoretic measure known as active information storage (see the MAX_CORR_AIS method of [32] for details).' Same text GitBook information-theory.md:206-226 (also 'tau-max-2'), which lists the five te_kraskov identifiers. metric_name_standard: transfer entropy T_{X→Y} in nats, KSG1 conditional MI (k=4 neighbours), fixed embedding k=1, kt=1, l=1, lt=1, u=1, Theiler window W_ij
canonical_ref: Schreiber 2000, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85, 461, Eq. (4) (supplement [35]); embedding delays and source-target delay u: Wibral et al. 2013, PLoS ONE 8, e55809; estimator: Frenzel & Pompe 2007, Phys. Rev. Lett. 99, 204101 (KSG-type conditional MI) with Kraskov et al. 2004 algorithm 1; JIDT: Lizier 2014, Front. Robot. AI 1:11 (supplement [32]). Equation numbers from memory. Theiler window: Theiler 1986, Phys. Rev. A 34, 2427.
canonical_definition: T_{X→Y} = I(Y_{t+1}; X_t^{(l,lt)} | Y_t^{(k,kt)}) = E[log p(y_{t+1} | y_t^{(k)}, x_t^{(l)}) / p(y_{t+1} | y_t^{(k)})], with y_t^{(k,kt)} = (y_t, y_{t−kt}, ..., y_{t−(k−1)kt}) and source embedding ending at t+1−u (u = 1). KSG CMI (algorithm 1): Î = ψ(K) + ⟨ψ(n_z+1) − ψ(n_xz+1) − ψ(n_yz+1)⟩, ε from the K-th neighbour (max-norm) in the joint (x, y, z) space. Here k=1, kt=1, l=1, lt=1, u=1, neighbours with |t − t'| <= W excluded.
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.5, p.10-11 (pack lines 486-510): 'Transfer entropy [35] is a measure of information transfer from a source time series x to a target time series y, based on the Takens time-delay embedding ... The embedding lengths are denoted by modifier's l and k for the source, x, and target, y, respectively; the time delay is denoted lt and kt ... The fixed parameters are minimal values, i.e., typically with a fixed target embedding length of 1 (denoted by k-1) or 2 (denoted by k-2). The optimized parameters are inferred by choosing the embedding parameters (up to a maximum embedding length of 10, denoted by k-max-10, and maximum time delay of 2, tau-max-2) that maximize a univariate information-theoretic measure known as active information storage (see the MAX_CORR_AIS method of [32] for details).' Same text GitBook information-theory.md:206-226 (also 'tau-max-2'), which lists the five te_kraskov identifiers. DCE: supplement §1.4, p.9-10 (window = 'the product of the autocorrelation functions of both time series').

metric_name_standard: transfer entropy T_{X→Y} in nats, KSG1 conditional MI (k=4 neighbours), fixed embedding k=1, kt=1, l=1, lt=1, u=1
canonical_ref: Schreiber 2000, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85, 461, Eq. (4) (supplement [35]); embedding delays and source-target delay u: Wibral et al. 2013, PLoS ONE 8, e55809; estimator: Frenzel & Pompe 2007, Phys. Rev. Lett. 99, 204101 (KSG-type conditional MI) with Kraskov et al. 2004 algorithm 1; JIDT: Lizier 2014, Front. Robot. AI 1:11 (supplement [32]). Equation numbers from memory.
canonical_definition: T_{X→Y} = I(Y_{t+1}; X_t^{(l,lt)} | Y_t^{(k,kt)}) = E[log p(y_{t+1} | y_t^{(k)}, x_t^{(l)}) / p(y_{t+1} | y_t^{(k)})], with y_t^{(k,kt)} = (y_t, y_{t−kt}, ..., y_{t−(k−1)kt}) and source embedding ending at t+1−u (u = 1). KSG CMI (algorithm 1): Î = ψ(K) + ⟨ψ(n_z+1) − ψ(n_xz+1) − ψ(n_yz+1)⟩, ε from the K-th neighbour (max-norm) in the joint (x, y, z) space. Here k=1, kt=1, l=1, lt=1, u=1.
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.5, p.10-11 (pack lines 486-510): 'Transfer entropy [35] is a measure of information transfer from a source time series x to a target time series y, based on the Takens time-delay embedding ... The embedding lengths are denoted by modifier's l and k for the source, x, and target, y, respectively; the time delay is denoted lt and kt ... The fixed parameters are minimal values, i.e., typically with a fixed target embedding length of 1 (denoted by k-1) or 2 (denoted by k-2). The optimized parameters are inferred by choosing the embedding parameters (up to a maximum embedding length of 10, denoted by k-max-10, and maximum time delay of 2, tau-max-2) that maximize a univariate information-theoretic measure known as active information storage (see the MAX_CORR_AIS method of [32] for details).' Same text GitBook information-theory.md:206-226 (also 'tau-max-2'), which lists the five te_kraskov identifiers.

metric_name_standard: Transfer entropy T_{X->Y} with target history k=1, source history l=1, lag 1, box-kernel (Schreiber) estimate, bits
canonical_ref: Schreiber T (2000) 'Measuring information transfer', Phys Rev Lett 85:461-464, Eq. (4) and the kernel estimator p_r(.) = (1/N) sum Theta(r - |.|) (max norm) described there; Kaiser A, Schreiber T (2002) Physica D 166:43-62; Kantz & Schreiber (1997)
canonical_definition: T_{X->Y} = sum p(y_{t+1}, y_t^(k), x_t^(l)) log2[ p(y_{t+1} | y_t^(k), x_t^(l)) / p(y_{t+1} | y_t^(k)) ]; with k=l=1 and box kernel: mean_t log2[ (C_nps/C_ps) / (C_np/C_p) ] over t = 1..T-1
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.5, pp.10-11 (supplement.txt:476-499; pack lines 486-510): 'Transfer entropy [35] is a measure of information transfer from a source time series x to a target time series y, based on the Takens time-delay embedding ... The embedding lengths are denoted by modifier's l and k for the source, x, and target, y ... The fixed parameters are minimal values, i.e., typically with a fixed target embedding length of 1 (denoted by k-1)'; identifier 77 te_kernel_W-0.25_k-1; keywords directed, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent. GitBook information-theory.md:206-231 same; identifier te_kernel_W-0.25_k-1.

implemented_as: For each ordered pair (i=source, j=target) on z-scored data, JIDT first runs MAX_CORR_AIS on the target alone: for k = 1..10 and tau = 1..2 (tau skipped when k = 1) it computes the Gaussian MI between the k-dim delay vector (spacing tau) and the next sample, N = T-(k-1)tau-1, subtracts the analytic chi-square null mean k/(2N), and keeps the argmax -> (k, k_tau); the same search on the source alone gives (l, l_tau). It then computes Gaussian TE with those embeddings and delay 1 (start = max((k-1)k_tau, (l-1)l_tau)). The search is repeated for every ordered pair. No bias correction of the final TE. Probe var2_bivariate_T1024: selected k=2, k_tau=1 for target x1 and l=9, l_tau=1 for source x0.

metric_name_standard: Gaussian transfer entropy with target history k=1 and source history l=1 (= one half of Geweke's lag-1 Granger causality log variance ratio)
canonical_ref: Geweke J. 1982, J Am Stat Assoc 77:304-313, eq. (2.3)-(2.4) F_{X->Y} = ln(var(e_restricted)/var(e_full)); Barnett L., Barrett A.B. & Seth A.K. 2009, Phys Rev Lett 103:238701 (F_{X->Y} = 2 TE_{X->Y} for Gaussian variables); Schreiber T. 2000, Phys Rev Lett 85:461, eq. (4)
canonical_definition: TE_{X->Y} = I(X_t; Y_{t+1} | Y_t) = 0.5*ln(sigma^2(Y_{t+1}|Y_t) / sigma^2(Y_{t+1}|Y_t,X_t)) = F_{X->Y}/2, where F = ln(RSS_restricted/RSS_full) is Geweke's GC
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.6, p.11 (supplement.txt:500-511): 'Granger causality [40] is obtained by assessing directed dependence of x -> y as the predictive power of a bivariate autoregressive model (comprising x and y) over the univariate autoregressive model (with y only). The statistic included in our framework is the log-ratio of residual variance for the two models, which is a variant of Granger causality popularized by Geweke [41] later found to be equivalent to transfer entropy with a Gaussian estimator [38]'; keywords 'directed, linear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent'. GitBook information-theory.md:90-107 same text. Supplement §1.4.5, p.10-11 (supplement.txt:476-493) defines k, kt (target) and l, lt (source).

implemented_as: For each ordered pair (i=source, j=target) on z-scored data: N = T-1 samples (t = 0..T-2) of (x_i(t), x_j(t+1), x_j(t)); JIDT Gaussian CMI with ddof=1 covariance: TE = 0.5*ln(det S(x_i(t),x_j(t)) det S(x_j(t+1),x_j(t)) / (det S(all three) var x_j(t))) = 0.5*ln(RSS_r/RSS_f) of the OLS-with-intercept regressions x_j(t+1) ~ x_j(t) and x_j(t+1) ~ x_j(t) + x_i(t) on the same samples. Properties confirmed by getProperty: k_HISTORY=1, k_TAU=1, l_HISTORY=1, l_TAU=1, DELAY=1, AUTO_EMBED_METHOD=NONE, BIAS_CORRECTION=false, NORMALISE=false.

canonical_ref: Oizumi M, Amari S, Yanagawa T, Fujii N, Tsuchiya N (2016) 'Measuring integrated information from the decoding perspective', PLoS Comput Biol 12:e1004654: Eq. 9 (Phi* = I - I*), Eq. 8 mismatched decoder q(X_t|X_t-tau) = prod_i p(M_i,t|M_i,t-tau), Eq. 20 I* = max_beta tilde-I(beta), Gaussian case in Methods 'Analytical computation of Phi* under the Gaussian assumption': Eq. 23 (Gaussian I), Eq. 24 (conditional covariance), Eq. 25 (closed form of tilde-I(beta)), Eqs. 26-27 (Q and R), Eq. 28 (block-diagonal covariances), Eqs. 29-33 (d tilde-I/d beta); the same Methods text states that I* is 'a convex function with respect to beta', that d tilde-I/d beta = 0 'is a quadratic equation with respect to beta', and that 'beta can be analytically computed without resorting to numerical optimization' (statements quoted, not re-derived here; equation numbers from a fetch of the article page, whose equations are images, consistent with the vendored code's comment '2nd term of eq. (26)' at phi_star_Gauss.m:87 and utility/I_s_I_s_d.m:2); mismatched decoding: Merhav et al. 1994 IEEE Trans Inf Theory 40:1953 (supplement [54]); PhiToolbox: Kitazono & Oizumi 2020 (supplement [52]).
canonical_definition: Phi* = I(X_{t-tau}; X_t) - I*(X_{t-tau}; X_t), I* = max_beta tilde-I(beta), tilde-I(beta) = -sum_y p(y) log sum_x p(x) q(y|x)^beta + sum_{x,y} p(x,y) log q(y|x)^beta with q(y|x) = prod_k p(y_k|x_k) over the parts of the partition; for the bivariate atomic partition the parts are the two channels. Gaussian case: tilde-I(beta) = 1/2 log|Q^-1| + 1/2 log|Sigma_X| + 1/2 tr(Sigma_Y R) - beta N/2, Q^-1 = Sigma_X^-1 + beta A_D' D^-1 A_D, R = beta D^-1 - beta^2 D^-1 A_D Q A_D' D^-1 (A_D, D block-diagonal regression and residual covariance of each part). Property 0 <= Phi* <= I.

deviation_from_canonical: Structure matches Oizumi et al. 2016 (Phi* = I - max_beta tilde-I) with plug-in sample covariances. Deviations: (1) the maximisation is approximate: L-BFGS-B stops at the initial beta = 1 whenever |d tilde-I/d beta| < 1e-5, so I* is under-estimated and Phi* over-estimated; absolute error up to ~5e-8 (max 4.65e-8 on narrowband_f0-0.25 T256 pair (1,2), phi* 3.891, pyspi beta stuck at 1.0 vs reference 0.922; next 3.3e-8 and 2.8e-8, all nit 0; over 136 pairs = 8 datasets x T in {64,256,1024,4096}), relative error up to ~6.4e-4 on near-null pairs (probe iid_gaussian T1024 (2,3): 1.50073e-05 vs independent maximum 1.49977e-05); inherited from pyspi's vendored PhiToolbox copy (fminunc, finite differences), whose Octave run gives 1.50072e-05. (2) beta is unconstrained; the paper (Methods) states that d tilde-I/d beta = 0 is quadratic in beta so beta can be computed analytically, whereas pyspi (like PhiToolbox) optimises numerically; all probe optima were 0.64-1.33. (3) degenerate (singular) covariances: a singular conditional covariance gives finite/complex values via the logdet eigenvalue filter instead of +inf/undefined (exact one-step delay pair); an exactly singular Cov_X (bit-identical copy, T <= 1024) gives NaN with a UserWarning; a numerically ill-conditioned Cov_X (same copy at T=4096) lets a complex logdet reach scipy.optimize.minimize, which raises TypeError -> NaN via the class except. None of these is +inf. Plug-in sample covariances with separate past/present means and T-2 denominators (the denominator cancels in the unnormalised value). Check-stage correction: (2) the stationarity condition is not quadratic in beta for the atomic bipartition in this parametrisation: d tilde-I/d beta x det(Q^-1)^2 is a quartic (dI x det(Q^-1) is not a polynomial) with exactly one positive root, the optimum (D15 0.86440, D5 0.96505), and tilde-I is concave in beta (scratchpad phi_check/beta_poly.py; pop runs ref_deriv_numerator_poly_degree 4, ref_deriv_decreasing_on_0_6 1). (3) on the exact-delay construction the check runs give small NEGATIVE values (z-scored -0.00110, raw -0.0215 at delayed_noise T1024), not only finite/complex ones.

what_changed: Canonical Phi* (Oizumi et al. 2016) with plug-in Gaussian covariances; agreement with an independent brentq optimum is limited by the optimiser: L-BFGS-B (default pgtol 1e-5) leaves beta at 1.0 when the gradient there is small, which over-estimates Phi* by <= 4.65e-8 absolute (relative up to 6.4e-4 on near-null pairs). Score 9 under the rubric clause "within statistical tolerance consistent with estimator variance", anchored on the independent references only (brentq optimum of the from-scratch tilde-I(beta), population covariances, Monte Carlo of Eq. 20): the largest gap, 4.65e-8 (narrowband_f0-0.25|256|pipeline|indep), is 5.6e-4 of the smallest Monte Carlo SD of the Phi* estimator in this family (8.3e-5, iid_gaussian|4096|pipeline|null), and the absolute gap of the run with the largest relative gap (6.4e-4), 9.55e-9 (iid_gaussian|1024|pipeline|indep), is 3.2e-5 of the null SD at that T (2.95e-4). The clause is applied by analogy: the gap is a one-sided optimiser bias (L-BFGS-B leaving beta at 1, pyspi - optimum in [-3.6e-14, 4.65e-8]), not estimator noise; it is admitted because it is at most 5.6e-4 of the smallest sampling SD of the estimator. Not 10: the agreement is not fp-exact (relative error up to 6.4e-4). Not 7: the canonical optimum is computed independently, so the check goes beyond optimality conditions. The Octave run of pyspi's vendored PhiToolbox is same-lineage (capped at 6) and does not contribute to the score. Separate confirmed finding: degenerate pairs (exact copy / exact delay) give NaN, -ln(2)/2-type or small negative values instead of +inf. canonical_ref: Oizumi M, Amari S, Yanagawa T, Fujii N, Tsuchiya N (2016) 'Measuring integrated information from the decoding perspective', PLoS Comput Biol 12:e1004654: Eq. 9 (Phi* = I - I*), Eq. 8 mismatched decoder q(X_t|X_t-tau) = prod_i p(M_i,t|M_i,t-tau), Eq. 20 I* = max_beta tilde-I(beta), Gaussian case in Methods 'Analytical computation of Phi* under the Gaussian assumption': Eq. 23 (Gaussian I), Eq. 24 (conditional covariance), Eq. 25 (closed form of tilde-I(beta)), Eqs. 26-27 (Q and R), Eq. 28 (block-diagonal covariances), Eqs. 29-33 (d tilde-I/d beta); the same Methods text states that I* is 'a convex function with respect to beta', that d tilde-I/d beta = 0 'is a quadratic equation with respect to beta', and that 'beta can be analytically computed without resorting to numerical optimization' (statements quoted, not re-derived here; equation numbers from a fetch of the article page, whose equations are images, consistent with the vendored code's comment '2nd term of eq. (26)' at phi_star_Gauss.m:87 and utility/I_s_I_s_d.m:2); mismatched decoding: Merhav et al. 1994 IEEE Trans Inf Theory 40:1953 (supplement [54]); PhiToolbox: Kitazono & Oizumi 2020 (supplement [52]).
canonical_definition: Phi* = I(X_{t-tau}; X_t) - I*(X_{t-tau}; X_t), I* = max_beta tilde-I(beta), tilde-I(beta) = -sum_y p(y) log sum_x p(x) q(y|x)^beta + sum_{x,y} p(x,y) log q(y|x)^beta with q(y|x) = prod_k p(y_k|x_k) over the parts of the partition; for the bivariate atomic partition the parts are the two channels. Gaussian case: tilde-I(beta) = 1/2 log|Q^-1| + 1/2 log|Sigma_X| + 1/2 tr(Sigma_Y R) - beta N/2, Q^-1 = Sigma_X^-1 + beta A_D' D^-1 A_D, R = beta D^-1 - beta^2 D^-1 A_D Q A_D' D^-1 (A_D, D block-diagonal regression and residual covariance of each part). Property 0 <= Phi* <= I.

implemented_as: Calculator default z-scores each channel (ddof=1). For pair (i,j), rows [i,j] form a 2xT array; tau = delay = 1; past window X1 = x[:, 0:T-1], present X2 = x[:, 1:T], each centred by its own mean, covariances with denominator T-2 (Cov_X, Cov_Y, Cov_XY = E[X(t-1)X(t)']); partition [1,2] (each channel its own part; the only bipartition, so no MIP search). I = H(Y) - H(Y|X) from Gaussian log-determinants; I_s(beta) is the closed-form Gaussian tilde-I(beta) of the per-channel mismatched decoder; beta maximised by scipy L-BFGS-B from beta=1 with finite-difference gradient and default tolerances (pgtol 1e-5), unbounded; Phi* = I - I_s(beta_opt) in nats. The closed form was re-derived from scratch in a probe and matches i_s_objective term by term (tr(D^-1 S) = N gives the beta*N/2 constant). Any exception inside bivariate returns NaN (logged).

deviation_from_documented: Supplement keyword 'nonlinear' (and config.yaml label) contradicts the Gaussian/linear implementation and the class label 'linear'. Otherwise the prose matches (undirected; Gaussian model; PhiToolbox algorithm). Beyond the prose: the documented 'proxy ... from the PhiToolbox' is reproduced in Python; the optimiser matches pyspi's vendored MATLAB copy (fminunc, finite differences) but not the published PhiToolbox, which uses minFunc L-BFGS with the analytic gradient of I_s_I_s_d; the native finite-difference L-BFGS-B is therefore a behavioural change relative to the toolbox the supplement cites [52] (size of the effect relative to minFunc not measured).
deviation_from_canonical: Structure matches Oizumi et al. 2016 (Phi* = I - max_beta tilde-I) with plug-in sample covariances. Deviations: (1) the maximisation is approximate: L-BFGS-B stops at the initial beta = 1 whenever |d tilde-I/d beta| < 1e-5, so I* is under-estimated and Phi* over-estimated; absolute error up to ~5e-8 (max 4.65e-8 on narrowband_f0-0.25 T256 pair (1,2), phi* 3.891, pyspi beta stuck at 1.0 vs reference 0.922; next 3.3e-8 and 2.8e-8, all nit 0; over 136 pairs = 8 datasets x T in {64,256,1024,4096}), relative error up to ~6.4e-4 on near-null pairs (probe iid_gaussian T1024 (2,3): 1.50073e-05 vs independent maximum 1.49977e-05); inherited from pyspi's vendored PhiToolbox copy (fminunc, finite differences), whose Octave run gives 1.50072e-05. (2) beta is unconstrained; the paper (Methods) states that d tilde-I/d beta = 0 is quadratic in beta so beta can be computed analytically, whereas pyspi (like PhiToolbox) optimises numerically; all probe optima were 0.64-1.33. (3) degenerate (singular) covariances: a singular conditional covariance gives finite/complex values via the logdet eigenvalue filter instead of +inf/undefined (exact one-step delay pair); an exactly singular Cov_X (bit-identical copy, T <= 1024) gives NaN with a UserWarning; a numerically ill-conditioned Cov_X (same copy at T=4096) lets a complex logdet reach scipy.optimize.minimize, which raises TypeError -> NaN via the class except. None of these is +inf. Plug-in sample covariances with separate past/present means and T-2 denominators (the denominator cancels in the unnormalised value). Check-stage correction: (2) the stationarity condition is not quadratic in beta for the atomic bipartition in this parametrisation: d tilde-I/d beta x det(Q^-1)^2 is a quartic (dI x det(Q^-1) is not a polynomial) with exactly one positive root, the optimum (D15 0.86440, D5 0.96505), and tilde-I is concave in beta (scratchpad phi_check/beta_poly.py; pop runs ref_deriv_numerator_poly_degree 4, ref_deriv_decreasing_on_0_6 1). (3) on the exact-delay construction the check runs give small NEGATIVE values (z-scored -0.00110, raw -0.0215 at delayed_noise T1024), not only finite/complex ones.
units_and_range: nats; 0 <= Phi* <= I in theory, finite-sample positive bias on independent data; invariant to per-channel affine rescaling; symmetric; NaN when an exception occurs (e.g. constant channel); degenerate pairs never give inf: an exactly predictable pair gives finite or complex-typed values, a bit-identical copy gives NaN at T <= 1024 and, at T=4096, NaN (star, TypeError caught) or a finite negative value -0.3466 (Geo). Check stage: exactly predictable pairs can also return small negative values (exact-delay construction, delayed_noise T1024).

Score 9 under the rubric clause "within statistical tolerance consistent with estimator variance", anchored on the independent references only (brentq optimum of the from-scratch tilde-I(beta), population covariances, Monte Carlo of Eq. 20): the largest gap, 4.65e-8 (narrowband_f0-0.25|256|pipeline|indep), is 5.6e-4 of the smallest Monte Carlo SD of the Phi* estimator in this family (8.3e-5, iid_gaussian|4096|pipeline|null), and the absolute gap of the run with the largest relative gap (6.4e-4), 9.55e-9 (iid_gaussian|1024|pipeline|indep), is 3.2e-5 of the null SD at that T (2.95e-4). metric_name_standard: integrated information Phi* (mismatched-decoding Phi, Gaussian), normalised by the minimum part entropy (IIT 2.0 style)
canonical_ref: Oizumi M, Amari S, Yanagawa T, Fujii N, Tsuchiya N (2016) 'Measuring integrated information from the decoding perspective', PLoS Comput Biol 12:e1004654: Eq. 9 (Phi* = I - I*), Eq. 8 mismatched decoder q(X_t|X_t-tau) = prod_i p(M_i,t|M_i,t-tau), Eq. 20 I* = max_beta tilde-I(beta), Gaussian case in Methods 'Analytical computation of Phi* under the Gaussian assumption': Eq. 23 (Gaussian I), Eq. 24 (conditional covariance), Eq. 25 (closed form of tilde-I(beta)), Eqs. 26-27 (Q and R), Eq. 28 (block-diagonal covariances), Eqs. 29-33 (d tilde-I/d beta); the same Methods text states that I* is 'a convex function with respect to beta', that d tilde-I/d beta = 0 'is a quadratic equation with respect to beta', and that 'beta can be analytically computed without resorting to numerical optimization' (statements quoted, not re-derived here; equation numbers from a fetch of the article page, whose equations are images, consistent with the vendored code's comment '2nd term of eq. (26)' at phi_star_Gauss.m:87 and utility/I_s_I_s_d.m:2); mismatched decoding: Merhav et al. 1994 IEEE Trans Inf Theory 40:1953 (supplement [54]); PhiToolbox: Kitazono & Oizumi 2020 (supplement [52]). Normalisation (norm-1): Balduzzi & Tononi 2008 PLoS Comput Biol 4:e1000091 (supplement [51]) normalise by N_P = (m-1) min_k H^max(M_k) to select the minimum information partition; Oizumi et al. 2016 PLoS CB Discussion state that for continuous variables this factor 'can be negative because entropy can be negative for continuous variables' and 'we need a different normalization factor when we deal with continuous variables'.
canonical_definition: Phi* = I(X_{t-tau}; X_t) - I*(X_{t-tau}; X_t), I* = max_beta tilde-I(beta), tilde-I(beta) = -sum_y p(y) log sum_x p(x) q(y|x)^beta + sum_{x,y} p(x,y) log q(y|x)^beta with q(y|x) = prod_k p(y_k|x_k) over the parts of the partition; for the bivariate atomic partition the parts are the two channels. Gaussian case: tilde-I(beta) = 1/2 log|Q^-1| + 1/2 log|Sigma_X| + 1/2 tr(Sigma_Y R) - beta N/2, Q^-1 = Sigma_X^-1 + beta A_D' D^-1 A_D, R = beta D^-1 - beta^2 D^-1 A_D Q A_D' D^-1 (A_D, D block-diagonal regression and residual covariance of each part). Property 0 <= Phi* <= I. norm-1: divide by (m-1) min_k H(M_k) (Balduzzi & Tononi 2008 normalisation; m = 2 parts).

For pair (i,j), rows [i,j] form a 2xT array; tau = delay = 1; past window X1 = x[:, 0:T-1], present X2 = x[:, 1:T], each centred by its own mean, covariances with denominator T-2 (Cov_X, Cov_Y, Cov_XY = E[X(t-1)X(t)']); partition [1,2] (each channel its own part; the only bipartition, so no MIP search). I = H(Y) - H(Y|X) from Gaussian log-determinants; I_s(beta) is the closed-form Gaussian tilde-I(beta) of the per-channel mismatched decoder; beta maximised by scipy L-BFGS-B from beta=1 with finite-difference gradient and default tolerances (pgtol 1e-5), unbounded; Phi* = I - I_s(beta_opt) in nats. The closed form was re-derived from scratch in a probe and matches i_s_objective term by term (tr(D^-1 S) = N gives the beta*N/2 constant). norm-1: result divided by (2-1)*min(h(var x_i past), h(var x_j past)), h = 1/2 log(2 pi e var) with var over the first T-1 samples (denominator T-2); on z-scored input the divisor is about 1.4185. Any exception inside bivariate returns NaN (logged).

deviation_from_documented: Supplement keyword 'nonlinear' (and config.yaml label) contradicts the Gaussian/linear implementation and the class label 'linear'. Otherwise the prose matches (undirected; Gaussian model; PhiToolbox algorithm). 'normalized (divided) by entropy' is underspecified: the code divides by the minimum of the two past-window Gaussian differential entropies (can be negative). Beyond the prose: the documented 'proxy ... from the PhiToolbox' is reproduced in Python; the optimiser matches pyspi's vendored MATLAB copy (fminunc, finite differences) but not the published PhiToolbox, which uses minFunc L-BFGS with the analytic gradient of I_s_I_s_d; the native finite-difference L-BFGS-B is therefore a behavioural change relative to the toolbox the supplement cites [52] (size of the effect relative to minFunc not measured).
deviation_from_canonical: Structure matches Oizumi et al. 2016 (Phi* = I - max_beta tilde-I) with plug-in sample covariances. Deviations: (1) the maximisation is approximate: L-BFGS-B stops at the initial beta = 1 whenever |d tilde-I/d beta| < 1e-5, so I* is under-estimated and Phi* over-estimated; the figures in (1) are from the norm-0 probes (norm-1 divides each pair by about 1.4185 under z-scoring, so its absolute gaps are about 1/1.42 of these and its relative gaps are the same): absolute error up to ~5e-8 (max 4.65e-8 on narrowband_f0-0.25 T256 pair (1,2), phi* 3.891, pyspi beta stuck at 1.0 vs reference 0.922; next 3.3e-8 and 2.8e-8, all nit 0; over 136 pairs = 8 datasets x T in {64,256,1024,4096}), relative error up to ~6.4e-4 on near-null pairs (probe iid_gaussian T1024 (2,3): 1.50073e-05 vs independent maximum 1.49977e-05); inherited from pyspi's vendored PhiToolbox copy (fminunc, finite differences), whose Octave run gives 1.50072e-05. (2) beta is unconstrained; the paper (Methods) states that d tilde-I/d beta = 0 is quadratic in beta so beta can be computed analytically, whereas pyspi (like PhiToolbox) optimises numerically; all probe optima were 0.64-1.33. (3) degenerate (singular) covariances: a singular conditional covariance gives finite/complex values via the logdet eigenvalue filter instead of +inf/undefined (exact one-step delay pair); an exactly singular Cov_X (bit-identical copy, T <= 1024) gives NaN with a UserWarning; a numerically ill-conditioned Cov_X (same copy at T=4096) lets a complex logdet reach scipy.optimize.minimize, which raises TypeError -> NaN via the class except. None of these is +inf. (4) normalisation by Gaussian differential entropy of the past marginals follows PhiToolbox, not a published continuous-variable definition; the PLoS CB paper itself warns this factor can be negative. Check-stage correction: (2) the stationarity condition is not quadratic in beta for the atomic bipartition in this parametrisation: d tilde-I/d beta x det(Q^-1)^2 is a quartic (dI x det(Q^-1) is not a polynomial) with exactly one positive root, the optimum (D15 0.86440, D5 0.96505), and tilde-I is concave in beta (scratchpad phi_check/beta_poly.py; pop runs ref_deriv_numerator_poly_degree 4, ref_deriv_decreasing_on_0_6 1). (3) on the exact-delay construction the check runs give small NEGATIVE values (z-scored -0.00110, raw -0.0215 at delayed_noise T1024), not only finite/complex ones.
units_and_range: nats divided by nats (dimensionless); 0 <= Phi* <= I in theory, finite-sample positive bias on independent data; can be negative when a past-window variance < 0.0585 (only without z-scoring); symmetric; NaN when an exception occurs (e.g. constant channel); degenerate pairs never give inf: an exactly predictable pair gives finite or complex-typed values, a bit-identical copy gives NaN at T <= 1024 and, at T=4096, NaN (star, TypeError caught) or a finite negative value -0.3466 (Geo). Check stage: exactly predictable pairs can also return small negative values (exact-delay construction, delayed_noise T1024).

what_changed: Phi* divided by (N_c - 1) min_k H(past_k), the PhiToolbox normalisation (Balduzzi & Tononi 2008 style), which Oizumi et al. 2016 say is unsuitable for continuous variables because the entropy can be negative. Under the default z-scoring the divisor is 1.37-1.43 (near-constant, rank-preserving); without z-scoring it is scale-dependent and negative for variance < 0.0585, giving negative values from an Unsigned SPI. metric_name_standard: integrated information Phi* (mismatched-decoding Phi, Gaussian), normalised by the minimum part entropy (IIT 2.0 style)
canonical_ref: Oizumi M, Amari S, Yanagawa T, Fujii N, Tsuchiya N (2016) 'Measuring integrated information from the decoding perspective', PLoS Comput Biol 12:e1004654: Eq. 9 (Phi* = I - I*), Eq. 8 mismatched decoder q(X_t|X_t-tau) = prod_i p(M_i,t|M_i,t-tau), Eq. 20 I* = max_beta tilde-I(beta), Gaussian case in Methods 'Analytical computation of Phi* under the Gaussian assumption': Eq. 23 (Gaussian I), Eq. 24 (conditional covariance), Eq. 25 (closed form of tilde-I(beta)), Eqs. 26-27 (Q and R), Eq. 28 (block-diagonal covariances), Eqs. 29-33 (d tilde-I/d beta); the same Methods text states that I* is 'a convex function with respect to beta', that d tilde-I/d beta = 0 'is a quadratic equation with respect to beta', and that 'beta can be analytically computed without resorting to numerical optimization' (statements quoted, not re-derived here; equation numbers from a fetch of the article page, whose equations are images, consistent with the vendored code's comment '2nd term of eq. (26)' at phi_star_Gauss.m:87 and utility/I_s_I_s_d.m:2); mismatched decoding: Merhav et al. 1994 IEEE Trans Inf Theory 40:1953 (supplement [54]); PhiToolbox: Kitazono & Oizumi 2020 (supplement [52]). Normalisation (norm-1): Balduzzi & Tononi 2008 PLoS Comput Biol 4:e1000091 (supplement [51]) normalise by N_P = (m-1) min_k H^max(M_k) to select the minimum information partition; Oizumi et al. 2016 PLoS CB Discussion state that for continuous variables this factor 'can be negative because entropy can be negative for continuous variables' and 'we need a different normalization factor when we deal with continuous variables'.
canonical_definition: Phi* = I(X_{t-tau}; X_t) - I*(X_{t-tau}; X_t), I* = max_beta tilde-I(beta), tilde-I(beta) = -sum_y p(y) log sum_x p(x) q(y|x)^beta + sum_{x,y} p(x,y) log q(y|x)^beta with q(y|x) = prod_k p(y_k|x_k) over the parts of the partition; for the bivariate atomic partition the parts are the two channels. Gaussian case: tilde-I(beta) = 1/2 log|Q^-1| + 1/2 log|Sigma_X| + 1/2 tr(Sigma_Y R) - beta N/2, Q^-1 = Sigma_X^-1 + beta A_D' D^-1 A_D, R = beta D^-1 - beta^2 D^-1 A_D Q A_D' D^-1 (A_D, D block-diagonal regression and residual covariance of each part). Property 0 <= Phi* <= I. norm-1: divide by (m-1) min_k H(M_k) (Balduzzi & Tononi 2008 normalisation; m = 2 parts).

implemented_as: Calculator default z-scores each channel (ddof=1). For pair (i,j), rows [i,j] form a 2xT array; tau = delay = 1; past window X1 = x[:, 0:T-1], present X2 = x[:, 1:T], each centred by its own mean, covariances with denominator T-2 (Cov_X, Cov_Y, Cov_XY = E[X(t-1)X(t)']); partition [1,2] (each channel its own part; the only bipartition, so no MIP search). I = H(Y) - H(Y|X) from Gaussian log-determinants; I_s(beta) is the closed-form Gaussian tilde-I(beta) of the per-channel mismatched decoder; beta maximised by scipy L-BFGS-B from beta=1 with finite-difference gradient and default tolerances (pgtol 1e-5), unbounded; Phi* = I - I_s(beta_opt) in nats. The closed form was re-derived from scratch in a probe and matches i_s_objective term by term (tr(D^-1 S) = N gives the beta*N/2 constant). norm-1: result divided by (2-1)*min(h(var x_i past), h(var x_j past)), h = 1/2 log(2 pi e var) with var over the first T-1 samples (denominator T-2); on z-scored input the divisor is about 1.4185. Any exception inside bivariate returns NaN (logged).

deviation_from_documented: Supplement keyword 'nonlinear' (and config.yaml label) contradicts the Gaussian/linear implementation and the class label 'linear'. Otherwise the prose matches (undirected; Gaussian model; PhiToolbox algorithm). 'normalized (divided) by entropy' is underspecified: the code divides by the minimum of the two past-window Gaussian differential entropies (can be negative). Beyond the prose: the documented 'proxy ... from the PhiToolbox' is reproduced in Python; the optimiser matches pyspi's vendored MATLAB copy (fminunc, finite differences) but not the published PhiToolbox, which uses minFunc L-BFGS with the analytic gradient of I_s_I_s_d; the native finite-difference L-BFGS-B is therefore a behavioural change relative to the toolbox the supplement cites [52] (size of the effect relative to minFunc not measured).
deviation_from_canonical: Structure matches Oizumi et al. 2016 (Phi* = I - max_beta tilde-I) with plug-in sample covariances. Deviations: (1) the maximisation is approximate: L-BFGS-B stops at the initial beta = 1 whenever |d tilde-I/d beta| < 1e-5, so I* is under-estimated and Phi* over-estimated; the figures in (1) are from the norm-0 probes (norm-1 divides each pair by about 1.4185 under z-scoring, so its absolute gaps are about 1/1.42 of these and its relative gaps are the same): absolute error up to ~5e-8 (max 4.65e-8 on narrowband_f0-0.25 T256 pair (1,2), phi* 3.891, pyspi beta stuck at 1.0 vs reference 0.922; next 3.3e-8 and 2.8e-8, all nit 0; over 136 pairs = 8 datasets x T in {64,256,1024,4096}), relative error up to ~6.4e-4 on near-null pairs (probe iid_gaussian T1024 (2,3): 1.50073e-05 vs independent maximum 1.49977e-05); inherited from pyspi's vendored PhiToolbox copy (fminunc, finite differences), whose Octave run gives 1.50072e-05. (2) beta is unconstrained; the paper (Methods) states that d tilde-I/d beta = 0 is quadratic in beta so beta can be computed analytically, whereas pyspi (like PhiToolbox) optimises numerically; all probe optima were 0.64-1.33. (3) degenerate (singular) covariances: a singular conditional covariance gives finite/complex values via the logdet eigenvalue filter instead of +inf/undefined (exact one-step delay pair); an exactly singular Cov_X (bit-identical copy, T <= 1024) gives NaN with a UserWarning; a numerically ill-conditioned Cov_X (same copy at T=4096) lets a complex logdet reach scipy.optimize.minimize, which raises TypeError -> NaN via the class except. None of these is +inf. (4) normalisation by Gaussian differential entropy of the past marginals follows PhiToolbox, not a published continuous-variable definition; the PLoS CB paper itself warns this factor can be negative. canonical_definition: Phi* = I(X_{t-tau}; X_t) - I*(X_{t-tau}; X_t), I* = max_beta tilde-I(beta), tilde-I(beta) = -sum_y p(y) log sum_x p(x) q(y|x)^beta + sum_{x,y} p(x,y) log q(y|x)^beta with q(y|x) = prod_k p(y_k|x_k) over the parts of the partition; for the bivariate atomic partition the parts are the two channels. Gaussian case: tilde-I(beta) = 1/2 log|Q^-1| + 1/2 log|Sigma_X| + 1/2 tr(Sigma_Y R) - beta N/2, Q^-1 = Sigma_X^-1 + beta A_D' D^-1 A_D, R = beta D^-1 - beta^2 D^-1 A_D Q A_D' D^-1 (A_D, D block-diagonal regression and residual covariance of each part). Property 0 <= Phi* <= I. norm-1: divide by (m-1) min_k H(M_k) (Balduzzi & Tononi 2008 normalisation; m = 2 parts).

For pair (i,j), rows [i,j] form a 2xT array; tau = delay = 1; past window X1 = x[:, 0:T-1], present X2 = x[:, 1:T], each centred by its own mean, covariances with denominator T-2 (Cov_X, Cov_Y, Cov_XY = E[X(t-1)X(t)']); partition [1,2] (each channel its own part; the only bipartition, so no MIP search). I = H(Y) - H(Y|X) from Gaussian log-determinants; I_s(beta) is the closed-form Gaussian tilde-I(beta) of the per-channel mismatched decoder; beta maximised by scipy L-BFGS-B from beta=1 with finite-difference gradient and default tolerances (pgtol 1e-5), unbounded; Phi* = I - I_s(beta_opt) in nats. The closed form was re-derived from scratch in a probe and matches i_s_objective term by term (tr(D^-1 S) = N gives the beta*N/2 constant). norm-1: result divided by (2-1)*min(h(var x_i past), h(var x_j past)), h = 1/2 log(2 pi e var) with var over the first T-1 samples (denominator T-2); on z-scored input the divisor is about 1.4185. Any exception inside bivariate returns NaN (logged).

deviation_from_canonical: Structure matches Oizumi et al. 2016 (Phi* = I - max_beta tilde-I) with plug-in sample covariances. (2) beta is unconstrained; the paper (Methods) states that d tilde-I/d beta = 0 is quadratic in beta so beta can be computed analytically, whereas pyspi (like PhiToolbox) optimises numerically; all probe optima were 0.64-1.33. metric_name_standard: geometric integrated information Phi_G (Gaussian AR(1) model), unnormalised, nats
canonical_ref: Oizumi M, Tsuchiya N, Amari S (2016) 'Unified framework for information integration based on information geometry', PNAS 113:14817 (supplement [55]); arXiv:1510.04455 v1: Eq. 8 constraint q(Y[P_i]|X) = q(Y[P_i]|X[P_i]), Eq. 9 Phi_G = min_{q in M_G} D_KL(p||q), Gaussian AR model Eqs. 15-17 (A'_ij = 0, i != j), stationarity Eqs. 18-20, Phi_G = 1/2 log |Sigma(E)'|/|Sigma(E)| Eq. 21, 0 <= Phi_G <= I(X;Y) (Discussion); augmented-Lagrangian solver from PhiToolbox (Kitazono & Oizumi, supplement [52]).
canonical_definition: Phi_G = min over disconnected models Y = A'X + E' with A' block-diagonal w.r.t. the partition (and q(X) = p(X)) of D_KL(p(X,Y)||q(X,Y)) = min_{A' blockdiag} 1/2 log |Sigma_E + (A-A') Sigma_X (A-A')'| / |Sigma_E|, A = Sigma_YX Sigma_X^-1, Sigma_E = Sigma_Y - Sigma_YX Sigma_X^-1 Sigma_XY; global minimum over A' (Eq. 9 is a min). Bounds 0 <= Phi_G <= I(X;Y) and Phi_G <= SI(X;Y).
documented_definition: supplement §1.4.10, p.12 (supplement.txt lines 550-562; keywords line 551 'undirected, nonlinear, unsigned, bivariate, time-dependent'): 'We implement two proxy measures for IIT 2.0 [51] from the PhiToolbox [52]'; 'Phi_G is a measure of integrated information derived from information geometry [55]. It is an undirected measure that quantifies the divergence between the actual probability distribution of a system and an approximated probability distribution where influences among elements are statistically disconnected. Here we implement the Gaussian-distribution model [53].' 'Both measures are optionally normalized (divided) by entropy (denoted by the modifier norm)' (supplement §1.4.10, p.12, line 564). GitBook information-theory.md lines 111-133 repeat the same text. Identifier phi_Geo_t-1_norm-0.

For pair (i,j), rows [i,j] form a 2xT array; tau = delay = 1; past window X1 = x[:, 0:T-1], present X2 = x[:, 1:T], each centred by its own mean, covariances with denominator T-2 (Cov_X, Cov_Y, Cov_XY = E[X(t-1)X(t)']); partition [1,2] (each channel its own part; the only bipartition, so no MIP search). VAR(1) parameters A = Cov_YX Cov_X^-1, Sigma_E = Cov_Y - Cov_YX Cov_X^-1 Cov_XY; Phi_G = 1/2 log|Sigma_E'|/|Sigma_E| with Sigma_E' = Sigma_E + (A-A_p) Cov_X (A-A_p)' minimised over diagonal A_p by an augmented Lagrangian (mu=2, alpha=0.9, gamma=1.01) that stops when the per-iteration change of logdet(Sigma_E') is below 1e-10 (maxiter 1e5); eigenvalues of Sigma_E' clamped at 1e-12. Any exception inside bivariate returns NaN (logged).

metric_name_standard: geometric integrated information Phi_G (Gaussian AR(1) model), normalised by the minimum part entropy (IIT 2.0 style)
canonical_ref: Oizumi M, Tsuchiya N, Amari S (2016) 'Unified framework for information integration based on information geometry', PNAS 113:14817 (supplement [55]); arXiv:1510.04455 v1: Eq. 8 constraint q(Y[P_i]|X) = q(Y[P_i]|X[P_i]), Eq. 9 Phi_G = min_{q in M_G} D_KL(p||q), Gaussian AR model Eqs. 15-17 (A'_ij = 0, i != j), stationarity Eqs. 18-20, Phi_G = 1/2 log |Sigma(E)'|/|Sigma(E)| Eq. 21, 0 <= Phi_G <= I(X;Y) (Discussion); augmented-Lagrangian solver from PhiToolbox (Kitazono & Oizumi, supplement [52]). Normalisation (norm-1): Balduzzi & Tononi 2008 PLoS Comput Biol 4:e1000091 (supplement [51]) normalise by N_P = (m-1) min_k H^max(M_k) to select the minimum information partition; Oizumi et al. 2016 PLoS CB Discussion state that for continuous variables this factor 'can be negative because entropy can be negative for continuous variables' and 'we need a different normalization factor when we deal with continuous variables'.
canonical_definition: Phi_G = min over disconnected models Y = A'X + E' with A' block-diagonal w.r.t. the partition (and q(X) = p(X)) of D_KL(p(X,Y)||q(X,Y)) = min_{A' blockdiag} 1/2 log |Sigma_E + (A-A') Sigma_X (A-A')'| / |Sigma_E|, A = Sigma_YX Sigma_X^-1, Sigma_E = Sigma_Y - Sigma_YX Sigma_X^-1 Sigma_XY; global minimum over A' (Eq. 9 is a min). Bounds 0 <= Phi_G <= I(X;Y) and Phi_G <= SI(X;Y). norm-1: divide by (m-1) min_k H(M_k) (Balduzzi & Tononi 2008 normalisation; m = 2 parts).

It is an undirected measure that quantifies the divergence between the actual probability distribution of a system and an approximated probability distribution where influences among elements are statistically disconnected. Here we implement the Gaussian-distribution model [53].' 'Both measures are optionally normalized (divided) by entropy (denoted by the modifier norm)' (supplement §1.4.10, p.12, line 564). implemented_as: Calculator default z-scores each channel (ddof=1). For pair (i,j), rows [i,j] form a 2xT array; tau = delay = 1; past window X1 = x[:, 0:T-1], present X2 = x[:, 1:T], each centred by its own mean, covariances with denominator T-2 (Cov_X, Cov_Y, Cov_XY = E[X(t-1)X(t)']); partition [1,2] (each channel its own part; the only bipartition, so no MIP search). VAR(1) parameters A = Cov_YX Cov_X^-1, Sigma_E = Cov_Y - Cov_YX Cov_X^-1 Cov_XY; Phi_G = 1/2 log|Sigma_E'|/|Sigma_E| with Sigma_E' = Sigma_E + (A-A_p) Cov_X (A-A_p)' minimised over diagonal A_p by an augmented Lagrangian (mu=2, alpha=0.9, gamma=1.01) that stops when the per-iteration change of logdet(Sigma_E') is below 1e-10 (maxiter 1e5); eigenvalues of Sigma_E' clamped at 1e-12. norm-1: result divided by (2-1)*min(h(var x_i past), h(var x_j past)), h = 1/2 log(2 pi e var) with var over the first T-1 samples (denominator T-2); on z-scored input the divisor is about 1.4185. Any exception inside bivariate returns NaN (logged).

deviation_from_documented: Supplement keyword 'nonlinear' (and config.yaml label) contradicts the Gaussian/linear implementation and the class label 'linear'. Otherwise the prose matches (undirected; Gaussian model; PhiToolbox algorithm). 'normalized (divided) by entropy' is underspecified: the code divides by the minimum of the two past-window Gaussian differential entropies (can be negative). Beyond the prose: same AL algorithm as PhiToolbox plus an eigenvalue clamp (phi_native.py:303) absent in phi_G_Gauss_AL.m.
deviation_from_canonical: Model matches the PNAS Gaussian formulation (constraint on A', Eq. 17; Phi_G from Eq. 21). Deviations: (1) the AL stopping rule tests only the change of the objective, so the iterate can stop at a non-stationary point in flat directions: probe delayed_noise T64 pair (0,1) returned 2.3439385 while direct minimisation reaches 2.3406849 (gap 3.25e-3, 0.14%; Eq. 19 residual 8.2e-3; mu had grown to 1.35e6 after 2681 iterations); Octave running pyspi's vendored PhiToolbox copy (phi_G files identical to upstream) returns the same 2.34393854875, so this is inherited from PhiToolbox. Other probe cases agree with the global minimum to <= 1e-8 except delayed_noise T1024 (0,1) gap 2.0e-5 and narrowband T64 (0,2) gap 4.0e-6. (2) the eigenvalue clamp at 1e-12 alters results only for near-singular Sigma_E'. (3) degenerate covariances: a singular conditional covariance gives finite values via the logdet fallback instead of +inf (exact one-step delay pair); an exactly singular Cov_X (bit-identical copy, T <= 1024) gives NaN with a UserWarning (solve raises LinAlgError, phi_native.py:374-378); a numerically ill-conditioned Cov_X (same copy at T=4096) gives a finite negative value -0.3466 with LinAlgWarning, violating Phi_G >= 0. (4) normalisation by Gaussian differential entropy of the past marginals follows PhiToolbox, not a published continuous-variable definition; the PLoS CB paper itself warns this factor can be negative. Check-stage correction: the trace statement that other cases agree with the global minimum to ~1e-8 does not hold at T = 4096 on weakly coupled pairs, where the AL stops before the constraint is met and UNDER-estimates Phi_G (cointegrated -3.46e-4, relative ~1.0; bivariate_gaussian -4.6e-6; iid_gaussian -2.7e-6; off-diagonal |A_p| up to 9.8e-4), and the non-optimal stop reaches 1.107 nats on shared_envelope (0,1) at T64; both reproduced by Octave on PhiToolbox. On the exact-delay construction the check runs give small NEGATIVE values (z-scored -0.00062, raw -0.0200 at delayed_noise T1024).
units_and_range: nats divided by nats (dimensionless); 0 <= Phi_G <= min(I, SI) in theory, positive finite-sample bias; can be negative when a past-window variance < 0.0585 (only without z-scoring); symmetric; NaN when an exception occurs (e.g. constant channel); degenerate pairs never give inf: an exactly predictable pair gives finite or complex-typed values, a bit-identical copy gives NaN at T <= 1024 and, at T=4096, NaN (star, TypeError caught) or a finite negative value -0.3466 (Geo). metric_name_standard: geometric integrated information Phi_G (Gaussian AR(1) model), normalised by the minimum part entropy (IIT 2.0 style)
canonical_ref: Oizumi M, Tsuchiya N, Amari S (2016) 'Unified framework for information integration based on information geometry', PNAS 113:14817 (supplement [55]); arXiv:1510.04455 v1: Eq. 8 constraint q(Y[P_i]|X) = q(Y[P_i]|X[P_i]), Eq. 9 Phi_G = min_{q in M_G} D_KL(p||q), Gaussian AR model Eqs. 15-17 (A'_ij = 0, i != j), stationarity Eqs. 18-20, Phi_G = 1/2 log |Sigma(E)'|/|Sigma(E)| Eq. 21, 0 <= Phi_G <= I(X;Y) (Discussion); augmented-Lagrangian solver from PhiToolbox (Kitazono & Oizumi, supplement [52]). Normalisation (norm-1): Balduzzi & Tononi 2008 PLoS Comput Biol 4:e1000091 (supplement [51]) normalise by N_P = (m-1) min_k H^max(M_k) to select the minimum information partition; Oizumi et al. 2016 PLoS CB Discussion state that for continuous variables this factor 'can be negative because entropy can be negative for continuous variables' and 'we need a different normalization factor when we deal with continuous variables'.
canonical_definition: Phi_G = min over disconnected models Y = A'X + E' with A' block-diagonal w.r.t. the partition (and q(X) = p(X)) of D_KL(p(X,Y)||q(X,Y)) = min_{A' blockdiag} 1/2 log |Sigma_E + (A-A') Sigma_X (A-A')'| / |Sigma_E|, A = Sigma_YX Sigma_X^-1, Sigma_E = Sigma_Y - Sigma_YX Sigma_X^-1 Sigma_XY; global minimum over A' (Eq. 9 is a min). Bounds 0 <= Phi_G <= I(X;Y) and Phi_G <= SI(X;Y). norm-1: divide by (m-1) min_k H(M_k) (Balduzzi & Tononi 2008 normalisation; m = 2 parts).

It is an undirected measure that quantifies the divergence between the actual probability distribution of a system and an approximated probability distribution where influences among elements are statistically disconnected. Here we implement the Gaussian-distribution model [53].' 'Both measures are optionally normalized (divided) by entropy (denoted by the modifier norm)' (supplement §1.4.10, p.12, line 564). For pair (i,j), rows [i,j] form a 2xT array; tau = delay = 1; past window X1 = x[:, 0:T-1], present X2 = x[:, 1:T], each centred by its own mean, covariances with denominator T-2 (Cov_X, Cov_Y, Cov_XY = E[X(t-1)X(t)']); partition [1,2] (each channel its own part; the only bipartition, so no MIP search). VAR(1) parameters A = Cov_YX Cov_X^-1, Sigma_E = Cov_Y - Cov_YX Cov_X^-1 Cov_XY; Phi_G = 1/2 log|Sigma_E'|/|Sigma_E| with Sigma_E' = Sigma_E + (A-A_p) Cov_X (A-A_p)' minimised over diagonal A_p by an augmented Lagrangian (mu=2, alpha=0.9, gamma=1.01) that stops when the per-iteration change of logdet(Sigma_E') is below 1e-10 (maxiter 1e5); eigenvalues of Sigma_E' clamped at 1e-12. norm-1: result divided by (2-1)*min(h(var x_i past), h(var x_j past)), h = 1/2 log(2 pi e var) with var over the first T-1 samples (denominator T-2); on z-scored input the divisor is about 1.4185. Any exception inside bivariate returns NaN (logged).

deviation_from_canonical: Model matches the PNAS Gaussian formulation (constraint on A', Eq. 17; Phi_G from Eq. 21). Deviations: (1) the AL stopping rule tests only the change of the objective, so the iterate can stop at a non-stationary point in flat directions: probe delayed_noise T64 pair (0,1) returned 2.3439385 while direct minimisation reaches 2.3406849 (gap 3.25e-3, 0.14%; Eq. 19 residual 8.2e-3; mu had grown to 1.35e6 after 2681 iterations); Octave running pyspi's vendored PhiToolbox copy (phi_G files identical to upstream) returns the same 2.34393854875, so this is inherited from PhiToolbox. (2) the eigenvalue clamp at 1e-12 alters results only for near-singular Sigma_E'. (3) degenerate covariances: a singular conditional covariance gives finite values via the logdet fallback instead of +inf (exact one-step delay pair); an exactly singular Cov_X (bit-identical copy, T <= 1024) gives NaN with a UserWarning (solve raises LinAlgError, phi_native.py:374-378); a numerically ill-conditioned Cov_X (same copy at T=4096) gives a finite negative value -0.3466 with LinAlgWarning, violating Phi_G >= 0. metric_name_standard: band arithmetic mean / band max of the principal-value multitaper coherence phase (cross-spectral phase) arg C_ij(f) in (-pi, pi]
canonical_ref: Cross-spectral phase phi_xy(f) = arg S_xy(f): Priestley 1981, Spectral Analysis and Time Series, ch. 9 (phase spectrum); Carter 1987, Proc. IEEE 75(2):236-255 (phase and time-delay); Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front. Syst. Neurosci. 9:175 (supplement [59], coherency phase; quotations checked in the spectral.cohmag record). Averaging angles: circular mean direction, Mardia & Jupp 2000, Directional Statistics, §2.2. The Priestley chapter, the Carter 1987 sections and the Mardia & Jupp section number are from memory, not re-checked.
canonical_definition: phi_ij(f) = arg C_ij(f) = arg S_ij(f) with S_ij = E[X_i(f) conj(X_j(f))]; for x_i(t) = x_j(t - tau) (i lags j) phi_ij(f) = -2 pi f tau (mod 2 pi); antisymmetric phi_ji = -phi_ij (mod 2 pi). A band summary of an angle is canonically the circular mean arg(sum_f e^{i phi(f)}) (or arg of the band-averaged coherency); a time delay is the slope of the unwrapped phase (group delay).
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.2, p.13 (supplement.txt:616-628): "By omitting the magnitude operator of the coherence (Sec. 1.5.1), we obtain the complex-valued coherency, where the phase-difference angle (which we refer to as the coherence phase) has been used to infer a time-delayed dependence between two signals [59]. We compute the coherence phase for the two summary statistics and three frequency ranges". Keywords "undirected, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent". Same text GitBook spectral.md:49-70. implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1; optional linear detrend first; Data defaults). The whole (P, T) record is one window: spectral_connectivity 1.1.2 Multitaper with defaults NW=3, n_tapers=floor(2*NW-1)=5, low-bias filter (DPSS concentration > 0.9; all 5 kept for T >= 8 in the probe), per-window constant (mean) detrend, tapers scaled by sqrt(fs), scipy.fftpack.fft with n_fft = next_fast_len(T) (zero padding when T is not 5-smooth, e.g. T=67 -> 72), divided by fs. Connectivity expectation "trials_tapers" = unweighted mean over the 5 tapers: S_ij(f) = (1/K) sum_k X_ik(f) conj(X_jk(f)). Coherency C_ij = S_ij / sqrt(S_ii S_jj). Only the first (n_fft+1)//2 FFT bins are kept: DC included, Nyquist dropped for even n_fft (T=256: 128 bins k/256, k=0..127). pyspi selects bins with fmin <= f <= fmax (closed at both ends) and applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over that axis, then sets the diagonal to NaN; no Undirected mirroring. The cached spectral result (keyed by (measure,)) is shared by all six band/statistic identifiers of the unit. Measure: numpy.angle(C_ij(f)), principal value in [-pi, pi] (+pi for a negative real value with +0 imaginary part). At DC the cross-spectrum of real input is exactly real (probe max|Im C(DC)| = 0.0), so the DC angle is exactly 0 or pi. Band summary is the ARITHMETIC np.nanmean or np.nanmax of these principal angles. Probe: equals the from-scratch reference to <= 2.0e-12.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labels: documented and labelled "undirected, unsigned", but the value is a signed relative phase whose sign encodes lead/lag; the matrix is (nearly) antisymmetric for mean and asymmetric for max, and it is not mirrored (REVIEW M4, M1). (2) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented FFT grid with DC included (angle exactly 0 or pi there) and Nyquist excluded for even n_fft; low/high bands share the 0.25 bin. (3) The documentation does not say how phases are summarised over a band; the code uses an arithmetic mean / max of wrapped angles.
deviation_from_canonical: Per bin the angle is the standard cross-spectral phase. The band summary is an arithmetic mean of principal angles, not a circular mean (REVIEW M4): where phase wraps across +-pi the result is not an angle estimate (probe delayed_noise T=1024 pair (3,0), delay 5: arithmetic mean -0.3202 vs circular mean -1.5609; var2_bivariate T=4096 high band 1.1765 vs population arithmetic mean of arg C 2.4658). DC bins with negative real cross-spectrum add pi in both directions, giving A[i,j] + A[j,i] = pi * (number of bins at exactly pi, counted over ij and ji) / n_bins (probe iid_gaussian T=64 low band: 0.369599 = 2 pi / 17 for two pairs, 0 for the others) (M4). The max statistic of a wrapped angle saturates near pi for broadband pairs (probe iid_gaussian T=256: all entries in [2.960, 3.142], A + A^T up to 6.283), so it carries little pair-specific information.
units_and_range: Radians, signed, in [-pi, pi]. Mean: antisymmetric up to the DC/branch offset above; max: asymmetric (A[j,i] = -min_f phi_ij). Exactly 0 for identical series (shared_envelope x0 == x2: mean 0.0, max 0.0). NaN on the diagonal; empty band -> all-NaN (mean) or ValueError (max).
direction_convention: A[i,j] = band statistic of arg S_ij(f), S_ij = mean_k X_i,k conj(X_j,k) (connectivity.py:205-207, 1187-1190, 1485-1487). Positive (unwrapped, small-lag) A[i,j] means channel i LEADS channel j. metric_name_standard: band arithmetic mean / band max of the principal-value multitaper coherence phase (cross-spectral phase) arg C_ij(f) in (-pi, pi]
canonical_ref: Cross-spectral phase phi_xy(f) = arg S_xy(f): Priestley 1981, Spectral Analysis and Time Series, ch. 9 (phase spectrum); Carter 1987, Proc. IEEE 75(2):236-255 (phase and time-delay); Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front. Syst. Neurosci. 9:175 (supplement [59], coherency phase; quotations checked in the spectral.cohmag record). Averaging angles: circular mean direction, Mardia & Jupp 2000, Directional Statistics, §2.2. The Priestley chapter, the Carter 1987 sections and the Mardia & Jupp section number are from memory, not re-checked.
canonical_definition: phi_ij(f) = arg C_ij(f) = arg S_ij(f) with S_ij = E[X_i(f) conj(X_j(f))]; for x_i(t) = x_j(t - tau) (i lags j) phi_ij(f) = -2 pi f tau (mod 2 pi); antisymmetric phi_ji = -phi_ij (mod 2 pi). A band summary of an angle is canonically the circular mean arg(sum_f e^{i phi(f)}) (or arg of the band-averaged coherency); a time delay is the slope of the unwrapped phase (group delay).

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1; optional linear detrend first; Data defaults). The whole (P, T) record is one window: spectral_connectivity 1.1.2 Multitaper with defaults NW=3, n_tapers=floor(2*NW-1)=5, low-bias filter (DPSS concentration > 0.9; all 5 kept for T >= 8 in the probe), per-window constant (mean) detrend, tapers scaled by sqrt(fs), scipy.fftpack.fft with n_fft = next_fast_len(T) (zero padding when T is not 5-smooth, e.g. T=67 -> 72), divided by fs. Connectivity expectation "trials_tapers" = unweighted mean over the 5 tapers: S_ij(f) = (1/K) sum_k X_ik(f) conj(X_jk(f)). Coherency C_ij = S_ij / sqrt(S_ii S_jj). Only the first (n_fft+1)//2 FFT bins are kept: DC included, Nyquist dropped for even n_fft (T=256: 128 bins k/256, k=0..127). pyspi selects bins with fmin <= f <= fmax (closed at both ends) and applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over that axis, then sets the diagonal to NaN; no Undirected mirroring. The cached spectral result (keyed by (measure,)) is shared by all six band/statistic identifiers of the unit. Measure: numpy.angle(C_ij(f)), principal value in [-pi, pi] (+pi for a negative real value with +0 imaginary part). At DC the cross-spectrum of real input is exactly real (probe max|Im C(DC)| = 0.0), so the DC angle is exactly 0 or pi. Band summary is the ARITHMETIC np.nanmean or np.nanmax of these principal angles. Probe: equals the from-scratch reference to <= 2.0e-12.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labels: documented and labelled "undirected, unsigned", but the value is a signed relative phase whose sign encodes lead/lag; the matrix is (nearly) antisymmetric for mean and asymmetric for max, and it is not mirrored (REVIEW M4, M1). (2) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented FFT grid with DC included (angle exactly 0 or pi there) and Nyquist excluded for even n_fft; low/high bands share the 0.25 bin. (3) The documentation does not say how phases are summarised over a band; the code uses an arithmetic mean / max of wrapped angles.
deviation_from_canonical: Per bin the angle is the standard cross-spectral phase. The band summary is an arithmetic mean of principal angles, not a circular mean (REVIEW M4): where phase wraps across +-pi the result is not an angle estimate (probe delayed_noise T=1024 pair (3,0), delay 5: arithmetic mean -0.3202 vs circular mean -1.5609; var2_bivariate T=4096 high band 1.1765 vs population arithmetic mean of arg C 2.4658). DC bins with negative real cross-spectrum add pi in both directions, giving A[i,j] + A[j,i] = pi * (number of bins at exactly pi, counted over ij and ji) / n_bins (probe iid_gaussian T=64 low band: 0.369599 = 2 pi / 17 for two pairs, 0 for the others) (M4). The max statistic of a wrapped angle saturates near pi for broadband pairs (probe iid_gaussian T=256: all entries in [2.960, 3.142], A + A^T up to 6.283), so it carries little pair-specific information.
units_and_range: Radians, signed, in [-pi, pi]. Mean: antisymmetric up to the DC/branch offset above; max: asymmetric (A[j,i] = -min_f phi_ij). Exactly 0 for identical series (shared_envelope x0 == x2: mean 0.0, max 0.0). NaN on the diagonal; empty band -> all-NaN (mean) or ValueError (max).
direction_convention: A[i,j] = band statistic of arg S_ij(f), S_ij = mean_k X_i,k conj(X_j,k) (connectivity.py:205-207, 1187-1190, 1485-1487). Positive (unwrapped, small-lag) A[i,j] means channel i LEADS channel j. Probe: delayed_noise T=1024 (x1 = x0 delayed 1 sample) low band A[0,1] = +0.7768, A[1,0] = -0.7768 (analytic mean of -2 pi f over the bins -0.7854 for [1,0]); narrowband_f0-0.1 T=1024 band [0.095, 0.105]: A[1,0] = +0.8044 (x1 phase +pi/4 leads x0), A[0,2] = +1.5609 (x0 leads x2 by pi/2).

The band summary is an arithmetic nanmean / nanmax of principal angles in (-pi, pi] (REVIEW M4), not a circular mean or the phase of the band-averaged coherency: wherever the phase crosses the branch cut inside the band the mean is not an angle estimate (delayed_noise lag 5: -0.320 vs circular -1.565; var2 high band 1.18 vs 2.47 and the error does not shrink with T), and the max statistic of wrapped angles saturates at pi for broadband pairs (null 3.14 at T=4096, |A + A.T| up to 2 pi).
