metric_name_standard: band arithmetic mean / band max of the principal-value multitaper coherence phase (cross-spectral phase) arg C_ij(f) in (-pi, pi]
canonical_ref: Cross-spectral phase phi_xy(f) = arg S_xy(f): Priestley 1981, Spectral Analysis and Time Series, ch. 9 (phase spectrum); Carter 1987, Proc. IEEE 75(2):236-255 (phase and time-delay); Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front. Syst. Neurosci. 9:175 (supplement [59], coherency phase; quotations checked in the spectral.cohmag record). Averaging angles: circular mean direction, Mardia & Jupp 2000, Directional Statistics, §2.2. The Priestley chapter, the Carter 1987 sections and the Mardia & Jupp section number are from memory, not re-checked.
canonical_definition: phi_ij(f) = arg C_ij(f) = arg S_ij(f) with S_ij = E[X_i(f) conj(X_j(f))]; for x_i(t) = x_j(t - tau) (i lags j) phi_ij(f) = -2 pi f tau (mod 2 pi); antisymmetric phi_ji = -phi_ij (mod 2 pi). A band summary of an angle is canonically the circular mean arg(sum_f e^{i phi(f)}) (or arg of the band-averaged coherency); a time delay is the slope of the unwrapped phase (group delay).
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.2, p.13 (supplement.txt:616-628): "By omitting the magnitude operator of the coherence (Sec. 1.5.1), we obtain the complex-valued coherency, where the phase-difference angle (which we refer to as the coherence phase) has been used to infer a time-delayed dependence between two signals [59]. We compute the coherence phase for the two summary statistics and three frequency ranges". Keywords "undirected, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent". Same text GitBook spectral.md:49-70. Common section: supplement §1.5, p.12 (heading at supplement.txt:570): "Each measure is based on the cross- and power-spectral densities at a given frequency and sampling rate, which is estimated via the multitaper technique ... we assume a sampling frequency fs = 1 throughout ... delegate_lib: spectral-connectivity==1.1.2 Connectivity.coherence_phase (connectivity.py:315-324) = numpy.angle(coherency()); spectra from Multitaper.fft (scipy.fftpack.fft); band selection and nanmean/nanmax in pyspi (numpy 2.5.4)
implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1; optional linear detrend first; Data defaults). The whole (P, T) record is one window: spectral_connectivity 1.1.2 Multitaper with defaults NW=3, n_tapers=floor(2*NW-1)=5, low-bias filter (DPSS concentration > 0.9; all 5 kept for T >= 8 in the probe), per-window constant (mean) detrend, tapers scaled by sqrt(fs), scipy.fftpack.fft with n_fft = next_fast_len(T) (zero padding when T is not 5-smooth, e.g. T=67 -> 72), divided by fs. Connectivity expectation "trials_tapers" = unweighted mean over the 5 tapers: S_ij(f) = (1/K) sum_k X_ik(f) conj(X_jk(f)). Coherency C_ij = S_ij / sqrt(S_ii S_jj). Only the first (n_fft+1)//2 FFT bins are kept: DC included, Nyquist dropped for even n_fft (T=256: 128 bins k/256, k=0..127). pyspi selects bins with fmin <= f <= fmax (closed at both ends) and applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over that axis, then sets the diagonal to NaN; no Undirected mirroring. The cached spectral result (keyed by (measure,)) is shared by all six band/statistic identifiers of the unit. Measure: numpy.angle(C_ij(f)), principal value in [-pi, pi] (+pi for a negative real value with +0 imaginary part). At DC the cross-spectrum of real input is exactly real (probe max|Im C(DC)| = 0.0), so the DC angle is exactly 0 or pi. Band summary is the ARITHMETIC np.nanmean or np.nanmax of these principal angles. Probe: equals the from-scratch reference to <= 2.0e-12.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labels: documented and labelled "undirected, unsigned", but the value is a signed relative phase whose sign encodes lead/lag; the matrix is (nearly) antisymmetric for mean and asymmetric for max, and it is not mirrored (REVIEW M4, M1). (2) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented FFT grid with DC included (angle exactly 0 or pi there) and Nyquist excluded for even n_fft; low/high bands share the 0.25 bin. (3) The documentation does not say how phases are summarised over a band; the code uses an arithmetic mean / max of wrapped angles.
deviation_from_canonical: Per bin the angle is the standard cross-spectral phase. The band summary is an arithmetic mean of principal angles, not a circular mean (REVIEW M4): where phase wraps across +-pi the result is not an angle estimate (probe delayed_noise T=1024 pair (3,0), delay 5: arithmetic mean -0.3202 vs circular mean -1.5609; var2_bivariate T=4096 high band 1.1765 vs population arithmetic mean of arg C 2.4658). DC bins with negative real cross-spectrum add pi in both directions, giving A[i,j] + A[j,i] = pi * (number of bins at exactly pi, counted over ij and ji) / n_bins (probe iid_gaussian T=64 low band: 0.369599 = 2 pi / 17 for two pairs, 0 for the others) (M4). The max statistic of a wrapped angle saturates near pi for broadband pairs (probe iid_gaussian T=256: all entries in [2.960, 3.142], A + A^T up to 6.283), so it carries little pair-specific information.
units_and_range: Radians, signed, in [-pi, pi]. Mean: antisymmetric up to the DC/branch offset above; max: asymmetric (A[j,i] = -min_f phi_ij). Exactly 0 for identical series (shared_envelope x0 == x2: mean 0.0, max 0.0). NaN on the diagonal; empty band -> all-NaN (mean) or ValueError (max).
direction_convention: A[i,j] = band statistic of arg S_ij(f), S_ij = mean_k X_i,k conj(X_j,k) (connectivity.py:205-207, 1187-1190, 1485-1487). Positive (unwrapped, small-lag) A[i,j] means channel i LEADS channel j. Probe: delayed_noise T=1024 (x1 = x0 delayed 1 sample) low band A[0,1] = +0.7768, A[1,0] = -0.7768 (analytic mean of -2 pi f over the bins -0.7854 for [1,0]); narrowband_f0-0.1 T=1024 band [0.095, 0.105]: A[1,0] = +0.8044 (x1 phase +pi/4 leads x0), A[0,2] = +1.5609 (x0 leads x2 by pi/2).

metric_name_standard: band mean / band max of the multitaper magnitude-squared coherence (MSC) |C_xy(f)|^2 (fixed NW=3, K=5 tapers, single window)
canonical_ref: Carter 1987, Proc. IEEE 75(2):236-255 "Coherence and time delay estimation" (MSC definition gamma^2 = |S_xy|^2/(S_xx S_yy) and estimator bias/variance); Thomson 1982, Proc. IEEE 70(9):1055-1096, section III Eigenestimates pp.1060-1061 (unit-weight average of the first K eigenspectra, eq. 3.7-3.8), section V Adaptive Weighting p.1065 (not used here), section XIV Estimation of Coherence and Polyspectra p.1087 (locations as checked in the spectral.multitaper_csm record); Percival & Walden 1993, Spectral Analysis for Physical Applications, ch. 7 Multitaper Spectral Estimation, pp.331-377 (chapter title and pages from the authors' table of contents, as in spectral.multitaper_csm; section contents not checked); Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front. Syst. Neurosci. 9:175 (supplement ref [59]; quotations below checked against the paper). Carter 1987 equation/section numbers and the bias formula are from memory, not re-checked against the paper.
canonical_definition: gamma^2_xy(f) = |S_xy(f)|^2 / (S_xx(f) S_yy(f)) in [0, 1]; multitaper estimate S_hat_xy(f) = (1/K) sum_k X_k(f) conj(Y_k(f)) with K DPSS tapers. Bastos & Schoffelen 2016 (supplement [59]) define the "coherence coefficient" as the unsquared normalised magnitude |C| ("a normalized quantity bounded by 0 and 1"; numerator "the length of the vector average of the individual trial cross-spectral densities", denominator "the square root of the product of the average of the individual trial power estimates"), say "Mathematically, the coherence is the frequency domain equivalent to the time domain cross-correlation function" (not squared), and refer to the square only as "Its squared value" / "the squared coherence coefficient"; the phrase "coherence magnitude" does not occur in that paper (the supplement attributes it to [60], Schlögl & Supp 2006, not opened). The squared form is MSC. For independent Gaussian white series with K effectively independent tapers MSC_hat ~ Beta(1, K-1), mean 1/K; Carter 1987 gives bias approx (1 - gamma^2)^2 / K. Band summary (mean/max over frequency) is a pyspi construction.
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.1, p.13 (supplement.txt:601-614): "The coherence (also known as coherence magnitude and ordinary coherence [60] or coherence coefficient [59]) is an undirected frequency-dependent measure of linear association between time series x and y. Mathematically, it is the frequency domain equivalent of the squared time-domain cross correlation [59]. We compute mean (denoted by mean) and maximum (max) summary statistics of the coherence for the three frequency ranges". Same text GitBook spectral.md:24-45 (keywords undirected, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent). Common section: supplement §1.5, p.12 (heading at supplement.txt:570): "Each measure is based on the cross- and power-spectral densities at a given frequency and sampling rate, which is estimated via the multitaper technique ... we assume a sampling frequency fs = 1 throughout ... We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f ∈ [f0, fs/2], where fs/2 is the Nyquist frequency and f0 = 4/T ... we take the mean (mean) and the maximum (max) values of each measure over three ranges ... fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f ∈ [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f ∈ [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f ∈ [fs/4, fs/2]" (supplement.txt:570-599; same text GitBook spectral.md:14-20). The briefing pack line ranges (582-613, 614-628, 629-642, 684-700) are offset by 12-14 lines from the headings in this copy of supplement.txt; the line numbers cited here are the ones opened.

The whole (P, T) record is one window: spectral_connectivity 1.1.2 Multitaper with defaults NW=3, n_tapers=floor(2*NW-1)=5, low-bias filter (DPSS concentration > 0.9; all 5 kept for T >= 8 in the probe), per-window constant (mean) detrend, tapers scaled by sqrt(fs), scipy.fftpack.fft with n_fft = next_fast_len(T) (zero padding when T is not 5-smooth, e.g. T=67 -> 72), divided by fs. Connectivity expectation "trials_tapers" = unweighted mean over the 5 tapers: S_ij(f) = (1/K) sum_k X_ik(f) conj(X_jk(f)). Coherency C_ij = S_ij / sqrt(S_ii S_jj). Only the first (n_fft+1)//2 FFT bins are kept: DC included, Nyquist dropped for even n_fft (T=256: 128 bins k/256, k=0..127). pyspi selects bins with fmin <= f <= fmax (closed at both ends) and applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over that axis, then sets the diagonal to NaN; no Undirected mirroring. The cached spectral result (keyed by (measure,)) is shared by all six band/statistic identifiers of the unit. Measure: |C_ij(f)|^2 (connectivity.py:1183-1184 abs(x)**2), i.e. MSC, per bin, then band nanmean / nanmax. Probe: equals the from-scratch numpy/scipy-dpss reference to <= 2.2e-13 on 5 datasets x T in {64,256,1024} x 6 configs.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Squaring: the code returns |C|^2; the supplement calls the SPI "coherence magnitude" but its text ("frequency domain equivalent of the squared time-domain cross correlation") describes the squared quantity, so the code agrees with the text and not with the plain reading of the name; that supplement sentence itself departs from its cited source [59], which calls the unsquared |C| the coherence coefficient and relates coherence to the (unsquared) cross-correlation function (pack hypothesis refined, see candidates). (2) Frequency grid: documented "125 uniformly sampled bins ... f ∈ [f0, fs/2], f0 = 4/T"; implemented the FFT grid k/n_fft, k = 0..(n_fft+1)//2 - 1 (T=64: 32 bins; T=256: 128 bins, 0..0.49609; T=67: zero-padded n_fft=72, 36 bins), DC (f=0) included in the [0, ...] bands, f0 = 4/T not applied, Nyquist (fs/2) never included for even n_fft. (3) Band edges closed at both ends: the f=0.25 bin (n_fft divisible by 4) belongs to both the low and the high band (probe T=256: low band last bin 0.25, high band first bin 0.25). (4) "undirected" with no mirroring (REVIEW M1; this was the earlier wording of tests/README.md bug 5, whose current item 5 is PLI signed antisymmetry, tests/README.md:206) has no numeric effect here: probe |A - A^T| = 0.0 exactly on every dataset tried. Items (2) and (3) are the shared band-selection rules owned and scored by the spectral.band_selection unit (its deviations (3) and (4)); they are listed here only with this unit's numbers.
deviation_from_canonical: Per bin the quantity is the standard multitaper MSC estimator (unweighted average over K=5 DPSS tapers, NW=3, no adaptive weights). Because NW is fixed at 3 for every T, K and hence the estimator degrees of freedom are fixed: the bias does not shrink as T grows (only the bandwidth 2W = 6/T narrows). Probe: iid_gaussian null mean of cohmag_mean_full 0.2295 / 0.1983 / 0.1964 / 0.1994 at T = 64 / 256 / 1024 / 4096 (theory 1/K = 0.2); var2_bivariate full band 0.3648 at T=4096 vs population band mean 0.2465 (Carter bias approx (1-0.2465)^2/5 = 0.114 accounts for it); bivariate_gaussian rho=0.3 pair 0.2647 vs rho^2 = 0.09 at T=4096. The max statistic is the maximum of n_fft/2 noisy estimates and increases with T under the null (0.666 / 0.765 / 0.791 / 0.878). No bias correction. The supplement cites [59] for "coherence coefficient", which Bastos & Schoffelen define as |C| (unsquared); pyspi returns |C|^2.
units_and_range: Dimensionless, non-negative, nominally [0, 1] (max can exceed 1 by rounding: shared_envelope x0==x2 gives max 1.0000000000000009, mean 1.0). Symmetric exactly (|S_ij| = |S_ji|). NaN on the diagonal; an empty band gives an all-NaN matrix for mean (np.nanmean of an empty axis) and ValueError for max (whole Calculator table NaN).
direction_convention: Undirected. A[i,j] = band statistic of |C_ij(f)|^2 with C_ij = S_ij/sqrt(S_ii S_jj), S_ij = mean_k X_i,k(f) conj(X_j,k(f)) (connectivity.py:205-207, 1187-1190, 1485-1487); A[i,j] == A[j,i] exactly in the probe (no mirror needed).

score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 squared-vs-not: pyspi returns |C|^2 under the name coherence magnitude, while ref [59] calls |C| the coherence coefficient (difference up to 0.25); the independent re-implementation agrees to max_abs 7.6e-13 (120/120 runs).
what_changed: Per bin the value is the canonical magnitude-squared coherence |S_xy|^2/(S_xx S_yy) (Carter 1987) of a K=5, NW=3 unweighted multitaper estimate, reproduced to 7.6e-13 by the independent re-implementation (120/120 impl runs); the score rests on those runs, because the identical-pair and f0-bin analytic runs equal 1 under |C|^2 and |C| alike and do not separate the forms (hence check_method independent-impl). (1) The one unit-level convention: the squared form under the name 'coherence magnitude'; the supplement text says "squared time-domain cross correlation" (supplement.txt:605), while Bastos & Schoffelen 2016 [59] call the unsquared |C| the coherence coefficient (difference up to 0.25 here); this is the anchor-9 squared-vs-not convention. Band-level deviations, not conventions, that also change these values: (2) the band summary runs over the FFT grid k/n_fft with DC included and fs/2 excluded, not the documented 125 bins on [4/T, fs/2] (excluding DC changes band means by up to 0.036 and band maxima by up to 0.092, impl runs ref_alt_no_dc_maxabs); (3) closed band edges, so the 0.25 bin is in both the low and the high band (a strict band moves band means by up to 0.031 in the impl runs and 0.16 on the narrow EEG bands of the eeg:mean-eeg11 run, and band maxima by up to 0.273; only the high band isolates the closed edge, because on fmin = 0 bands the strict alternative also drops DC); the empty-band NaN/ValueError behaviour belongs here too. Items (2) and (3) are owned and scored by spectral.band_selection (variant 6, its deviations (3) and (4)); they are recorded here with this unit's numbers and are not scored again in this unit or counted as new findings of it. (4) fixed NW=3 keeps the estimator bias constant in T (null level about 1/K = 0.2 at every T; var2 0.365 vs population 0.2465 at T=4096) and the max statistic grows with T. Finite-sample bias is reported separately (pop runs), not as a formula error.

metric_name_standard: band mean / band max of the multitaper magnitude-squared coherence (MSC) |C_xy(f)|^2 (fixed NW=3, K=5 tapers, single window)
canonical_ref: Carter 1987, Proc. IEEE 75(2):236-255 "Coherence and time delay estimation" (MSC definition gamma^2 = |S_xy|^2/(S_xx S_yy) and estimator bias/variance); Thomson 1982, Proc. IEEE 70(9):1055-1096, section III Eigenestimates pp.1060-1061 (unit-weight average of the first K eigenspectra, eq. 3.7-3.8), section V Adaptive Weighting p.1065 (not used here), section XIV Estimation of Coherence and Polyspectra p.1087 (locations as checked in the spectral.multitaper_csm record); Percival & Walden 1993, Spectral Analysis for Physical Applications, ch. 7 Multitaper Spectral Estimation, pp.331-377 (chapter title and pages from the authors' table of contents, as in spectral.multitaper_csm; section contents not checked); Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front. Syst. Neurosci. 9:175 (supplement ref [59]; quotations below checked against the paper). Carter 1987 equation/section numbers and the bias formula are from memory, not re-checked against the paper.
canonical_definition: gamma^2_xy(f) = |S_xy(f)|^2 / (S_xx(f) S_yy(f)) in [0, 1]; multitaper estimate S_hat_xy(f) = (1/K) sum_k X_k(f) conj(Y_k(f)) with K DPSS tapers. Bastos & Schoffelen 2016 (supplement [59]) define the "coherence coefficient" as the unsquared normalised magnitude |C| ("a normalized quantity bounded by 0 and 1"; numerator "the length of the vector average of the individual trial cross-spectral densities", denominator "the square root of the product of the average of the individual trial power estimates"), say "Mathematically, the coherence is the frequency domain equivalent to the time domain cross-correlation function" (not squared), and refer to the square only as "Its squared value" / "the squared coherence coefficient"; the phrase "coherence magnitude" does not occur in that paper (the supplement attributes it to [60], Schlögl & Supp 2006, not opened). The squared form is MSC. For independent Gaussian white series with K effectively independent tapers MSC_hat ~ Beta(1, K-1), mean 1/K; Carter 1987 gives bias approx (1 - gamma^2)^2 / K. Band summary (mean/max over frequency) is a pyspi construction.
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.1, p.13 (supplement.txt:601-614): "The coherence (also known as coherence magnitude and ordinary coherence [60] or coherence coefficient [59]) is an undirected frequency-dependent measure of linear association between time series x and y. Mathematically, it is the frequency domain equivalent of the squared time-domain cross correlation [59]. We compute mean (denoted by mean) and maximum (max) summary statistics of the coherence for the three frequency ranges". Same text GitBook spectral.md:24-45 (keywords undirected, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent). Common section: supplement §1.5, p.12 (heading at supplement.txt:570): "Each measure is based on the cross- and power-spectral densities at a given frequency and sampling rate, which is estimated via the multitaper technique ... we assume a sampling frequency fs = 1 throughout ... We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f ∈ [f0, fs/2], where fs/2 is the Nyquist frequency and f0 = 4/T ... we take the mean (mean) and the maximum (max) values of each measure over three ranges ... fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f ∈ [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f ∈ [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f ∈ [fs/4, fs/2]" (supplement.txt:570-599; same text GitBook spectral.md:14-20). The briefing pack line ranges (582-613, 614-628, 629-642, 684-700) are offset by 12-14 lines from the headings in this copy of supplement.txt; the line numbers cited here are the ones opened.

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1; optional linear detrend first; Data defaults). The whole (P, T) record is one window: spectral_connectivity 1.1.2 Multitaper with defaults NW=3, n_tapers=floor(2*NW-1)=5, low-bias filter (DPSS concentration > 0.9; all 5 kept for T >= 8 in the probe), per-window constant (mean) detrend, tapers scaled by sqrt(fs), scipy.fftpack.fft with n_fft = next_fast_len(T) (zero padding when T is not 5-smooth, e.g. T=67 -> 72), divided by fs. Connectivity expectation "trials_tapers" = unweighted mean over the 5 tapers: S_ij(f) = (1/K) sum_k X_ik(f) conj(X_jk(f)). Coherency C_ij = S_ij / sqrt(S_ii S_jj). Only the first (n_fft+1)//2 FFT bins are kept: DC included, Nyquist dropped for even n_fft (T=256: 128 bins k/256, k=0..127). pyspi selects bins with fmin <= f <= fmax (closed at both ends) and applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over that axis, then sets the diagonal to NaN; no Undirected mirroring. The cached spectral result (keyed by (measure,)) is shared by all six band/statistic identifiers of the unit. Measure: |C_ij(f)|^2 (connectivity.py:1183-1184 abs(x)**2), i.e. MSC, per bin, then band nanmean / nanmax. Probe: equals the from-scratch numpy/scipy-dpss reference to <= 2.2e-13 on 5 datasets x T in {64,256,1024} x 6 configs.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Squaring: the code returns |C|^2; the supplement calls the SPI "coherence magnitude" but its text ("frequency domain equivalent of the squared time-domain cross correlation") describes the squared quantity, so the code agrees with the text and not with the plain reading of the name; that supplement sentence itself departs from its cited source [59], which calls the unsquared |C| the coherence coefficient and relates coherence to the (unsquared) cross-correlation function (pack hypothesis refined, see candidates). (2) Frequency grid: documented "125 uniformly sampled bins ... f ∈ [f0, fs/2], f0 = 4/T"; implemented the FFT grid k/n_fft, k = 0..(n_fft+1)//2 - 1 (T=64: 32 bins; T=256: 128 bins, 0..0.49609; T=67: zero-padded n_fft=72, 36 bins), DC (f=0) included in the [0, ...] bands, f0 = 4/T not applied, Nyquist (fs/2) never included for even n_fft. (3) Band edges closed at both ends: the f=0.25 bin (n_fft divisible by 4) belongs to both the low and the high band (probe T=256: low band last bin 0.25, high band first bin 0.25). (4) "undirected" with no mirroring (REVIEW M1; this was the earlier wording of tests/README.md bug 5, whose current item 5 is PLI signed antisymmetry, tests/README.md:206) has no numeric effect here: probe |A - A^T| = 0.0 exactly on every dataset tried. Items (2) and (3) are the shared band-selection rules owned and scored by the spectral.band_selection unit (its deviations (3) and (4)); they are listed here only with this unit's numbers.
deviation_from_canonical: Per bin the quantity is the standard multitaper MSC estimator (unweighted average over K=5 DPSS tapers, NW=3, no adaptive weights). Because NW is fixed at 3 for every T, K and hence the estimator degrees of freedom are fixed: the bias does not shrink as T grows (only the bandwidth 2W = 6/T narrows). Probe: iid_gaussian null mean of cohmag_mean_full 0.2295 / 0.1983 / 0.1964 / 0.1994 at T = 64 / 256 / 1024 / 4096 (theory 1/K = 0.2); var2_bivariate full band 0.3648 at T=4096 vs population band mean 0.2465 (Carter bias approx (1-0.2465)^2/5 = 0.114 accounts for it); bivariate_gaussian rho=0.3 pair 0.2647 vs rho^2 = 0.09 at T=4096. The max statistic is the maximum of n_fft/2 noisy estimates and increases with T under the null (0.666 / 0.765 / 0.791 / 0.878). No bias correction. The supplement cites [59] for "coherence coefficient", which Bastos & Schoffelen define as |C| (unsquared); pyspi returns |C|^2.
units_and_range: Dimensionless, non-negative, nominally [0, 1] (max can exceed 1 by rounding: shared_envelope x0==x2 gives max 1.0000000000000009, mean 1.0). Symmetric exactly (|S_ij| = |S_ji|). NaN on the diagonal; an empty band gives an all-NaN matrix for mean (np.nanmean of an empty axis) and ValueError for max (whole Calculator table NaN).
direction_convention: Undirected. A[i,j] = band statistic of |C_ij(f)|^2 with C_ij = S_ij/sqrt(S_ii S_jj), S_ij = mean_k X_i,k(f) conj(X_j,k(f)) (connectivity.py:205-207, 1187-1190, 1485-1487); A[i,j] == A[j,i] exactly in the probe (no mirror needed).

score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 squared-vs-not: pyspi returns |C|^2 under the name coherence magnitude, while ref [59] calls |C| the coherence coefficient (difference up to 0.25); the independent re-implementation agrees to max_abs 7.6e-13 (120/120 runs).
what_changed: Per bin the value is the canonical magnitude-squared coherence |S_xy|^2/(S_xx S_yy) (Carter 1987) of a K=5, NW=3 unweighted multitaper estimate, reproduced to 7.6e-13 by the independent re-implementation (120/120 impl runs); the score rests on those runs, because the identical-pair and f0-bin analytic runs equal 1 under |C|^2 and |C| alike and do not separate the forms (hence check_method independent-impl). (1) The one unit-level convention: the squared form under the name 'coherence magnitude'; the supplement text says "squared time-domain cross correlation" (supplement.txt:605), while Bastos & Schoffelen 2016 [59] call the unsquared |C| the coherence coefficient (difference up to 0.25 here); this is the anchor-9 squared-vs-not convention. Band-level deviations, not conventions, that also change these values: (2) the band summary runs over the FFT grid k/n_fft with DC included and fs/2 excluded, not the documented 125 bins on [4/T, fs/2] (excluding DC changes band means by up to 0.036 and band maxima by up to 0.092, impl runs ref_alt_no_dc_maxabs); (3) closed band edges, so the 0.25 bin is in both the low and the high band (a strict band moves band means by up to 0.031 in the impl runs and 0.16 on the narrow EEG bands of the eeg:mean-eeg11 run, and band maxima by up to 0.273; only the high band isolates the closed edge, because on fmin = 0 bands the strict alternative also drops DC); the empty-band NaN/ValueError behaviour belongs here too. Items (2) and (3) are owned and scored by spectral.band_selection (variant 6, its deviations (3) and (4)); they are recorded here with this unit's numbers and are not scored again in this unit or counted as new findings of it. (4) fixed NW=3 keeps the estimator bias constant in T (null level about 1/K = 0.2 at every T; var2 0.365 vs population 0.2465 at T=4096) and the max statistic grows with T. Finite-sample bias is reported separately (pop runs), not as a formula error.

metric_name_standard: band mean / band max of the ABSOLUTE imaginary part of multitaper coherency |Im C_ij(f)| (absolute imaginary coherence)
canonical_ref: Nolte, Bai, Wheaton, Mari, Vorbach & Hallett 2004, Clin. Neurophysiol. 115:2292-2307 (imaginary part of coherency; supplement ref [64]); Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front. Syst. Neurosci. 9:175 (supplement [59]). Equation numbers not re-checked (from memory: coherency defined as C_ij = S_ij/sqrt(S_ii S_jj), S_ij = <x_i(f) x_j*(f)>, ImCoh = Im C_ij).
canonical_definition: ImCoh_ij(f) = Im[S_ij(f)/sqrt(S_ii(f) S_jj(f))], signed, in [-1, 1], antisymmetric (ImCoh_ji = -ImCoh_ij); zero in expectation for instantaneous (zero-lag) mixing; the sign indicates which signal leads at frequency f. Many applications report |ImCoh|, but Nolte 2004 defines and interprets the signed quantity.
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.5, p.14 (supplement.txt:670-682): "The imaginary part of the complex-valued coherency (referred to as imaginary coherence [59]) is argued as a means to obtain the coherence exclusively caused by a time delay (i.e., by removing instantaneous interactions that are present in the real axis) [64]. We compute the imaginary coherence for the three typical frequency ranges and two summary statistics". Keywords "undirected, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent". Same text GitBook spectral.md:152-173. Common section: supplement §1.5, p.12 (heading at supplement.txt:570): "Each measure is based on the cross- and power-spectral densities at a given frequency and sampling rate, which is estimated via the multitaper technique ... we assume a sampling frequency fs = 1 throughout ... We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f ∈ [f0, fs/2], where fs/2 is the Nyquist frequency and f0 = 4/T ... we take the mean (mean) and the maximum (max) values of each measure over three ranges ... fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f ∈ [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f ∈ [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f ∈ [fs/4, fs/2]" (supplement.txt:570-599; same text GitBook spectral.md:14-20). The briefing pack line ranges (582-613, 614-628, 629-642, 684-700) are offset by 12-14 lines from the headings in this copy of supplement.txt; the line numbers cited here are the ones opened.
delegate_lib: spectral-connectivity==1.1.2 Connectivity.imaginary_coherence (connectivity.py:345-373) = abs(E[S].imag / sqrt(P_i P_j)) on non-negative frequencies; spectra from Multitaper.fft (scipy.fftpack.fft); band selection and nanmean/nanmax in pyspi (numpy 2.5.4)
implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1; optional linear detrend first; Data defaults). The whole (P, T) record is one window: spectral_connectivity 1.1.2 Multitaper with defaults NW=3, n_tapers=floor(2*NW-1)=5, low-bias filter (DPSS concentration > 0.9; all 5 kept for T >= 8 in the probe), per-window constant (mean) detrend, tapers scaled by sqrt(fs), scipy.fftpack.fft with n_fft = next_fast_len(T) (zero padding when T is not 5-smooth, e.g. T=67 -> 72), divided by fs. Connectivity expectation "trials_tapers" = unweighted mean over the 5 tapers: S_ij(f) = (1/K) sum_k X_ik(f) conj(X_jk(f)). Coherency C_ij = S_ij / sqrt(S_ii S_jj). Only the first (n_fft+1)//2 FFT bins are kept: DC included, Nyquist dropped for even n_fft (T=256: 128 bins k/256, k=0..127). pyspi selects bins with fmin <= f <= fmax (closed at both ends) and applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over that axis, then sets the diagonal to NaN; no Undirected mirroring. The cached spectral result (keyed by (measure,)) is shared by all six band/statistic identifiers of the unit. Measure: |Im S_ij(f)| / sqrt(S_ii(f) S_jj(f)) per bin (absolute value taken per frequency BEFORE the band mean/max; no norm==0 guard and no NaN diagonal in this library method, pyspi sets the diagonal to NaN). At DC Im S_ij = 0 exactly for real input, so a band containing f=0 averages one structural zero. Probe: equals the from-scratch reference to <= 1.4e-13.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Documented as "the imaginary part of the complex-valued coherency"; implemented as its absolute value per frequency (consistent with the "unsigned"/"undirected" labels, not with "imaginary part"). (2) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented FFT grid with DC included (where Im C = 0 exactly, so bands starting at 0 are scaled by (n-1)/n relative to excluding DC: probe var2 T=256 low band 0.389088 = 0.395168 * 64/65) and Nyquist excluded; low/high bands share the 0.25 bin. (3) No mirroring (REVIEW M1; tests/README.md bug 5 before b2f6d7e) has no numeric effect: |A - A^T| = 0.0 exactly in the probe.
deviation_from_canonical: Nolte 2004 ImCoh is signed and antisymmetric; pyspi takes |.| per bin, discarding lead/lag (probe delayed_noise T=1024: A[0,1] = A[1,0] = 0.6293 while signed mean ImC is +0.6283 / -0.6283). Because abs is applied before the band mean, mean|Im C| differs from |mean Im C| when the sign changes over the band (probe delayed_noise pair (0,3), delay 5, full band: 0.6315 vs 0.1262). The absolute value plus fixed K=5 tapers gives a positive null level that does not shrink with T (probe iid_gaussian mean 0.2623 / 0.2517 / 0.2554 / 0.2577 at T=64/256/1024/4096; population 0) and upward bias (var2_bivariate T=4096 full band 0.3626 vs population mean |Im C| 0.2871).
units_and_range: Dimensionless, non-negative, in [0, 1]. Symmetric exactly. 0.0 exactly for identical series (shared_envelope x0 == x2). NaN on the diagonal (set by pyspi; the library returns 0 there); a zero-power channel gives 0/0 = NaN in its row and column (no guard in the library method; check stage: spectral.icoh|iid_gaussian|1024|kernel|const0:* and const3.7:*); empty band -> all-NaN (mean) or ValueError (max).
direction_convention: Undirected by construction: A[i,j] = A[j,i] = band statistic of |Im S_ij|/sqrt(S_ii S_jj) with S_ij = mean_k X_i,k conj(X_j,k). The sign that would indicate lead/lag (positive Im C_ij means i leads j under this S_ij convention, consistent with the phase unit) is discarded by spectral_connectivity/connectivity.py:370.

score_rubric_note: Anchor 8 fails because abs comes before the band mean (delayed_noise lag 5: 0.6315 vs |mean Im C| 0.1262). Anchor 7's supplement-variant clause holds only through the 'unsigned' keyword. The supplement prose names the imaginary part of coherency, while pyspi takes |Im C| per bin. Keywords are metadata, so the row keeps 7 as the nearest anchor. Grid deviations are scored under spectral.band_selection.
what_changed: pyspi returns |Im C_ij(f)| per bin (library spectral_connectivity/connectivity.py:370-373), then the band mean / max, whereas Nolte et al. 2004 define the signed, antisymmetric Im C_ij whose sign gives lead/lag; the supplement text says 'the imaginary part' while the labels say unsigned. Consequences measured here: the matrix is exactly symmetric and carries no direction; the absolute value is taken before the band mean, so a band where Im C changes sign averages magnitudes (0.6315 vs |mean Im C| 0.1262 for lag 5 over the full band); with K=5 tapers the absolute value gives a positive null level of about 0.26 at every T (population 0) and 0.24 for purely zero-lag (instantaneous) coupling, which is the case imaginary coherence is meant to suppress. DC adds one structural zero to every band starting at 0 (|Im C(DC)| = 0.0 exactly). Grid, shared 0.25 bin and empty-band behaviour as for cohmag. Rubric anchor 7 (matches the supplement variant, keywords 'undirected, unsigned', but differs from canonical in a value-changing way). Anchor 8 (monotone relationship, abs of a signed canonical quantity) holds only per bin: the SPI is the band mean / max taken after the absolute value, which has no monotone relation to the canonical signed band mean (0.6315 vs 0.1262 above; 0.24-0.26 where the population value is 0). The score was 8 before the check-stage review. Rubric reading is nearest-anchor 7 (score_rubric_note), because the supplement-variant clause holds only through the 'unsigned' keyword, which is metadata; the 'Rubric anchor 7' wording above is the original reasoning for score_0_10.

metric_name_standard: band mean / band max of the ABSOLUTE imaginary part of multitaper coherency |Im C_ij(f)| (absolute imaginary coherence)
canonical_ref: Nolte, Bai, Wheaton, Mari, Vorbach & Hallett 2004, Clin. Neurophysiol. 115:2292-2307 (imaginary part of coherency; supplement ref [64]); Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front. Syst. Neurosci. 9:175 (supplement [59]). Equation numbers not re-checked (from memory: coherency defined as C_ij = S_ij/sqrt(S_ii S_jj), S_ij = <x_i(f) x_j*(f)>, ImCoh = Im C_ij).
canonical_definition: ImCoh_ij(f) = Im[S_ij(f)/sqrt(S_ii(f) S_jj(f))], signed, in [-1, 1], antisymmetric (ImCoh_ji = -ImCoh_ij); zero in expectation for instantaneous (zero-lag) mixing; the sign indicates which signal leads at frequency f. Many applications report |ImCoh|, but Nolte 2004 defines and interprets the signed quantity.
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.5, p.14 (supplement.txt:670-682): "The imaginary part of the complex-valued coherency (referred to as imaginary coherence [59]) is argued as a means to obtain the coherence exclusively caused by a time delay (i.e., by removing instantaneous interactions that are present in the real axis) [64]. We compute the imaginary coherence for the three typical frequency ranges and two summary statistics". Keywords "undirected, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent". Same text GitBook spectral.md:152-173. Common section: supplement §1.5, p.12 (heading at supplement.txt:570): "Each measure is based on the cross- and power-spectral densities at a given frequency and sampling rate, which is estimated via the multitaper technique ... we assume a sampling frequency fs = 1 throughout ... We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f ∈ [f0, fs/2], where fs/2 is the Nyquist frequency and f0 = 4/T ... we take the mean (mean) and the maximum (max) values of each measure over three ranges ... fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f ∈ [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f ∈ [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f ∈ [fs/4, fs/2]" (supplement.txt:570-599; same text GitBook spectral.md:14-20). The briefing pack line ranges (582-613, 614-628, 629-642, 684-700) are offset by 12-14 lines from the headings in this copy of supplement.txt; the line numbers cited here are the ones opened.
delegate_lib: spectral-connectivity==1.1.2 Connectivity.imaginary_coherence (connectivity.py:345-373) = abs(E[S].imag / sqrt(P_i P_j)) on non-negative frequencies; spectra from Multitaper.fft (scipy.fftpack.fft); band selection and nanmean/nanmax in pyspi (numpy 2.5.4)
implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1; optional linear detrend first; Data defaults). The whole (P, T) record is one window: spectral_connectivity 1.1.2 Multitaper with defaults NW=3, n_tapers=floor(2*NW-1)=5, low-bias filter (DPSS concentration > 0.9; all 5 kept for T >= 8 in the probe), per-window constant (mean) detrend, tapers scaled by sqrt(fs), scipy.fftpack.fft with n_fft = next_fast_len(T) (zero padding when T is not 5-smooth, e.g. T=67 -> 72), divided by fs. Connectivity expectation "trials_tapers" = unweighted mean over the 5 tapers: S_ij(f) = (1/K) sum_k X_ik(f) conj(X_jk(f)). Coherency C_ij = S_ij / sqrt(S_ii S_jj). Only the first (n_fft+1)//2 FFT bins are kept: DC included, Nyquist dropped for even n_fft (T=256: 128 bins k/256, k=0..127). pyspi selects bins with fmin <= f <= fmax (closed at both ends) and applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over that axis, then sets the diagonal to NaN; no Undirected mirroring. The cached spectral result (keyed by (measure,)) is shared by all six band/statistic identifiers of the unit. Measure: |Im S_ij(f)| / sqrt(S_ii(f) S_jj(f)) per bin (absolute value taken per frequency BEFORE the band mean/max; no norm==0 guard and no NaN diagonal in this library method, pyspi sets the diagonal to NaN). At DC Im S_ij = 0 exactly for real input, so a band containing f=0 averages one structural zero. Probe: equals the from-scratch reference to <= 1.4e-13.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Documented as "the imaginary part of the complex-valued coherency"; implemented as its absolute value per frequency (consistent with the "unsigned"/"undirected" labels, not with "imaginary part"). (2) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented FFT grid with DC included (where Im C = 0 exactly, so bands starting at 0 are scaled by (n-1)/n relative to excluding DC: probe var2 T=256 low band 0.389088 = 0.395168 * 64/65) and Nyquist excluded; low/high bands share the 0.25 bin. (3) No mirroring (REVIEW M1; tests/README.md bug 5 before b2f6d7e) has no numeric effect: |A - A^T| = 0.0 exactly in the probe.
deviation_from_canonical: Nolte 2004 ImCoh is signed and antisymmetric; pyspi takes |.| per bin, discarding lead/lag (probe delayed_noise T=1024: A[0,1] = A[1,0] = 0.6293 while signed mean ImC is +0.6283 / -0.6283). Because abs is applied before the band mean, mean|Im C| differs from |mean Im C| when the sign changes over the band (probe delayed_noise pair (0,3), delay 5, full band: 0.6315 vs 0.1262). The absolute value plus fixed K=5 tapers gives a positive null level that does not shrink with T (probe iid_gaussian mean 0.2623 / 0.2517 / 0.2554 / 0.2577 at T=64/256/1024/4096; population 0) and upward bias (var2_bivariate T=4096 full band 0.3626 vs population mean |Im C| 0.2871).
units_and_range: Dimensionless, non-negative, in [0, 1]. Symmetric exactly. 0.0 exactly for identical series (shared_envelope x0 == x2). NaN on the diagonal (set by pyspi; the library returns 0 there); a zero-power channel gives 0/0 = NaN in its row and column (no guard in the library method; check stage: spectral.icoh|iid_gaussian|1024|kernel|const0:* and const3.7:*); empty band -> all-NaN (mean) or ValueError (max).
direction_convention: Undirected by construction: A[i,j] = A[j,i] = band statistic of |Im S_ij|/sqrt(S_ii S_jj) with S_ij = mean_k X_i,k conj(X_j,k). The sign that would indicate lead/lag (positive Im C_ij means i leads j under this S_ij convention, consistent with the phase unit) is discarded by spectral_connectivity/connectivity.py:370.

what_changed: pyspi returns |Im C_ij(f)| per bin (library spectral_connectivity/connectivity.py:370-373), then the band mean / max, whereas Nolte et al. 2004 define the signed, antisymmetric Im C_ij whose sign gives lead/lag; the supplement text says 'the imaginary part' while the labels say unsigned. Consequences measured here: the matrix is exactly symmetric and carries no direction; the absolute value is taken before the band mean, so a band where Im C changes sign averages magnitudes (0.6315 vs |mean Im C| 0.1262 for lag 5 over the full band); with K=5 tapers the absolute value gives a positive null level of about 0.26 at every T (population 0) and 0.24 for purely zero-lag (instantaneous) coupling, which is the case imaginary coherence is meant to suppress. DC adds one structural zero to every band starting at 0 (|Im C(DC)| = 0.0 exactly). Grid, shared 0.25 bin and empty-band behaviour as for cohmag. Rubric anchor 7 (matches the supplement variant, keywords 'undirected, unsigned', but differs from canonical in a value-changing way). Anchor 8 (monotone relationship, abs of a signed canonical quantity) holds only per bin: the SPI is the band mean / max taken after the absolute value, which has no monotone relation to the canonical signed band mean (0.6315 vs 0.1262 above; 0.24-0.26 where the population value is 0). The score was 8 before the check-stage review. metric_name_standard: phase slope index (PSI, Nolte et al. 2008), here a non-standard all-frequency-pairs variant summed over a decimated band, unnormalised
canonical_ref: Nolte G, Ziehe A, Nikulin VV, Schloegl A, Kraemer N, Brismar T, Mueller K-R (2008), Robustly estimating the flow direction of information in complex physical systems, Phys. Rev. Lett. 100, 234101; equation numbers and sign statement checked against arXiv:0712.2352v1 p.2 (the copy REVIEW M5 cites; not against the PRL journal copy); eq. 2 (cross-spectrum phase of a delayed copy and the sign rule), eq. 3 (raw PSI Psi_tilde), eq. 4 (coherency definition), eq. 5 (weighted phase-slope form of eq. 3), eq. 6 (normalised Psi = Psi_tilde / std(Psi_tilde), std estimated by the jackknife)
canonical_definition: Psi_tilde_ij = Im( sum_{f in F} C_ij^*(f) C_ij(f + delta_f) ), C_ij(f) = S_ij(f) / sqrt(S_ii(f) S_jj(f)), S_ij = <x_i(f) x_j^*(f)> (eq. 3 with eq. 4), F the band of interest, delta_f the frequency resolution (adjacent frequencies only); normalised Psi = Psi_tilde / std(Psi_tilde) with std from a jackknife (eq. 6); sign (arXiv p.2, eq. 2 and the next sentence) for y2(t) = a y1(t - tau), S_12(f) = <y1(f) y2^*(f)> ~ exp(i 2 pi f tau), and 'the causal direction is estimated to go from y1 to y2 (y2 to y1) if it [the slope] is positive (negative)', so Psi_ij > 0 means i leads (sends to) j

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1; detrend optional). Multitaper over the whole series: NW=3, 5 DPSS tapers, per-window constant detrend, n_fft = next_fast_len(T), non-negative bins k/n_fft for k = 0..n_fft/2-1. Coherency C_ij(f) = mean_tapers(X_i X_j^*) / sqrt(P_i P_j). Band: bins with fmin < f < fmax (strict). Decimation: every s-th in-band bin starting at the first, s = ceil(((fmax-fmin)/50) * n_fft); K kept bins (probe: full band K = 31/43/47/50 at T = 64/256/1024/4096; half bands K = 15/32/43/49). Value: A[i,j] = Im( sum over ALL unordered pairs a<b of kept bins of conj(C_ij(f_a)) C_ij(f_b) ), i.e. K(K-1)/2 terms, not K-1 adjacent terms; no normalisation, no averaging (the 'mean' in the identifier and np.nanmean are never applied: pyspi's 4-index slice of the 3-D result raises IndexError and the except branch returns adj_freq[0]). Each pair uses only its own two channels (bivariate in effect); result exactly antisymmetric (probe max|A + A.T| = 0); diagonal NaN.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labels/class: documented 'directed' (supplement §1.5.4 keywords, config.yaml:724) but the class is Undirected with labels ['unsigned','spectral','undirected'] (spectral.py:288-290); output is signed and antisymmetric, so 'unsigned' is also contrary to the values (already documented: REVIEW M1 and M5; tests/README.md bug 5 before b2f6d7e). (2) Identifier says 'mean' but no average over frequency or pairs is taken: the value is a raw SUM over K(K-1)/2 frequency pairs (spectral.py:91-93; probe all-pairs recomputation from library coherency equals pyspi to 0.0). (3) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniformly sampled bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins k/n_fft (k >= 1 in band since fmin=0 is strictly excluded), then decimated to ~50 bins by s = ceil(band*n_fft/50) (probe K = 31..50). (4) Band endpoints: documented closed intervals [0, fs/4], [fs/4, fs/2]; implemented open (fmin < f < fmax, connectivity.py:1329-1331), so the bin f = 0.25 belongs to neither half band and DC/Nyquist are never used. (5) The method weights 'consistency of the changes in phase differences' over every pair of decimated frequencies, not over neighbouring frequencies (already REVIEW M5). (6) Narrow bands (EEG identifiers) with 0 or 1 in-band bins raise IndexError inside _inner_combination, giving an all-NaN matrix (probe: fmin 0.5/1024, fmax 2/1024 at T=512 and 1024; also 2-4 and 4-6 'Hz' bands); not documented.
deviation_from_canonical: Sums conj(C(f_a)) C(f_b) over every unordered pair of kept frequencies instead of adjacent pairs at spacing delta_f (Nolte 2008 eq. 3; already REVIEW M5). Consequences found here: (a) magnitude scales roughly with K^2 and therefore with T and band through the decimation rule (delayed_noise pair (0,1), full band: pyspi 296 / 580 / 694 / 787 at T = 64 / 256 / 1024 / 4096 (spectral.psi|delayed_noise|64|kernel|rep:full and spectral.psi|delayed_noise|{256,1024,4096}|pipeline|nolte:full), while Nolte's adjacent-pair sum is 3.061 / 3.094 / 3.081 at T = 256 / 1024 / 4096 (ref_nolte_triu[0] of the same nolte:full runs; check-stage numbers that replace the trace-stage probe values 3.06 / 3.03 / 3.01); the T = 64 adjacent value 2.75 is a trace-stage probe value with no check run behind it); (b) for a pure delay with |C| = 1 the all-pairs value DEcreases with the delay (full band, T=256: tau=1 588, tau=5 116, tau=30 10.6) whereas Nolte's PSI increases with the delay until wrap (3.09, 15.1, 33.7) (analytic probe), so pairwise ranking by this value can invert the ranking by delay magnitude for broadband delays (elaboration of REVIEW M5, not a new finding); (c) sign can differ from Nolte's (REVIEW M5 example). The decimation spacing s/n_fft = (fmax-fmin)/50 rounded up is a band-relative step, not the multitaper resolution 2W = 6/T; for T=64 s=1 (spacing 1/64 < 6/64). No jackknife normalisation (Nolte's eq. 6; the paper defines Psi_tilde (eq. 3) and the normalised Psi (eq. 6) separately, so reporting the raw form is a choice, not a deviation in kind). With K = 2 kept bins the all-pairs and adjacent formulas coincide.
units_and_range: Dimensionless; signed; antisymmetric (A[j,i] = -A[i,j] exactly, probe max|A + A.T| = 0); bounded by |A| <= K(K-1)/2 (each term has |C||C'| <= 1), K up to 50, observed up to ~790; NaN diagonal; whole matrix NaN (exception) when the band holds 0 or 1 bins. Not comparable across T or bands because K depends on both.
direction_convention: A[i,j] = Im sum_{a<b} conj(C_ij(f_a)) C_ij(f_b) with C_ij from S_ij = X_i X_j^*. If x_j(t) = x_i(t - tau) (i leads), S_ij ~ exp(+i 2 pi f tau), phase rises with f and A[i,j] > 0 for small tau. Probe delayed_noise T=256 band 0-0.25 (x0 leads x1, x2, x3 by 1, 3, 5): A[0,1] = +238.2, A[0,2] = +255.1, A[0,3] = +105.3, A[1,0] = -238.2. So A[i,j] > 0 means row i leads column j, same as Nolte's convention; the magnitude is not monotone in the delay. If the REVIEW M1 bypass were fixed by mirroring (Undirected.multivariate), the antisymmetric matrix would be replaced by its upper triangle mirrored and the sign of the lower triangle would be lost.

metric_name_standard: phase slope index (PSI, Nolte et al. 2008), here a non-standard all-frequency-pairs variant summed over a decimated band, unnormalised
canonical_ref: Nolte G, Ziehe A, Nikulin VV, Schloegl A, Kraemer N, Brismar T, Mueller K-R (2008), Robustly estimating the flow direction of information in complex physical systems, Phys. Rev. Lett. 100, 234101; equation numbers and sign statement checked against arXiv:0712.2352v1 p.2 (the copy REVIEW M5 cites; not against the PRL journal copy); eq. 2 (cross-spectrum phase of a delayed copy and the sign rule), eq. 3 (raw PSI Psi_tilde), eq. 4 (coherency definition), eq. 5 (weighted phase-slope form of eq. 3), eq. 6 (normalised Psi = Psi_tilde / std(Psi_tilde), std estimated by the jackknife)
canonical_definition: Psi_tilde_ij = Im( sum_{f in F} C_ij^*(f) C_ij(f + delta_f) ), C_ij(f) = S_ij(f) / sqrt(S_ii(f) S_jj(f)), S_ij = <x_i(f) x_j^*(f)> (eq. 3 with eq. 4), F the band of interest, delta_f the frequency resolution (adjacent frequencies only); normalised Psi = Psi_tilde / std(Psi_tilde) with std from a jackknife (eq. 6); sign (arXiv p.2, eq. 2 and the next sentence) for y2(t) = a y1(t - tau), S_12(f) = <y1(f) y2^*(f)> ~ exp(i 2 pi f tau), and 'the causal direction is estimated to go from y1 to y2 (y2 to y1) if it [the slope] is positive (negative)', so Psi_ij > 0 means i leads (sends to) j

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1; detrend optional). Multitaper over the whole series: NW=3, 5 DPSS tapers, per-window constant detrend, n_fft = next_fast_len(T), non-negative bins k/n_fft for k = 0..n_fft/2-1. Coherency C_ij(f) = mean_tapers(X_i X_j^*) / sqrt(P_i P_j). Band: bins with fmin < f < fmax (strict). Decimation: every s-th in-band bin starting at the first, s = ceil(((fmax-fmin)/50) * n_fft); K kept bins (probe: full band K = 31/43/47/50 at T = 64/256/1024/4096; half bands K = 15/32/43/49). Value: A[i,j] = Im( sum over ALL unordered pairs a<b of kept bins of conj(C_ij(f_a)) C_ij(f_b) ), i.e. K(K-1)/2 terms, not K-1 adjacent terms; no normalisation, no averaging (the 'mean' in the identifier and np.nanmean are never applied: pyspi's 4-index slice of the 3-D result raises IndexError and the except branch returns adj_freq[0]). Each pair uses only its own two channels (bivariate in effect); result exactly antisymmetric (probe max|A + A.T| = 0); diagonal NaN.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labels/class: documented 'directed' (supplement §1.5.4 keywords, config.yaml:724) but the class is Undirected with labels ['unsigned','spectral','undirected'] (spectral.py:288-290); output is signed and antisymmetric, so 'unsigned' is also contrary to the values (already documented: REVIEW M1 and M5; tests/README.md bug 5 before b2f6d7e). (2) Identifier says 'mean' but no average over frequency or pairs is taken: the value is a raw SUM over K(K-1)/2 frequency pairs (spectral.py:91-93; probe all-pairs recomputation from library coherency equals pyspi to 0.0). (3) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniformly sampled bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins k/n_fft (k >= 1 in band since fmin=0 is strictly excluded), then decimated to ~50 bins by s = ceil(band*n_fft/50) (probe K = 31..50). (4) Band endpoints: documented closed intervals [0, fs/4], [fs/4, fs/2]; implemented open (fmin < f < fmax, connectivity.py:1329-1331), so the bin f = 0.25 belongs to neither half band and DC/Nyquist are never used. (5) The method weights 'consistency of the changes in phase differences' over every pair of decimated frequencies, not over neighbouring frequencies (already REVIEW M5). (6) Narrow bands (EEG identifiers) with 0 or 1 in-band bins raise IndexError inside _inner_combination, giving an all-NaN matrix (probe: fmin 0.5/1024, fmax 2/1024 at T=512 and 1024; also 2-4 and 4-6 'Hz' bands); not documented.
deviation_from_canonical: Sums conj(C(f_a)) C(f_b) over every unordered pair of kept frequencies instead of adjacent pairs at spacing delta_f (Nolte 2008 eq. 3; already REVIEW M5). Consequences found here: (a) magnitude scales roughly with K^2 and therefore with T and band through the decimation rule (delayed_noise pair (0,1), full band: pyspi 296 / 580 / 694 / 787 at T = 64 / 256 / 1024 / 4096 (spectral.psi|delayed_noise|64|kernel|rep:full and spectral.psi|delayed_noise|{256,1024,4096}|pipeline|nolte:full), while Nolte's adjacent-pair sum is 3.061 / 3.094 / 3.081 at T = 256 / 1024 / 4096 (ref_nolte_triu[0] of the same nolte:full runs; check-stage numbers that replace the trace-stage probe values 3.06 / 3.03 / 3.01); the T = 64 adjacent value 2.75 is a trace-stage probe value with no check run behind it); (b) for a pure delay with |C| = 1 the all-pairs value DEcreases with the delay (full band, T=256: tau=1 588, tau=5 116, tau=30 10.6) whereas Nolte's PSI increases with the delay until wrap (3.09, 15.1, 33.7) (analytic probe), so pairwise ranking by this value can invert the ranking by delay magnitude for broadband delays (elaboration of REVIEW M5, not a new finding); (c) sign can differ from Nolte's (REVIEW M5 example). The decimation spacing s/n_fft = (fmax-fmin)/50 rounded up is a band-relative step, not the multitaper resolution 2W = 6/T; for T=64 s=1 (spacing 1/64 < 6/64). No jackknife normalisation (Nolte's eq. 6; the paper defines Psi_tilde (eq. 3) and the normalised Psi (eq. 6) separately, so reporting the raw form is a choice, not a deviation in kind). With K = 2 kept bins the all-pairs and adjacent formulas coincide.
units_and_range: Dimensionless; signed; antisymmetric (A[j,i] = -A[i,j] exactly, probe max|A + A.T| = 0); bounded by |A| <= K(K-1)/2 (each term has |C||C'| <= 1), K up to 50, observed up to ~790; NaN diagonal; whole matrix NaN (exception) when the band holds 0 or 1 bins. Not comparable across T or bands because K depends on both.
direction_convention: A[i,j] = Im sum_{a<b} conj(C_ij(f_a)) C_ij(f_b) with C_ij from S_ij = X_i X_j^*. If x_j(t) = x_i(t - tau) (i leads), S_ij ~ exp(+i 2 pi f tau), phase rises with f and A[i,j] > 0 for small tau. Probe delayed_noise T=256 band 0-0.25 (x0 leads x1, x2, x3 by 1, 3, 5): A[0,1] = +238.2, A[0,2] = +255.1, A[0,3] = +105.3, A[1,0] = -238.2. So A[i,j] > 0 means row i leads column j, same as Nolte's convention; the magnitude is not monotone in the delay. If the REVIEW M1 bypass were fixed by mirroring (Undirected.multivariate), the antisymmetric matrix would be replaced by its upper triangle mirrored and the sign of the lower triangle would be lost.

metric_name_standard: phase slope index (PSI, Nolte et al. 2008), here a non-standard all-frequency-pairs variant summed over a decimated band, unnormalised
canonical_ref: Nolte G, Ziehe A, Nikulin VV, Schloegl A, Kraemer N, Brismar T, Mueller K-R (2008), Robustly estimating the flow direction of information in complex physical systems, Phys. Rev. Lett. 100, 234101; equation numbers and sign statement checked against arXiv:0712.2352v1 p.2 (the copy REVIEW M5 cites; not against the PRL journal copy); eq. 2 (cross-spectrum phase of a delayed copy and the sign rule), eq. 3 (raw PSI Psi_tilde), eq. 4 (coherency definition), eq. 5 (weighted phase-slope form of eq. 3), eq. 6 (normalised Psi = Psi_tilde / std(Psi_tilde), std estimated by the jackknife)
canonical_definition: Psi_tilde_ij = Im( sum_{f in F} C_ij^*(f) C_ij(f + delta_f) ), C_ij(f) = S_ij(f) / sqrt(S_ii(f) S_jj(f)), S_ij = <x_i(f) x_j^*(f)> (eq. 3 with eq. 4), F the band of interest, delta_f the frequency resolution (adjacent frequencies only); normalised Psi = Psi_tilde / std(Psi_tilde) with std from a jackknife (eq. 6); sign (arXiv p.2, eq. 2 and the next sentence) for y2(t) = a y1(t - tau), S_12(f) = <y1(f) y2^*(f)> ~ exp(i 2 pi f tau), and 'the causal direction is estimated to go from y1 to y2 (y2 to y1) if it [the slope] is positive (negative)', so Psi_ij > 0 means i leads (sends to) j

delegate_lib: spectral_connectivity==1.1.2 Connectivity.phase_slope_index(frequencies_of_interest=[fmin, fmax], frequency_resolution=(fmax-fmin)/50) on a Multitaper(T x P, sampling_frequency=1) transform; pyspi only selects time window 0
implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1; detrend optional). Multitaper over the whole series: NW=3, 5 DPSS tapers, per-window constant detrend, n_fft = next_fast_len(T), non-negative bins k/n_fft for k = 0..n_fft/2-1. Coherency C_ij(f) = mean_tapers(X_i X_j^*) / sqrt(P_i P_j). Band: bins with fmin < f < fmax (strict). Decimation: every s-th in-band bin starting at the first, s = ceil(((fmax-fmin)/50) * n_fft); K kept bins (probe: full band K = 31/43/47/50 at T = 64/256/1024/4096; half bands K = 15/32/43/49). Value: A[i,j] = Im( sum over ALL unordered pairs a<b of kept bins of conj(C_ij(f_a)) C_ij(f_b) ), i.e. K(K-1)/2 terms, not K-1 adjacent terms; no normalisation, no averaging (the 'mean' in the identifier and np.nanmean are never applied: pyspi's 4-index slice of the 3-D result raises IndexError and the except branch returns adj_freq[0]). Each pair uses only its own two channels (bivariate in effect); result exactly antisymmetric (probe max|A + A.T| = 0); diagonal NaN.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labels/class: documented 'directed' (supplement §1.5.4 keywords, config.yaml:724) but the class is Undirected with labels ['unsigned','spectral','undirected'] (spectral.py:288-290); output is signed and antisymmetric, so 'unsigned' is also contrary to the values (already documented: REVIEW M1 and M5; tests/README.md bug 5 before b2f6d7e). (2) Identifier says 'mean' but no average over frequency or pairs is taken: the value is a raw SUM over K(K-1)/2 frequency pairs (spectral.py:91-93; probe all-pairs recomputation from library coherency equals pyspi to 0.0). (3) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniformly sampled bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins k/n_fft (k >= 1 in band since fmin=0 is strictly excluded), then decimated to ~50 bins by s = ceil(band*n_fft/50) (probe K = 31..50). (4) Band endpoints: documented closed intervals [0, fs/4], [fs/4, fs/2]; implemented open (fmin < f < fmax, connectivity.py:1329-1331), so the bin f = 0.25 belongs to neither half band and DC/Nyquist are never used. (5) The method weights 'consistency of the changes in phase differences' over every pair of decimated frequencies, not over neighbouring frequencies (already REVIEW M5). (6) Narrow bands (EEG identifiers) with 0 or 1 in-band bins raise IndexError inside _inner_combination, giving an all-NaN matrix (probe: fmin 0.5/1024, fmax 2/1024 at T=512 and 1024; also 2-4 and 4-6 'Hz' bands); not documented.
deviation_from_canonical: Sums conj(C(f_a)) C(f_b) over every unordered pair of kept frequencies instead of adjacent pairs at spacing delta_f (Nolte 2008 eq. 3; already REVIEW M5). Consequences found here: (a) magnitude scales roughly with K^2 and therefore with T and band through the decimation rule (delayed_noise pair (0,1), full band: pyspi 296 / 580 / 694 / 787 at T = 64 / 256 / 1024 / 4096 (spectral.psi|delayed_noise|64|kernel|rep:full and spectral.psi|delayed_noise|{256,1024,4096}|pipeline|nolte:full), while Nolte's adjacent-pair sum is 3.061 / 3.094 / 3.081 at T = 256 / 1024 / 4096 (ref_nolte_triu[0] of the same nolte:full runs; check-stage numbers that replace the trace-stage probe values 3.06 / 3.03 / 3.01); the T = 64 adjacent value 2.75 is a trace-stage probe value with no check run behind it); (b) for a pure delay with |C| = 1 the all-pairs value DEcreases with the delay (full band, T=256: tau=1 588, tau=5 116, tau=30 10.6) whereas Nolte's PSI increases with the delay until wrap (3.09, 15.1, 33.7) (analytic probe), so pairwise ranking by this value can invert the ranking by delay magnitude for broadband delays (elaboration of REVIEW M5, not a new finding); (c) sign can differ from Nolte's (REVIEW M5 example). The decimation spacing s/n_fft = (fmax-fmin)/50 rounded up is a band-relative step, not the multitaper resolution 2W = 6/T; for T=64 s=1 (spacing 1/64 < 6/64). No jackknife normalisation (Nolte's eq. 6; the paper defines Psi_tilde (eq. 3) and the normalised Psi (eq. 6) separately, so reporting the raw form is a choice, not a deviation in kind). With K = 2 kept bins the all-pairs and adjacent formulas coincide.
units_and_range: Dimensionless; signed; antisymmetric (A[j,i] = -A[i,j] exactly, probe max|A + A.T| = 0); bounded by |A| <= K(K-1)/2 (each term has |C||C'| <= 1), K up to 50, observed up to ~790; NaN diagonal; whole matrix NaN (exception) when the band holds 0 or 1 bins. Not comparable across T or bands because K depends on both.
direction_convention: A[i,j] = Im sum_{a<b} conj(C_ij(f_a)) C_ij(f_b) with C_ij from S_ij = X_i X_j^*. If x_j(t) = x_i(t - tau) (i leads), S_ij ~ exp(+i 2 pi f tau), phase rises with f and A[i,j] > 0 for small tau. Probe delayed_noise T=256 band 0-0.25 (x0 leads x1, x2, x3 by 1, 3, 5): A[0,1] = +238.2, A[0,2] = +255.1, A[0,3] = +105.3, A[1,0] = -238.2. So A[i,j] > 0 means row i leads column j, same as Nolte's convention; the magnitude is not monotone in the delay. If the REVIEW M1 bypass were fixed by mirroring (Undirected.multivariate), the antisymmetric matrix would be replaced by its upper triangle mirrored and the sign of the lower triangle would be lost.

metric_name_standard: phase locking value (multitaper, taper-averaged), band mean / band max
canonical_ref: Lachaux, Rodriguez, Martinerie & Varela 1999, Human Brain Mapping 8:194-208 ("Measuring phase synchrony in brain signals"), PLV definition in Methods (equation number not re-checked); multitaper/Fourier formulation reviewed in Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front. canonical_definition: PLV(f) = | (1/N) sum_{n=1}^{N} exp(i (phi_x,n(f) - phi_y,n(f))) |, the modulus of the mean unit phasor of the relative phase over N trials (independent realisations) at fixed frequency (and latency); range [0, 1]; bias E[PLV] ~ sqrt(pi/(4N)) under independence.
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.6, p.15 (supplement.txt:686-699): "The phase locking value (PLV) [65] is computed using the same formula as coherence, however applied to the amplitude-normalized Fourier transformed signals (i.e., normalized by individual tapers), which is argued to make it a more robust measure of phase synchronization than the coherence measures presented earlier [59]." We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2], where fs/2 is the Nyquist frequency and f0 = 4/T ... we take the mean (mean) and the maximum (max) values of each measure over three ranges ... fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]." implemented_as: Whole series (after pyspi preprocessing; dependency subtracts each channel mean) tapered by K=5 DPSS tapers (NW=3), FFT length next_fast_len(T). Per bin f_m = m/n_fft (m = 0..n_fft/2-1, DC included, Nyquist excluded): PLV_ij(f) = | (1/5) sum_k S_ij,k / |S_ij,k| |, S_ij,k = X_i,k conj(X_j,k). Expectation is over the 5 tapers of one window (no trials, no time windows). pyspi then applies np.absolute (redundant, already non-negative) and np.nanmean or np.nanmax over bins with fmin <= f <= fmax. A bin is NaN if any |S_ij,k| = 0 (0/0), dropped by nan-aggregation. Pairwise-separable (probe: P-channel and 2-channel results identical).

metric_name_standard: phase locking value (multitaper, taper-averaged), band mean / band max
canonical_ref: Lachaux, Rodriguez, Martinerie & Varela 1999, Human Brain Mapping 8:194-208 ("Measuring phase synchrony in brain signals"), PLV definition in Methods (equation number not re-checked); multitaper/Fourier formulation reviewed in Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front. canonical_definition: PLV(f) = | (1/N) sum_{n=1}^{N} exp(i (phi_x,n(f) - phi_y,n(f))) |, the modulus of the mean unit phasor of the relative phase over N trials (independent realisations) at fixed frequency (and latency); range [0, 1]; bias E[PLV] ~ sqrt(pi/(4N)) under independence.
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.6, p.15 (supplement.txt:686-699): "The phase locking value (PLV) [65] is computed using the same formula as coherence, however applied to the amplitude-normalized Fourier transformed signals (i.e., normalized by individual tapers), which is argued to make it a more robust measure of phase synchronization than the coherence measures presented earlier [59]." GitBook spectral.md:297-316 (same wording, identifiers plv_multitaper_{mean,max}_...). We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2], where fs/2 is the Nyquist frequency and f0 = 4/T ... we take the mean (mean) and the maximum (max) values of each measure over three ranges ... fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]." implemented_as: Whole series (after pyspi preprocessing; dependency subtracts each channel mean) tapered by K=5 DPSS tapers (NW=3), FFT length next_fast_len(T). Per bin f_m = m/n_fft (m = 0..n_fft/2-1, DC included, Nyquist excluded): PLV_ij(f) = | (1/5) sum_k S_ij,k / |S_ij,k| |, S_ij,k = X_i,k conj(X_j,k). Expectation is over the 5 tapers of one window (no trials, no time windows). pyspi then applies np.absolute (redundant, already non-negative) and np.nanmean or np.nanmax over bins with fmin <= f <= fmax. A bin is NaN if any |S_ij,k| = 0 (0/0), dropped by nan-aggregation. Pairwise-separable (probe: P-channel and 2-channel results identical).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniform bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins (n_fft = next_fast_len(T) = T for the probed powers of two) at f = m/n_fft, m = 0..n_fft/2-1, i.e. DC included, Nyquist excluded, f0 = 0 not 4/T (probe: 32/128/512/2048 bins at T = 64/256/1024/4096, first bin 0.0, last 0.484375 at T=64). Band rule freq >= fmin & freq <= fmax is inclusive at both ends, so the f = 0.25 bin is counted in both the low and the high band whenever 0.25 is a grid point, i.e. when n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T) is a multiple of 4; this holds for every manifest size (T = 64/256/1024/4096) and for the 512- and 1024-sample EEG windows (probe: low band 17 bins 0..0.25, high band 16 bins 0.25..0.484 at T=64), but not in general (probe grid_tie.py: at T = 30 and 250, n_fft = 30 and 250 has no 0.25 bin and the inclusive low/high counts are 8/7 and 63/62). Taper count: K = 5 tapers pass the eigenvalue > 0.9 filter at every probed T >= 10 (10, 16, 30, 64, 100, 250, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 4096); at T = 7 and 8 (n_fft = 8) only 4 tapers are kept and n_observations = 4, so every K = 5 statement in this record assumes T >= 10. (2) Otherwise consistent: per-taper amplitude normalisation S/|S| equals normalising each Fourier coefficient before forming the coherence-type ratio. (3) Values are symmetric, so the missing symmetrisation (REVIEW M1; tests/README.md bug 5 before b2f6d7e) has no effect for this unit.
deviation_from_canonical: Expectation over K=5 tapers of a single window instead of over trials (or time): the sample size behind each per-bin PLV is fixed at 5 regardless of T, so the independence-null level is E|mean of 5 unit phasors| = 0.4016 (Monte Carlo, probe3; asymptotic sqrt(pi/(4K)) = 0.396) at every T (probe iid_gaussian band mean: 0.418, 0.398, 0.395, 0.402 at T = 64, 256, 1024, 4096) and does not shrink with longer data. Taper estimates are only approximately independent (orthogonal DPSS on a locally flat spectrum). Phase is taken per FFT bin of the whole window, not from narrowband-filtered instantaneous phase. The DC bin has a real-valued cross-spectrum (relative phase 0 or pi only; per-bin PLV in {0.2, 0.6, 1.0}; probe delayed_noise T=256 DC PLV[0,1] = 0.6) and enters the fmin=0 bands. Band mean / band max over bins is a pyspi summary with no canonical counterpart; band max is a maximum over n_fft/2 biased estimates.
units_and_range: dimensionless, in [0, 1], symmetric, non-negative; null (independent) level ~0.40 for the mean variants at every T; max variants under the null grow with the number of bins (probe iid_gaussian upper-triangle mean of plv_max: 0.835, 0.934, 0.951, 0.978 at T = 64, 256, 1024, 4096); identical channels give 1.0 (shared_envelope x2==x0). NaN only if all bins in the band are NaN.
direction_convention: Undirected. PLV_ij(f) = |E_k exp(i(phi_i - phi_j))| is invariant to conjugation, so A[i,j] = A[j,i] exactly (probe: max |A - A^T| = 0.0 on iid_gaussian at every T and on delayed_noise). The value carries no lead/lag information.

metric_name_standard: phase lag index, SIGNED variant (mean sign of the imaginary cross-spectrum over tapers), band mean / band max
canonical_ref: Stam, Nolte & Daffertshofer 2007, Human Brain Mapping 28:1178-1193 ("Phase lag index: assessment of functional connectivity from multi channel EEG and MEG with diminished bias from common sources"), PLI definition in Methods; cross-spectral form PLI = |E{sign(Im X)}| in Vinck et al. 2011, NeuroImage 55:1548-1565 (section on PLI)
canonical_definition: PLI = | < sign( sin(dphi(t_k)) ) > |, the absolute value of the average sign of the relative phase (Stam 2007: average over time samples t_k of Hilbert phases); in cross-spectral form PLI = |E{sign(Im X_ij)}| with the expectation over trials. Range [0, 1], symmetric, 0 for zero-lag (volume-conducted) coupling.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labels say unsigned/undirected but values are signed and antisymmetric (mean variants) [already documented: M3, bug 5]. (2) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniform bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins (n_fft = next_fast_len(T) = T for the probed powers of two) at f = m/n_fft, m = 0..n_fft/2-1, i.e. DC included, Nyquist excluded, f0 = 0 not 4/T (probe: 32/128/512/2048 bins at T = 64/256/1024/4096, first bin 0.0, last 0.484375 at T=64). Band rule freq >= fmin & freq <= fmax is inclusive at both ends, so the f = 0.25 bin is counted in both the low and the high band whenever 0.25 is a grid point, i.e. when n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T) is a multiple of 4; this holds for every manifest size (T = 64/256/1024/4096) and for the 512- and 1024-sample EEG windows (probe: low band 17 bins 0..0.25, high band 16 bins 0.25..0.484 at T=64), but not in general (probe grid_tie.py: at T = 30 and 250, n_fft = 30 and 250 has no 0.25 bin and the inclusive low/high counts are 8/7 and 63/62). Taper count: K = 5 tapers pass the eigenvalue > 0.9 filter at every probed T >= 10 (10, 16, 30, 64, 100, 250, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 4096); at T = 7 and 8 (n_fft = 8) only 4 tapers are kept and n_observations = 4, so every K = 5 statement in this record assumes T >= 10. (3) "averaging the sign of the (per taper) phase difference" matches sign(Im S) = sign(sin dphi). (4) The max variants are neither symmetric nor antisymmetric (max over f of an antisymmetric per-bin matrix).
deviation_from_canonical: (1) No absolute value: signed E[sign Im S] instead of |E[sign Im S]| (M3). (2) Expectation over 5 tapers of one window instead of time samples (Stam) or trials (Vinck), so per-bin values are quantised to multiples of 0.2 and have a large variance at every T. (3) Band mean of the signed per-bin value cancels where the lag sign flips with frequency: probe delayed_noise T=1024, x3 = x0 delayed 5 samples: band mean 0.180 vs mean |PLI(f)| 0.937 (delay 3: 0.302 vs 0.933); this is the abs(mean) vs mean(abs) point raised in M3. (4) DC bin always contributes PLI = 0 to fmin=0 bands (dilution by (n-1)/n). (5) Band max of a signed quantity: pli_max[i,j] = max_f PLI_ij(f), pli_max[j,i] = -min_f PLI_ij(f).

metric_name_standard: phase lag index, SIGNED variant (mean sign of the imaginary cross-spectrum over tapers), band mean / band max
canonical_ref: Stam, Nolte & Daffertshofer 2007, Human Brain Mapping 28:1178-1193 ("Phase lag index: assessment of functional connectivity from multi channel EEG and MEG with diminished bias from common sources"), PLI definition in Methods; cross-spectral form PLI = |E{sign(Im X)}| in Vinck et al. 2011, NeuroImage 55:1548-1565 (section on PLI)
canonical_definition: PLI = | < sign( sin(dphi(t_k)) ) > |, the absolute value of the average sign of the relative phase (Stam 2007: average over time samples t_k of Hilbert phases); in cross-spectral form PLI = |E{sign(Im X_ij)}| with the expectation over trials. Range [0, 1], symmetric, 0 for zero-lag (volume-conducted) coupling.
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.8, p.15 (supplement.txt:715-750): "The phase lag index (PLI) [67] measures phase synchronization by averaging the sign of the (per taper) phase difference [59]." Labels (config.yaml:768-774, spectral.py:182): undirected, unsigned. GitBook spectral.md:233-254 (same wording). Grid/band text: supplement §1.5, pp.12-13 (heading supplement.txt:570; grid text :582-599; the pack line ranges for §1.5.6-1.5.8 are offset, actual headings at :686, :701, :715): "Each measure is based on the cross- and power-spectral densities at a given frequency and sampling rate, which is estimated via the multitaper technique ... We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2], where fs/2 is the Nyquist frequency and f0 = 4/T ... we take the mean (mean) and the maximum (max) values of each measure over three ranges ... fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]." Same text on GitBook spectral.md:16-20.

implemented_as: Same multitaper front end as PLV (K=5 DPSS, NW=3, whole series, n_fft = next_fast_len(T), bins m/n_fft for m = 0..n_fft/2-1). Per bin: PLI_ij(f) = (1/5) sum_k sign(Im S_ij,k), S_ij,k = X_i,k conj(X_j,k). Signed: no absolute value is taken anywhere (connectivity.py:571-574 returns E[sign Im S]; the docstring at :554-556 states it is the signed version). deviation_from_documented: (1) Labels say unsigned/undirected but values are signed and antisymmetric (mean variants) [already documented: M3, bug 5]. (2) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniform bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins (n_fft = next_fast_len(T) = T for the probed powers of two) at f = m/n_fft, m = 0..n_fft/2-1, i.e. DC included, Nyquist excluded, f0 = 0 not 4/T (probe: 32/128/512/2048 bins at T = 64/256/1024/4096, first bin 0.0, last 0.484375 at T=64). Band rule freq >= fmin & freq <= fmax is inclusive at both ends, so the f = 0.25 bin is counted in both the low and the high band whenever 0.25 is a grid point, i.e. when n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T) is a multiple of 4; this holds for every manifest size (T = 64/256/1024/4096) and for the 512- and 1024-sample EEG windows (probe: low band 17 bins 0..0.25, high band 16 bins 0.25..0.484 at T=64), but not in general (probe grid_tie.py: at T = 30 and 250, n_fft = 30 and 250 has no 0.25 bin and the inclusive low/high counts are 8/7 and 63/62). Taper count: K = 5 tapers pass the eigenvalue > 0.9 filter at every probed T >= 10 (10, 16, 30, 64, 100, 250, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 4096); at T = 7 and 8 (n_fft = 8) only 4 tapers are kept and n_observations = 4, so every K = 5 statement in this record assumes T >= 10. (3) "averaging the sign of the (per taper) phase difference" matches sign(Im S) = sign(sin dphi). (4) The max variants are neither symmetric nor antisymmetric (max over f of an antisymmetric per-bin matrix).
deviation_from_canonical: (1) No absolute value: signed E[sign Im S] instead of |E[sign Im S]| (M3). (2) Expectation over 5 tapers of one window instead of time samples (Stam) or trials (Vinck), so per-bin values are quantised to multiples of 0.2 and have a large variance at every T. (3) Band mean of the signed per-bin value cancels where the lag sign flips with frequency: probe delayed_noise T=1024, x3 = x0 delayed 5 samples: band mean 0.180 vs mean |PLI(f)| 0.937 (delay 3: 0.302 vs 0.933); this is the abs(mean) vs mean(abs) point raised in M3. (4) DC bin always contributes PLI = 0 to fmin=0 bands (dilution by (n-1)/n). (5) Band max of a signed quantity: pli_max[i,j] = max_f PLI_ij(f), pli_max[j,i] = -min_f PLI_ij(f).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labels unsigned/undirected but values signed and antisymmetric for the mean variants [REVIEW M3 and M1; tests/README.md bug 5 names PLI only]. (2) The weighting is by |Im S| of the per-taper cross-spectrum, not by the imaginary coherence as the text says (wording). (3) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniform bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins (n_fft = next_fast_len(T) = T for the probed powers of two) at f = m/n_fft, m = 0..n_fft/2-1, i.e. DC included, Nyquist excluded, f0 = 0 not 4/T (probe: 32/128/512/2048 bins at T = 64/256/1024/4096, first bin 0.0, last 0.484375 at T=64). Band rule freq >= fmin & freq <= fmax is inclusive at both ends, so the f = 0.25 bin is counted in both the low and the high band whenever 0.25 is a grid point, i.e. when n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T) is a multiple of 4; this holds for every manifest size (T = 64/256/1024/4096) and for the 512- and 1024-sample EEG windows (probe: low band 17 bins 0..0.25, high band 16 bins 0.25..0.484 at T=64), but not in general (probe grid_tie.py: at T = 30 and 250, n_fft = 30 and 250 has no 0.25 bin and the inclusive low/high counts are 8/7 and 63/62). metric_name_standard: weighted phase lag index, SIGNED variant (E[Im S] / E[|Im S|] over tapers), band mean / band max
canonical_ref: Vinck, Oostenveld, van Wingerden, Battaglia & Pennartz 2011, NeuroImage 55:1548-1565 ("An improved index of phase-synchronization for electrophysiological data in the presence of volume-conduction, noise and sample-size bias"), wPLI definition (equation number not re-checked)
canonical_definition: Phi = |E{Im X}| / E{|Im X|}, X the cross-spectrum per trial (observation); equivalently |E{|Im X| sign(Im X)}| / E{|Im X|}; range [0, 1], symmetric.
