deviation_from_documented: (1) Labels unsigned/undirected but values signed and antisymmetric for the mean variants [REVIEW M3 and M1; tests/README.md bug 5 names PLI only]. (2) The weighting is by |Im S| of the per-taper cross-spectrum, not by the imaginary coherence as the text says (wording). (3) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniform bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins (n_fft = next_fast_len(T) = T for the probed powers of two) at f = m/n_fft, m = 0..n_fft/2-1, i.e. DC included, Nyquist excluded, f0 = 0 not 4/T (probe: 32/128/512/2048 bins at T = 64/256/1024/4096, first bin 0.0, last 0.484375 at T=64). Band rule freq >= fmin & freq <= fmax is inclusive at both ends, so the f = 0.25 bin is counted in both the low and the high band whenever 0.25 is a grid point, i.e. when n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T) is a multiple of 4; this holds for every manifest size (T = 64/256/1024/4096) and for the 512- and 1024-sample EEG windows (probe: low band 17 bins 0..0.25, high band 16 bins 0.25..0.484 at T=64), but not in general (probe grid_tie.py: at T = 30 and 250, n_fft = 30 and 250 has no 0.25 bin and the inclusive low/high counts are 8/7 and 63/62). Taper count: K = 5 tapers pass the eigenvalue > 0.9 filter at every probed T >= 10 (10, 16, 30, 64, 100, 250, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 4096); at T = 7 and 8 (n_fft = 8) only 4 tapers are kept and n_observations = 4, so every K = 5 statement in this record assumes T >= 10. (4) Max variants are asymmetric.
deviation_from_canonical: (1) Signed numerator E[Im S] instead of |E[Im S]| (M3). (2) Expectation over 5 tapers of one window instead of trials. (3) The absolute eps floor (connectivity.py:600) maps an all-zero imaginary part to 0 instead of undefined, and makes the value scale-dependent for raw input with tiny amplitude: probe delayed_noise T=256 with normalise=False, A[0,1] = 0.9536 at scale 1 and 1e-6 but 6.2e-17 at scale 1e-8 and 6.2e-21 at 1e-10 (check run spectral.wpli|delayed_noise|256|kernel|scale-canon; the raw mean Im S once the denominator is floored to 1) (PLI, PLV, dswPLI unchanged). (4) Signed band means cancel across frequency for delays (probe delayed_noise T=1024 delay 5: mean wPLI 0.199, delay 3: 0.319, delay 1: 0.957). (5) Band max of a signed quantity: asymmetric.

metric_name_standard: debiased (unbiased) estimator of the squared phase lag index, with tapers as observations, band mean / band max
canonical_ref: Vinck, Oostenveld, van Wingerden, Battaglia & Pennartz 2011, NeuroImage 55:1548-1565, unbiased estimator of the squared PLI (pairwise-product form; equation number not re-checked)
canonical_definition: PLI^2_unbiased = (1/(N(N-1))) sum_{j != k} sign(Im X_j) sign(Im X_k) over N independent observations; when no sign is zero this equals (N PLI_hat^2 - 1)/(N - 1) with PLI_hat = (1/N) sum sign(Im X). Targets PLI^2 (can be negative in finite samples), symmetric.

deviation_from_documented: (1) dsPLI involves no weighting by imaginary coherence (the text groups it with the weighted variations). (2) Labelled unsigned but takes negative values (M7). (3) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniform bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins (n_fft = next_fast_len(T) = T for the probed powers of two) at f = m/n_fft, m = 0..n_fft/2-1, i.e. DC included, Nyquist excluded, f0 = 0 not 4/T (probe: 32/128/512/2048 bins at T = 64/256/1024/4096, first bin 0.0, last 0.484375 at T=64). Band rule freq >= fmin & freq <= fmax is inclusive at both ends, so the f = 0.25 bin is counted in both the low and the high band whenever 0.25 is a grid point, i.e. when n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T) is a multiple of 4; this holds for every manifest size (T = 64/256/1024/4096) and for the 512- and 1024-sample EEG windows (probe: low band 17 bins 0..0.25, high band 16 bins 0.25..0.484 at T=64), but not in general (probe grid_tie.py: at T = 30 and 250, n_fft = 30 and 250 has no 0.25 bin and the inclusive low/high counts are 8/7 and 63/62). Taper count: K = 5 tapers pass the eigenvalue > 0.9 filter at every probed T >= 10 (10, 16, 30, 64, 100, 250, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 4096); at T = 7 and 8 (n_fft = 8) only 4 tapers are kept and n_observations = 4, so every K = 5 statement in this record assumes T >= 10.
deviation_from_canonical: (1) Observations are the 5 tapers of one window, not trials; the estimator is unbiased only if the 5 taper estimates are independent (approximately, for locally flat spectra; hypothesis). (2) The closed form (K PLI^2 - 1)/(K - 1) differs from the pairwise-product definition whenever some sign(Im S) = 0: then sum_k sign^2 < K. This happens exactly at DC for real input (probe: dsPLI(DC) = -0.25 on delayed_noise T=256, pairwise form gives 0) and at every bin for identical channels (shared_envelope x2==x0: A[0,2] = -0.25, pairwise form 0). Bands with fmin = 0 therefore carry an offset of -0.25/n_bins (-0.0078 full band and -0.0147 low band at T=64). (3) Band max over a 3-valued per-bin statistic reaches 1 under independence for every pair of the audit iid_gaussian dataset at T >= 256, for 0.997 of off-diagonal entries at T = 256 over 30 fresh seeds (minimum per seed 0.9; review probe, upper triangle, 1.0) and for every entry at T >= 1024 (probe sat.py; 0.78 at T = 64).
units_and_range: dimensionless; per bin in {-0.25 (DC or zero Im only), -0.2, 0.2, 1}; band values in [-0.25, 1]; negative values are valid finite-sample outcomes (M7); symmetric (probe max |A - A^T| = 0.0); null band mean ~0 (probe iid: -0.0016, -0.0223, -0.0074, -0.0004 at T = 64..4096); dspli_max = 1.0 under independence for every pair of the audit iid_gaussian dataset at T >= 256 and for every entry over 30 fresh seeds at T >= 1024, but for 0.997 of entries at T = 256 (probe sat.py), so not universally at T = 256.
direction_convention: Undirected: PLI^2 is invariant to conjugation, so A[i,j] = A[j,i] exactly (probe). No lead/lag information.

canonical_definition: PLI^2_unbiased = (1/(N(N-1))) sum_{j != k} sign(Im X_j) sign(Im X_k) over N independent observations; when no sign is zero this equals (N PLI_hat^2 - 1)/(N - 1) with PLI_hat = (1/N) sum sign(Im X). Targets PLI^2 (can be negative in finite samples), symmetric.

deviation_from_documented: (1) dsPLI involves no weighting by imaginary coherence (the text groups it with the weighted variations). (2) Labelled unsigned but takes negative values (M7). (3) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniform bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins (n_fft = next_fast_len(T) = T for the probed powers of two) at f = m/n_fft, m = 0..n_fft/2-1, i.e. DC included, Nyquist excluded, f0 = 0 not 4/T (probe: 32/128/512/2048 bins at T = 64/256/1024/4096, first bin 0.0, last 0.484375 at T=64). Band rule freq >= fmin & freq <= fmax is inclusive at both ends, so the f = 0.25 bin is counted in both the low and the high band whenever 0.25 is a grid point, i.e. when n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T) is a multiple of 4; this holds for every manifest size (T = 64/256/1024/4096) and for the 512- and 1024-sample EEG windows (probe: low band 17 bins 0..0.25, high band 16 bins 0.25..0.484 at T=64), but not in general (probe grid_tie.py: at T = 30 and 250, n_fft = 30 and 250 has no 0.25 bin and the inclusive low/high counts are 8/7 and 63/62). Taper count: K = 5 tapers pass the eigenvalue > 0.9 filter at every probed T >= 10 (10, 16, 30, 64, 100, 250, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 4096); at T = 7 and 8 (n_fft = 8) only 4 tapers are kept and n_observations = 4, so every K = 5 statement in this record assumes T >= 10.
deviation_from_canonical: (1) Observations are the 5 tapers of one window, not trials; the estimator is unbiased only if the 5 taper estimates are independent (approximately, for locally flat spectra; hypothesis). (2) The closed form (K PLI^2 - 1)/(K - 1) differs from the pairwise-product definition whenever some sign(Im S) = 0: then sum_k sign^2 < K. This happens exactly at DC for real input (probe: dsPLI(DC) = -0.25 on delayed_noise T=256, pairwise form gives 0) and at every bin for identical channels (shared_envelope x2==x0: A[0,2] = -0.25, pairwise form 0). Bands with fmin = 0 therefore carry an offset of -0.25/n_bins (-0.0078 full band and -0.0147 low band at T=64). (3) Band max over a 3-valued per-bin statistic reaches 1 under independence for every pair of the audit iid_gaussian dataset at T >= 256, for 0.997 of off-diagonal entries at T = 256 over 30 fresh seeds (minimum per seed 0.9; review probe, upper triangle, 1.0) and for every entry at T >= 1024 (probe sat.py; 0.78 at T = 64).

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labelled unsigned but takes negative values (M7). (2) Weighting is by |Im S| of the per-taper cross-spectrum, not by imaginary coherence (wording). (3) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniform bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins (n_fft = next_fast_len(T) = T for the probed powers of two) at f = m/n_fft, m = 0..n_fft/2-1, i.e. DC included, Nyquist excluded, f0 = 0 not 4/T (probe: 32/128/512/2048 bins at T = 64/256/1024/4096, first bin 0.0, last 0.484375 at T=64). Band rule freq >= fmin & freq <= fmax is inclusive at both ends, so the f = 0.25 bin is counted in both the low and the high band whenever 0.25 is a grid point, i.e. when n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T) is a multiple of 4; this holds for every manifest size (T = 64/256/1024/4096) and for the 512- and 1024-sample EEG windows (probe: low band 17 bins 0..0.25, high band 16 bins 0.25..0.484 at T=64), but not in general (probe grid_tie.py: at T = 30 and 250, n_fft = 30 and 250 has no 0.25 bin and the inclusive low/high counts are 8/7 and 63/62). Taper count: K = 5 tapers pass the eigenvalue > 0.9 filter at every probed T >= 10 (10, 16, 30, 64, 100, 250, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 4096); at T = 7 and 8 (n_fft = 8) only 4 tapers are kept and n_observations = 4, so every K = 5 statement in this record assumes T >= 10. The DC bin is NaN and therefore effectively excluded from band values.
deviation_from_canonical: Formula matches the canonical pairwise estimator exactly (algebraic identity; probe2 reproduction from the same coefficients max diff 2.2e-15). Deviations: observations are the 5 tapers of one window rather than trials (unbiasedness relies on taper independence; hypothesis); band max of a 5-observation estimate reaches 1 under independence for every pair of the audit iid_gaussian dataset at T >= 256, for 0.997 of off-diagonal entries at T = 256 over 30 fresh seeds and for every entry at T >= 1024 (probe sat.py); band aggregation is a pyspi construction.
units_and_range: dimensionless, symmetric (probe max |A - A^T| = 0.0), can be negative (M7; probe iid T=64 minimum band mean -0.18), <= 1; NaN at DC and for pairs with Im S identically 0 (shared_envelope x2==x0: A[0,2] = nan); null band mean ~0 (probe iid: 0.0139, -0.024, -0.0104, 0.0018 at T = 64..4096); dswpli_max = 1.0 for every pair of the audit iid_gaussian dataset at T >= 256 and every entry over 30 fresh seeds at T >= 1024, but for 0.997 of entries at T = 256 (probe sat.py).
direction_convention: Undirected: numerator and denominator are invariant to Im S -> -Im S, so A[i,j] = A[j,i] exactly (probe). No lead/lag information.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labelled unsigned but takes negative values (M7). (2) Weighting is by |Im S| of the per-taper cross-spectrum, not by imaginary coherence (wording). (3) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniform bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins (n_fft = next_fast_len(T) = T for the probed powers of two) at f = m/n_fft, m = 0..n_fft/2-1, i.e. DC included, Nyquist excluded, f0 = 0 not 4/T (probe: 32/128/512/2048 bins at T = 64/256/1024/4096, first bin 0.0, last 0.484375 at T=64). Band rule freq >= fmin & freq <= fmax is inclusive at both ends, so the f = 0.25 bin is counted in both the low and the high band whenever 0.25 is a grid point, i.e. when n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T) is a multiple of 4; this holds for every manifest size (T = 64/256/1024/4096) and for the 512- and 1024-sample EEG windows (probe: low band 17 bins 0..0.25, high band 16 bins 0.25..0.484 at T=64), but not in general (probe grid_tie.py: at T = 30 and 250, n_fft = 30 and 250 has no 0.25 bin and the inclusive low/high counts are 8/7 and 63/62). Taper count: K = 5 tapers pass the eigenvalue > 0.9 filter at every probed T >= 10 (10, 16, 30, 64, 100, 250, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 4096); at T = 7 and 8 (n_fft = 8) only 4 tapers are kept and n_observations = 4, so every K = 5 statement in this record assumes T >= 10. The DC bin is NaN and therefore effectively excluded from band values.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Labelled unsigned but negative values occur (M7). (2) "Not biased by the sample size" holds for independent observations; here the sample size is always K = 5 tapers (independent of T), and the target is PLV^2 (a squared scale, so values are not comparable to plv). (3) Frequency grid: documented 125 uniform bins on [f0 = 4/T, fs/2]; implemented n_fft/2 bins (n_fft = next_fast_len(T) = T for the probed powers of two) at f = m/n_fft, m = 0..n_fft/2-1, i.e. DC included, Nyquist excluded, f0 = 0 not 4/T (probe: 32/128/512/2048 bins at T = 64/256/1024/4096, first bin 0.0, last 0.484375 at T=64). Band rule freq >= fmin & freq <= fmax is inclusive at both ends, so the f = 0.25 bin is counted in both the low and the high band whenever 0.25 is a grid point, i.e. when n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T) is a multiple of 4; this holds for every manifest size (T = 64/256/1024/4096) and for the 512- and 1024-sample EEG windows (probe: low band 17 bins 0..0.25, high band 16 bins 0.25..0.484 at T=64), but not in general (probe grid_tie.py: at T = 30 and 250, n_fft = 30 and 250 has no 0.25 bin and the inclusive low/high counts are 8/7 and 63/62). Taper count: K = 5 tapers pass the eigenvalue > 0.9 filter at every probed T >= 10 (10, 16, 30, 64, 100, 250, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 4096); at T = 7 and 8 (n_fft = 8) only 4 tapers are kept and n_observations = 4, so every K = 5 statement in this record assumes T >= 10.

metric_name_standard: pairwise phase consistency (unbiased estimator of squared PLV), with tapers as observations, band mean / band max
canonical_ref: Vinck, van Wingerden, Womelsdorf, Fries & Pennartz 2010, NeuroImage 51:112-122 ("The pairwise phase consistency: a bias-free measure of rhythmic neuronal synchronization"), PPC definition (equation number not re-checked)
canonical_definition: PPC = (2/(N(N-1))) sum_{j<k} cos(theta_j - theta_k), theta_n the relative phase in observation (trial) n; equals (N PLV_hat^2 - 1)/(N - 1) = (|sum_n exp(i theta_n)|^2 - N)/(N^2 - N); unbiased for the population PLV^2 when observations are independent; range [-1/(N-1), 1], symmetric.

metric_name_standard: Directed transfer function (normalised DTF, squared), band mean / band max, bivariate nonparametric (multitaper + Wilson) estimate
canonical_ref: Kaminski M, Blinowska KJ (1991) A new method of the description of the information flow in the brain structures. Biol Cybern 65:203-210 (normalised DTF); nonparametric H via Wilson factorisation: Dhamala, Rangarajan, Ding (2008) NeuroImage 41:354-362
canonical_definition: gamma^2_ij(f) = |H_ij(f)|^2 / sum_m |H_im(f)|^2, flow from j to i, H(f) = Abar(f)^{-1} the transfer matrix of the full multivariate model; sum_j gamma^2_ij(f) = 1; reflects direct and indirect flow
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.9, p.16 (line 752): DTF 'quantifies the inflow from x -> y (according to the transfer matrix) normalized by the total inflow from all other signals into y (the row-wise sum of the spectral transfer matrix)'; same text GitBook spectral.md:107. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. Directed measures 'are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]' (§1.5, p.12). Row/column meaning of the MPI: GitBook glossary-of-terms.md:27 'The rows in this table reflect the sources while the columns reflect the targets'.

deviation_from_documented: (i) Direction: documented 'from x -> y' with rows = sources; implemented A[i, j] = flow x_j -> x_i (row = target), probe p3_pipeline.py var2_bivariate A[1,0] = 0.2617 > A[0,1] = 0.1281 for x0 -> x1. (ii) 'nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization' holds, but each ordered pair is factorised on its own 2-channel spectrum (bivariate, unconditioned on the other P-2 channels). (iii) Band rule: documented 125 bins from f0 = 4/T with closed bands; implemented: the multitaper grid k/n_fft (n_fft = T for power-of-two T, so T/2 non-negative bins, DC included, Nyquist absent) with open bands (fmin < f < fmax): DC is always dropped and the f = 0.25 bin belongs to neither half-band (p6_misc.py T=64: full band 31 bins 0.0156-0.4844, low band 15 bins ending 0.2344, high band 15 bins starting 0.2656).
deviation_from_canonical: Formula matches the squared normalised DTF exactly (p2_kernel.py, 1e-15). Deviations are in the estimation setting: (a) bivariate: H is the transfer matrix of the 2-channel marginal process, so for P > 2 it is not the multivariate DTF (for 2 channels this is the canonical DTF of that pair); (b) because H = adj(Abar)/det(Abar) in 2x2, the off-diagonal DTF equals the off-diagonal PDC exactly (p10_dc_gpdc.py 2.2e-16; pipeline p3_pipeline.py max|dtf - pdcoh| = 1.1e-16), so dtf carries no information beyond pdcoh; (c) the multitaper estimator has a fixed 5 tapers, so per-bin variance does not shrink with T and the band mean has a positive bias floor (null direction ~0.11 at T = 64..16384, p5_bias_T.py); (d) DTF is not invariant to unequal innovation variances; with a 100:1 innovation-variance ratio the null direction is estimated at 0.83 and the true direction at 0.17 (p4_delay.py), i.e. the estimated direction inverts.
units_and_range: dimensionless, squared, per-frequency value in [0, 1]; band mean/max in [0, 1]; non-negative; asymmetric; diagonal NaN; not invariant to relative scaling of channels at kernel level (p6_misc.py: x1*10 changes mean L[1,0] 0.2749 -> 0.9375), pipeline z-scoring removes that
direction_convention: A[i, j] = statfn over the band of L[0, 1] where L is the library measure on the ordered 2-channel array [x_i, x_j]; the library's [a, b] entry is the flow from channel b to channel a (H[a, b] maps innovation b into signal a; kernel probe p2_kernel.py on the exact var2_bivariate spectrum: x0 -> x1 appears at L[1, 0], L[0, 1] = 0). Hence A[i, j] = estimated flow x_j -> x_i: ROW = TARGET, COLUMN = SOURCE. Confirming evidence: exact-spectrum toy VAR(1) with x0 -> x1 gives library DTF L[1,0] = 0.1608, L[0,1] = 0 (review probe pD_kernel_directed.py); pipeline probe p3_pipeline.py (T=4096, z-scored) var2_bivariate A[1,0] = 0.2617 > A[0,1] = 0.1281 (x0 -> x1). logistic_maps (y = process 1 drives x = process 0, audit/checks/make_data.py:207 (beta_xy = 0.1, beta_yx = 0) and :309-310 (update equations)) shows A[0,1] > A[1,0] in the pipeline, but the Wilson factorisation does not converge on that dataset at T >= 1024 (60 iterations, residual 0.32-0.38; p7_wilson.py, review pF_wilson.py), so it is not used as confirming evidence. This is the opposite of the glossary's row = source convention. On delayed_noise the DTF/PDC/dcoh/ddtf matrices look row = source only because the estimator fails there (see candidates); gpdcoh on delayed_noise follows row = target.

deviation_from_documented: (i) Direction: documented 'from x -> y' with rows = sources; implemented A[i, j] = flow x_j -> x_i (row = target), probe p3_pipeline.py var2_bivariate A[1,0] = 0.2617 > A[0,1] = 0.1281 for x0 -> x1. (ii) 'nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization' holds, but each ordered pair is factorised on its own 2-channel spectrum (bivariate, unconditioned on the other P-2 channels). (iii) Band rule: documented 125 bins from f0 = 4/T with closed bands; implemented: the multitaper grid k/n_fft (n_fft = T for power-of-two T, so T/2 non-negative bins, DC included, Nyquist absent) with open bands (fmin < f < fmax): DC is always dropped and the f = 0.25 bin belongs to neither half-band (p6_misc.py T=64: full band 31 bins 0.0156-0.4844, low band 15 bins ending 0.2344, high band 15 bins starting 0.2656).
deviation_from_canonical: Formula matches the squared normalised DTF exactly (p2_kernel.py, 1e-15). Deviations are in the estimation setting: (a) bivariate: H is the transfer matrix of the 2-channel marginal process, so for P > 2 it is not the multivariate DTF (for 2 channels this is the canonical DTF of that pair); (b) because H = adj(Abar)/det(Abar) in 2x2, the off-diagonal DTF equals the off-diagonal PDC exactly (p10_dc_gpdc.py 2.2e-16; pipeline p3_pipeline.py max|dtf - pdcoh| = 1.1e-16), so dtf carries no information beyond pdcoh; (c) the multitaper estimator has a fixed 5 tapers, so per-bin variance does not shrink with T and the band mean has a positive bias floor (null direction ~0.11 at T = 64..16384, p5_bias_T.py); (d) DTF is not invariant to unequal innovation variances; with a 100:1 innovation-variance ratio the null direction is estimated at 0.83 and the true direction at 0.17 (p4_delay.py), i.e. the estimated direction inverts.
units_and_range: dimensionless, squared, per-frequency value in [0, 1]; band mean/max in [0, 1]; non-negative; asymmetric; diagonal NaN; not invariant to relative scaling of channels at kernel level (p6_misc.py: x1*10 changes mean L[1,0] 0.2749 -> 0.9375), pipeline z-scoring removes that
direction_convention: A[i, j] = statfn over the band of L[0, 1] where L is the library measure on the ordered 2-channel array [x_i, x_j]; the library's [a, b] entry is the flow from channel b to channel a (H[a, b] maps innovation b into signal a; kernel probe p2_kernel.py on the exact var2_bivariate spectrum: x0 -> x1 appears at L[1, 0], L[0, 1] = 0). Hence A[i, j] = estimated flow x_j -> x_i: ROW = TARGET, COLUMN = SOURCE. Confirming evidence: exact-spectrum toy VAR(1) with x0 -> x1 gives library DTF L[1,0] = 0.1608, L[0,1] = 0 (review probe pD_kernel_directed.py); pipeline probe p3_pipeline.py (T=4096, z-scored) var2_bivariate A[1,0] = 0.2617 > A[0,1] = 0.1281 (x0 -> x1). logistic_maps (y = process 1 drives x = process 0, audit/checks/make_data.py:207 (beta_xy = 0.1, beta_yx = 0) and :309-310 (update equations)) shows A[0,1] > A[1,0] in the pipeline, but the Wilson factorisation does not converge on that dataset at T >= 1024 (60 iterations, residual 0.32-0.38; p7_wilson.py, review pF_wilson.py), so it is not used as confirming evidence. This is the opposite of the glossary's row = source convention. On delayed_noise the DTF/PDC/dcoh/ddtf matrices look row = source only because the estimator fails there (see candidates); gpdcoh on delayed_noise follows row = target.

metric_name_standard: Directed transfer function (normalised DTF, squared), band mean / band max, bivariate nonparametric (multitaper + Wilson) estimate
canonical_ref: Kaminski M, Blinowska KJ (1991) A new method of the description of the information flow in the brain structures. Biol Cybern 65:203-210 (normalised DTF); nonparametric H via Wilson factorisation: Dhamala, Rangarajan, Ding (2008) NeuroImage 41:354-362
canonical_definition: gamma^2_ij(f) = |H_ij(f)|^2 / sum_m |H_im(f)|^2, flow from j to i, H(f) = Abar(f)^{-1} the transfer matrix of the full multivariate model; sum_j gamma^2_ij(f) = 1; reflects direct and indirect flow
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.9, p.16 (line 752): DTF 'quantifies the inflow from x -> y (according to the transfer matrix) normalized by the total inflow from all other signals into y (the row-wise sum of the spectral transfer matrix)'; same text GitBook spectral.md:107. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. Directed measures 'are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]' (§1.5, p.12). Row/column meaning of the MPI: GitBook glossary-of-terms.md:27 'The rows in this table reflect the sources while the columns reflect the targets'.

deviation_from_documented: (i) Direction: documented 'from x -> y' with rows = sources; implemented A[i, j] = flow x_j -> x_i (row = target), probe p3_pipeline.py var2_bivariate A[1,0] = 0.2617 > A[0,1] = 0.1281 for x0 -> x1. (ii) 'nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization' holds, but each ordered pair is factorised on its own 2-channel spectrum (bivariate, unconditioned on the other P-2 channels). (iii) Band rule: documented 125 bins from f0 = 4/T with closed bands; implemented: the multitaper grid k/n_fft (n_fft = T for power-of-two T, so T/2 non-negative bins, DC included, Nyquist absent) with open bands (fmin < f < fmax): DC is always dropped and the f = 0.25 bin belongs to neither half-band (p6_misc.py T=64: full band 31 bins 0.0156-0.4844, low band 15 bins ending 0.2344, high band 15 bins starting 0.2656).
deviation_from_canonical: Formula matches the squared normalised DTF exactly (p2_kernel.py, 1e-15). Deviations are in the estimation setting: (a) bivariate: H is the transfer matrix of the 2-channel marginal process, so for P > 2 it is not the multivariate DTF (for 2 channels this is the canonical DTF of that pair); (b) because H = adj(Abar)/det(Abar) in 2x2, the off-diagonal DTF equals the off-diagonal PDC exactly (p10_dc_gpdc.py 2.2e-16; pipeline p3_pipeline.py max|dtf - pdcoh| = 1.1e-16), so dtf carries no information beyond pdcoh; (c) the multitaper estimator has a fixed 5 tapers, so per-bin variance does not shrink with T and the band mean has a positive bias floor (null direction ~0.11 at T = 64..16384, p5_bias_T.py); (d) DTF is not invariant to unequal innovation variances; with a 100:1 innovation-variance ratio the null direction is estimated at 0.83 and the true direction at 0.17 (p4_delay.py), i.e. the estimated direction inverts.
units_and_range: dimensionless, squared, per-frequency value in [0, 1]; band mean/max in [0, 1]; non-negative; asymmetric; diagonal NaN; not invariant to relative scaling of channels at kernel level (p6_misc.py: x1*10 changes mean L[1,0] 0.2749 -> 0.9375), pipeline z-scoring removes that
direction_convention: A[i, j] = statfn over the band of L[0, 1] where L is the library measure on the ordered 2-channel array [x_i, x_j]; the library's [a, b] entry is the flow from channel b to channel a (H[a, b] maps innovation b into signal a; kernel probe p2_kernel.py on the exact var2_bivariate spectrum: x0 -> x1 appears at L[1, 0], L[0, 1] = 0). Hence A[i, j] = estimated flow x_j -> x_i: ROW = TARGET, COLUMN = SOURCE. Confirming evidence: exact-spectrum toy VAR(1) with x0 -> x1 gives library DTF L[1,0] = 0.1608, L[0,1] = 0 (review probe pD_kernel_directed.py); pipeline probe p3_pipeline.py (T=4096, z-scored) var2_bivariate A[1,0] = 0.2617 > A[0,1] = 0.1281 (x0 -> x1). logistic_maps (y = process 1 drives x = process 0, audit/checks/make_data.py:207 (beta_xy = 0.1, beta_yx = 0) and :309-310 (update equations)) shows A[0,1] > A[1,0] in the pipeline, but the Wilson factorisation does not converge on that dataset at T >= 1024 (60 iterations, residual 0.32-0.38; p7_wilson.py, review pF_wilson.py), so it is not used as confirming evidence. (ii) 'nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization' holds, but each ordered pair is factorised on its own 2-channel spectrum (bivariate, unconditioned on the other P-2 channels); this pairwise fit agrees with the section keyword 'bivariate' (supplement.txt:775) and departs only from a multivariate reading of the factorisation sentence. (iii) Band rule: documented 125 bins from f0 = 4/T with closed bands; implemented: the multitaper grid k/n_fft (n_fft = T for power-of-two T, so T/2 non-negative bins, DC included, Nyquist absent) with open bands (fmin < f < fmax): DC is always dropped and the f = 0.25 bin belongs to neither half-band (p6_misc.py T=64: full band 31 bins 0.0156-0.4844, low band 15 bins ending 0.2344, high band 15 bins starting 0.2656). deviation_from_canonical: Formula deviates: the library returns |H_ij|^2 / sqrt(sum_k |H_ik|^2) (= |H_ij| * sqrt(DTF_ij)), which (a) contains no innovation variances (sigma_i cancels; canonical weights by the SOURCE variance sigma_j), (b) mixes powers (squared numerator, square-root denominator), so it is neither the squared nor the modulus DC, (c) is unbounded (p2_kernel.py max 1.606 on the exact var2 spectrum; p3_pipeline.py logistic_maps A[0,1] = 94.46; delayed_noise A[0,k] about 2.9), (d) is not invariant to channel scaling at kernel level (p6_misc.py x1*10: 0.3661 -> 6.3443). Canonical squared DC for 2 channels equals canonical gPDC off-diagonal (p10_dc_gpdc.py 2.2e-16), so the canonical bivariate quantity is what gpdcoh already reports. Hence A[i, j] = estimated flow x_j -> x_i: ROW = TARGET, COLUMN = SOURCE. what_changed: spectral_connectivity 1.1.2 weights by the noise variance of the TARGET row, which cancels, and mixes powers: the result |H_ij| sqrt(DTF_ij) is neither the squared nor the modulus directed coherence of Baccala et al. 1998 (Eq. 21: gamma_ij = sigma_jj H_ij / sqrt(S_i), Eq. 22: S_i = sum_j sigma_jj^2 |H_ij|^2, checked on the scanned paper p.43), is unbounded (up to 2833 in pyspi), not scale invariant, and the formula alone can reverse the direction relative to the canonical DC: on the exact spectrum of a bidirectional VAR(1) (A1 = [[0.2, b], [a, 0.2]], a = 0.4, b = 0.45, innovation SDs 1 and 0.1) the as-coded band-mean A[1,0] - A[0,1] is -0.040 while the canonical squared DC gives +0.937 (a = 0.4, b = 0.5, SDs 1 and 0.2: -0.083 vs +0.786; scratchpad wf4b_low-spectral/probe_directed_population.py (numpy only, exact VAR(1) spectrum, library formula transcribed from spectral_connectivity/connectivity.py:800-805 and :1222-1238)). These two cases are on the raw channel scale, which pyspi sees only with normalise=False: on unit-variance channels, as pyspi's default z-scoring gives, the same two systems have as-coded A[1,0] - A[0,1] = +0.612 and +0.531, the sign of the canonical DC. For two channels the canonical squared DC equals the off-diagonal squared gPDC (2.2e-16..3.9e-16), i.e. what gpdcoh reports. score_rubric_note: Anchor 2, with 'sign' read as the direction (the sign of A[1,0] - A[0,1]), because the values themselves are non-negative. On the exact spectrum of a bidirectional VAR(1), the as-coded band mean A[1,0] - A[0,1] is -0.040, while canonical squared DC gives +0.937.
what_changed: spectral_connectivity 1.1.2 weights by the noise variance of the TARGET row, which cancels, and mixes powers: the result |H_ij| sqrt(DTF_ij) is neither the squared nor the modulus directed coherence of Baccala et al. 1998 (Eq. 21: gamma_ij = sigma_jj H_ij / sqrt(S_i), Eq. 22: S_i = sum_j sigma_jj^2 |H_ij|^2, checked on the scanned paper p.43), is unbounded (up to 2833 in pyspi), not scale invariant, and the formula alone can reverse the direction relative to the canonical DC: on the exact spectrum of a bidirectional VAR(1) (A1 = [[0.2, b], [a, 0.2]], a = 0.4, b = 0.45, innovation SDs 1 and 0.1) the as-coded band-mean A[1,0] - A[0,1] is -0.040 while the canonical squared DC gives +0.937 (a = 0.4, b = 0.5, SDs 1 and 0.2: -0.083 vs +0.786; scratchpad wf4b_low-spectral/probe_directed_population.py (numpy only, exact VAR(1) spectrum, library formula transcribed from spectral_connectivity/connectivity.py:800-805 and :1222-1238)). These two cases are on the raw channel scale, which pyspi sees only with normalise=False: on unit-variance channels, as pyspi's default z-scoring gives, the same two systems have as-coded A[1,0] - A[0,1] = +0.612 and +0.531, the sign of the canonical DC. Reversals also occur after z-scoring: 158 of 4000 random stable 2-channel VAR(1) systems, e.g. A1 = [[-0.522, -0.708], [-0.545, 0.031]], SDs (0.119, 0.922): canonical -0.961 against z-scored as-coded +0.043 (scratchpad/wf4b2_low-spectral_recheck/zscored_dcoh.py and zscored_search.py, numpy only). On delayed_noise the pyspi asymmetry is also opposite to the canonical DC (estimator means gpdcoh = 2x2 canonical DC 0.88 vs 0.11, as-coded dcoh 0.39 vs 2.99), but there the population of the as-coded quantity matches the designed direction (ref_truth [1,0] = 0.70, [0,1] about 0 in spectral.dcoh|delayed_noise|1024|pipeline|mc:mean-full), so that reversal is an estimator effect shared with dtf, pdcoh and ddtf, not evidence about the formula. The latest release v2.0.1 still has this formula; upstream master (commit 138f3f7f0f, unreleased 3.0) replaced it by the canonical squared DC (and changed the output to source-first). For two channels the canonical squared DC equals the off-diagonal squared gPDC (2.2e-16..3.9e-16), i.e. what gpdcoh reports. Other deviations as for dtf (bivariate, 5-taper bias, row = target, open bands). Rubric anchor 2 (shown by the exact-spectrum VAR(1) case above): non-standard formula whose direction (sign of A - A.T) can differ from canonical.

A batch must keep that whole-SPI failure or record the change. The random start from the global numpy RNG (minimum_phase_decomposition.py:54-63), which in a batched call would hit every pair, is reachable only under a numpy that still has the deprecated numpy.linalg.linalg shim (numpy < 2.4 as checked: 2.2.6 and 2.3.3 resolve xp.linalg.linalg.LinAlgError with a DeprecationWarning, 2.4.6 and 2.5.4 raise AttributeError) or a spectral_connectivity release whose handler catches xp.linalg.LinAlgError (v2.0.1 does, notes/spectral_directed.md); that rng-stream risk is conditional on such a numpy or library version and does not apply in this environment (pyproject.toml pins numpy>=2.5.4,<2.6)

metric_name_standard: Directed coherence (Baccala-Sameshima DC, a noise-variance-weighted DTF), band mean / band max, bivariate nonparametric estimate
canonical_ref: Baccala LA, Sameshima K, Ballester G, Do Valle AC, Timo-Iaria C (1998) Studying the interaction between brain structures via directed coherence and Granger causality. Applied Signal Processing 5:40-48, Eq. (21)-(24), p.43 (checked on the scanned asp.pdf linked from the GitBook: gamma_ij(f) = sigma_jj H_ij(f) / sqrt(S_i(f)), S_i(f) = sum_j sigma_jj^2 |H_ij(f)|^2, 0 <= |gamma_ij|^2 <= 1, sum_j |gamma_ij|^2 = 1; Remark 6: DTF is the case sigma_jj = 1)
canonical_definition: gamma_ij(f) = sigma_j H_ij(f) / sqrt( sum_k sigma_k^2 |H_ik(f)|^2 ) for diagonal innovation covariance (sigma_k^2 = innovation variance of source k); flow j -> i; |gamma_ij|^2 in [0, 1] with sum_j |gamma_ij|^2 = 1 (squared form sigma_j^2|H_ij|^2 / sum_k sigma_k^2 |H_ik|^2)
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.10, p.16 (line 774): 'The directed coherence [71] is obtained from the inflow of x -> y using the spectral transfer matrix (as per DTF, Sec. 1.5.9), normalized by their noise covariance'; same text GitBook spectral.md:82. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. Directed measures 'are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]' (§1.5, p.12). Row/column meaning of the MPI: GitBook glossary-of-terms.md:27 'The rows in this table reflect the sources while the columns reflect the targets'. Section keywords (supplement.txt:775): 'directed, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent'.

implemented_as: Same per-pair multitaper + Wilson pipeline as dtf. Library formula (connectivity.py:800-805): sqrt(nv) * |H|^2 / _total_inflow(H, nv) with nv = diag(Sigma) broadcast along the ROW (target) axis by _get_noise_variance (shape (..., 1, n, 1)). The row noise variance cancels: value = sigma_i |H_ij|^2 / (sigma_i sqrt(sum_k |H_ik|^2)) = |H_ij|^2 / sqrt(sum_k |H_ik|^2) = |H_ij| * sqrt(DTF_ij). Kernel probe p2_kernel.py: library equals |H|^2/sqrt(sum|H|^2) to 1.8e-15 and differs from the canonical squared DC by up to 0.61; range observed up to 1.606 on the exact var2 spectrum. A[i, j] = nanmean/nanmax over fmin < f < fmax of that quantity at [0, 1].

metric_name_standard: Partial directed coherence (squared |PDC|^2), band mean / band max, bivariate nonparametric estimate
canonical_ref: Baccala LA, Sameshima K (2001) Partial directed coherence: a new concept in neural structure determination. Biol Cybern 84:463-474
canonical_definition: pi_ij(f) = Abar_ij(f) / sqrt( sum_k |Abar_kj(f)|^2 ), Abar(f) = I - sum_r A_r e^{-i2pi f r} of the FULL multivariate VAR; flow j -> i normalised by the total outflow of source j; sum_i |pi_ij|^2 = 1; pi_ij = 0 iff no direct j -> i coupling (conditional on all other channels). Defined as a modulus quantity (|pi| in [0, 1])
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.11, p.17 (line 789): 'The partial directed coherence [72] from x -> y is the inflow (as per DTF, Sec. 1.5.9) normalized by the total outflow from all other signals into y (the column-wise sum of the spectral transfer matrix)'; same text GitBook spectral.md:210. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. Directed measures 'are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]' (§1.5, p.12). Row/column meaning of the MPI: GitBook glossary-of-terms.md:27 'The rows in this table reflect the sources while the columns reflect the targets'. Section keywords (supplement.txt:790): 'directed, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent'.

what_changed: The formula is the canonical squared PDC (fp-exact), but PDC's defining property, partialisation on all other channels so that it vanishes without a direct link, is lost because every ordered pair is fitted as its own 2-channel model: on var2_chain the conditioned PDC(0->2) is 0 while the bivariate population value is 0.0887 and pyspi reports 0.2117. In 2x2, H = adj(A)/det(A) makes the off-diagonal |PDC|^2 identical to DTF, so for any P pdcoh returns exactly the dtf matrix (already documented in tests/README.md; the mechanism is the 2x2 adjugate identity). Squared rather than modulus (Baccala & Sameshima 2001 define the modulus; monotone). Estimator bias, inversion on delayed_noise, row = target and open bands as for dtf. Rubric anchor 3 (label does not describe the computation; same case as the rubric's 'dDTF bivariate' example): the output is exactly the dtf matrix for every P and every identifier (ident 7/7, 4.4e-16), so nothing partial is left and the label 'partial directed coherence' does not describe what is returned. Anchor 7 (supplement variant with bivariate instead of multivariate normalisation) was considered, because the pdcoh keywords say 'bivariate' (supplement.txt:790), and rejected: the pairwise fit does not merely renormalise PDC, it removes the partialisation that defines it, and the 2x2 adjugate identity makes the output exactly the dtf matrix. That is the situation of the rubric's own anchor-3 example 'dDTF bivariate', whose supplement section (supplement.txt:753) also carries the 'bivariate' keyword. Rescored from 4 after review: anchor 3 names this case (a conditioning measure computed on a 2-channel model), whereas anchor 4 (related but different quantity) does not. For P = 2 inputs the value equals the canonical squared PDC of the 2-channel model, which in 2x2 is itself identical to DTF.

what_changed: The formula is the canonical squared PDC (fp-exact), but PDC's defining property, partialisation on all other channels so that it vanishes without a direct link, is lost because every ordered pair is fitted as its own 2-channel model: on var2_chain the conditioned PDC(0->2) is 0 while the bivariate population value is 0.0887 and pyspi reports 0.2117. In 2x2, H = adj(A)/det(A) makes the off-diagonal |PDC|^2 identical to DTF, so for any P pdcoh returns exactly the dtf matrix (already documented in tests/README.md; the mechanism is the 2x2 adjugate identity). Squared rather than modulus (Baccala & Sameshima 2001 define the modulus; monotone). Estimator bias, inversion on delayed_noise, row = target and open bands as for dtf. Rubric anchor 3 (label does not describe the computation; same case as the rubric's 'dDTF bivariate' example): the output is exactly the dtf matrix for every P and every identifier (ident 7/7, 4.4e-16), so nothing partial is left and the label 'partial directed coherence' does not describe what is returned. Anchor 7 (supplement variant with bivariate instead of multivariate normalisation) was considered, because the pdcoh keywords say 'bivariate' (supplement.txt:790), and rejected: the pairwise fit does not merely renormalise PDC, it removes the partialisation that defines it, and the 2x2 adjugate identity makes the output exactly the dtf matrix. That is the situation of the rubric's own anchor-3 example 'dDTF bivariate', whose supplement section (supplement.txt:753) also carries the 'bivariate' keyword. Rescored from 4 after review: anchor 3 names this case (a conditioning measure computed on a 2-channel model), whereas anchor 4 (related but different quantity) does not. For P = 2 inputs the value equals the canonical squared PDC of the 2-channel model, which in 2x2 is itself identical to DTF.

metric_name_standard: Partial directed coherence (squared |PDC|^2), band mean / band max, bivariate nonparametric estimate
canonical_ref: Baccala LA, Sameshima K (2001) Partial directed coherence: a new concept in neural structure determination. Biol Cybern 84:463-474
canonical_definition: pi_ij(f) = Abar_ij(f) / sqrt( sum_k |Abar_kj(f)|^2 ), Abar(f) = I - sum_r A_r e^{-i2pi f r} of the FULL multivariate VAR; flow j -> i normalised by the total outflow of source j; sum_i |pi_ij|^2 = 1; pi_ij = 0 iff no direct j -> i coupling (conditional on all other channels). Defined as a modulus quantity (|pi| in [0, 1])
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.11, p.17 (line 789): 'The partial directed coherence [72] from x -> y is the inflow (as per DTF, Sec. 1.5.9) normalized by the total outflow from all other signals into y (the column-wise sum of the spectral transfer matrix)'; same text GitBook spectral.md:210. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. Directed measures 'are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]' (§1.5, p.12). Row/column meaning of the MPI: GitBook glossary-of-terms.md:27 'The rows in this table reflect the sources while the columns reflect the targets'. Section keywords (supplement.txt:790): 'directed, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent'.

implemented_as: Same per-pair multitaper + Wilson pipeline; Abar = inv(H) (_MVAR_Fourier_coefficients, on the non-negative bins); L = |Abar|^2 / sum over rows |Abar|^2 (column-normalised, SQUARED). what_changed: The formula is the canonical squared PDC (fp-exact), but PDC's defining property, partialisation on all other channels so that it vanishes without a direct link, is lost because every ordered pair is fitted as its own 2-channel model: on var2_chain the conditioned PDC(0->2) is 0 while the bivariate population value is 0.0887 and pyspi reports 0.2117. In 2x2, H = adj(A)/det(A) makes the off-diagonal |PDC|^2 identical to DTF, so for any P pdcoh returns exactly the dtf matrix (already documented in tests/README.md; the mechanism is the 2x2 adjugate identity). Squared rather than modulus (Baccala & Sameshima 2001 define the modulus; monotone). Estimator bias, inversion on delayed_noise, row = target and open bands as for dtf. Rubric anchor 3 (label does not describe the computation; same case as the rubric's 'dDTF bivariate' example): the output is exactly the dtf matrix for every P and every identifier (ident 7/7, 4.4e-16), so nothing partial is left and the label 'partial directed coherence' does not describe what is returned. Anchor 7 (supplement variant with bivariate instead of multivariate normalisation) was considered, because the pdcoh keywords say 'bivariate' (supplement.txt:790), and rejected: the pairwise fit does not merely renormalise PDC, it removes the partialisation that defines it, and the 2x2 adjugate identity makes the output exactly the dtf matrix. That is the situation of the rubric's own anchor-3 example 'dDTF bivariate', whose supplement section (supplement.txt:753) also carries the 'bivariate' keyword. Rescored from 4 after review: anchor 3 names this case (a conditioning measure computed on a 2-channel model), whereas anchor 4 (related but different quantity) does not. For P = 2 inputs the value equals the canonical squared PDC of the 2-channel model, which in 2x2 is itself identical to DTF.

deviation_from_canonical: Formula matches squared gPDC exactly (p2_kernel.py 8.9e-16); canonical is a modulus, library returns the square. Setting deviation: bivariate 2-channel model per pair, so not partial/conditional for P > 2 (p3_pipeline.py var2_chain A[2,0] = 0.1847 with no direct 0 -> 2). For 2 channels the off-diagonal squared gPDC equals the canonical squared directed coherence (p10_dc_gpdc.py 2.2e-16), so this unit is what canonical bivariate DC would be. Estimator bias floor ~0.11 in the null direction at every T (p5_bias_T.py). units_and_range: dimensionless, squared, per-frequency in [0, 1]; band mean/max in [0, 1]; non-negative; asymmetric; diagonal NaN; invariant to channel scaling up to estimation noise (p6_misc.py x1*10: 0.3152 -> 0.3149)
direction_convention: A[i, j] = statfn over the band of L[0, 1] where L is the library measure on the ordered 2-channel array [x_i, x_j]; the library's [a, b] entry is the flow from channel b to channel a (H[a, b] maps innovation b into signal a; kernel probe p2_kernel.py on the exact var2_bivariate spectrum: x0 -> x1 appears at L[1, 0], L[0, 1] = 0). metric_name_standard: Generalised partial directed coherence (squared |gPDC|^2), band mean / band max, bivariate nonparametric estimate
canonical_ref: Baccala LA, Sameshima K, Takahashi DY (2007) Generalized partial directed coherence. Proc. 15th Int. Conf. Digital Signal Processing (DSP 2007), IEEE, pp. 163-166
canonical_definition: pi^g_ij(f) = (1/sigma_i) Abar_ij(f) / sqrt( sum_k (1/sigma_k^2) |Abar_kj(f)|^2 ), sigma_k^2 = innovation variance of channel k, full multivariate VAR; flow j -> i; sum_i |pi^g_ij|^2 = 1; invariant to channel scaling; modulus quantity
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.11, p.17 (line 789-794): 'we include the generalized partial directed coherence (gpdoh) [73], which scales the relative strength of inflow from x -> y by their noise covariance'; same text GitBook spectral.md:210. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. Directed measures 'are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]' (§1.5, p.12). metric_name_standard: Direct directed transfer function (dDTF), band mean / band max, bivariate nonparametric estimate
canonical_ref: Korzeniewska A, Manczak M, Kaminski M, Blinowska KJ, Kasicki S (2003) Determination of information flow direction among brain structures by a modified directed transfer function (dDTF) method. J Neurosci Methods 125:195-207 (the PDF was not opened, so no equation numbers are given. The canonical form below, chi^2_ij = ffDTF^2_ij x kappa^2_ij with ffDTF^2 normalised over frequencies and inflows and kappa the partial coherence from the inverse spectral matrix, was checked against the docstring and code of direct_directed_transfer_function in upstream spectral_connectivity master 138f3f7f0f (unreleased), which cites this paper; that docstring also notes that SCoT and ConnectiviPy report the square root |ffDTF| |kappa|)
canonical_definition: full-frequency DTF F^2_ij(f) = |H_ij(f)|^2 / sum_f sum_m |H_im(f)|^2 (sum over the analysed frequency range); partial coherence C_ij(f) = M_ij(f) / sqrt(M_ii(f) M_jj(f)) from the minors (equivalently the inverse) of the full multivariate spectral matrix; dDTF chi^2_ij(f) = F^2_ij(f) C^2_ij(f), flow j -> i, nonzero only for direct coupling
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.9, p.16 (line 757-759): 'we include direct-DTF (ddtf) [70], which extends DTF by conditioning out the influence of other signals (using the partialized cross-spectrum)'; same text GitBook spectral.md:107. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. Directed measures 'are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]' (§1.5, p.12). Row/column meaning of the MPI: GitBook glossary-of-terms.md:27 'The rows in this table reflect the sources while the columns reflect the targets'. Section keywords for dtf/ddtf (supplement.txt:753): 'directed, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent'.

what_changed: The delegate computes |ffDTF| x |PDC| instead of the dDTF of Korzeniewska et al. 2003 (ffDTF^2 x squared partial coherence): PDC replaces the partial coherence and moduli replace squares. Upstream master (138f3f7f0f, unreleased) now computes ffDTF^2 x partial coherence^2; v2.0.1 still has the 1.1.2 formula. Canonical ffDTF on a T-dependent grid has the same property (the Korzeniewska form scales as T^-1 on the same exact spectrum, ddtfscale slopes -1.007/-1.002/-1.000), so only the exponent and the normalisation of the half-band identifiers by full-band energy are library-specific. metric_name_standard: Direct directed transfer function (dDTF), band mean / band max, bivariate nonparametric estimate
canonical_ref: Korzeniewska A, Manczak M, Kaminski M, Blinowska KJ, Kasicki S (2003) Determination of information flow direction among brain structures by a modified directed transfer function (dDTF) method. J Neurosci Methods 125:195-207 (the PDF was not opened, so no equation numbers are given. The canonical form below, chi^2_ij = ffDTF^2_ij x kappa^2_ij with ffDTF^2 normalised over frequencies and inflows and kappa the partial coherence from the inverse spectral matrix, was checked against the docstring and code of direct_directed_transfer_function in upstream spectral_connectivity master 138f3f7f0f (unreleased), which cites this paper; that docstring also notes that SCoT and ConnectiviPy report the square root |ffDTF| |kappa|)
canonical_definition: full-frequency DTF F^2_ij(f) = |H_ij(f)|^2 / sum_f sum_m |H_im(f)|^2 (sum over the analysed frequency range); partial coherence C_ij(f) = M_ij(f) / sqrt(M_ii(f) M_jj(f)) from the minors (equivalently the inverse) of the full multivariate spectral matrix; dDTF chi^2_ij(f) = F^2_ij(f) C^2_ij(f), flow j -> i, nonzero only for direct coupling
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.9, p.16 (line 757-759): 'we include direct-DTF (ddtf) [70], which extends DTF by conditioning out the influence of other signals (using the partialized cross-spectrum)'; same text GitBook spectral.md:107. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. Directed measures 'are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]' (§1.5, p.12). Row/column meaning of the MPI: GitBook glossary-of-terms.md:27 'The rows in this table reflect the sources while the columns reflect the targets'. Section keywords for dtf/ddtf (supplement.txt:753): 'directed, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent'.

deviation_from_documented: (i) Direction: documented 'from x -> y' with rows = sources; implemented A[i, j] = flow x_j -> x_i (row = target), probe p3_pipeline.py var2_bivariate A[1,0] = 0.0055 > A[0,1] = 0.0025 for x0 -> x1. (ii) 'nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization' holds, but each ordered pair is factorised on its own 2-channel spectrum (bivariate, unconditioned on the other P-2 channels); the section keyword 'bivariate' (supplement.txt:753) documents the pairwise fit, but the ddtf sentence promises conditioning on other signals, which a 2-channel fit cannot provide (rubric anchor 3 example 'dDTF bivariate'). (iii) Band rule: documented 125 bins from f0 = 4/T with closed bands; implemented: the multitaper grid k/n_fft (n_fft = T for power-of-two T, so T/2 non-negative bins, DC included, Nyquist absent) with open bands (fmin < f < fmax): DC is always dropped and the f = 0.25 bin belongs to neither half-band (p6_misc.py T=64: full band 31 bins 0.0156-0.4844, low band 15 bins ending 0.2344, high band 15 bins starting 0.2656). (iv) 'conditioning out the influence of other signals (using the partialized cross-spectrum)': no partialised cross-spectrum/partial coherence is computed; the conditioning factor is the PDC of a 2-channel model, so nothing is conditioned out.
deviation_from_canonical: (a) Uses |PDC| where Korzeniewska et al. use partial coherence; (b) returns the product of moduli |F||PDC| instead of the product of squares F^2 C^2 (p2_kernel.py: equals |F||pi| to 6e-17, differs from F^2 C^2 by 0.048); (c) bivariate 2-channel model, so for P > 2 nothing is partialised, and in 2x2 |PDC_ij| = sqrt(DTF_ij), i.e. the pyspi value is |F_ij| sqrt(DTF_ij); canonical bivariate dDTF would use the ordinary coherence (partial coherence with no third signal), which is symmetric; (d) length and band dependence: the ffDTF normalisation over the frequency grid is part of the canonical definition, so on an n_fft = T grid the canonical ffDTF^2 x pcoh^2 itself scales as about T^-1 (check run ddtfscale: slopes -1.007, -1.002, -1.000 on the exact var2_bivariate spectrum); the library-specific parts are only the exponent T^-1/2 (a consequence of the moduli in (b); p5_bias_T.py true direction 0.084, 0.044, 0.022, 0.011, 0.005 at T = 64..16384) and the normalisation over all T/2 non-negative bins for the half-band identifiers (fmin-0_fmax-0-25, fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5), where a band-restricted canonical analysis would normalise over the analysed band only. Values are not comparable across series lengths in either form.
units_and_range: dimensionless, non-negative, per-frequency in [0, 1] but O(1/sqrt(n_fft/2)) in practice (pipeline values about 0.002-0.018 at T=4096); asymmetric; diagonal NaN; magnitude depends on T

what_changed: The delegate computes |ffDTF| x |PDC| instead of the dDTF of Korzeniewska et al. 2003 (ffDTF^2 x squared partial coherence): PDC replaces the partial coherence and moduli replace squares. Upstream master (138f3f7f0f, unreleased) now computes ffDTF^2 x partial coherence^2; v2.0.1 still has the 1.1.2 formula. In the bivariate setting nothing is conditioned out (the value is |ffDTF_ij| sqrt(DTF_ij); a canonical 2-channel dDTF would use the ordinary coherence), so on var2_chain the indirect 0 -> 2 gets 0.0091 where the conditioned value is 0. Values depend on the series length: the full-frequency normalisation runs over every non-negative bin, so the library value scales as (T/2)^-1/2. Canonical ffDTF on a T-dependent grid has the same property (the Korzeniewska form scales as T^-1 on the same exact spectrum, ddtfscale slopes -1.007/-1.002/-1.000), so only the exponent and the normalisation of the half-band identifiers by full-band energy are library-specific. Rubric anchor 3 (dDTF bivariate: the label does not describe the computation). Anchor 2 was checked and is not supported: in 3961 random stable 2-channel VAR(1) systems with unequal innovation variances, the band-mean sign of A - A.T from the library formula never differed from the canonical 2-channel dDTF (ffDTF^2 x coherence^2) on the exact spectrum (scratchpad wf4b_low-spectral/probe_ddtf_sign.py, numpy only; re-run in Workflow 4b-2, flips 0/3961).

metric_name_standard: Direct directed transfer function (dDTF), band mean / band max, bivariate nonparametric estimate
canonical_ref: Korzeniewska A, Manczak M, Kaminski M, Blinowska KJ, Kasicki S (2003) Determination of information flow direction among brain structures by a modified directed transfer function (dDTF) method. J Neurosci Methods 125:195-207 (the PDF was not opened, so no equation numbers are given. The canonical form below, chi^2_ij = ffDTF^2_ij x kappa^2_ij with ffDTF^2 normalised over frequencies and inflows and kappa the partial coherence from the inverse spectral matrix, was checked against the docstring and code of direct_directed_transfer_function in upstream spectral_connectivity master 138f3f7f0f (unreleased), which cites this paper; that docstring also notes that SCoT and ConnectiviPy report the square root |ffDTF| |kappa|)
canonical_definition: full-frequency DTF F^2_ij(f) = |H_ij(f)|^2 / sum_f sum_m |H_im(f)|^2 (sum over the analysed frequency range); partial coherence C_ij(f) = M_ij(f) / sqrt(M_ii(f) M_jj(f)) from the minors (equivalently the inverse) of the full multivariate spectral matrix; dDTF chi^2_ij(f) = F^2_ij(f) C^2_ij(f), flow j -> i, nonzero only for direct coupling
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.9, p.16 (line 757-759): 'we include direct-DTF (ddtf) [70], which extends DTF by conditioning out the influence of other signals (using the partialized cross-spectrum)'; same text GitBook spectral.md:107. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. Directed measures 'are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]' (§1.5, p.12). Row/column meaning of the MPI: GitBook glossary-of-terms.md:27 'The rows in this table reflect the sources while the columns reflect the targets'. Section keywords for dtf/ddtf (supplement.txt:753): 'directed, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent'.
delegate_lib: spectral_connectivity==1.1.2 Connectivity.direct_directed_transfer_function (numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.17.1)
implemented_as: Same per-pair multitaper + Wilson pipeline; ffDTF = H / sqrt(sum over columns AND over all T/2 non-negative frequency bins of |H|^2) (modulus); value = |ffDTF| * sqrt(PDC^2) = |ffDTF_ij| * |PDC_ij| (product of MODULI, PDC in place of partial coherence). Kernel probe p2_kernel.py: library equals |F_ij| |pi_ij| to 6.2e-17 and differs from Korzeniewska F^2 C^2 by up to 0.048. The ffDTF normalisation is over the whole grid regardless of fmin/fmax, so values scale like 1/sqrt(T/2) (the canonical squared form on the same grid scales like 1/(T/2), see deviation (d)). A[i, j] = nanmean/nanmax of L[f, 0, 1] over fmin < f < fmax.

deviation_from_documented: (i) Direction: documented 'from x -> y' with rows = sources; implemented A[i, j] = flow x_j -> x_i (row = target), probe p3_pipeline.py var2_bivariate A[1,0] = 0.0055 > A[0,1] = 0.0025 for x0 -> x1. (ii) 'nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization' holds, but each ordered pair is factorised on its own 2-channel spectrum (bivariate, unconditioned on the other P-2 channels); the section keyword 'bivariate' (supplement.txt:753) documents the pairwise fit, but the ddtf sentence promises conditioning on other signals, which a 2-channel fit cannot provide (rubric anchor 3 example 'dDTF bivariate'). (iii) Band rule: documented 125 bins from f0 = 4/T with closed bands; implemented: the multitaper grid k/n_fft (n_fft = T for power-of-two T, so T/2 non-negative bins, DC included, Nyquist absent) with open bands (fmin < f < fmax): DC is always dropped and the f = 0.25 bin belongs to neither half-band (p6_misc.py T=64: full band 31 bins 0.0156-0.4844, low band 15 bins ending 0.2344, high band 15 bins starting 0.2656). (iv) 'conditioning out the influence of other signals (using the partialized cross-spectrum)': no partialised cross-spectrum/partial coherence is computed; the conditioning factor is the PDC of a 2-channel model, so nothing is conditioned out.
deviation_from_canonical: (a) Uses |PDC| where Korzeniewska et al. use partial coherence; (b) returns the product of moduli |F||PDC| instead of the product of squares F^2 C^2 (p2_kernel.py: equals |F||pi| to 6e-17, differs from F^2 C^2 by 0.048); (c) bivariate 2-channel model, so for P > 2 nothing is partialised, and in 2x2 |PDC_ij| = sqrt(DTF_ij), i.e. the pyspi value is |F_ij| sqrt(DTF_ij); canonical bivariate dDTF would use the ordinary coherence (partial coherence with no third signal), which is symmetric; (d) length and band dependence: the ffDTF normalisation over the frequency grid is part of the canonical definition, so on an n_fft = T grid the canonical ffDTF^2 x pcoh^2 itself scales as about T^-1 (check run ddtfscale: slopes -1.007, -1.002, -1.000 on the exact var2_bivariate spectrum); the library-specific parts are only the exponent T^-1/2 (a consequence of the moduli in (b); p5_bias_T.py true direction 0.084, 0.044, 0.022, 0.011, 0.005 at T = 64..16384) and the normalisation over all T/2 non-negative bins for the half-band identifiers (fmin-0_fmax-0-25, fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5), where a band-restricted canonical analysis would normalise over the analysed band only. Values are not comparable across series lengths in either form.
units_and_range: dimensionless, non-negative, per-frequency in [0, 1] but O(1/sqrt(n_fft/2)) in practice (pipeline values about 0.002-0.018 at T=4096); asymmetric; diagonal NaN; magnitude depends on T
direction_convention: A[i, j] = statfn over the band of L[0, 1] where L is the library measure on the ordered 2-channel array [x_i, x_j]; the library's [a, b] entry is the flow from channel b to channel a (H[a, b] maps innovation b into signal a; kernel probe p2_kernel.py on the exact var2_bivariate spectrum: x0 -> x1 appears at L[1, 0], L[0, 1] = 0). Hence A[i, j] = estimated flow x_j -> x_i: ROW = TARGET, COLUMN = SOURCE. Confirming evidence: exact-spectrum toy VAR(1) with x0 -> x1 gives library DTF L[1,0] = 0.1608, L[0,1] = 0 (review probe pD_kernel_directed.py); pipeline probe p3_pipeline.py (T=4096, z-scored) var2_bivariate A[1,0] = 0.2617 > A[0,1] = 0.1281 (x0 -> x1). logistic_maps (y = process 1 drives x = process 0, audit/checks/make_data.py:207 (beta_xy = 0.1, beta_yx = 0) and :309-310 (update equations)) shows A[0,1] > A[1,0] in the pipeline, but the Wilson factorisation does not converge on that dataset at T >= 1024 (60 iterations, residual 0.32-0.38; p7_wilson.py, review pF_wilson.py), so it is not used as confirming evidence. This is the opposite of the glossary's row = source convention. what_changed: The delegate computes |ffDTF| x |PDC| instead of the dDTF of Korzeniewska et al. 2003 (ffDTF^2 x squared partial coherence): PDC replaces the partial coherence and moduli replace squares. Upstream master (138f3f7f0f, unreleased) now computes ffDTF^2 x partial coherence^2; v2.0.1 still has the 1.1.2 formula. In the bivariate setting nothing is conditioned out (the value is |ffDTF_ij| sqrt(DTF_ij); a canonical 2-channel dDTF would use the ordinary coherence), so on var2_chain the indirect 0 -> 2 gets 0.0091 where the conditioned value is 0. Values depend on the series length: the full-frequency normalisation runs over every non-negative bin, so the library value scales as (T/2)^-1/2. metric_name_standard: group delay (time delay from the slope of the coherency phase spectrum over frequencies with significant coherence)
canonical_ref: Gotman J (1983), Measurement of small time differences between EEG channels: method and application to epileptic seizure propagation, Electroencephalography and Clinical Neurophysiology 56(5), 501-514 (as cited by the supplement [61] and by the library docstring connectivity.py:922-927). The exact Gotman procedure (coherence threshold, regression weighting, intercept handling) is from memory and not re-checked against the paper; see Open questions.
canonical_definition: phi_ij(f) = arg C_ij(f) (unwrapped); over the frequencies in the band where coherence is significant, fit phi_ij(f) = a + b f by linear regression; delay tau_ij = b / (2 pi) (in samples when fs = 1); positive tau when i leads j under S_ij = X_i X_j^*
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.3, p.13-14 (heading at supplement.txt line 630): "The group delay [61] infers a directed, average time-delay between two signals by measuring the slope of the phase differences (coherence phase, Sec. 1.5.2) as a function of the frequency (obtained through linear regression). The slope is only computed for statistically significant coherence values and the time delay is obtained by a simple rescaling of the slope by 2 pi." Keywords "directed, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent"; identifiers 107-109 gd_multitaper_delay_fs-1_fmin-0_fmax-0-5 / fmin-0_fmax-0-25 / fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; frequency grid and bands from §1.5, p.12-13 (heading at supplement.txt line 570). implemented_as: Same multitaper coherency as PSI (NW=3, 5 tapers, constant detrend, n_fft = next_fast_len(T), strict band fmin < f < fmax at full 1/n_fft resolution). For every unordered pair (i<j): z = (atanh(min(|C|, 1-eps)) - b) / sqrt(b) with b = coherence_bias(5) = 1/(2*5-2) = 0.125; one-sided p = 1 - Phi(z); Benjamini-Hochberg at 0.05 applied jointly over ALL (frequency x pair) entries of the band (the whole flattened array, so the set of other channels changes each pair's threshold); per pair keep the largest contiguous run of significant bins (scipy.ndimage.label; ties -> first), take every s-th bin of that run (s = ceil(((fmax-fmin)/50) n_fft)), discard if fewer than 3 points. Phase = numpy.unwrap(angle(C)) along the full in-band grid (before masking), masked to the kept points; OLS of phase on frequency with free intercept (mstats.linregress); slope -> A[i,j] = slope/(2 pi), A[j,i] = -slope/(2 pi); all-masked -> slope None -> NaN for the pair. Units: samples (fs = 1). Diagonal NaN.

deviation_from_documented: (1) 'unsigned' keyword/label vs signed antisymmetric output (A[j,i] = -A[i,j]; already REVIEW M6). (2) 'bivariate' keyword vs implementation: the Benjamini-Hochberg threshold is computed over all channel pairs jointly, so a pair's delay (and whether it is NaN) depends on which other channels are in the dataset (probe: var2_bivariate T=256 full band pair alone -0.4725, same pair plus 5 iid channels NaN; narrowband_f0-0.1 T=256 full band -0.0277 vs -0.9866; gauss_ar1_pair T=1024 full band -1.793 vs NaN). (3) 'statistically significant coherence values' is implemented as: one-sided Fisher-z test with bias 1/8, BH-FDR 0.05 over all frequencies x pairs, then only the LARGEST contiguous significant run, decimated to every s-th bin, minimum 3 points; none of these rules is documented. (4) Frequency grid/endpoints as for PSI: n_fft/2 bins (not 125 bins from 4/T), strict endpoints so f = 0.25 is in neither half band and DC is excluded. (5) Missing outputs are frequent and undocumented: all-NaN pairs whenever no run of >= 3 'independent' significant bins exists (probe NaN fractions: iid_gaussian 20/20 for most T and bands, var2_bivariate 2/2 for the high band at T >= 256, narrowband_f0-0.25 6/6 at T >= 1024, logistic_maps 2/2 everywhere); bands with zero bins raise ValueError (whole matrix NaN) and bands with one bin give all-NaN (EEG bands 0.5-2, 2-4, 4-6 /1024 at T=512 and T=1024).
deviation_from_canonical: Core estimator (OLS slope of unwrapped coherency phase vs frequency over significant frequencies, divided by 2 pi) matches the canonical group-delay idea; intercept is free. Differences: significance is FDR-controlled across all pairs of the dataset (a pair's estimate depends on unrelated channels); only the largest contiguous significant cluster is used; the 'independent frequency' spacing is band-relative ((fmax-fmin)/50 rounded up to bins) rather than the multitaper resolution 2W = 6/T, so at T = 64 adjacent, strongly correlated bins count as independent (s = 1 < 6) and iid_gaussian yields spurious finite delays (probe T=64 full band: A[0,2] = 0.716, A[2,3] = -0.744), while at large T the spacing exceeds the coherence bandwidth of narrowband couplings so they never reach 3 points (narrowband_f0-0.25 all NaN at T >= 1024); phase is unwrapped across the whole in-band grid before masking (check stage: this does NOT change the slope, because the kept points lie in one contiguous significant run and a grid unwrap equals the run's own unwrap up to a constant 2 pi k absorbed by the free intercept; max difference 2.8e-14 over 125 replica runs); regression is unweighted (no coherence weighting). Gotman's exact selection and weighting rules are not re-checked (open question).
units_and_range: Samples (fs = 1; cycles/sample frequency axis), signed, unbounded in principle (|delay| limited in practice by the phase slope over the band); antisymmetric (A[j,i] = -A[i,j] exactly, probe max|A + A.T| = 0 when finite); NaN on the diagonal and for every pair without a qualifying significant run; whole matrix NaN when the band has no bins (exception).
direction_convention: S_ij = X_i X_j^*; if x_j(t) = x_i(t - tau) then arg C_ij(f) = +2 pi f tau, slope = 2 pi tau and A[i,j] = +tau. Probe delayed_noise T=256 band 0-0.25 (x0 leads x1, x2, x3 by 1, 3, 5): A[0,1] = +1.033, A[0,2] = +3.008, A[0,3] = +5.081, A[1,2] = +1.973, A[2,3] = +2.075, A[1,0] = -1.033. So A[i,j] > 0 means row i leads column j by A[i,j] samples. For var2_bivariate (X -> Y) the population group delay from the true spectrum is +1.13 samples (A[0,1] > 0, X leads); pyspi's A[0,1] = -0.47 at T=256 full band is a finite-sample artefact of the significance selection, not a property of group delay (check stage, popgd runs). Workflow 4b challenge probe (scratchpad wf4b_mid-eeg/gd_localslope.py): on the 7-bin run pyspi kept at T = 256 (f = 0.176-0.199) the true VAR coherency phase has local slope +1.53 samples (whole band +1.13), while the replica gives -0.4725 (full band) and -0.5550 (low band), so the negative sign is not a local property of the true phase.

what_changed: The estimator core (OLS slope of the unwrapped coherency phase, delay = slope/2 pi, A[j,i] = -A[i,j]) is the canonical group delay and is exact on pure delays, but which bins enter is decided by library machinery that neither the supplement nor Gotman 1983 (as cited) specifies: a per-bin Fisher-z test with only 5 tapers (power does not grow with T), Benjamini-Hochberg pooled over all channel pairs (a pair's delay changes or becomes NaN when unrelated channels are added), only the largest contiguous run, and decimation by the band-relative step ceil(((fmax-fmin)/50) n_fft) instead of the multitaper bandwidth (spurious delays on white noise at T=64 and in EEG bands at T=1024; narrowband couplings never reach 3 points at large T). Result: frequent NaN, unstable or wrong-sign delays for moderately coherent couplings (var2_bivariate). Signed and antisymmetric despite the 'unsigned' label (REVIEW M6). EEG consequence (elaborates the all-NaN cases of REVIEW M6): the retained selection holds 10 gd bands with edges at k/2048 cycles/sample; at the workflow window T = 1024 (2048 Hz, 0.5 s) the 0.5-2, 2-4 and 4-6 /1024 bands (1-4, 4-8 and 8-12 Hz) hold one bin each under the strict endpoint rule and are all-NaN by construction (spectral.gd|*|eeg:* runs), and at T = 512 they hold no bin (analytic bin count), so the delegate raises ValueError and the Calculator returns an all-NaN matrix (as observed at T = 256). Rubric anchor 6 (group-delay significance machinery).

metric_name_standard: group delay (time delay from the slope of the coherency phase spectrum over frequencies with significant coherence)
canonical_ref: Gotman J (1983), Measurement of small time differences between EEG channels: method and application to epileptic seizure propagation, Electroencephalography and Clinical Neurophysiology 56(5), 501-514 (as cited by the supplement [61] and by the library docstring connectivity.py:922-927). The exact Gotman procedure (coherence threshold, regression weighting, intercept handling) is from memory and not re-checked against the paper; see Open questions.
canonical_definition: phi_ij(f) = arg C_ij(f) (unwrapped); over the frequencies in the band where coherence is significant, fit phi_ij(f) = a + b f by linear regression; delay tau_ij = b / (2 pi) (in samples when fs = 1); positive tau when i leads j under S_ij = X_i X_j^*
documented_definition: supplement §1.5.3, p.13-14 (heading at supplement.txt line 630): "The group delay [61] infers a directed, average time-delay between two signals by measuring the slope of the phase differences (coherence phase, Sec. 1.5.2) as a function of the frequency (obtained through linear regression). The slope is only computed for statistically significant coherence values and the time delay is obtained by a simple rescaling of the slope by 2 pi." Keywords "directed, linear, unsigned, bivariate, frequency-dependent"; identifiers 107-109 gd_multitaper_delay_fs-1_fmin-0_fmax-0-5 / fmin-0_fmax-0-25 / fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; frequency grid and bands from §1.5, p.12-13 (heading at supplement.txt line 570). Same text on GitBook spectral.md:130-148 (Group Delay).

implemented_as: Same multitaper coherency as PSI (NW=3, 5 tapers, constant detrend, n_fft = next_fast_len(T), strict band fmin < f < fmax at full 1/n_fft resolution). For every unordered pair (i<j): z = (atanh(min(|C|, 1-eps)) - b) / sqrt(b) with b = coherence_bias(5) = 1/(2*5-2) = 0.125; one-sided p = 1 - Phi(z); Benjamini-Hochberg at 0.05 applied jointly over ALL (frequency x pair) entries of the band (the whole flattened array, so the set of other channels changes each pair's threshold); per pair keep the largest contiguous run of significant bins (scipy.ndimage.label; ties -> first), take every s-th bin of that run (s = ceil(((fmax-fmin)/50) n_fft)), discard if fewer than 3 points. Phase = numpy.unwrap(angle(C)) along the full in-band grid (before masking), masked to the kept points; OLS of phase on frequency with free intercept (mstats.linregress); slope -> A[i,j] = slope/(2 pi), A[j,i] = -slope/(2 pi); all-masked -> slope None -> NaN for the pair. Units: samples (fs = 1). Diagonal NaN.
