metric_name_standard: magnitude coherence (|coherency|) from Morlet-wavelet cross-spectra, summarised by mean/max over a frequency band and time
canonical_ref: Coherence/coherency: Nolte et al. 2004, Clin Neurophysiol 115:2292, eqs. 1-2 (C_ij(f) = S_ij(f)/sqrt(S_ii S_jj), S = expectation over trials); Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front Syst Neurosci 9:175, coherence section (supplement ref [59]). Single-trial wavelet coherence: Lachaux et al. 2002, Neurophysiol Clin 32:157 (cross-spectrum integrated over a time window of n_co cycles before normalising); Torrence & Webster 1999, J Climate 12:2679; Grinsted et al. 2004, Nonlin Proc Geophys 11:561 (smoothing in time and scale). Equation numbers from memory, not re-checked.
canonical_definition: |C_xy(f,t)| = |<W_x(f,t) W_y*(f,t)>| / sqrt(<|W_x|^2> <|W_y|^2>) where <.> is an average over trials (or a smoothing window in time/scale for a single trial) taken BEFORE the normalisation; with no averaging the quantity is identically 1. Supplement describes it as 'the frequency domain equivalent of the squared time-domain cross correlation' (magnitude-squared coherence |C|^2).
documented_definition: Not documented as such: the nine wavelet classes are absent from pyspi/config.yaml (tests/README.md:155 'run today but are absent from pyspi/config.yaml'), from the supplement SPI list and from the GitBook page. Supplement §1.5.4, p.14 (supplement.txt heading line 644) states the opposite: PSI 'is the only spectral measure that is computed in the time-frequency domain (denoted by modifier wavelet)'; same on GitBook spectral.md:330. The closest documented text is the multitaper version: supplement §1.5.1, p.13 (supplement.txt heading line 601) / GitBook spectral.md:24-35: 'The coherence (also known as coherence magnitude and ordinary coherence ... ) is an undirected frequency-dependent measure of linear association ... the frequency domain equivalent of the squared time-domain cross correlation ... mean (mean) and maximum (max) summary statistics of the coherence for the three frequency ranges'. The 'CWT' is X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) for all 125 f up to FFT round-off (probe: max|Re X - sqrt2 x| 2.7e-15, max|Im X| 7.2e-16, ~2-5% of Im exactly 0). csd(f,t) = X_hi(f,t) conj(X_lo(f,t)) = 2 x_hi(t) x_lo(t) + i*roundoff (hi = higher channel index, lower-triangular connections), psd = |X|^2 = 2 x^2. n_epochs = 1, so every across-epoch average in the estimator is a single term. pyspi then keeps the frequencies with fmin <= f <= fmax on the 0.2..0.5 grid (21 bins for fmin-0_fmax-0-25: 0.2..0.2476; 104 for fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; all 125 for 0..0.5), applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over (freq, time) jointly, mirrors the lower triangle to the upper, sets the diagonal NaN. Estimator coh (mne_connectivity/spectral/epochs_bivariate.py:71-81): |csd/1| / sqrt(psd_x psd_y) = |2 x_hi x_lo| / (2 |x_hi| |x_lo|) = 1 at every (f,t) where x_hi x_lo != 0. Output: 1.0 for every pair and band (mean identifiers exactly 1.0; max identifiers 1 + 2^-52 = 1.0000000000000002, check stage) (probe: all 19 datasets at T=64 and T=1024, every off-diagonal entry 1.0).

deviation_from_documented: (a) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented 125 bins over [0.2, 0.5] for every T (wavelet.py:54), so the 'low' band [0, 0.25] contains only 21 bins in [0.2, 0.248] and frequencies below 0.2 are never analysed; the mne fmin argument is 5/T, not 4/T (it only masks cwt freqs when T < 25). (b) No time-frequency decomposition: n_cycles = f/7 makes every Morlet wavelet one sample long (W = sqrt(2)), so X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) at all 125 frequencies; the band choice changes nothing except which round-off pattern is averaged. (c) Aggregation runs over frequency AND time (axis=(2,3)) of per-(f,t) single-epoch values; the documentation for the multitaper versions describes a summary over frequency only. (d) Not in the documented SPI set at all (extra classes). (e) Output is the constant 1 on any input (probe), so it is not a 'measure of linear association'. mne 'coh' is |C| (magnitude), while the documentation's 'equivalent of the squared ... cross correlation' suggests |C|^2; irrelevant here because the value is 1.
deviation_from_canonical: Canonical coherence normalises a cross-spectrum averaged over trials or over a time/scale window; pyspi normalises each single-epoch, single-time-point cross-spectrum (|z|/|z| = 1) and only afterwards averages over time and frequency, so the result is identically 1 (degenerate). Additionally the wavelet carries no frequency resolution (1 sample) so even a time-averaged version would be the broadband lag-0 quantity |sum_t x_i x_j| / sqrt(sum x_i^2 sum x_j^2) = |Pearson r| (hypothesis for the time-averaged variant, not probed), identical in all bands.
units_and_range: Dimensionless, nominally [0,1]; implemented output is 1.0 off the diagonal (max identifiers 1 + 2^-52) (NaN if some x_i(t) x_j(t) = 0 at every point of the band, practically never); diagonal NaN; symmetric by the mirror.
direction_convention: Undirected. A[i,j] = A[j,i] = nanmean/nanmax over (f,t) of conn[max(i,j), min(i,j)] (mne computes lower-triangular connections only, mne_connectivity/spectral/epochs.py:276; pyspi mirrors lower->upper, wavelet.py:87-88). Magnitude is order-invariant.

metric_name_standard: coherency phase (phase of the complex coherency) from Morlet-wavelet cross-spectra, summarised by mean/max over band and time
canonical_ref: Nolte et al. 2004, Clin Neurophysiol 115:2292 (coherency C_ij = S_ij/sqrt(S_ii S_jj), phase = arg C_ij); Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front Syst Neurosci 9:175 (supplement ref [59]); time-frequency version: Lachaux et al. 2002, Neurophysiol Clin 32:157. For a pure delay d the coherency phase is linear in f (phase = -2 pi f d up to sign convention).
canonical_definition: phi_xy(f) = arg(<W_x(f,t) W_y*(f,t)>) with <.> over trials or a time window; antisymmetric: phi_yx = -phi_xy; circular quantity (a summary over frequencies needs a circular mean or a slope, cf. group delay).

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1, Data default; optional detrend first). pyspi hands mne-connectivity ONE epoch (z = moveaxis(data (P,T,1), 2, 0) -> (1,P,T)) with cwt_freqs = linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125) and cwt_n_cycles = cwt_freqs/7 (0.029..0.071 cycles). mne.morlet sets sigma_t = n_cycles/(2 pi f) = 1/(14 pi) = 0.0227 samples for every f, so the time grid arange(0, 5 sigma_t, 1) = [0] and every wavelet is the single sample W = sqrt(2)+0j (probe: 125 wavelets, length 1, value 1.41421356). The 'CWT' is X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) for all 125 f up to FFT round-off (probe: max|Re X - sqrt2 x| 2.7e-15, max|Im X| 7.2e-16, ~2-5% of Im exactly 0). csd(f,t) = X_hi(f,t) conj(X_lo(f,t)) = 2 x_hi(t) x_lo(t) + i*roundoff (hi = higher channel index, lower-triangular connections), psd = |X|^2 = 2 x^2. n_epochs = 1, so every across-epoch average in the estimator is a single term. pyspi then keeps the frequencies with fmin <= f <= fmax on the 0.2..0.5 grid (21 bins for fmin-0_fmax-0-25: 0.2..0.2476; 104 for fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; all 125 for 0..0.5), applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over (freq, time) jointly, mirrors the lower triangle to the upper, sets the diagonal NaN. Estimator cohy (epochs_bivariate.py:60-68 accumulate, :84-94 compute_con): the csd accumulator is np.zeros (+0.0) and csd is added to it (:64, :68), so an exact-zero imaginary part is stored as +0.0 whatever its sign (IEEE (+0.0) + (-0.0) = +0.0; probe narrowband_f0-0.25 T=256 pair (1,0): the raw csd has 515 exact-zero imaginary parts, 265 of them -0.0; the mne cohy tensor has the same 515 exact zeros and none is -0.0). The coherency is csd/sqrt(psd psd) = sign(x_hi x_lo) + i*eps. pyspi applies np.angle before the statistic (wavelet.py:119-120 modify_stats): angle = atan2(eps, Re), which lies within round-off (4.6e-14 at T=256, up to 2.41e-12 at T=1024, check stage) of 0 where x_hi x_lo > 0 and within 4.6e-14 of +pi or -pi where x_hi x_lo < 0. The sign of pi is set by the sign of the FFT round-off imaginary part, and every exact-zero imaginary part with negative real part gives +pi because of the +0.0 accumulator. The angles are only approximately in {0, +pi, -pi} (probe iid T=256 pair (1,0), 32000 (f,t) points: exactly 0: 416, exactly +pi: 6169, exactly -pi: 4672, none of the three: 20743; near -pi 6533, near 0 16500, near +pi 8967). mean = pi (n_{+pi} - n_{-pi}) / N up to round-off, counting angles near +-pi (probe: mean 0.23895739121367354 vs pi*(frac(+pi) - frac(-pi)) = 0.23895739121367365, difference -1.1e-16). max = pi or 1 ulp below pi whenever at least one near-+pi point exists (sweep over the 19 datasets: exactly pi for 83 of 85 pairs at T=64 and 84 of 85 at T=1024; anm T=64 gives 3.14159265358979 = pi - 1 ulp), and about 1e-31, not exactly 0, for the bit-identical pair shared_envelope (0,2) (1.0e-31 at T=64, 2.0e-31 at T=1024). The value depends on the round-off pattern, not only on the data: re-z-scoring an already z-scored input (sample changes <= 4.4e-16) moves A[0,1] from 0.2372 to 0.2682 on narrowband_f0-0.25 T=256 and from 0.1367 to -0.0383 on delayed_noise T=256 (probe wl_fix/fx1.py).

deviation_from_documented: (a) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented 125 bins over [0.2, 0.5] for every T (wavelet.py:54), so the 'low' band [0, 0.25] contains only 21 bins in [0.2, 0.248] and frequencies below 0.2 are never analysed; the mne fmin argument is 5/T, not 4/T (it only masks cwt freqs when T < 25). (b) No time-frequency decomposition: n_cycles = f/7 makes every Morlet wavelet one sample long (W = sqrt(2)), so X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) at all 125 frequencies; the band choice changes nothing except which round-off pattern is averaged. (c) Aggregation runs over frequency AND time (axis=(2,3)) of per-(f,t) single-epoch values; the documentation for the multitaper versions describes a summary over frequency only. (d) Not in the documented SPI set at all (extra classes). (e) No delay information survives: phases lie within 5e-14 of 0 or +-pi (sign of the lag-0 product; sign of pi from round-off, +pi at every exact-zero imaginary part); the documented use 'to infer a time-delayed dependence' is impossible (probe narrowband_f0-0.25, true shift pi/4 between x0 and x1: A[0,1] = 0.237, and -0.185 after reversing the channel order).
deviation_from_canonical: Canonical: arg of the averaged cross-spectrum per frequency (antisymmetric, circular). Implemented: arithmetic mean (or max) of principal angles of per-(f,t) single-epoch, single-sample cross-products over frequency and time, which with the 1-sample wavelet is pi*(n_{+pi} - n_{-pi})/N; the split between +pi and -pi depends on floating-point round-off of the FFT convolution, so the value is not a function of the data to round-off precision (re-z-scoring an already z-scored input, sample changes <= 4.4e-16, moves narrowband_f0-0.25 T=256 A[0,1] from 0.2372 to 0.2682 and delayed_noise T=256 A[0,1] from 0.1367 to -0.0383). Under channel reversal the points with a nonzero imaginary part negate, but the exact-zero imaginary parts are +0.0 in both orders (zero-initialised accumulator, epochs_bivariate.py:64, :68), so their negative-real points stay at +pi: A_rev = -A + 2 pi n(Im csd == 0 and Re csd < 0)/N (probe: narrowband_f0-0.25 T=256 0.2372 + (-0.1852) = 0.05203 = 2 pi 265/32000; delayed_noise T=256 0.1367 + (-0.0736) = 0.06303 = 2 pi 321/32000; agreement within 3e-16). Arithmetic mean of angles is not a circular mean (same aggregation issue as M4 for the multitaper version). Forced symmetric by the mirror although canonical phase is antisymmetric.
units_and_range: Radians, signed, in [-pi, pi]; 'max' variant pi or 1 ulp below pi for every non-identical pair probed (about 1e-31 for a bit-identical pair; near 0 only if no negative lag-0 product); the mean variant is fixed by the FFT round-off pattern and is not stable to input changes at round-off level (re-z-scoring an already z-scored input, sample changes <= 4.4e-16: narrowband_f0-0.25 T=256 A[0,1] 0.2372 -> 0.2682 and reversed-order value -0.1852 -> -0.2109; delayed_noise T=256 0.1367 -> -0.0383), so the snapshot value depends on the FFT implementation (a numpy.fft replay gives a different exact-zero pattern); between scipy.fft 1.17.1 (project venv, pyspi) and 1.18.1 (comparison venv, rep replay) no difference was observed on this machine (rep runs bitwise), while other CPUs and SIMD paths are untested; class labels say 'unsigned' (wavelet.py:112) though the quantity is signed; symmetric by mirror; diagonal NaN.
direction_convention: A[i,j] = A[j,i] = statistic of angle(conn[max(i,j), min(i,j)]) with conn from csd = X_hi conj(X_lo) (epochs.py:652, tril indices epochs.py:276; mirror wavelet.py:87-88). Canonical sign: positive arg(S_hi,lo) would mean a phase lead of the higher-index channel under MNE's convolution convention (unverified; with the 1-sample wavelet no lead/lag is encoded). Empirical confirmation is a check-stage task.

metric_name_standard: imaginary part of coherency (imaginary coherence) from Morlet-wavelet cross-spectra, summarised by mean/max over band and time
canonical_ref: Nolte et al. 2004, Clin Neurophysiol 115:2292 (supplement ref [64]): ImC_ij(f) = Im(S_ij(f)) / sqrt(S_ii(f) S_jj(f)) with S averaged over trials; insensitive to zero-lag (volume-conducted) coupling.
canonical_definition: ImC_xy(f) = Im(<W_x W_y*>) / sqrt(<|W_x|^2> <|W_y|^2>), <.> over trials/time window; signed, antisymmetric (ImC_yx = -ImC_xy); nonzero only for time-lagged interactions.

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1, Data default; optional detrend first). pyspi hands mne-connectivity ONE epoch (z = moveaxis(data (P,T,1), 2, 0) -> (1,P,T)) with cwt_freqs = linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125) and cwt_n_cycles = cwt_freqs/7 (0.029..0.071 cycles). mne.morlet sets sigma_t = n_cycles/(2 pi f) = 1/(14 pi) = 0.0227 samples for every f, so the time grid arange(0, 5 sigma_t, 1) = [0] and every wavelet is the single sample W = sqrt(2)+0j (probe: 125 wavelets, length 1, value 1.41421356). The 'CWT' is X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) for all 125 f up to FFT round-off (probe: max|Re X - sqrt2 x| 2.7e-15, max|Im X| 7.2e-16, ~2-5% of Im exactly 0). csd(f,t) = X_hi(f,t) conj(X_lo(f,t)) = 2 x_hi(t) x_lo(t) + i*roundoff (hi = higher channel index, lower-triangular connections), psd = |X|^2 = 2 x^2. n_epochs = 1, so every across-epoch average in the estimator is a single term. pyspi then keeps the frequencies with fmin <= f <= fmax on the 0.2..0.5 grid (21 bins for fmin-0_fmax-0-25: 0.2..0.2476; 104 for fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; all 125 for 0..0.5), applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over (freq, time) jointly, mirrors the lower triangle to the upper, sets the diagonal NaN. Estimator imcoh (epochs_bivariate.py:97-107): Im(csd)/sqrt(psd psd) = eps/(2|x_hi x_lo|) = FFT round-off. Output: |values| ~1e-16..1e-14 (probe iid T=256 per-(f,t) max |imcoh| 4.6e-14; up to 2.41e-12 at T=1024 in the check stage; pair-level means ~1e-16), sign arbitrary; flips sign exactly under channel reversal (probe narrowband 7.6e-17 vs -7.6e-17).

deviation_from_documented: (a) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented 125 bins over [0.2, 0.5] for every T (wavelet.py:54), so the 'low' band [0, 0.25] contains only 21 bins in [0.2, 0.248] and frequencies below 0.2 are never analysed; the mne fmin argument is 5/T, not 4/T (it only masks cwt freqs when T < 25). (b) No time-frequency decomposition: n_cycles = f/7 makes every Morlet wavelet one sample long (W = sqrt(2)), so X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) at all 125 frequencies; the band choice changes nothing except which round-off pattern is averaged. (c) Aggregation runs over frequency AND time (axis=(2,3)) of per-(f,t) single-epoch values; the documentation for the multitaper versions describes a summary over frequency only. (d) Not in the documented SPI set at all (extra classes). (e) Output is floating-point noise; the documented purpose (coherence caused by a time delay) is unreachable because the 1-sample wavelet yields real CWT coefficients (probe delayed_noise, 1-5 sample delays: A[0,1] -2.3e-16).
deviation_from_canonical: Canonical ImC is Im of a trial/time-averaged coherency at a resolved frequency; implemented is the average over (f,t) of per-point single-epoch Im(csd)/|csd| with real wavelet coefficients, i.e. round-off. Canonical is antisymmetric; pyspi mirrors to symmetric. Even with proper wavelets (n_cycles = 7) the single-epoch per-point value is sin(phase difference) (probe: values spread -1..1, mean 0.029), not ImC.
units_and_range: Dimensionless, signed, nominally [-1, 1]; implemented |values| <= ~1e-13 (round-off); labelled 'unsigned' (wavelet.py:125) though signed; symmetric by mirror; diagonal NaN.

metric_name_standard: phase locking value (PLV) from Morlet-wavelet phases, summarised by mean/max over band and time
canonical_ref: Lachaux, Rodriguez, Martinerie & Varela 1999, Hum Brain Mapp 8:194 (supplement ref [65]): PLV(t,f) = |N^-1 sum_n exp(i theta(t,n))| over N trials, theta = phase difference from complex Gabor (Morlet) wavelet convolution; single-trial variant averages over a time window (Lachaux et al. 2000, Int J Bifurcation Chaos 10:2429).
canonical_definition: PLV = |E_n[ exp(i (phi_x,n(t,f) - phi_y,n(t,f))) ]| over trials n (or over time within a window for single-trial PLV); in [0,1]; with a single observation identically 1.

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1, Data default; optional detrend first). pyspi hands mne-connectivity ONE epoch (z = moveaxis(data (P,T,1), 2, 0) -> (1,P,T)) with cwt_freqs = linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125) and cwt_n_cycles = cwt_freqs/7 (0.029..0.071 cycles). mne.morlet sets sigma_t = n_cycles/(2 pi f) = 1/(14 pi) = 0.0227 samples for every f, so the time grid arange(0, 5 sigma_t, 1) = [0] and every wavelet is the single sample W = sqrt(2)+0j (probe: 125 wavelets, length 1, value 1.41421356). The 'CWT' is X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) for all 125 f up to FFT round-off (probe: max|Re X - sqrt2 x| 2.7e-15, max|Im X| 7.2e-16, ~2-5% of Im exactly 0). csd(f,t) = X_hi(f,t) conj(X_lo(f,t)) = 2 x_hi(t) x_lo(t) + i*roundoff (hi = higher channel index, lower-triangular connections), psd = |X|^2 = 2 x^2. n_epochs = 1, so every across-epoch average in the estimator is a single term. pyspi then keeps the frequencies with fmin <= f <= fmax on the 0.2..0.5 grid (21 bins for fmin-0_fmax-0-25: 0.2..0.2476; 104 for fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; all 125 for 0..0.5), applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over (freq, time) jointly, mirrors the lower triangle to the upper, sets the diagonal NaN. Estimator plv (epochs_bivariate.py:110-131): accumulate csd/|csd|, then |acc/n_epochs| with n_epochs = 1 -> 1 at every (f,t) with nonzero csd. Output exactly 1.0 for every pair, band, statistic (probe).

deviation_from_documented: (a) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented 125 bins over [0.2, 0.5] for every T (wavelet.py:54), so the 'low' band [0, 0.25] contains only 21 bins in [0.2, 0.248] and frequencies below 0.2 are never analysed; the mne fmin argument is 5/T, not 4/T (it only masks cwt freqs when T < 25). (b) No time-frequency decomposition: n_cycles = f/7 makes every Morlet wavelet one sample long (W = sqrt(2)), so X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) at all 125 frequencies; the band choice changes nothing except which round-off pattern is averaged. (c) Aggregation runs over frequency AND time (axis=(2,3)) of per-(f,t) single-epoch values; the documentation for the multitaper versions describes a summary over frequency only. (d) Not in the documented SPI set at all (extra classes). (e) Output is the constant 1 on any input.
deviation_from_canonical: PLV requires averaging unit phasors over trials (or over a time window); pyspi takes |single phasor| = 1 per (f,t) and then averages the ones over time and frequency. Degenerate (constant 1). Phases additionally carry no frequency-specific information (1-sample wavelet).

metric_name_standard: pairwise phase consistency (PPC) from Morlet-wavelet phases, summarised by mean/max over band and time
canonical_ref: Vinck, van Wingerden, Womelsdorf, Fries & Pennartz 2010, NeuroImage 51:112 (supplement ref [66]): PPC = 2/(N(N-1)) sum_{j<k} cos(theta_j - theta_k) over N trials; closed form (|sum_n e^{i theta_n}|^2 - N)/(N(N-1)); unbiased estimator of PLV^2; requires N >= 2.
canonical_definition: PPC = (|sum_{n=1}^N exp(i theta_n)|^2 - N) / (N (N-1)), theta_n = relative phase in trial n at (f,t); undefined for N = 1.

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1, Data default; optional detrend first). pyspi hands mne-connectivity ONE epoch (z = moveaxis(data (P,T,1), 2, 0) -> (1,P,T)) with cwt_freqs = linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125) and cwt_n_cycles = cwt_freqs/7 (0.029..0.071 cycles). mne.morlet sets sigma_t = n_cycles/(2 pi f) = 1/(14 pi) = 0.0227 samples for every f, so the time grid arange(0, 5 sigma_t, 1) = [0] and every wavelet is the single sample W = sqrt(2)+0j (probe: 125 wavelets, length 1, value 1.41421356). The 'CWT' is X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) for all 125 f up to FFT round-off (probe: max|Re X - sqrt2 x| 2.7e-15, max|Im X| 7.2e-16, ~2-5% of Im exactly 0). csd(f,t) = X_hi(f,t) conj(X_lo(f,t)) = 2 x_hi(t) x_lo(t) + i*roundoff (hi = higher channel index, lower-triangular connections), psd = |X|^2 = 2 x^2. n_epochs = 1, so every across-epoch average in the estimator is a single term. pyspi then keeps the frequencies with fmin <= f <= fmax on the 0.2..0.5 grid (21 bins for fmin-0_fmax-0-25: 0.2..0.2476; 104 for fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; all 125 for 0..0.5), applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over (freq, time) jointly, mirrors the lower triangle to the upper, sets the diagonal NaN. Estimator ppc (epochs_bivariate.py:314-347): acc = csd/|csd| (0 where csd = 0); con = Re((acc conj(acc) - n_epochs)/(n_epochs (n_epochs - 1))) = (|e^{i theta}|^2 - 1)/0 = (+-eps or 0)/0 -> -inf or NaN per point (probe iid T=256: 4756 -inf, 0 +inf, 27244 NaN, 0 finite of 32000). numpy divides the complex csd by the real |csd| as Re csd * fl(1/|csd|) (probe: bitwise at every point), and |csd| equals |Re csd| bitwise at every probed point, so |Re acc| = c*fl(1/c) with c = |Re csd|; in round-to-nearest binary64 this is 1 or 1 - 2^-53, so Re(acc)^2 <= 1. That bounds Re(acc)^2 only: |acc|^2 - 1 = Re(acc)^2 + Im(acc)^2 - 1 is positive (+inf after the division by 0) once Im(acc)^2 >= 2^-53, i.e. |Im csd|/|Re csd| >~ 1.05e-8, and bitwise equality of |csd| and |Re csd| does not exclude that (mne-connectivity's own _PPCEst returns +inf from ratio 1.1e-8 with |csd| == |Re csd| bitwise, run wavelet.ppc|iid_gaussian|64|pipeline|pinf). On the audit data the ratio stays at or below 2.41e-12 (runs wavelet.ppc|*|1024|pipeline|ratio), so there |acc|^2 - 1 is 0 or negative (probe over all lower pairs of the 19 datasets at T = 64, 256, 1024, 14,280,000 points: |csd| != |Re csd| at 0 points, |acc|^2 - 1 > 0 at 0, < 0 at 1,984,491, == 0 at 12,295,509; wl_fix/fx1.py). nanmean/nanmax -> -inf (probe: every dataset, T, band, statistic).

deviation_from_documented: (a) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented 125 bins over [0.2, 0.5] for every T (wavelet.py:54), so the 'low' band [0, 0.25] contains only 21 bins in [0.2, 0.248] and frequencies below 0.2 are never analysed; the mne fmin argument is 5/T, not 4/T (it only masks cwt freqs when T < 25). (b) No time-frequency decomposition: n_cycles = f/7 makes every Morlet wavelet one sample long (W = sqrt(2)), so X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) at all 125 frequencies; the band choice changes nothing except which round-off pattern is averaged. (c) Aggregation runs over frequency AND time (axis=(2,3)) of per-(f,t) single-epoch values; the documentation for the multitaper versions describes a summary over frequency only. (d) Not in the documented SPI set at all (extra classes). (e) Output -inf: a division by zero (n_epochs - 1 = 0), not a phase-consistency value.
deviation_from_canonical: PPC is undefined for one trial; the library divides by N(N-1) = 0 without a guard, the numerator is |unit phasor|^2 - 1 = floating-point residue, and pyspi's nanmean/nanmax keeps the infinities. The resulting -inf is a round-off artefact: per point |unit phasor|^2 - 1 is 0 or slightly negative at every probed point (it turns positive only once |Im csd| exceeds about 1.05e-8 |Re csd|, i.e. Im(acc)^2 >= 2^-53, even where |csd| equals |Re csd| bitwise; the largest ratio in the audit data is 2.41e-12), giving NaN or -inf, and nanmean/nanmax return -inf as soon as one -inf point is in the band.
units_and_range: Nominally [-1/(N-1), 1] (bias-corrected; negative values legitimate per REVIEW M7 for N >= 2); implemented -inf for every pair (observed); +inf needs a point with |Im csd| above about 1.05e-8 |Re csd| (Im(acc)^2 >= 2^-53 makes |acc|^2 - 1 positive whether or not |csd| equals |Re csd| bitwise; synthetic Re = 1, Im = 1.2e-8 gives +inf), i.e. a lag-0 product close to zero relative to the FFT round-off (not observed; the largest |Im csd|/|Re csd| over the 14,280,000 audit points is 2.41e-12); NaN would need every (f,t) point of the band to be 0/0 (not observed); symmetric; diagonal NaN.
direction_convention: Undirected; A[i,j] = A[j,i] from conn[max(i,j), min(i,j)] (mne_connectivity/spectral/epochs.py:276, :652; wavelet.py:87-88).

canonical_ref: Stam, Nolte & Daffertshofer 2007, Hum Brain Mapp 28:1178 (supplement ref [67]): PLI = |<sign(Delta phi(t_k))>| (average of the sign of the phase difference over time samples t_k, magnitude taken after averaging); equivalently |E[sign(Im S_xy)]| over trials (Vinck et al. 2011, NeuroImage 55:1548).
canonical_definition: PLI = |(1/K) sum_k sign(Im S_xy,k)|, with k over trials or time samples; in [0,1]; 0 for zero-lag or symmetric phase-difference distributions.

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1, Data default; optional detrend first). pyspi hands mne-connectivity ONE epoch (z = moveaxis(data (P,T,1), 2, 0) -> (1,P,T)) with cwt_freqs = linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125) and cwt_n_cycles = cwt_freqs/7 (0.029..0.071 cycles). mne.morlet sets sigma_t = n_cycles/(2 pi f) = 1/(14 pi) = 0.0227 samples for every f, so the time grid arange(0, 5 sigma_t, 1) = [0] and every wavelet is the single sample W = sqrt(2)+0j (probe: 125 wavelets, length 1, value 1.41421356). The 'CWT' is X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) for all 125 f up to FFT round-off (probe: max|Re X - sqrt2 x| 2.7e-15, max|Im X| 7.2e-16, ~2-5% of Im exactly 0). csd(f,t) = X_hi(f,t) conj(X_lo(f,t)) = 2 x_hi(t) x_lo(t) + i*roundoff (hi = higher channel index, lower-triangular connections), psd = |X|^2 = 2 x^2. n_epochs = 1, so every across-epoch average in the estimator is a single term. pyspi then keeps the frequencies with fmin <= f <= fmax on the 0.2..0.5 grid (21 bins for fmin-0_fmax-0-25: 0.2..0.2476; 104 for fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; all 125 for 0..0.5), applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over (freq, time) jointly, mirrors the lower triangle to the upper, sets the diagonal NaN. Estimator pli (epochs_bivariate.py:163-184): acc = sign(Im csd); con = |acc/n_epochs| = |sign(eps)| per (f,t): 1 where the FFT round-off imaginary part is nonzero, 0 where it is exactly 0. pyspi mean over (f,t) = fraction of points with nonzero round-off Im (probe iid T=256 pair (1,0): 0.9791875 = 1 - frac(Im == 0) exactly); max = 1. Observed ceilings 0.875 at T=64 and 0.9922 at T=1024 (probe sweep), low values for identical pairs (shared_envelope (0,2): 0.465 at T=64).

deviation_from_documented: (a) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented 125 bins over [0.2, 0.5] for every T (wavelet.py:54), so the 'low' band [0, 0.25] contains only 21 bins in [0.2, 0.248] and frequencies below 0.2 are never analysed; the mne fmin argument is 5/T, not 4/T (it only masks cwt freqs when T < 25). (b) No time-frequency decomposition: n_cycles = f/7 makes every Morlet wavelet one sample long (W = sqrt(2)), so X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) at all 125 frequencies; the band choice changes nothing except which round-off pattern is averaged. (c) Aggregation runs over frequency AND time (axis=(2,3)) of per-(f,t) single-epoch values; the documentation for the multitaper versions describes a summary over frequency only. (d) Not in the documented SPI set at all (extra classes). (e) The value is the fraction of time-frequency points whose FFT round-off imaginary part is nonzero, not a phase-lag statistic (probe: delayed_noise T=1024, 1-5 sample delays, 0.991-0.992, same as iid_gaussian 0.988-0.991).
deviation_from_canonical: Canonical PLI averages sign(Im S) over trials/time THEN takes the magnitude; implemented takes |sign(Im csd)| per single-epoch (f,t) point and THEN averages over time (and frequency), so lag direction cancellation never happens and the value is ~1 for any input; and Im csd is pure round-off because the 1-sample wavelet is real. Note: mne-connectivity 0.9.0 takes the magnitude (epochs_bivariate.py:184), unlike spectral_connectivity's signed PLI (REVIEW M3), so M3 does not apply to this unit.
units_and_range: Dimensionless, [0,1]; implemented mean ~ 1 - k/T (round-off zero fraction), max = 1; the mean is set by the exact-zero pattern of the FFT round-off and is not stable to input changes at round-off level (re-z-scoring an already z-scored input, sample changes <= 4.4e-16: narrowband_f0-0.25 T=256 A[0,1] 0.983906 -> 0.982594, delayed_noise T=256 0.977781 -> 0.973969; probe wl_fix/fx1.py), so the snapshot value depends on the FFT implementation (a numpy.fft replay gives a different exact-zero pattern); between scipy.fft 1.17.1 (project venv, pyspi) and 1.18.1 (comparison venv, rep replay) no difference was observed on this machine (rep runs bitwise), while other CPUs and SIMD paths are untested; symmetric; diagonal NaN.
direction_convention: Undirected; A[i,j] = A[j,i] from conn[max(i,j), min(i,j)] (mne_connectivity/spectral/epochs.py:276, :652; wavelet.py:87-88); |sign| is order-invariant (probe: channel reversal gives identical values).

metric_name_standard: debiased squared phase lag index (unbiased estimator of PLI^2) from Morlet-wavelet cross-spectra, summarised by mean/max over band and time
canonical_ref: Vinck, Oostenveld, van Wingerden, Battaglia & Pennartz 2011, NeuroImage 55:1548 (supplement ref [68]): unbiased estimator of squared PLI, (N PLI_hat^2 - 1)/(N - 1) (mne-connectivity comment epochs_bivariate.py:199 cites 'Vinck paper Eq. (30)'; equation number not re-checked).
canonical_definition: dsPLI = (N * PLI_hat^2 - 1)/(N - 1) = (1/(N(N-1))) sum_{j != k} sign(Im X_j) sign(Im X_k) over N trials; undefined for N = 1; can be negative.

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1, Data default; optional detrend first). pyspi hands mne-connectivity ONE epoch (z = moveaxis(data (P,T,1), 2, 0) -> (1,P,T)) with cwt_freqs = linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125) and cwt_n_cycles = cwt_freqs/7 (0.029..0.071 cycles). mne.morlet sets sigma_t = n_cycles/(2 pi f) = 1/(14 pi) = 0.0227 samples for every f, so the time grid arange(0, 5 sigma_t, 1) = [0] and every wavelet is the single sample W = sqrt(2)+0j (probe: 125 wavelets, length 1, value 1.41421356). The 'CWT' is X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) for all 125 f up to FFT round-off (probe: max|Re X - sqrt2 x| 2.7e-15, max|Im X| 7.2e-16, ~2-5% of Im exactly 0). csd(f,t) = X_hi(f,t) conj(X_lo(f,t)) = 2 x_hi(t) x_lo(t) + i*roundoff (hi = higher channel index, lower-triangular connections), psd = |X|^2 = 2 x^2. n_epochs = 1, so every across-epoch average in the estimator is a single term. pyspi then keeps the frequencies with fmin <= f <= fmax on the 0.2..0.5 grid (21 bins for fmin-0_fmax-0-25: 0.2..0.2476; 104 for fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; all 125 for 0..0.5), applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over (freq, time) jointly, mirrors the lower triangle to the upper, sets the diagonal NaN. Estimator pli2_unbiased (epochs_bivariate.py:187-202): (n_epochs * pli_mean^2 - 1)/(n_epochs - 1) with n_epochs = 1 and pli_mean = sign(eps): 0/0 = NaN where Im != 0, -1/0 = -inf where Im == 0 exactly (probe iid T=256: 666 -inf, 31334 NaN, 0 finite). nanmean/nanmax -> -inf whenever any exact-zero Im point lies in the band (every probe), NaN if none (hypothesis). Identifier 'dspli', class DebiasedSquaredWeightedPhaseLagIndex.

deviation_from_documented: (a) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented 125 bins over [0.2, 0.5] for every T (wavelet.py:54), so the 'low' band [0, 0.25] contains only 21 bins in [0.2, 0.248] and frequencies below 0.2 are never analysed; the mne fmin argument is 5/T, not 4/T (it only masks cwt freqs when T < 25). (b) No time-frequency decomposition: n_cycles = f/7 makes every Morlet wavelet one sample long (W = sqrt(2)), so X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) at all 125 frequencies; the band choice changes nothing except which round-off pattern is averaged. (c) Aggregation runs over frequency AND time (axis=(2,3)) of per-(f,t) single-epoch values; the documentation for the multitaper versions describes a summary over frequency only. (d) Not in the documented SPI set at all (extra classes). (e) Output -inf (division by zero). (f) Naming: class name says 'Weighted', computed measure is the unweighted debiased squared PLI; this matches the identifier 'dspli' and the supplement's dspli, not the class name.

metric_name_standard: weighted phase lag index (wPLI, not squared) from Morlet-wavelet cross-spectra, summarised by mean/max over band and time
canonical_ref: Vinck, Oostenveld, van Wingerden, Battaglia & Pennartz 2011, NeuroImage 55:1548 (supplement ref [68]): wPLI = |E{Im X}| / E{|Im X|} with X the cross-spectrum and E over trials.
canonical_definition: wPLI = |sum_n Im X_n| / sum_n |Im X_n| over N trials (or time samples); in [0,1]; 1 for a single observation with Im X != 0.

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1, Data default; optional detrend first). pyspi hands mne-connectivity ONE epoch (z = moveaxis(data (P,T,1), 2, 0) -> (1,P,T)) with cwt_freqs = linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125) and cwt_n_cycles = cwt_freqs/7 (0.029..0.071 cycles). mne.morlet sets sigma_t = n_cycles/(2 pi f) = 1/(14 pi) = 0.0227 samples for every f, so the time grid arange(0, 5 sigma_t, 1) = [0] and every wavelet is the single sample W = sqrt(2)+0j (probe: 125 wavelets, length 1, value 1.41421356). The 'CWT' is X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) for all 125 f up to FFT round-off (probe: max|Re X - sqrt2 x| 2.7e-15, max|Im X| 7.2e-16, ~2-5% of Im exactly 0). csd(f,t) = X_hi(f,t) conj(X_lo(f,t)) = 2 x_hi(t) x_lo(t) + i*roundoff (hi = higher channel index, lower-triangular connections), psd = |X|^2 = 2 x^2. n_epochs = 1, so every across-epoch average in the estimator is a single term. pyspi then keeps the frequencies with fmin <= f <= fmax on the 0.2..0.5 grid (21 bins for fmin-0_fmax-0-25: 0.2..0.2476; 104 for fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; all 125 for 0..0.5), applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over (freq, time) jointly, mirrors the lower triangle to the upper, sets the diagonal NaN. Estimator wpli (epochs_bivariate.py:231-267): num = |sum Im csd|, denom = sum |Im csd|; denom == 0 -> con = 0. With one epoch: |eps|/|eps| = 1 where round-off Im != 0, 0 where Im == 0 exactly, i.e. bitwise the same per-point values as pli (probe: identical outputs to pli on every dataset). Identifier 'wspli', name 'Weighted squared phase lag index (wavelet)'.

deviation_from_documented: (a) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented 125 bins over [0.2, 0.5] for every T (wavelet.py:54), so the 'low' band [0, 0.25] contains only 21 bins in [0.2, 0.248] and frequencies below 0.2 are never analysed; the mne fmin argument is 5/T, not 4/T (it only masks cwt freqs when T < 25). (b) No time-frequency decomposition: n_cycles = f/7 makes every Morlet wavelet one sample long (W = sqrt(2)), so X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) at all 125 frequencies; the band choice changes nothing except which round-off pattern is averaged. (c) Aggregation runs over frequency AND time (axis=(2,3)) of per-(f,t) single-epoch values; the documentation for the multitaper versions describes a summary over frequency only. (d) Not in the documented SPI set at all (extra classes). (e) Round-off artefact identical to pli (see wavelet.pli). (f) Naming: identifier 'wspli' and name 'Weighted squared phase lag index' but the measure is the unsquared wPLI (documented identifier for the multitaper version is 'wpli').
deviation_from_canonical: Canonical wPLI averages Im X over trials before the magnitude; with N = 1 it is trivially 1 (or 0); the implementation's per-point values therefore equal the PLI per-point values, and the time/frequency average yields the round-off zero fraction. Note mne-connectivity takes |sum Im| (magnitude), unlike the signed spectral_connectivity version (REVIEW M3).
units_and_range: Dimensionless, [0,1]; implemented equals pli_wavelet (~1 - k/T for mean, 1 for max); the mean is set by the exact-zero pattern of the FFT round-off and is not stable to input changes at round-off level (re-z-scoring an already z-scored input, sample changes <= 4.4e-16: narrowband_f0-0.25 T=256 A[0,1] 0.983906 -> 0.982594, delayed_noise T=256 0.977781 -> 0.973969; probe wl_fix/fx1.py), so the snapshot value depends on the FFT implementation (a numpy.fft replay gives a different exact-zero pattern); between scipy.fft 1.17.1 (project venv, pyspi) and 1.18.1 (comparison venv, rep replay) no difference was observed on this machine (rep runs bitwise), while other CPUs and SIMD paths are untested; symmetric; diagonal NaN.
direction_convention: Undirected; A[i,j] = A[j,i] from conn[max(i,j), min(i,j)] (mne_connectivity/spectral/epochs.py:276, :652; wavelet.py:87-88); magnitude is order-invariant.

metric_name_standard: debiased weighted squared phase lag index (debiased wPLI^2) from Morlet-wavelet cross-spectra, summarised by mean/max over band and time
canonical_ref: Vinck, Oostenveld, van Wingerden, Battaglia & Pennartz 2011, NeuroImage 55:1548 (supplement ref [68]): debiased wPLI^2 = sum_{j != k} Im X_j Im X_k / sum_{j != k} |Im X_j| |Im X_k| over trial pairs.
canonical_definition: dwPLI^2 = ((sum_n Im X_n)^2 - sum_n (Im X_n)^2) / ((sum_n |Im X_n|)^2 - sum_n (Im X_n)^2); undefined for N = 1 (0/0).

implemented_as: Input z-scored per channel (ddof=1, Data default; optional detrend first). pyspi hands mne-connectivity ONE epoch (z = moveaxis(data (P,T,1), 2, 0) -> (1,P,T)) with cwt_freqs = linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125) and cwt_n_cycles = cwt_freqs/7 (0.029..0.071 cycles). mne.morlet sets sigma_t = n_cycles/(2 pi f) = 1/(14 pi) = 0.0227 samples for every f, so the time grid arange(0, 5 sigma_t, 1) = [0] and every wavelet is the single sample W = sqrt(2)+0j (probe: 125 wavelets, length 1, value 1.41421356). The 'CWT' is X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) for all 125 f up to FFT round-off (probe: max|Re X - sqrt2 x| 2.7e-15, max|Im X| 7.2e-16, ~2-5% of Im exactly 0). csd(f,t) = X_hi(f,t) conj(X_lo(f,t)) = 2 x_hi(t) x_lo(t) + i*roundoff (hi = higher channel index, lower-triangular connections), psd = |X|^2 = 2 x^2. n_epochs = 1, so every across-epoch average in the estimator is a single term. pyspi then keeps the frequencies with fmin <= f <= fmax on the 0.2..0.5 grid (21 bins for fmin-0_fmax-0-25: 0.2..0.2476; 104 for fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; all 125 for 0..0.5), applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over (freq, time) jointly, mirrors the lower triangle to the upper, sets the diagonal NaN. Estimator wpli2_debiased (epochs_bivariate.py:270-311): denom = (sum|Im|)^2 - sum Im^2 = 0 for one epoch -> denom set to 1 and con set to 0 (303-309). Output exactly 0.0 for every pair, band, statistic (probe).

deviation_from_documented: (a) Frequency grid: documented 125 bins over [4/T, fs/2]; implemented 125 bins over [0.2, 0.5] for every T (wavelet.py:54), so the 'low' band [0, 0.25] contains only 21 bins in [0.2, 0.248] and frequencies below 0.2 are never analysed; the mne fmin argument is 5/T, not 4/T (it only masks cwt freqs when T < 25). (b) No time-frequency decomposition: n_cycles = f/7 makes every Morlet wavelet one sample long (W = sqrt(2)), so X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) at all 125 frequencies; the band choice changes nothing except which round-off pattern is averaged. (c) Aggregation runs over frequency AND time (axis=(2,3)) of per-(f,t) single-epoch values; the documentation for the multitaper versions describes a summary over frequency only. (d) Not in the documented SPI set at all (extra classes). (e) Output constant 0 (zero-denominator guard), on any input. (f) Identifier 'dwspli' vs documented multitaper identifier 'dswpli'.
deviation_from_canonical: Undefined for one trial (0/0); the library's guard maps it to 0, so the SPI is identically 0 regardless of the data (degenerate). A legitimate 0 (no lagged coupling) and 'undefined' are indistinguishable.
units_and_range: Nominally about [-1, 1] (negative legitimate for N >= 2, REVIEW M7); implemented exactly 0.0; symmetric; diagonal NaN.

metric_name_standard: maximum of the sample cross-correlation function over lags |h| <= T/4 (and of its square for the -sq identifier)
canonical_ref: Brockwell & Davis, Time Series: Theory and Methods (Springer Science & Business Media, 2009, as cited in the supplement; edition not stated there), the supplement's reference [8] (supplement.txt:1987-1988): sample cross-covariance gamma_hat_ij(h), sample cross-correlation rho_hat_ij(h) and the +-1.96 n^-1/2 bound for two independent series of which one is white noise. UNVERIFIED locator: the section/theorem numbers (§11.2, Theorem 11.2.2) were recalled from memory and no copy of the book was consulted; see Open questions. Lag truncation: the supplement (§1.1.5, p.5; supplement.txt:197-198) cites [9] Afyouni, Smith & Nichols 2019, NeuroImage 199:609 and [10] Cliff, Novelli, Fulcher, Shine & Lizier 2021, Phys Rev Res 3:013145 (supplement.txt:1990-1995) for the practice of truncating the CCF "at a given level"; the specific T/4 cut is pyspi's choice, and no canonical source for it was consulted.
canonical_definition: rho_hat_xy(h) = gamma_hat_xy(h) / sqrt(gamma_hat_xx(0) gamma_hat_yy(0)), gamma_hat_xy(h) = (1/n) sum_{t=1}^{n-h} (x_{t+h} - xbar)(y_t - ybar) for 0 <= h < n and gamma_hat_xy(h) = gamma_hat_yx(-h) for h < 0 (mean-centred, divisor n at every lag, so |rho_hat| <= 1); lag-h sample CCF considered significant when |rho_hat| > 1.96/sqrt(n) (valid under independence with at least one white series). The scalar summary (max or mean of the CCF over a lag window) is a pyspi construction with no canonical source.
documented_definition: supplement §1.1.5, p.5 (pack lines 197-213; heading at supplement.txt line 192): "The cross-correlation function is defined as the Pearson correlation between two time series for all lags [8], giving values in [-1, 1] for each lag ... the correlation from the MLE of the cross-covariance at a given lag, normalised by the autocovariance ... we do by only using the first T/4 lags ... a correlation below 1.96/sqrt(T) is considered statistically insignificant [8], thus we optionally cut-off the lags at this level (sig-True means we only use the statistically significant values, and sig-False means we use all values) ... the maximum over the considered lags (max), and the average over the considered lags (mean)." Same text on GitBook basic-statistics.md:55-57 (Cross Correlation), which lists xcorr_max_sig-True, xcorr_mean_sig-True, xcorr_mean_sig-False and their -sq versions (lines 63-75). [8] = Brockwell & Davis, Time Series: Theory and Methods (supplement.txt:1987). NOTE: xcorr_max_sig-False / xcorr-sq_max_sig-False are not among the identifiers listed in the supplement or GitBook; the definition is the class description applied with sigonly=False.

For the pair (x=x_hi, y=x_lo) pyspi computes z = scipy.signal.correlate(x, y, 'full'), r = z / (std0(x) std0(y) (T-1)) which for z-scored input equals T/(T-1) times the Brockwell-Davis sample CCF at every lag, keeps lags -(T//4-1)..+T//4 (2*(T//4) values, one more positive than negative lag); sigonly=False uses all 2*(T//4) lags; returns np.max of r (signed) or of r**2 (-sq). deviation_from_documented: (1) Normalisation: documented as 'Pearson correlation ... giving values in [-1, 1]', but r = z/(std_ddof0(x) std_ddof0(y)(T-1)) on ddof=1 z-scored input equals T/(T-1) times the sample correlation at every lag (probe T=64: lag-0 ratio to Pearson r 1.0158730 = 64/63; ratio to the B&D CCF 1.0158730 at every lag), so identical series give 1.0159 > 1 at T=64. (2) Lag window: documented 'first T/4 lags'; implemented lags -(T//4-1)..+T//4 (both sides, 2*(T//4) lags, asymmetric by one lag). (3) This configuration (statistic='max', sigonly=False) is not listed in the supplement, the GitBook page or pyspi/config.yaml / fast_config.yaml; it comes from the retained EEG metric list (audit/env/retained_metrics.txt:186,188), so its documented definition is inferred from the class description.
deviation_from_canonical: Constant inflation by T/(T-1) relative to the B&D sample CCF (divisor (T-1)^2/T instead of T-1 for z-scored data); window not symmetric about lag 0 (+T//4 included, -T//4 excluded); with normalise=False no centring at all (non-centred cross-product), whereas rho_hat is mean-centred; the max/mean summary over lags has no canonical definition (pyspi construction); signed max ignores negative peaks (max |rho_hat| is the more common peak-CCF summary; -sq covers it).
units_and_range: Dimensionless, signed (plain) / non-negative (-sq). Nominally in [-1, 1] / [0, 1] but scaled by T/(T-1) so can slightly exceed 1 (1.0159 at T=64 for identical series). Symmetric by construction (mirror); channel order matters only when the maximum sits on lag +-T//4 (not observed on the datasets, perm-selfcons gap <= 2.2e-16; on a constructed pair with the peak at lag T//4 the value changes from 0.7596 to 0.1054 at T=1024, |endlag runs). No error path; finite for finite input. In the EEG selection.
direction_convention: Undirected; A is symmetric by the mirror in pyspi/base.py:137. A[i,j] = A[j,i] = statistic over a lag window of r from scipy.signal.correlate(x_hi, x_lo) where hi = max(i,j), lo = min(i,j) (first bivariate call is (i=hi, j=lo), and the cache at basic.py:113 returns the same unreversed array for (lo,hi)); probe: data.xcorr[(0,1)] equals the slice computed from correlate(x1, x0). Sign convention of the lag axis (probe and scipy docstring :168): a peak at positive lag k in correlate(x, y) means x(t) ~ y(t-k), i.e. y leads x by k; so positive lags in the stored r mean the LOWER-index channel leads. Same orientation as Brockwell & Davis gamma_12(h) = Cov(X_{t+h,1}, X_{t,2}) with series 1 = x_hi.

score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 fails: the T/(T-1) factor is not a documented convention, and identical series give 1.0159 at T=64 against the documented [-1, 1]. Anchor 8's monotone clause also fails on the constructed end-lag pair (0.7596 vs 0.1054 by channel order at T=1024, canonical 0.7589 in both orders). Every dataset pipeline run equals the canonical maximum times T/(T-1) to <= 6.7e-16, so the row sits at 8.
what_changed: pyspi returns T/(T-1) times the canonical value: the maximum of the Brockwell-Davis sample CCF over the lag window (r = correlate / (std_ddof0 x std_ddof0 x (T-1)) on ddof=1 z-scored data). Every pipeline run agrees with canonical x T/(T-1) to <= 6.7e-16, so identical series give T/(T-1) > 1 (1.0159 at T=64), outside the documented [-1, 1]. The window -(T//4-1)..T//4 is asymmetric by one lag. It did not change the max on any dataset run, because no maximum fell on +-T//4, but on a constructed pair with the CCF peak at lag T//4 the value depends on channel order (0.7596 vs 0.1054 at T=1024, |endlag). The max is signed (negative peaks ignored; -sq takes max r^2). With normalise=False the SPI does not centre, so the value is a non-centred cross-product (raw scaled_offset pair (2,3) 0.597 vs 0.797). The identifier is not listed in the supplement, GitBook or config. It is a retained EEG identifier, so it was judged against the family's documented 'maximum over the considered lags'. Rubric anchor 8: constant factor T/(T-1); the end-lag order dependence needs a peak exactly at +-T//4 and was kept as a caveat rather than a lower anchor. Rubric reading is nearest-anchor 8 (score_rubric_note), because anchor 8's monotone clause fails on the constructed end-lag pair; the 'Rubric anchor 8' wording above is the original reasoning for score_0_10.

metric_name_standard: Linear least-squares detrending (removal of a fitted degree-1 polynomial a + b t per channel)
canonical_ref: Bendat & Piersol 2010, Random Data: Analysis and Measurement Procedures, 4th ed., Wiley, data-preparation chapter (trend removal by least-squares polynomial fit, first order); equivalently ordinary least squares on the design [1, t]
canonical_definition: r_t = x_t - (a_hat + b_hat t), with (a_hat, b_hat) = argmin sum_t (x_t - a - b t)^2; b_hat = sum (t - tbar)(x_t - xbar) / sum (t - tbar)^2, a_hat = xbar - b_hat tbar; the residual has exactly zero mean and zero sample correlation with t
documented_definition: Supplement gives no detrending rule (supplement §1, line 95, p.3 only says 'we standardize (z-score) the MTS along the time axis'). GitBook api-reference/pyspi.calculator.calculator.md:19: 'Detrend the dataset along the time axis before normalising (if enabled), default=False.' api-reference/pyspi.data.data.md:29: 'If True, detrend the dataset along the time axis before normalising (if enabled), default=True.' (the signature on line 31 of the same page says detrend=False). Docstring pyspi/data.py:44-45: 'If True, detrend each time series in the MTS dataset individually along the time axis, default=False.'
delegate_lib: scipy==1.17.1 scipy.signal.detrend(data, axis=1) with defaults type='linear', bp=0, overwrite_data=False
implemented_as: Calculator(detrend=False default) forwards the flag to Data only when the dataset is not already a Data object. Data.set_data runs reorder to (processes, observations, replications) -> truncation to n_processes/n_observations -> scipy.signal.detrend(data, axis=1) if self.detrend -> zscore if self.normalise -> NaN check. scipy fits the design A = [t/N, 1], t = 1..N, per column by scipy.linalg.lstsq and subtracts A @ coef (one segment because bp=0), i.e. an ordinary OLS linear-trend residual per (process, replication) along time. Dtype: float32 input stays float32 (dtype char 'f' is kept), integer input is promoted to float64. A ValueError from detrend (NaN/inf input) is caught, printed as 'Could not detrend data: ...' and the data continue undetrended. The EEG workflow uses detrend=True then z-score (order fixed by the code: detrend precedes zscore). Probe p1_data.py: Data(normalise=False, detrend=True) matches a numpy.polyfit degree-1 residual to 5.3e-15; detrend then zscore matches to 2.7e-15; 3-D (p,s,r) input is detrended per replication (max abs diff 0.0 vs scipy on axis=1).

method_or_estimator: scipy.stats.zscore(ddof=1, axis=1) after truncation and detrend
metric_name_standard: Standard score (z-score) per channel along time with the sample (n-1) standard deviation
canonical_ref: Textbook standard score z = (x - mean)/sd (e.g. Freedman, Pisani & Purves, Statistics, 4th ed., Norton 2007, ch. 5 'standard units'); the sd convention (population n vs sample n-1) varies by source; maximum |z| with the n-1 sd is (n-1)/sqrt(n) (Shiffler 1988, The American Statistician 42(1):79-80)
canonical_definition: z_t = (x_t - xbar)/s, xbar = (1/T) sum x_t, s = sqrt(sum (x_t - xbar)^2/(T - ddof)); pyspi uses ddof = 1, so sum z_t = 0, sum z_t^2/(T-1) = 1 and the population (1/T) variance of z is (T-1)/T

score_rubric_note: No anchor is written for infrastructure units, so anchor 3 is applied with the documented z-score contract as the label. Anchor 4 fails because the output is not a coherent related quantity. It depends on the raw scale of every array after the first and on argument order: dtw gives 159.48 or 68.86, against 8.714 on z-scored inputs.
what_changed: The direct-array API (spi.bivariate(x, y), spi.multivariate([x1, x2, ...])) z-scores only the first array; every later array reaches the SPI raw (no z-score, and no detrend on this path), contrary to the documented 'standardize (z-score) the MTS ... prior to evaluating each statistic'. Scale- and offset-sensitive SPIs therefore return a different quantity (dtw 159.5 vs 8.71, Ridge MSE 31.7 vs 0.32, cov 8.08 vs 0.82); scale-invariant SPIs are unaffected. Calculator and the Data path are not affected. An unset i/j is never reported as such (base.py builds a Warning object and discards it); two SPIs (cds, igci) return a finite number for the ill-posed call with no message at all, and ten infotheory identifiers return NaN with a logging-module message that names a different cause. Score 3 by analogy to README anchor 3, 'An identifier hyperparameter is ignored or the label does not describe the computation': no anchor is written for infrastructure units, and here the documented contract (supplement.txt:101-102 'Prior to evaluating each statistic, we standardize (z-score) the MTS') plays the role of the label, which the direct-array path does not honour for any array after the first; it also makes argument order matter (dtw 159.48 / 68.86 with x and y swapped, against 8.714 on z-scored inputs). Not 2, 1 or 0: no sign change against a canonical quantity, no substituted estimator and no degenerate output; each SPI computes its own formula on wrongly scaled input.

method_or_estimator: Directed loops all ordered pairs; Undirected then mirrors the upper triangle
metric_name_standard: Assembly of the matrix of pairwise interactions (MPI) from a bivariate statistic: ordered-pair loop for directed SPIs, triangle mirroring for undirected SPIs
canonical_ref: Cliff et al. 2023, Nature Computational Science 3:883-893 (pyspi), supplement §1 (line 95-104), p.3 and §3.1 (line 1437-1449), p.29: an M-by-M MPI with s(x, y) per pair; undirected statistics satisfy f(x, y) = f(y, x)
canonical_definition: Directed SPI: A[i, j] = s(x_i -> x_j) for all i != j, diagonal undefined. Undirected SPI: A[i, j] = A[j, i] = s(x_i, x_j) with s symmetric, so one evaluation per unordered pair suffices
documented_definition: supplement §3.1, p.29: 'undirected statistics have repeated entries in the upper and lower diagonals of the MPIs'. GitBook spis/glossary-of-terms.md:27: 'entry calc.table[\'di_gaussian\'][0,1] will be the directed information from process 0 to process 1. The rows in this table reflect the sources while the columns reflect the targets'. GitBook development/development/incorporating-new-spis.md:376-378: Undirected 'Only entries below the diagonal (lower triangle) will be computed' and the base class 'overrides the multivariate method to ensure that the resulting matrix is symmetric by copying the lower triangular values to the upper triangle'.
delegate_lib: pyspi (base.Directed.multivariate, base.Undirected.multivariate, calculator.Calculator.compute)
implemented_as: Directed.multivariate allocates a P x P NaN matrix and, for j in 0..P-1 (outer) and i != j (inner), sets A[i, j] = self.bivariate(data, i=i, j=j); P(P-1) calls. SPI bivariate methods read src, targ = z[[i, j]] (e.g. TransferEntropy, pyspi/statistics/infotheory.py:383), so A[i, j] = i -> j (row = source). Undirected.multivariate calls the same loop (all P(P-1) ordered pairs) and then sets A[tril] = A.T[tril], i.e. it keeps the upper triangle (values from bivariate(i, j) with i < j) and overwrites the lower triangle; the P(P-1)/2 lower-triangle evaluations are discarded, and because j is the outer loop several of them run before the kept ones. Classes that override multivariate bypass this (285 identifiers: 50 Undirected-mirror, 108 Undirected with an override, 91 Directed loop, 36 Directed with own multivariate; probe p4_classes.py). Calculator.compute then forces the diagonal to NaN and, if multivariate raises, stores an all-NaN matrix for that SPI. Probe p5_pairs.py: toy Undirected SPI returning 10i+j gives [[nan 1 2 3] [1 nan 12 13] [2 12 nan 23] [3 13 23 nan]] with 12 bivariate calls for P=4, first calls (1,0), (2,0), (3,0). Three mirror classes cache each pair under both (i, j) and (j, i) on the shared Data: CrossCorrelation (basic.py:109-113), Cointegration (misc.py:62-97) and JointEntropy (infotheory.py:160-177). For them the kept call bivariate(i<j) is a cache hit that returns the value computed by the first-visited call bivariate(j, i). Probe p10_cache_order.py: for xcorr_max_sig-True, coint_aeg_tstat_trend-c_autolag-aic_maxlag-10 and je_kozachenko, loop A[0,1] equals an isolated bivariate(1,0) exactly and differs from an isolated bivariate(0,1).

deviation_from_documented: (1) The developer guide says only the lower triangle is computed and lower values are copied to the upper triangle; the code computes every ordered pair and copies the UPPER triangle into the lower (probe p5_pairs.py). (2) 108 identifiers in Undirected classes override multivariate and so are not symmetrised by the base class (REVIEW M1, which was tests/README.md bug 5 before b2f6d7e; elaborated here with counts only). (3) Barycenter (16 identifiers) is labelled 'undirected' but inherits Directed; its matrix is symmetric only through its own (i, j)/(j, i) cache. The glossary's row = source convention matches the Directed loop for TransferEntropy (probe: gc_gaussian on delayed_noise rows 0-1 gives A[0,1] = 2.259, A[1,0] = 0.003, x0 leads).
deviation_from_canonical: For symmetric bivariate statistics the result is the canonical MPI but with twice the bivariate calls. For bivariate statistics that are numerically asymmetric, the Undirected mirror keeps the value returned by the bivariate(i<j) call. For the three classes that cache both orderings (xcorr, coint, je), that call returns the cached i>j evaluation (probe p10_cache_order.py). Probe p9_mirror_rng.py found no random-number consumption that couples calls: see the RNG candidate.
units_and_range: Not a statistic; preserves the units of the bivariate statistic; diagonal always NaN after Calculator.compute; an exception in any pair makes the whole SPI matrix NaN in Calculator.
direction_convention: A[i, j] = bivariate(data, i=i, j=j); pyspi bivariate implementations read (source, target) = (row i, column j), so A[i, j] = i -> j, rows are sources and columns targets (glossary-of-terms.md:27). STATUS: established empirically for one SPI only, gc_gaussian_k-1_kt-1_l-1_lt-1 (TransferEntropy, gaussian estimator) on delayed_noise rows 0-1 (A[0,1] = 2.259, A[1,0] = 0.003; probe p5_pairs.py). It is a code reading for every other directed SPI; the check stage must not inherit it as established and each directed family must confirm its own SPI. Undirected: A[i, j] = A[j, i] = the value returned by bivariate(i=min, j=max), which for xcorr, coint and je is the cached bivariate(i=max, j=min) evaluation (probe p10_cache_order.py).

method_or_estimator: spectral_connectivity Multitaper(NW=3, 5 DPSS) + Connectivity cross-spectral matrix
metric_name_standard: multitaper (Thomson) estimate of the cross-spectral density matrix S(f): K=5 Slepian (DPSS) tapers with NW=3, equal-weight average of the taper eigen-cross-spectra, whole series as a single window (infrastructure shared by every multitaper spectral SPI)
canonical_ref: Thomson 1982, Proc. IEEE 70(9):1055-1096, checked against a scanned copy with an OCR text layer (math.ucdavis.edu/~saito/data/ONR15/thomson_spect-est-harm-anal.pdf; the displayed equations are images and are not readable in that layer): section III Eigenestimates, p.1060-1061: eigencoefficients y_k(f) (eq. 3.2, p.1060); the estimate (3.7) is formed with "unit coefficient weights for the first K = [2NW] terms" (p.1060); the kth eigenspectrum is S_k(f) = |y_k(f)|^2 (eq. 3.8, p.1061); "the estimate (3.7) has about 2K degrees of freedom" (p.1061); section IV.B Distributions of Eigenspectrum Estimates, p.1064 (each eigenspectrum is chi^2 with 2 degrees of freedom for Gaussian data); section V Adaptive Weighting, p.1065; section XIV Estimation of Coherence and Polyspectra, p.1087 (cross-spectra and coherence). Percival & Walden 1993, Spectral Analysis for Physical Applications, Cambridge UP; chapter and section titles and pages checked against the authors' table of contents (faculty.washington.edu/dbp/SAPA/sapatoc.html), section contents not checked: ch. 7 Multitaper Spectral Estimation, pp.331-377 (7.2 Multitapering of Gaussian White Noise, p.347); 3.9 Concentration Problem -- Discrete/Continuous Case, p.101 (DPSS); 8.3 Tridiagonal Formulation, p.386 (the tridiagonal matrix used by the library dpss_windows). Slepian 1978, Prolate spheroidal wave functions, Fourier analysis, and uncertainty V: the discrete case, Bell Syst. Tech. J. 57(5):1371-1430 (definition of the DPSS); citation details confirmed from bibliographic listings, text not checked. Walden 2000, A unified view of multitaper multivariate spectral estimation, Biometrika 87(4):767-788; citation and abstract checked (cross-spectral matrix estimators written as weighted averages of orthogonally tapered cross-periodograms, including the Thomson Slepian-taper estimator); full text not obtained, so no section or equation is cited. Mitra & Pesaran 1999, Biophys. J. 76(2):691-708, checked against the arXiv preprint q-bio/0309028v1, not the journal copy: section 4.1.5 eq. 6-7, the direct multitaper estimate S_MT(f) = (1/K) sum_k |x_k(f)|^2 with DPSS tapers, and "take the leading 2NW - 1 DPSS as data tapers"; section 4.3 eq. 25-26, transfer function and coherence from sums over the tapers (the "local frequency ensemble") of a single pair of series. K = 2NW - 1 is therefore sourced to Mitra & Pesaran section 4.1.5 and the 2K degrees of freedom to Thomson p.1061; neither is attributed to Percival & Walden.
canonical_definition: J_{k,i}(f) = sqrt(dt) * sum_{t=0}^{T-1} h_k(t) (x_i(t) - mean(x_i)) exp(-i 2 pi f t dt), where h_k is the k-th unit-energy DPSS of length T with half-bandwidth W = NW/(T dt); S_ij(f) = (1/K) sum_{k=0}^{K-1} J_{k,i}(f) conj(J_{k,j}(f)). S is two-sided and Hermitian; S_ii(f) is the PSD, whose integral over [-fs/2, fs/2] is the variance. With K = 2NW-1, S_ii(f)/S_true,ii(f) is approximately chi^2_{2K}/(2K) away from 0 and Nyquist.

implemented_as: Input is the Data array (P, T) after optional linear detrend and z-scoring with ddof=1, transposed to (T, P). The multivariate path takes all P channels; the bivariate path for directed SPIs takes only columns [i, j]. Multitaper(z, sampling_frequency=fs=1) uses the library defaults: NW = time_halfbandwidth_product = 3; n_tapers = floor(2*NW - 1) = 5; is_low_bias=True, which drops tapers with concentration <= 0.9 (probe: the 5th taper has 0.946 at every T, so all 5 are kept); the whole series is one window (n_windows = 1, step = T); detrend_type "constant" removes each window mean, which is a no-op after z-scoring; n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T), a 5-smooth length that equals T for T in {64, 256, 1024, 4096} and zero-pads otherwise (probe: T=1009 -> 1024, T=63 -> 64). The tapers have unit energy and are scaled by sqrt(fs); the FFT is divided by fs, so J_k = sqrt(dt) * FFT(h_k x), which gives two-sided PSD scaling (probe: power scales as 1/fs). The Fourier coefficients have shape (1 window, 1 trial, 5 tapers, n_fft, P). The per-taper CSM is X_i conj(X_j) (matmul with the conjugate transpose), and expectation_type "trials_tapers" takes an equal-weight mean over the 5 tapers. There are no adaptive weights and no eigenvalue weights. n_observations is 5 (the tapers), and the debiased phase estimators and group-delay coherence_bias use it downstream. Each measure first builds the full two-sided CSM, then _non_negative_frequencies keeps indices 0..(n_fft+1)//2-1, i.e. f_k = k/n_fft: DC is kept and the Nyquist bin (fftfreq -0.5) is dropped for even n_fft. Results are cached per Data object and per measure key. Every distinct measure rebuilds the Multitaper, the FFT and the full CSM.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Frequency grid. The documentation says "125 uniformly sampled bins ... f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T". The implementation uses the FFT grid f_k = k/n_fft, k = 0..(n_fft+1)//2-1. That gives 32/128/512/2048 bins at T=64/256/1024/4096, starting at DC (f=0, not 4/T) and ending at 0.5 - 1/n_fft (probe at T=64: "nfreq kept 32 first [0. 0.015625] last 0.484375"). The 125-bin figure matches pyspi's wavelet path (pyspi/statistics/wavelet.py:54 cwt_freqs = np.linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125)), whose minimum frequency is 5/T (wavelet.py:62), not 4/T; where the text comes from remains a hypothesis (check stage: grid confirmed by the grid-n* runs). (2) The documented ranges are closed at fs/2, but the Nyquist bin is never available (already documented, REVIEW M4). (3) The supplement cites toolbox v0.2.5.dev0; 1.1.2 is executed. (4) NW=3, K=5, the single window, constant detrend and next_fast_len padding are not documented, so there is nothing to contradict.
deviation_from_canonical: This is the simple (equal-weight) multitaper CSM estimator with NW=3 and K=2NW-1=5. It agrees with a from-scratch implementation to round-off (probe at T=256: max |S_lib - S_scratch| = 2.6e-14 over the two-sided CSM, reference built from scipy.signal.windows.dpss + numpy.fft). The tapers equal the eigenvectors of the dense Slepian sinc kernel to 2.3e-12 (T=64), 1.0e-12 (T=256) and 1.3e-12 (T=1024). Variants rather than errors: (a) no Thomson adaptive weighting; (b) the 5th taper (concentration 0.946) is included; (c) one window, so the "expectation" behind every downstream measure is an average over the 5 tapers only (n_observations = 5), not over trials or time segments; (d) two-sided PSD scaling with no doubling of positive frequencies, which cancels in every normalised measure; (e) S(0) is real (probe: max |Im S(0)| = 0.0) and is estimated after mean removal, so it is biased low within |f| < W = 3/T; (f) for T that is not 5-smooth, the series is zero-padded to next_fast_len(T), so the grid spacing is 1/n_fft instead of 1/T.
units_and_range: Complex, Hermitian matrix per frequency (probe: max |S - S^H| = 0.0). The diagonal is real and >= 0, in units of x^2 per unit frequency (two-sided). With z-scored input and fs=1, the mean of the two-sided power over all n_fft bins equals sum_t (1/K sum_k h_k(t)^2) x_c(t)^2, close to 1 (Parseval; probe agreement 1.2e-15). The DC entries are real. Not a scalar SPI; the only NaNs are set by downstream measures (zero-power normalisation, diagonal).
direction_convention: S[i,j](f) = mean_k X_{k,i}(f) conj(X_{k,j}(f)), with row i = process i (column i of the (T,P) input). Probe on delayed_noise T=1024 (x_j = x0 delayed by d_j): the slope of the unwrapped phase of S[0,j] over f in (0, 0.1), divided by 2 pi, is +1.019, +2.986 and +5.034 for d = 1, 3, 5. A positive phase slope therefore means the row process leads the column process. Every multivariate spectral SPI computes A[i,j] from S[i,j] (spectral.py:91). The bivariate path computes the 2-channel [i, j] result and reads entry [0,1], which has the same orientation. Multivariate and bivariate CSM entries are identical (probe: max |S_mv[2,0] - S_bv[0,1]| = 0.0).

method_or_estimator: spectral_connectivity Multitaper(NW=3, 5 DPSS) + Connectivity cross-spectral matrix
metric_name_standard: multitaper (Thomson) estimate of the cross-spectral density matrix S(f): K=5 Slepian (DPSS) tapers with NW=3, equal-weight average of the taper eigen-cross-spectra, whole series as a single window (infrastructure shared by every multitaper spectral SPI)
canonical_ref: Thomson 1982, Proc. IEEE 70(9):1055-1096, checked against a scanned copy with an OCR text layer (math.ucdavis.edu/~saito/data/ONR15/thomson_spect-est-harm-anal.pdf; the displayed equations are images and are not readable in that layer): section III Eigenestimates, p.1060-1061: eigencoefficients y_k(f) (eq. 3.2, p.1060); the estimate (3.7) is formed with "unit coefficient weights for the first K = [2NW] terms" (p.1060); the kth eigenspectrum is S_k(f) = |y_k(f)|^2 (eq. 3.8, p.1061); "the estimate (3.7) has about 2K degrees of freedom" (p.1061); section IV.B Distributions of Eigenspectrum Estimates, p.1064 (each eigenspectrum is chi^2 with 2 degrees of freedom for Gaussian data); section V Adaptive Weighting, p.1065; section XIV Estimation of Coherence and Polyspectra, p.1087 (cross-spectra and coherence). Percival & Walden 1993, Spectral Analysis for Physical Applications, Cambridge UP; chapter and section titles and pages checked against the authors' table of contents (faculty.washington.edu/dbp/SAPA/sapatoc.html), section contents not checked: ch. 7 Multitaper Spectral Estimation, pp.331-377 (7.2 Multitapering of Gaussian White Noise, p.347); 3.9 Concentration Problem -- Discrete/Continuous Case, p.101 (DPSS); 8.3 Tridiagonal Formulation, p.386 (the tridiagonal matrix used by the library dpss_windows). Slepian 1978, Prolate spheroidal wave functions, Fourier analysis, and uncertainty V: the discrete case, Bell Syst. Tech. J. 57(5):1371-1430 (definition of the DPSS); citation details confirmed from bibliographic listings, text not checked. Walden 2000, A unified view of multitaper multivariate spectral estimation, Biometrika 87(4):767-788; citation and abstract checked (cross-spectral matrix estimators written as weighted averages of orthogonally tapered cross-periodograms, including the Thomson Slepian-taper estimator); full text not obtained, so no section or equation is cited. Mitra & Pesaran 1999, Biophys. J. 76(2):691-708, checked against the arXiv preprint q-bio/0309028v1, not the journal copy: section 4.1.5 eq. 6-7, the direct multitaper estimate S_MT(f) = (1/K) sum_k |x_k(f)|^2 with DPSS tapers, and "take the leading 2NW - 1 DPSS as data tapers"; section 4.3 eq. 25-26, transfer function and coherence from sums over the tapers (the "local frequency ensemble") of a single pair of series. K = 2NW - 1 is therefore sourced to Mitra & Pesaran section 4.1.5 and the 2K degrees of freedom to Thomson p.1061; neither is attributed to Percival & Walden.
canonical_definition: J_{k,i}(f) = sqrt(dt) * sum_{t=0}^{T-1} h_k(t) (x_i(t) - mean(x_i)) exp(-i 2 pi f t dt), where h_k is the k-th unit-energy DPSS of length T with half-bandwidth W = NW/(T dt); S_ij(f) = (1/K) sum_{k=0}^{K-1} J_{k,i}(f) conj(J_{k,j}(f)). S is two-sided and Hermitian; S_ii(f) is the PSD, whose integral over [-fs/2, fs/2] is the variance. With K = 2NW-1, S_ii(f)/S_true,ii(f) is approximately chi^2_{2K}/(2K) away from 0 and Nyquist.

implemented_as: Input is the Data array (P, T) after optional linear detrend and z-scoring with ddof=1, transposed to (T, P). The multivariate path takes all P channels; the bivariate path for directed SPIs takes only columns [i, j]. Multitaper(z, sampling_frequency=fs=1) uses the library defaults: NW = time_halfbandwidth_product = 3; n_tapers = floor(2*NW - 1) = 5; is_low_bias=True, which drops tapers with concentration <= 0.9 (probe: the 5th taper has 0.946 at every T, so all 5 are kept); the whole series is one window (n_windows = 1, step = T); detrend_type "constant" removes each window mean, which is a no-op after z-scoring; n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T), a 5-smooth length that equals T for T in {64, 256, 1024, 4096} and zero-pads otherwise (probe: T=1009 -> 1024, T=63 -> 64). The tapers have unit energy and are scaled by sqrt(fs); the FFT is divided by fs, so J_k = sqrt(dt) * FFT(h_k x), which gives two-sided PSD scaling (probe: power scales as 1/fs). The Fourier coefficients have shape (1 window, 1 trial, 5 tapers, n_fft, P). The per-taper CSM is X_i conj(X_j) (matmul with the conjugate transpose), and expectation_type "trials_tapers" takes an equal-weight mean over the 5 tapers. There are no adaptive weights and no eigenvalue weights. n_observations is 5 (the tapers), and the debiased phase estimators and group-delay coherence_bias use it downstream. Each measure first builds the full two-sided CSM, then _non_negative_frequencies keeps indices 0..(n_fft+1)//2-1, i.e. f_k = k/n_fft: DC is kept and the Nyquist bin (fftfreq -0.5) is dropped for even n_fft. Results are cached per Data object and per measure key. Every distinct measure rebuilds the Multitaper, the FFT and the full CSM.

deviation_from_documented: (1) Frequency grid. The documentation says "125 uniformly sampled bins ... f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T". The implementation uses the FFT grid f_k = k/n_fft, k = 0..(n_fft+1)//2-1. That gives 32/128/512/2048 bins at T=64/256/1024/4096, starting at DC (f=0, not 4/T) and ending at 0.5 - 1/n_fft (probe at T=64: "nfreq kept 32 first [0. 0.015625] last 0.484375"). The 125-bin figure matches pyspi's wavelet path (pyspi/statistics/wavelet.py:54 cwt_freqs = np.linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125)), whose minimum frequency is 5/T (wavelet.py:62), not 4/T; where the text comes from remains a hypothesis (check stage: grid confirmed by the grid-n* runs). (2) The documented ranges are closed at fs/2, but the Nyquist bin is never available (already documented, REVIEW M4). (3) The supplement cites toolbox v0.2.5.dev0; 1.1.2 is executed. (4) NW=3, K=5, the single window, constant detrend and next_fast_len padding are not documented, so there is nothing to contradict.
deviation_from_canonical: This is the simple (equal-weight) multitaper CSM estimator with NW=3 and K=2NW-1=5. It agrees with a from-scratch implementation to round-off (probe at T=256: max |S_lib - S_scratch| = 2.6e-14 over the two-sided CSM, reference built from scipy.signal.windows.dpss + numpy.fft). The tapers equal the eigenvectors of the dense Slepian sinc kernel to 2.3e-12 (T=64), 1.0e-12 (T=256) and 1.3e-12 (T=1024). Variants rather than errors: (a) no Thomson adaptive weighting; (b) the 5th taper (concentration 0.946) is included; (c) one window, so the "expectation" behind every downstream measure is an average over the 5 tapers only (n_observations = 5), not over trials or time segments; (d) two-sided PSD scaling with no doubling of positive frequencies, which cancels in every normalised measure; (e) S(0) is real (probe: max |Im S(0)| = 0.0) and is estimated after mean removal, so it is biased low within |f| < W = 3/T; (f) for T that is not 5-smooth, the series is zero-padded to next_fast_len(T), so the grid spacing is 1/n_fft instead of 1/T.
units_and_range: Complex, Hermitian matrix per frequency (probe: max |S - S^H| = 0.0). The diagonal is real and >= 0, in units of x^2 per unit frequency (two-sided). With z-scored input and fs=1, the mean of the two-sided power over all n_fft bins equals sum_t (1/K sum_k h_k(t)^2) x_c(t)^2, close to 1 (Parseval; probe agreement 1.2e-15). The DC entries are real. Not a scalar SPI; the only NaNs are set by downstream measures (zero-power normalisation, diagonal).
direction_convention: S[i,j](f) = mean_k X_{k,i}(f) conj(X_{k,j}(f)), with row i = process i (column i of the (T,P) input). Probe on delayed_noise T=1024 (x_j = x0 delayed by d_j): the slope of the unwrapped phase of S[0,j] over f in (0, 0.1), divided by 2 pi, is +1.019, +2.986 and +5.034 for d = 1, 3, 5. A positive phase slope therefore means the row process leads the column process. Every multivariate spectral SPI computes A[i,j] from S[i,j] (spectral.py:91). The bivariate path computes the 2-channel [i, j] result and reads entry [0,1], which has the same orientation. Multivariate and bivariate CSM entries are identical (probe: max |S_mv[2,0] - S_bv[0,1]| = 0.0).

metric_name_standard: multitaper (Thomson) estimate of the cross-spectral density matrix S(f): K=5 Slepian (DPSS) tapers with NW=3, equal-weight average of the taper eigen-cross-spectra, whole series as a single window (infrastructure shared by every multitaper spectral SPI)

Walden 2000, A unified view of multitaper multivariate spectral estimation, Biometrika 87(4):767-788; citation and abstract checked (cross-spectral matrix estimators written as weighted averages of orthogonally tapered cross-periodograms, including the Thomson Slepian-taper estimator); full text not obtained, so no section or equation is cited. J. 76(2):691-708, checked against the arXiv preprint q-bio/0309028v1, not the journal copy: section 4.1.5 eq. 6-7, the direct multitaper estimate S_MT(f) = (1/K) sum_k |x_k(f)|^2 with DPSS tapers, and "take the leading 2NW - 1 DPSS as data tapers"; section 4.3 eq. 25-26, transfer function and coherence from sums over the tapers (the "local frequency ensemble") of a single pair of series. canonical_definition: J_{k,i}(f) = sqrt(dt) * sum_{t=0}^{T-1} h_k(t) (x_i(t) - mean(x_i)) exp(-i 2 pi f t dt), where h_k is the k-th unit-energy DPSS of length T with half-bandwidth W = NW/(T dt); S_ij(f) = (1/K) sum_{k=0}^{K-1} J_{k,i}(f) conj(J_{k,j}(f)). S is two-sided and Hermitian; S_ii(f) is the PSD, whose integral over [-fs/2, fs/2] is the variance. With K = 2NW-1, S_ii(f)/S_true,ii(f) is approximately chi^2_{2K}/(2K) away from 0 and Nyquist.

implemented_as: Input is the Data array (P, T) after optional linear detrend and z-scoring with ddof=1, transposed to (T, P). The multivariate path takes all P channels; the bivariate path for directed SPIs takes only columns [i, j]. Multitaper(z, sampling_frequency=fs=1) uses the library defaults: NW = time_halfbandwidth_product = 3; n_tapers = floor(2*NW - 1) = 5; is_low_bias=True, which drops tapers with concentration <= 0.9 (probe: the 5th taper has 0.946 at every T, so all 5 are kept); the whole series is one window (n_windows = 1, step = T); detrend_type "constant" removes each window mean, which is a no-op after z-scoring; n_fft = scipy.fftpack.next_fast_len(T), a 5-smooth length that equals T for T in {64, 256, 1024, 4096} and zero-pads otherwise (probe: T=1009 -> 1024, T=63 -> 64). The tapers have unit energy and are scaled by sqrt(fs); the FFT is divided by fs, so J_k = sqrt(dt) * FFT(h_k x), which gives two-sided PSD scaling (probe: power scales as 1/fs). The Fourier coefficients have shape (1 window, 1 trial, 5 tapers, n_fft, P). The per-taper CSM is X_i conj(X_j) (matmul with the conjugate transpose), and expectation_type "trials_tapers" takes an equal-weight mean over the 5 tapers. There are no adaptive weights and no eigenvalue weights. n_observations is 5 (the tapers), and the debiased phase estimators and group-delay coherence_bias use it downstream. Each measure first builds the full two-sided CSM, then _non_negative_frequencies keeps indices 0..(n_fft+1)//2-1, i.e. f_k = k/n_fft: DC is kept and the Nyquist bin (fftfreq -0.5) is dropped for even n_fft. Results are cached per Data object and per measure key. Every distinct measure rebuilds the Multitaper, the FFT and the full CSM.
