deviation_from_documented: (1) Frequency grid. The documentation says "125 uniformly sampled bins ... f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T". The implementation uses the FFT grid f_k = k/n_fft, k = 0..(n_fft+1)//2-1. That gives 32/128/512/2048 bins at T=64/256/1024/4096, starting at DC (f=0, not 4/T) and ending at 0.5 - 1/n_fft (probe at T=64: "nfreq kept 32 first [0. 0.015625] last 0.484375"). The 125-bin figure matches pyspi's wavelet path (pyspi/statistics/wavelet.py:54 cwt_freqs = np.linspace(0.2, 0.5, 125)), whose minimum frequency is 5/T (wavelet.py:62), not 4/T; where the text comes from remains a hypothesis (check stage: grid confirmed by the grid-n* runs). (2) The documented ranges are closed at fs/2, but the Nyquist bin is never available (already documented, REVIEW M4). (3) The supplement cites toolbox v0.2.5.dev0; 1.1.2 is executed. (4) NW=3, K=5, the single window, constant detrend and next_fast_len padding are not documented, so there is nothing to contradict.
deviation_from_canonical: This is the simple (equal-weight) multitaper CSM estimator with NW=3 and K=2NW-1=5. It agrees with a from-scratch implementation to round-off (probe at T=256: max |S_lib - S_scratch| = 2.6e-14 over the two-sided CSM, reference built from scipy.signal.windows.dpss + numpy.fft). The tapers equal the eigenvectors of the dense Slepian sinc kernel to 2.3e-12 (T=64), 1.0e-12 (T=256) and 1.3e-12 (T=1024). Variants rather than errors: (a) no Thomson adaptive weighting; (b) the 5th taper (concentration 0.946) is included; (c) one window, so the "expectation" behind every downstream measure is an average over the 5 tapers only (n_observations = 5), not over trials or time segments; (d) two-sided PSD scaling with no doubling of positive frequencies, which cancels in every normalised measure; (e) S(0) is real (probe: max |Im S(0)| = 0.0) and is estimated after mean removal, so it is biased low within |f| < W = 3/T; (f) for T that is not 5-smooth, the series is zero-padded to next_fast_len(T), so the grid spacing is 1/n_fft instead of 1/T.
units_and_range: Complex, Hermitian matrix per frequency (probe: max |S - S^H| = 0.0). The diagonal is real and >= 0, in units of x^2 per unit frequency (two-sided). With z-scored input and fs=1, the mean of the two-sided power over all n_fft bins equals sum_t (1/K sum_k h_k(t)^2) x_c(t)^2, close to 1 (Parseval; probe agreement 1.2e-15). The DC entries are real. Not a scalar SPI; the only NaNs are set by downstream measures (zero-power normalisation, diagonal).
direction_convention: S[i,j](f) = mean_k X_{k,i}(f) conj(X_{k,j}(f)), with row i = process i (column i of the (T,P) input). Probe on delayed_noise T=1024 (x_j = x0 delayed by d_j): the slope of the unwrapped phase of S[0,j] over f in (0, 0.1), divided by 2 pi, is +1.019, +2.986 and +5.034 for d = 1, 3, 5. A positive phase slope therefore means the row process leads the column process. Every multivariate spectral SPI computes A[i,j] from S[i,j] (spectral.py:91). The bivariate path computes the 2-channel [i, j] result and reads entry [0,1], which has the same orientation. Multivariate and bivariate CSM entries are identical (probe: max |S_mv[2,0] - S_bv[0,1]| = 0.0).

method_or_estimator: fmin/fmax selection on the FFT grid (inclusive multivariate, strict bivariate/PSI/GD)
metric_name_standard: band-limited summary (arithmetic mean or maximum over the frequency bins inside [fmin, fmax]) of a per-frequency spectral connectivity measure
canonical_ref: No canonical source fixes inclusive vs exclusive band edges. The documented rule (supplement §1.5) uses closed intervals. For PSI the canonical band rule is Nolte et al. 2008, Phys. Rev. Lett. 100:234101, eq. 3 (sum over frequency pairs (f, f + df) at the native resolution within band F). Bastos & Schoffelen 2016, Front. Syst. Neurosci. 9:175 (supplement [59]) describes band-averaging of spectral measures. Nolte eq. 3 checked against arXiv:0712.2352v1 p.2 (not the PRL journal copy): Psi_tilde_ij = Im(sum_{f in F} C_ij^*(f) C_ij(f + delta_f)), where delta_f "is the frequency resolution", with C_ij from eq. 4. Bastos & Schoffelen is cited for practice only, without a section or equation, and was not re-checked.
canonical_definition: For a grid f_k and band [fmin, fmax]: B = {k : fmin <= f_k <= fmax} (closed, as documented); summary = (1/|B|) sum_{k in B} m(f_k) or max_{k in B} m(f_k). The same B for every SPI that shares an (fmin, fmax) label. For PSI: Psi = Im sum_{f in F} conj(C(f)) C(f + df) over adjacent frequencies.

implemented_as: The grid is conn.frequencies = k/n_fft for k = 0..(n_fft+1)//2 - 1 (DC included, Nyquist excluded). Four paths apply different rules. (a) Multivariate SPIs (cohmag, phase, icoh, plv, pli, wpli, dspli, dswpli, ppc) use freq_id = (freq >= fmin) & (freq <= fmax), inclusive, then np.nanmean or np.nanmax over the frequency axis. NaN bins are skipped silently; an empty selection gives NaN with a RuntimeWarning (mean) or raises ValueError (max). For plv the statistic is applied to |PLV|. (b) Nonparametric SGC uses the same inclusive rule, but fmin <= 0 is overridden to 1e-5, which excludes DC. (c) Bivariate directed SPIs (dcoh, pdcoh, gpdcoh, dtf, ddtf) use a strict rule, (freq > fmin) & (freq < fmax). This drops DC from fmin=0 bands and drops the f = 0.25 bin from both half bands. (d) PSI and GD: pyspi first calls the library method with default arguments, which raises TypeError (PSI at connectivity.py:1329; GD at :1357). It then passes frequencies_of_interest=[fmin, fmax] and frequency_resolution=(fmax-fmin)/50. _bandpass is strict (connectivity.py:1329-1331). PSI keeps every step-th bandpassed bin, with step = ceil(n_fft (fmax-fmin)/50); at T=1024 the full band has step 11 and uses 47 bins. PSI then sums over all unordered pairs (M5). GD regresses the unwrapped phase on the largest significant cluster of the bandpassed bins, subsampled by step, and requires at least 3 points; otherwise the result is NaN. pyspi's own freq_id is computed but not used for PSI (IndexError fallback) or GD (TypeError fallback). Bin counts (inclusive/strict): T=64 full 32/31, low 17/15, high 16/15; T=256 128/127, 65/63, 64/63; T=1024 512/511, 257/255, 256/255; T=4096 2048/2047, 1025/1023, 1024/1023. The f = 0.25 bin lies on the grid at every manifest T and is counted in both the low band and the high band under the inclusive rule.

deviation_from_documented: (1) The documentation uses closed intervals. The bivariate directed SPIs (spectral.py:132), PSI and GD (connectivity.py:1329-1331) use open intervals: DC is dropped from fmin=0 bands and f = fs/4 from both half bands. At T=1024 the strict path averages 511, 255 and 255 bins against 512, 257 and 256 for the multivariate path under the same identifier suffix. (2) The Nyquist bin is never on the grid, so [.., fs/2] is in effect [.., fs/2 - 1/n_fft] (already documented, REVIEW M4). (3) The inclusive multivariate rule puts the f = fs/4 bin in both the low and the high band, so the documented "lower" and "higher" ranges overlap by one bin. (4) The documented 125-bin grid from f0 = 4/T is not used: DC is inside every multivariate fmin=0 band and the bin count is n_fft/2. (5) PSI is computed on a sub-sampled grid (step = ceil(n_fft (fmax-fmin)/50)), which is not documented, and GD only on the largest significant cluster with at least 3 points.
deviation_from_canonical: There is no canonical edge rule, but one (fmin, fmax) label should denote one bin set. Here the bin set depends on the SPI class (inclusive multivariate, strict bivariate/PSI/GD, DC-excluded SGC). For PSI, Nolte 2008 eq. 3 uses adjacent frequency pairs at the native resolution. The library instead sums all pairs (M5, already documented) on a grid sub-sampled with frequency_resolution = band/50, which is not tied to the multitaper bandwidth 2W = 6/T (at T=1024: band/50 = 0.01 for the full band vs 2W = 0.0059). For the narrow EEG bands the bin sets are tiny. With the exact edges configured in pyspi/workflow/retained185.yaml (0.5, 2, 4, 6, 15, 35, 75 and 125 divided by 1024; check stage confirmed, the earlier hypothesis is resolved), T=1024 gives inclusive counts 2, 3, 3 and strict counts 1, 1, 1 for (0.5-2), (2-4) and (4-6); T=512 gives inclusive 1, 2, 2 and strict 0, 0, 0. With the rounded identifier values (0.000488, 0.00195, 0.00391, 0.00586), T=1024 would give inclusive and strict counts 1, 3, 2; the identifier string keeps only 3 significant digits, but the workflow configuration (retained185.yaml) stores the exact floats, so the exact-edge counts are the ones computed (check stage: masks runs).
units_and_range: n/a (selection and aggregation step). The output keeps the units of the per-frequency measure. nanmean/nanmax ignore NaN bins. An empty multivariate selection gives an all-NaN matrix (nanmean) or ValueError -> NaN table (nanmax). metric_name_standard: Nonparametric spectral-matrix factorisation (Wilson 1972 minimum-phase factor) of a multitaper cross-spectral matrix, giving transfer function H and innovation covariance Sigma (shared by dtf, dcoh, pdcoh, gpdcoh, ddtf and sgc_nonparametric)
canonical_ref: Wilson GT (1972) The factorization of matricial spectral densities. SIAM J Appl Math 23(4):420-426; Dhamala M, Rangarajan G, Ding M (2008) Analyzing information flow in brain networks with nonparametric Granger causality. NeuroImage 41:354-362; multitaper: Thomson DJ (1982) Proc IEEE 70:1055-1096
canonical_definition: Find Psi(f) = sum_{k>=0} psi_k e^{-i2pi f k} (minimum phase, causal) with S(f) = Psi(f) Psi(f)^H; iterate Psi <- Psi [Psi^{-1} S Psi^{-H} + I]_+ where [.]_+ keeps positive lags and half the zero lag (upper triangular); then Sigma = psi_0 psi_0^T and H(f) = Psi(f) psi_0^{-1} (H(lag 0) = I)
documented_definition: supplement §1.5, p.12 (line 575-576): 'All directed measures (excluding parametric spectral Granger causality) are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]'; §1.5.9 p.16: 'The cross-spectral density matrix can be decomposed into a noise covariance matrix and a spectral transfer matrix'. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. deviation_from_documented: Documented as a matrix factorisation of the cross-spectral matrix; implemented as such, but per ordered pair on a 2-channel matrix (not the P-channel matrix), recomputed separately for each measure and for (i, j) and (j, i). The multitaper grid and band rule deviate from the documented 125-bin grid (see the measure records).
deviation_from_canonical: Algorithm follows Wilson 1972 / Dhamala et al. 2008 (same plus operator as their MATLAB code, including halving the upper zero-lag triangle). Deviations: (a) no zero padding (n_fft = T): the multitaper CSM has autocovariance up to lag T-1, which wraps on a T-point grid; the factor cannot represent lag n/2, leaving a relative factorisation residual |Psi Psi^H - S|/max|S| of 1e-3..2e-2 on regular data. In the lag domain the residual peaks at lag n/2 but is spread around it: on var2_bivariate T=1024 lag 512 is the largest single lag yet carries only 5% of the summed lag-domain residual, lags within +/-8 of n/2 carry 19%, within +/-32 33%, within +/-128 66% (pR_lagshare.py; review pF_wilson.py 'share of lag-sum at top lag 0.05'). Zero padding removes most of it (p8_resid.py: 2.06e-2 with n_fft=T, 9.1e-5 with n_fft=2T; DTF[1,0] band mean 0.2689 vs 0.2682); (b) convergence is declared on the change of Psi, not on the residual; on logistic_maps T >= 1024 it does not converge in 60 iterations and the result is used anyway (p7_wilson.py); on narrowband_f0-0.25 it "converges" with residual 0.6 (line spectra violate the factorisability (Szego) condition); (c) a 5-taper single-window CSM has variance that does not fall with T, so every downstream directed measure has a T-independent positive bias in the null direction (~0.11, p5_bias_T.py); (d) the result depends on channel order by up to 5e-3 per bin (p6_misc.py equivariance: dtf 5.3e-3, dcoh 8.5e-3, gpdcoh 4.6e-3), whereas the exact factor is order-equivariant.

metric_name_standard: Nonparametric spectral-matrix factorisation (Wilson 1972 minimum-phase factor) of a multitaper cross-spectral matrix, giving transfer function H and innovation covariance Sigma (shared by dtf, dcoh, pdcoh, gpdcoh, ddtf and sgc_nonparametric)
canonical_ref: Wilson GT (1972) The factorization of matricial spectral densities. SIAM J Appl Math 23(4):420-426; Dhamala M, Rangarajan G, Ding M (2008) Analyzing information flow in brain networks with nonparametric Granger causality. canonical_definition: Find Psi(f) = sum_{k>=0} psi_k e^{-i2pi f k} (minimum phase, causal) with S(f) = Psi(f) Psi(f)^H; iterate Psi <- Psi [Psi^{-1} S Psi^{-H} + I]_+ where [.]_+ keeps positive lags and half the zero lag (upper triangular); then Sigma = psi_0 psi_0^T and H(f) = Psi(f) psi_0^{-1} (H(lag 0) = I)
documented_definition: supplement §1.5, p.12 (line 575-576): 'All directed measures (excluding parametric spectral Granger causality) are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]'; §1.5.9 p.16: 'The cross-spectral density matrix can be decomposed into a noise covariance matrix and a spectral transfer matrix'. Band rule, supplement §1.5, p.12-13 (supplement.txt lines 570-599 in this checkout; the pack's line numbers are offset by about 12-16): 'We use 125 uniformly sampled bins across the entire frequency range, f in [f0, fs/2] ... f0 = 4/T' and bands 'fmin-0_fmax-0-5: f in [0, fs/2]; fmin-0_fmax-0-25: f in [0, fs/4]; fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5: f in [fs/4, fs/2]', summary = mean or max over the band. Directed measures 'are nonparametrically estimated through spectral matrix factorization [57, 58]' (§1.5, p.12). deviation_from_documented: Documented as a matrix factorisation of the cross-spectral matrix; implemented as such, but per ordered pair on a 2-channel matrix (not the P-channel matrix), recomputed separately for each measure and for (i, j) and (j, i). The multitaper grid and band rule deviate from the documented 125-bin grid (see the measure records).
deviation_from_canonical: Algorithm follows Wilson 1972 / Dhamala et al. 2008 (same plus operator as their MATLAB code, including halving the upper zero-lag triangle). Deviations: (a) no zero padding (n_fft = T): the multitaper CSM has autocovariance up to lag T-1, which wraps on a T-point grid; the factor cannot represent lag n/2, leaving a relative factorisation residual |Psi Psi^H - S|/max|S| of 1e-3..2e-2 on regular data. In the lag domain the residual peaks at lag n/2 but is spread around it: on var2_bivariate T=1024 lag 512 is the largest single lag yet carries only 5% of the summed lag-domain residual, lags within +/-8 of n/2 carry 19%, within +/-32 33%, within +/-128 66% (pR_lagshare.py; review pF_wilson.py 'share of lag-sum at top lag 0.05'). Zero padding removes most of it (p8_resid.py: 2.06e-2 with n_fft=T, 9.1e-5 with n_fft=2T; DTF[1,0] band mean 0.2689 vs 0.2682); (b) convergence is declared on the change of Psi, not on the residual; on logistic_maps T >= 1024 it does not converge in 60 iterations and the result is used anyway (p7_wilson.py); on narrowband_f0-0.25 it "converges" with residual 0.6 (line spectra violate the factorisability (Szego) condition); (c) a 5-taper single-window CSM has variance that does not fall with T, so every downstream directed measure has a T-independent positive bias in the null direction (~0.11, p5_bias_T.py); (d) the result depends on channel order by up to 5e-3 per bin (p6_misc.py equivariance: dtf 5.3e-3, dcoh 8.5e-3, gpdcoh 4.6e-3), whereas the exact factor is order-equivariant.

score_rubric_note: Anchor 7: the Wilson iteration agrees with an independent implementation to 4.3e-13, but the configuration changes values. With no zero padding the residual is 2.06e-2 against 9.1e-5 at n_fft = 2T (DTF[1,0] 0.2689 vs 0.2682), and the 5-taper CSM gives the downstream bias.
what_changed: The Wilson iteration (Dhamala et al. 2008 form) and the H / Sigma extraction match an independent implementation to 4e-13 and the analytic factors to 4e-15 (Sigma to the stopping tolerance). The configuration deviates: (a) no zero padding, so the factor cannot represent lags >= n/2 and the factorisation residual is 0.3-3% on regular data; (b) convergence is declared on the step size and non-convergence only logs a warning, so factorisations with residual 0.3-0.6 (logistic maps, narrowband) feed every directed measure; (c) the 5-taper single-window CSM makes every downstream measure inconsistent (T-independent bias, measure records); (d) the step-converged factor of the non-factorisable CSM is not equivariant: swapping or rescaling channels changes per-bin H by up to O(1) at isolated bins and band means by 1e-3..3e-2; (e) under numpy >= 2.4 (as checked) the Cholesky fallback raises AttributeError (mpd:48 xp.linalg.linalg), turning the whole SPI matrix NaN, but only when rounding makes the duplicated pair's lag-0 covariance fail Cholesky; otherwise the degenerate pair silently gets a finite value (dtf 0.528, gpdcoh 0.507). spectral_connectivity v2.0.1 already catches xp.linalg.LinAlgError. canonical_ref: Morlet wavelet as used in electrophysiology: Tallon-Baudry, Bertrand, Delpuech & Pernier 1997, J Neurosci 17:722 (w(t,f0) = A exp(-t^2/(2 sigma_t^2)) exp(2 i pi f0 t), sigma_f = 1/(2 pi sigma_t), f0/sigma_f = 7, i.e. about 7 cycles); Grossmann & Morlet 1984, SIAM J Math Anal 15:723; Torrence & Compo 1998, Bull Am Meteorol Soc 79:61 (admissibility, omega0 = 6). Single-trial wavelet coherence/smoothing: Lachaux et al. 2002, Neurophysiol Clin 32:157; Grinsted et al. 2004, Nonlin Proc Geophys 11:561.
canonical_definition: X(f,t) = sum_tau x(t - tau) w_f(tau), w_f(t) = A exp(-t^2/(2 sigma_t^2)) exp(2 i pi f t), sigma_t = n_cycles/(2 pi f) with n_cycles of order 3-7 so the wavelet spans several periods; requires sigma_t >> 1 sample for f < fs/2 to resolve frequency; cross-spectrum X_x X_y* averaged over trials or a time/scale window before forming connectivity ratios.

The 'CWT' is X(f,t) = sqrt(2) x(t) for all 125 f up to FFT round-off (probe: max|Re X - sqrt2 x| 2.7e-15, max|Im X| 7.2e-16, ~2-5% of Im exactly 0). csd(f,t) = X_hi(f,t) conj(X_lo(f,t)) = 2 x_hi(t) x_lo(t) + i*roundoff (hi = higher channel index, lower-triangular connections), psd = |X|^2 = 2 x^2. n_epochs = 1, so every across-epoch average in the estimator is a single term. pyspi then keeps the frequencies with fmin <= f <= fmax on the 0.2..0.5 grid (21 bins for fmin-0_fmax-0-25: 0.2..0.2476; 104 for fmin-0-25_fmax-0-5; all 125 for 0..0.5), applies np.nanmean or np.nanmax over (freq, time) jointly, mirrors the lower triangle to the upper, sets the diagonal NaN. (c) The classes using it are not documented at all (absent from config.yaml, supplement and GitBook).
deviation_from_canonical: Canonical Morlet analysis uses n_cycles of several cycles (Tallon-Baudry f0/sigma_f = 7; MNE default n_cycles = 7) so that sigma_t spans several samples; here n_cycles = f/7 (the Tallon-Baudry ratio sigma_f = f/7 passed where MNE expects a cycle count, or a copy of the Hz-scaled MNE example) gives 0.029-0.071 cycles and a single-sample wavelet with no frequency selectivity; the zero-mean correction is then a near-total cancellation (1 - 0.9996 .. 1 - 0.9975) rescaled by the norm, leaving W = sqrt(2). The CWT output has an imaginary part consisting only of FFT round-off. One epoch is passed, so no across-trial averaging occurs in any downstream estimator.

metric_name_standard: Linear-Gaussian (plug-in maximum-likelihood covariance) estimator of differential entropy, mutual information and conditional mutual information / transfer entropy
canonical_ref: Cover T.M. & Thomas J.A. 2006, Elements of Information Theory, 2nd ed., Wiley, Theorem 8.4.1 (h(N_n(mu,K)) = 0.5 log((2 pi e)^n |K|)) and Example 8.5.1 (I = -0.5 log(1-rho^2)); Barnett, Barrett & Seth 2009, Phys Rev Lett 103:238701 (Gaussian TE = half Geweke GC)
canonical_definition: h(X) = 0.5*(d*(1+ln 2pi) + ln det Sigma_X); I(X;Y) = 0.5*ln(det Sigma_X det Sigma_Y / det Sigma_XY); I(X;Y|Z) = 0.5*ln(det Sigma_XZ det Sigma_YZ / (det Sigma_XYZ det Sigma_Z)), all in nats with Sigma the (sample) covariance
documented_definition: supplement §1.4, p.9 (supplement.txt:405-415): 'The Gaussian-distribution model (denoted by modifier gaussian) assumes a linear-Gaussian multivariate, where the measure is derived from the cross-covariance matrix'; the supplement says JIDT 'v1.5' while GitBook information-theory.md:11-13 says 'v1.6.1'. Units (nats) and covariance normalisation are not documented.

implemented_as: Input is the pyspi Data array after optional detrend and default z-scoring with ddof=1. Entropies: sample covariance with divisor n-1 (JIDT MatrixUtils), Cholesky (non-PD -> Java NonPositiveDefiniteMatrixException propagated to Python), h = 0.5*(d(1+ln 2pi)+ln det) in nats; the jar's entropy class reports NORMALISE=true but the Gaussian path never normalises. MI/CMI: covariance determinants with linearly redundant components pruned, NORMALISE=false, BIAS_CORRECTION=false (set by pyspi), returns 0 for fully redundant marginals and +Infinity for joint redundancy. Because pyspi z-scores with ddof=1 and JIDT also uses ddof=1, every univariate Gaussian entropy is exactly 0.5*(1+ln 2pi) = 1.4189385332 nats. pyspi caches univariate entropies in data.entropy[(estimator,)] and joint entropies in data.joint_entropy (infotheory.py:137-177).

metric_name_standard: Kozachenko-Leonenko (k=1 nearest-neighbour) differential entropy estimator, Euclidean norm, natural units; the shared entropy kernel behind every *_kozachenko SPI (je, ce, cce, xme, di, si)
canonical_ref: Kozachenko LF, Leonenko NN (1987) "Sample estimate of the entropy of a random vector", Problems of Information Transmission 23(2):95-101 (Probl. Peredachi Inf. 23(2):9-16); in the digamma form of Kraskov A, Stoegbauer H, Grassberger P (2004) "Estimating mutual information", Phys Rev E 69:066138, Eq. (20) with k=1 (c_d = volume of the d-dimensional ball of unit diameter; Euclidean c_d = pi^(d/2) / Gamma(1+d/2) / 2^d).
canonical_definition: For N iid samples x_i in R^d, eps_i = 2 * min_{j != i} ||x_i - x_j||_2 and H_hat = -psi(1) + psi(N) + log c_d + (d/N) sum_i log eps_i (nats); equivalently -psi(1) + psi(N) + log V_d + (d/N) sum_i log rho_i with rho_i the NN distance and V_d the unit-radius ball volume. The 1987 original uses log(N-1) + gamma instead of psi(N) - psi(1) (difference O(1/N)). Consistent for the differential entropy of a density; assumes iid samples, no ties.
documented_definition: Supplement §1.4, p.9 (supplement.txt:405; the pack lists line 414): "The Kozachenko-Leonenko technique (kozachenko) is a nearest-neighbour approach that is suitable when measures can only be constructed using entropy or joint entropy (not mutual information)"; "We primarily use v1.5 of the Java Information Dynamics Toolkit [32]". GitBook information-theory.md lines 11 and 15 repeat the description and say "v1.6.1" of JIDT. No norm, k, noise or normalisation setting is documented.

implemented_as: pyspi builds one EntropyCalculatorMultiVariateKozachenko per SPI instance (JIDTBase.__init__ -> _getcalc('entropy')) and sets BIAS_CORRECTION=false (ignored by this class) and NOISE_SEED=42 (honoured by this jar). Inputs are the pyspi Data rows, z-scored per series with ddof=1 by the Calculator default (normalise=True); every composed SPI passes a (n_obs x d) double[][] to initialise(d)/setObservations. JIDT then: (1) copies observations; (2) adds iid N(0, (1e-8)^2) noise to every coordinate from java.util.Random seeded with 42 at every setObservations call (same noise sequence each call, so results are deterministic); (3) does NOT normalise, although getProperty ('NORMALISE') returns 'true'; (4) computes each point's Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance, by an O(N^2) 'fast' routine with O(N^2) memory when N <= 2000 and by a 'naive' routine when N > 2000; (5) returns (d/N) sum log(2 rho_i) + [psi(N) - psi(1)] + log[(pi/4)^(d/2) / Gamma(d/2+1)] in nats. psi(N) - psi(1) is the exact harmonic number H_{N-1} for N < 10000 (the truncated constant gamma = 0.5772156 cancels). No Theiler window, no k > 1.

implemented_as: Preprocessing: Calculator z-scores every series (ddof=1). pyspi passes KERNEL_WIDTH = str(kernel_width) (0.5 for je/ce/cce/xme/di/si, 0.25 for mi/tlmi/te via config); JIDT keeps NORMALISE=true, so per dimension the half-width is w_d = width * sampleSD(column passed to JIDT) (n-1 divisor), recomputed for every sub-array (lagged/embedded columns are not exactly unit-SD). Counting: closed box (a point is excluded only if |dx_d| > w_d), max norm, the query point counts itself, no Theiler window (pyspi never sets DYN_CORR_EXCL for kernel), no added noise, no bias correction (no kernel class has a bias-correction property; TransferEntropyCalculatorKernel.computeAverageLocalOfObservationsWithCorrection L338 at the JIDT v1.6.1 tag (byte-identical at a9b6b3e), a Grassberger digamma variant, is never called by pyspi). Bins of width w_d with +-1 neighbour search, hash bins, or all-pairs comparison give identical integer counts. Entropy = -mean log2(C/(N*prod 2w_d)); MI = mean log2(N C_xy/(C_x C_y)); TE = mean log2((C_nps/C_ps)/(C_np/C_p)). pyspi's BIAS_CORRECTION='false' is not a property of any kernel class and is ignored. NOISE_SEED='42' is stored by EntropyCalculatorMultiVariateKernel (via EntropyCalculatorMultiVariateCommon) and by MutualInfoCalculatorMultiVariateKernel (via MutualInfoMultiVariateCommon), but noise is added only when NOISE_LEVEL_TO_ADD is non-zero and pyspi leaves it at the default 0, so the seed has no numerical effect; TransferEntropyCalculatorKernel ignores NOISE_SEED. Copy path: JIDTBase.__deepcopy__ resets the JIDT calculators to their defaults (KERNEL_WIDTH 0.25), so a CalculatorFrame computes every W-0.5 kernel SPI at width 0.25 under its W-0.5 identifier; the W-0.25 SPIs are unchanged only because 0.25 is JIDT's default. Caches on the Data object: data.entropy and data.joint_entropy keyed by ('kernel', width) shared by je/ce; data.causal_entropy keyed by ('kernel', width, n) shared by cce/di.

implemented_as: Preprocessing: Calculator z-scores every series (ddof=1). pyspi passes KERNEL_WIDTH = str(kernel_width) (0.5 for je/ce/cce/xme/di/si, 0.25 for mi/tlmi/te via config); JIDT keeps NORMALISE=true, so per dimension the half-width is w_d = width * sampleSD(column passed to JIDT) (n-1 divisor), recomputed for every sub-array (lagged/embedded columns are not exactly unit-SD). Counting: closed box (a point is excluded only if |dx_d| > w_d), max norm, the query point counts itself, no Theiler window (pyspi never sets DYN_CORR_EXCL for kernel), no added noise, no bias correction (no kernel class has a bias-correction property; TransferEntropyCalculatorKernel.computeAverageLocalOfObservationsWithCorrection L338 at the JIDT v1.6.1 tag (byte-identical at a9b6b3e), a Grassberger digamma variant, is never called by pyspi). Bins of width w_d with +-1 neighbour search, hash bins, or all-pairs comparison give identical integer counts. Entropy = -mean log2(C/(N*prod 2w_d)); MI = mean log2(N C_xy/(C_x C_y)); TE = mean log2((C_nps/C_ps)/(C_np/C_p)). pyspi's BIAS_CORRECTION='false' is not a property of any kernel class and is ignored. NOISE_SEED='42' is stored by EntropyCalculatorMultiVariateKernel (via EntropyCalculatorMultiVariateCommon) and by MutualInfoCalculatorMultiVariateKernel (via MutualInfoMultiVariateCommon), but noise is added only when NOISE_LEVEL_TO_ADD is non-zero and pyspi leaves it at the default 0, so the seed has no numerical effect; TransferEntropyCalculatorKernel ignores NOISE_SEED. Copy path: JIDTBase.__deepcopy__ resets the JIDT calculators to their defaults (KERNEL_WIDTH 0.25), so a CalculatorFrame computes every W-0.5 kernel SPI at width 0.25 under its W-0.5 identifier; the W-0.25 SPIs are unchanged only because 0.25 is JIDT's default. Caches on the Data object: data.entropy and data.joint_entropy keyed by ('kernel', width) shared by je/ce; data.causal_entropy keyed by ('kernel', width, n) shared by cce/di.

method_or_estimator: DYN_CORR_EXCL = int(2 * dot(acf(src), acf(targ))) per pair
metric_name_standard: Theiler window (dynamic correlation exclusion) size chosen from the autocorrelation time of the pair via Bartlett's formula
canonical_ref: Theiler 1986, Phys. Rev. A 34, 2427 (window, supplement [36]); Bartlett 1946, J. R. Stat. Soc. Suppl. 8, 27 (supplement [37]) for the variance of the sample cross-correlation of two autocorrelated series, Var(r_xy) ≈ (1/T) Σ_{k=−∞}^{∞} ρ_x(k) ρ_y(k); the effective-sample-size form T_eff = T / (1 + 2 Σ_{k>=1} ρ_x(k) ρ_y(k)) as used by Cliff et al. 2021, Phys. Rev. Research 3, 013145 (supplement [10]). Forms from memory; see Open questions.
canonical_definition: Autocorrelation time of the pair τ = Σ_{k=−∞}^{∞} ρ_x(k) ρ_y(k) = 1 + 2 Σ_{k>=1} ρ_x(k) ρ_y(k) (population ACFs; in practice the sum is truncated at a lag where the sample ACF is no longer distinguishable from 0); Theiler window W of about τ samples, excluding neighbours with |t − t'| <= W.
documented_definition: supplement §1.4, p.9-10 (pack lines 414-453): 'The window size should be large enough to render observations included in the density estimate uncorrelated (sometimes called the "autocorrelation time" [36]); here, we set the window as the product of the autocorrelation functions of both time series (a heuristic for the autocorrelation time based on Bartlett's formula [10, 37]). The DCE modifier indicates that the Theiler window is used for the KSG estimator.' GitBook information-theory.md:20 same text.
delegate_lib: pyspi (numpy 2.5.4 np.correlate / np.dot, scipy 1.17.1 scipy.stats.zscore); consumed by JIDT DYN_CORR_EXCL
implemented_as: On the first DCE call for a Data object: for every pair _i < _j, W[_i,_j] = W[_j,_i] = 2 · Σ_{k=0}^{T−1} r_i(k) r_j(k), with r the biased sample ACF of the z-scored (ddof=0) preprocessed series over all lags 0..T−1 (np.correlate 'full', normalised by lag 0); cached as data.theiler and shared by every DCE SPI on that Data. Per pair the calculator receives DYN_CORR_EXCL = int(W[i,j]) (truncation toward 0). In JIDT a neighbour is excluded when |t − t'| <= W; W = 0 or 1 still excludes only very close points.

deviation_from_documented: Documented as 'the product of the autocorrelation functions of both time series'; implemented as twice the inner product of the two full sample ACFs (lags 0..T−1), then int(). Documented as a heuristic for the autocorrelation time; for oscillatory, periodic, trending or random-walk inputs the value grows linearly with T (probe p3: narrowband 22/85/339/1353 at T=64/256/1024/4096) and is not an autocorrelation time.
deviation_from_canonical: Relative to Bartlett's 1 + 2Σ_{k>=1} ρ_xρ_y: (1) the lag-0 term is doubled, so the raw value is exactly Bartlett + 1 (probe p3: difference 1.00 on every pair); (2) int() truncation; (3) the sum uses the biased sample ACF over all T−1 lags with no truncation, so noisy high-lag products accumulate and periodic components contribute ≈ T/3 (2 Σ (1−k/T)² cos²(ωk)); (4) the window is a pair quantity (product of both ACFs) while a Theiler window is usually set from the autocorrelation time of the embedded variables. For white noise W = 1 or 2 depending on sampling noise (probe p3 iid_gaussian T=1024: [2,2,1,1,2,2,2,2,1,1]).
